FILE: backend/agents/explorer_agent.py
================================================
"""
agents/explorer_agent.py

EXPLORER AGENT

Purpose:
    Given a live browser session and one plain-English test case, carries
    it out by reading the screen, deciding what to interact with, and
    verifying the expected outcome. Produces a trace that the compiler
    turns into a saved, reusable Selenium/pytest script.

Inputs:
    driver       — a live Selenium WebDriver, already on the target page.
    test_case    — plain-English description of what to verify.
    provider     — an LLMProvider instance (from llm/provider_factory.py).
    on_step      — optional callback(step_num, step_dict) for live progress.

Output:
    A list of trace steps ending in a "done" step with passed/notes/source.
    source="model" means the agent reached a real verdict.
    source="system" means the agent gave up (quota, timeout, error) —
    this distinction is critical: system give-ups must never be compiled
    or reported as genuine test failures.
"""

import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Optional

from llm.base import LLMProvider, LLMProviderError
from core import tools
from core.tools_registry import TOOL_DEFINITIONS

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_STEPS = 20
SYSTEM_PROMPT = (Path(__file__).parent.parent / "prompts" / "explorer_system_prompt.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

EXPLORER_TOOLS = [
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["get_snapshot"],
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["click"],
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["type_text"],
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["done"],
]


def run_explorer(
    driver,
    test_case: str,
    provider: LLMProvider,
    on_step: Optional[Callable] = None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Runs the Explorer Agent loop.

    Args:
        driver: A live Selenium WebDriver instance, already on the right page.
        test_case: Plain-English description of what to carry out.
        provider: LLM provider instance from provider_factory.get_provider().
        on_step: Optional callback called after every step with
            (step_number: int, step: dict). Used for live progress streaming.

    Returns:
        A trace: a list of step dicts. The last step is always a "done" step.
        Check step["input"]["source"] to distinguish a real model verdict
        from a system give-up.
    """
    tool = provider.build_tool(EXPLORER_TOOLS)
    trace: list[dict] = []
    last_snapshot_by_ref: dict[str, dict] = {}

    contents = [provider.user_text_content(
        f"Test case: {test_case}\n\nExplore the current screen and carry out this test case."
    )]

    try:
        for step_num in range(1, MAX_STEPS + 1):
            response = provider.call_model(SYSTEM_PROMPT, tool, contents)
            name, args = provider.extract_function_call(response)

            if name is None:
                step = _system_done("Model responded without a tool call.")
                trace.append(step)
                if on_step:
                    on_step(step_num, step)
                return trace

            contents.append(response.candidates[0].content)
            result = _execute_tool(driver, name, args, last_snapshot_by_ref)

            step = {"action": name, "input": args}
            if name in ("click", "type_text"):
                step["ref_info"] = last_snapshot_by_ref.get(args.get("ref"), {})
            if name == "done":
                # This is a real model verdict — tag it so the compiler knows.
                step["input"] = {**step["input"], "source": "model"}

            trace.append(step)
            if on_step:
                on_step(step_num, step)

            contents.append(provider.function_response_content(name, result))

            if name == "done":
                return trace

        # Ran out of steps without calling done
        step = _system_done(f"Gave up after {MAX_STEPS} steps without reaching a verdict.")
        trace.append(step)
        if on_step:
            on_step(MAX_STEPS, step)
        return trace

    except LLMProviderError as e:
        # Provider failed after all retries — this is NOT a real test result.
        logger.error("Explorer agent LLM failure: %s", e)
        step = _system_done(f"LLM provider error: {e}")
        trace.append(step)
        if on_step:
            on_step(len(trace), step)
        return trace

    except Exception as e:
        # Catch-all so callers always get a well-formed trace, never a crash.
        logger.exception("Unexpected error in Explorer agent")
        step = _system_done(f"Unexpected error: {e}")
        trace.append(step)
        if on_step:
            on_step(len(trace), step)
        return trace


def _execute_tool(
    driver, name: str, args: dict, last_snapshot_by_ref: dict
) -> object:
    """Dispatches a tool call to the appropriate core/tools function."""
    if name == "get_snapshot":
        snapshot = tools.get_snapshot(driver)
        last_snapshot_by_ref.clear()
        last_snapshot_by_ref.update({
            el["ref"]: el for el in snapshot if "ref" in el
        })
        return snapshot
    if name == "click":
        return tools.click(args["ref"])
    if name == "type_text":
        return tools.type_text(args["ref"], args["text"])
    if name == "done":
        return tools.done(args.get("passed", False), args.get("notes", ""))
    return {"error": f"Unknown tool: {name}"}


def _system_done(notes: str) -> dict:
    """
    Creates a system-level done step (not a real model verdict).
    source="system" tells the compiler this is an infrastructure failure,
    not a genuine test result — it must never become an assert False.
    """
    return {
        "action": "done",
        "input": {"passed": False, "notes": notes, "source": "system"},
    }

"""
agents/healer_agent.py

HEALER AGENT

Purpose:
    Given a broken selector and why it failed, finds the element that now
    serves the same purpose. Never applies its own proposal — always returns
    a proposal for human review and explicit approval.

Inputs:
    driver           — live Selenium WebDriver.
    test_case        — the original test case this selector belonged to.
    failed_selector  — the CSS selector that stopped matching.
    failure_notes    — why it broke.
    provider         — LLMProvider instance.
    on_step          — optional progress callback.

Output:
    {"found": bool, "role"?, "name"?, "confidence"?, "reasoning"?, "trace": [...]}
"""

import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Optional

from llm.base import LLMProvider, LLMProviderError
from core import tools
from core.tools_registry import TOOL_DEFINITIONS

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_STEPS = 10
SYSTEM_PROMPT = (Path(__file__).parent.parent / "prompts" / "healer_system_prompt.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

HEALER_TOOLS = [
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["get_snapshot"],
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["click"],
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["done"],
    TOOL_DEFINITIONS["propose_replacement"],
]


def run_healer(
    driver,
    test_case: str,
    failed_selector: str,
    failure_notes: str,
    provider: LLMProvider,
    on_step: Optional[Callable] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Runs the Healer Agent loop.

    Args:
        driver: Live Selenium WebDriver.
        test_case: The original test case context.
        failed_selector: The selector that broke.
        failure_notes: Why it failed.
        provider: LLM provider from provider_factory.get_provider().
        on_step: Optional progress callback.

    Returns:
        On success: {"found": True, "role": ..., "name": ...,
                     "confidence": ..., "reasoning": ..., "trace": [...]}
        On failure: {"found": False, "notes": ..., "trace": [...]}
    """
    tool = provider.build_tool(HEALER_TOOLS)
    trace: list[dict] = []

    contents = [provider.user_text_content(
        f"Test case: {test_case}\n\n"
        f"Broken selector: {failed_selector}\n"
        f"Reason: {failure_notes}\n\n"
        "Find the current equivalent element and call propose_replacement, "
        "or call done if nothing plausibly matches."
    )]

    try:
        for step_num in range(1, MAX_STEPS + 1):
            response = provider.call_model(SYSTEM_PROMPT, tool, contents)
            name, args = provider.extract_function_call(response)

            if name is None:
                step = {"action": "done", "input": {"passed": False, "notes": "No tool call"}}
                trace.append(step)
                if on_step:
                    on_step(step_num, step)
                return {"found": False, "notes": "Model responded without a tool call.", "trace": trace}

            contents.append(response.candidates[0].content)

            if name == "propose_replacement":
                step = {"action": name, "input": args}
                trace.append(step)
                if on_step:
                    on_step(step_num, step)
                return {
                    "found": True,
                    "role": args["role"],
                    "name": args["name"],
                    "confidence": args["confidence"],
                    "reasoning": args["reasoning"],
                    "trace": trace,
                }

            if name == "get_snapshot":
                result = tools.get_snapshot(driver)
            elif name == "click":
                result = tools.click(args["ref"])
            elif name == "done":
                result = tools.done(args.get("passed", False), args.get("notes", ""))
            else:
                result = {"error": f"Unknown tool: {name}"}

            step = {"action": name, "input": args}
            trace.append(step)
            if on_step:
                on_step(step_num, step)

            if name == "done":
                return {"found": False, "notes": args.get("notes", ""), "trace": trace}

            contents.append(provider.function_response_content(name, result))

        return {"found": False, "notes": f"Gave up after {MAX_STEPS} steps", "trace": trace}

    except LLMProviderError as e:
        logger.error("Healer agent LLM failure: %s", e)
        return {"found": False, "notes": f"LLM provider error: {e}", "trace": trace}

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Unexpected error in Healer agent")
        return {"found": False, "notes": f"Unexpected error: {e}", "trace": trace}

"""
api/main.py

FastAPI application entry point.

Startup sequence:
1. Settings are validated (happens at import time in core/settings.py)
2. Database pool is initialised
3. Routers are registered
4. Central error middleware is registered

If any required environment variable is missing, the application fails
here with a clear error message — not mid-request, not silently.
"""

import logging
import os
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from core.db.connection import init_pool
from core.logging_config import configure_logging
from core.settings import settings
from api.routes import run as run_routes
from api.routes import test_data as test_data_routes
from api.routes import dashboard as dashboard_routes

# Configure structured JSON logging to stdout before any other code runs.
# Level can be overridden with LOG_LEVEL env var (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR).
_log_level = getattr(logging, os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO").upper(), logging.INFO)
configure_logging(level=_log_level)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """Runs once at startup and once at shutdown."""
    logger.info("NextGen2 backend starting")
    init_pool()
    logger.info("Database pool ready")

    # Background scheduler: wakes every 30s and runs whatever is due.
    from service import scheduler as scheduler_service
    scheduler_service.start()
    yield
    logger.info("NextGen2 backend shutting down")
    from service import scheduler as scheduler_service
    scheduler_service.stop()


app = FastAPI(
    title="NextGen2 API",
    version="1.0.0",
    lifespan=lifespan,
    docs_url="/docs",
    redoc_url="/redoc",
)

# CORS — allows the Next.js frontend to call this API
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=settings.app.cors_origins,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)


# ─── Central error handler ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One place that maps typed exceptions to safe response shapes.
# The full exception and stack trace are logged on the backend.
# The frontend never receives a raw traceback.

@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def global_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception):
    logger.exception(
        "Unhandled exception on %s %s", request.method, request.url.path
    )
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=500,
        content={"error": {"code": "INTERNAL_ERROR", "message": "An unexpected error occurred."}},
    )


# ─── Health check ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@app.get("/health", tags=["health"])
async def health():
    """
    Returns the application's health status.
    Checks database connectivity. Used by monitoring, not business logic.
    """
    from core.db.connection import get_conn
    try:
        with get_conn() as conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute("SELECT 1")
        db_status = "ok"
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error("Health check: database unreachable — %s", e)
        db_status = "error"

    return {"status": "ok" if db_status == "ok" else "degraded", "database": db_status}

================================================
FILE: backend/api/sse.py
================================================
"""
api/sse.py

Server-Sent Events helper used by every long-running endpoint:
survey, generate, execute, and batch.

The orchestrator calls the progress_callback with (event_type, data).
The callback puts the event on an asyncio Queue.
The queue_to_stream generator pulls events off the queue.
The event_stream generator serialises each event as an SSE chunk.
The StreamingResponse in each route consumes event_stream.

Flow: orchestrator -> callback -> queue -> queue_to_stream -> event_stream -> browser
"""
import asyncio
import base64
import datetime
import decimal
import json
import logging
import uuid
from typing import AsyncGenerator

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# How often to emit a keep-alive when no real progress event has arrived.
# Real deployments (server behind a corporate proxy/VPN/load balancer) commonly
# have an idle-connection timeout of 60-120s. A single slow step -- e.g. an
# LLM call stuck in a multi-attempt retry loop against a gateway that is
# itself timing out -- can leave this stream silent for minutes with the
# orchestrator still working, since queue_to_stream previously only wrote a
# byte when a real event arrived. On localhost that silence is invisible
# (nothing on that path has an idle timeout); on a real deployment it gets
# read as the connection being dead, and the browser reports a network
# error even though the backend is still working and would have delivered
# the result. This value must stay comfortably under the shortest idle
# timeout in the real network path; 15s is a conservative default.
SSE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS = float(__import__("os").environ.get("SSE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS", "15"))

# Sentinel event type used internally between queue_to_stream and
# event_stream to signal "write a keep-alive", never surfaced to the caller
# of make_progress_queue and never seen by the orchestrator.
_KEEPALIVE = "__sse_keepalive__"


class _SafeEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    """
    Custom JSON encoder that handles every type PostgreSQL rows commonly
    return that the stdlib encoder rejects.

    Without this, a single datetime column in a proposal row crashes the
    entire SSE stream with a TypeError before the frontend receives anything.

    Handles:
        datetime / date / time  -> ISO 8601 string (e.g. "2026-07-09T21:56:53")
        Decimal                 -> float           (e.g. cost_usd columns)
        UUID                    -> string          (e.g. future ID fields)
        bytes                   -> base64 string   (e.g. binary columns)
        anything else           -> str(obj)        (never crashes, always streams)
    """

    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, (datetime.datetime, datetime.date, datetime.time)):
            return obj.isoformat()
        if isinstance(obj, decimal.Decimal):
            return float(obj)
        if isinstance(obj, uuid.UUID):
            return str(obj)
        if isinstance(obj, bytes):
            return base64.b64encode(obj).decode()
        try:
            return super().default(obj)
        except TypeError:
            # Last resort — convert to string so the stream never dies
            logger.warning(
                "SSE encoder: unhandled type %s, converting to str", type(obj).__name__
            )
            return str(obj)


def _dumps(obj: object) -> str:
    """
    Serialises obj to a JSON string using _SafeEncoder.

    Args:
        obj: Any Python object. Typically a dict with "type" and "data" keys.

    Returns:
        A JSON string safe to embed in an SSE data line.
    """
    return json.dumps(obj, cls=_SafeEncoder)


async def event_stream(generator: AsyncGenerator) -> AsyncGenerator[str, None]:
    """
    Converts an async generator of (event_type, data) tuples into a stream
    of SSE-formatted text chunks ready for a StreamingResponse.

    Each chunk looks like:
        data: {"type": "status", "data": {"message": "Surveying..."}}\n\n

    A keep-alive tuple (see _KEEPALIVE) is written as a bare SSE comment
    line (": ...") instead of a data event — comment lines are valid SSE
    syntax, are silently ignored by the browser's EventSource/fetch-stream
    parser, and exist purely to keep bytes flowing so nothing on the network
    path (proxy, VPN gateway, load balancer) treats the connection as idle
    and drops it while the orchestrator is still legitimately working.

    Args:
        generator: An async generator yielding (event_type, data) tuples.
            event_type: Short string — "status", "step", "agent_step",
                        "complete", "error", or the internal keep-alive
                        sentinel.
            data:       A dict. May contain datetime/Decimal values from
                        Postgres rows — _dumps handles those safely.

    Yields:
        SSE-formatted strings, each ending with a double newline as required
        by the SSE spec so the browser flushes the event immediately.
    """
    async for event_type, data in generator:
        if event_type == _KEEPALIVE:
            logger.debug("SSE keep-alive sent")
            yield ": keep-alive\n\n"
            continue
        payload = _dumps({"type": event_type, "data": data})
        logger.debug("SSE event: type=%s payload_len=%d", event_type, len(payload))
        yield f"data: {payload}\n\n"


def make_progress_queue():
    """
    Creates an asyncio Queue and an async callback function together.

    The callback is passed to the orchestrator, which calls it with
    (event_type, data) after each meaningful step. The queue is passed
    to queue_to_stream, which feeds the SSE generator.

    Using a queue decouples the orchestrator (which runs in a background
    asyncio task) from the SSE response (which runs in the request task).

    Returns:
        Tuple of (queue, callback):
            queue:    asyncio.Queue — pass to queue_to_stream().
            callback: async function(event_type, data) — pass to orchestrator.
    """
    queue: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()
    owner_loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    async def callback(event_type: str, data: dict) -> None:
        """
        Puts one event on the queue. Called by the orchestrator.

        Args:
            event_type: "status", "step", "agent_step", "complete", or "error".
            data:       Dict of event-specific fields.
        """
        # Wizard workers have their own event loop so blocking work does not
        # prevent cancellation requests. Queue wakeups must stay on its owner.
        if asyncio.get_running_loop() is owner_loop:
            await queue.put((event_type, data))
        else:
            future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(queue.put((event_type, data)), owner_loop)
            await asyncio.wrap_future(future)

    return queue, callback


async def queue_to_stream(queue: asyncio.Queue) -> AsyncGenerator:
    """
    Pulls events off the queue and yields them one by one.

    Stops automatically when it receives a "complete" or "error" event,
    which signals that the orchestrator has finished (successfully or not).
    Without this stop condition the SSE connection would hang open forever.

    While waiting for the next real event, this now yields a keep-alive
    (see _KEEPALIVE) at most once every SSE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS. Previously
    this was a bare `await queue.get()` with no timeout, so a single slow
    orchestrator step (e.g. one LLM call stuck retrying against a slow
    gateway) produced total silence on the stream for however long that
    step took — invisible on localhost, but long enough on a real
    deployment (behind a proxy/VPN/load balancer with its own idle-timeout)
    to have the connection dropped and reported to the user as a network
    error, even though the backend was still working correctly.

    Args:
        queue: The asyncio.Queue returned by make_progress_queue().

    Yields:
        (event_type, data) tuples — consumed by event_stream(). A keep-alive
        is yielded as (_KEEPALIVE, None) and is never a terminal event.
    """
    while True:
        try:
            event_type, data = await asyncio.wait_for(
                queue.get(), timeout=SSE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS
            )
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            yield _KEEPALIVE, None
            continue
        logger.debug("SSE queue: dequeued event_type=%s", event_type)
        yield event_type, data
        if event_type in ("complete", "error", "cancelled"):
            logger.info("SSE stream closing: received terminal event type=%s", event_type)
            break

"""
api/routes/alm.py

Read-only ALM endpoints for requirements ingestion.
Credentials are supplied per request and are never persisted.
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from core.settings import settings
from service.alm_adapter.auth import login
from service.alm_adapter.requirements import (
    fetch_requirement_by_id,
    fetch_requirements,
    summarize_requirement_fields,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
from api.routes.workflows import WorkflowRoute

router = APIRouter(route_class=WorkflowRoute)


class ALMAuthIn(BaseModel):
    username: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
    password: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
    domain: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
    project: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
    base_url: Optional[str] = None


class ALMRequirementsIn(ALMAuthIn):
    page: int = Field(default=1, ge=1)
    page_size: int = Field(default=50, ge=1, le=200)


class ALMFieldsIn(ALMAuthIn):
    pages: int = Field(default=3, ge=1, le=20)
    page_size: int = Field(default=50, ge=1, le=200)


def _resolve_base_url(body_base_url: Optional[str]) -> str:
    base_url = (body_base_url or settings.alm.base_url or "").strip()
    if not base_url:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail={
                "code": "ALM_BASE_URL_REQUIRED",
                "message": "ALM base URL is required. Provide base_url or configure ALM_BASE_URL.",
            },
        )
    return base_url


def _auth(body: ALMAuthIn):
    try:
        return login(
            base_url=_resolve_base_url(body.base_url),
            username=body.username,
            password=body.password,
            domain=body.domain,
            project=body.project,
        )
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail={"code": "ALM_AUTH_FAILED", "message": str(exc)})
    except PermissionError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail={"code": "ALM_AUTH_FAILED", "message": str(exc)})
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.exception("ALM authentication error for domain=%s project=%s", body.domain, body.project)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail={"code": "ALM_UPSTREAM_ERROR", "message": str(exc)})


@router.post("/alm/requirements")
def list_alm_requirements(body: ALMRequirementsIn):
    ctx = _auth(body)
    try:
        payload = fetch_requirements(ctx, page=body.page, page_size=body.page_size)
        payload["domain"] = body.domain
        payload["project"] = body.project
        return payload
    except PermissionError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail={"code": "ALM_AUTH_EXPIRED", "message": str(exc)})
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.exception(
            "ALM requirements fetch failed domain=%s project=%s page=%d",
            body.domain, body.project, body.page,
        )
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail={"code": "ALM_REQUIREMENTS_FETCH_FAILED", "message": str(exc)})


@router.post("/alm/requirements/{requirement_id}")
def get_alm_requirement(requirement_id: str, body: ALMAuthIn):
    ctx = _auth(body)
    try:
        data = fetch_requirement_by_id(ctx, requirement_id=requirement_id)
        return {"data": data, "domain": body.domain, "project": body.project}
    except LookupError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail={"code": "ALM_REQUIREMENT_NOT_FOUND", "message": str(exc)})
    except PermissionError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail={"code": "ALM_AUTH_EXPIRED", "message": str(exc)})
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.exception(
            "ALM requirement fetch failed id=%s domain=%s project=%s",
            requirement_id, body.domain, body.project,
        )
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail={"code": "ALM_REQUIREMENT_FETCH_FAILED", "message": str(exc)})


@router.post("/alm/requirements/fields")
def list_alm_requirement_fields(body: ALMFieldsIn):
    ctx = _auth(body)
    try:
        payload = summarize_requirement_fields(ctx, pages=body.pages, page_size=body.page_size)
        payload["domain"] = body.domain
        payload["project"] = body.project
        return payload
    except PermissionError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail={"code": "ALM_AUTH_EXPIRED", "message": str(exc)})
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.exception(
            "ALM requirement field summary failed domain=%s project=%s",
            body.domain, body.project,
        )
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail={"code": "ALM_FIELDS_FETCH_FAILED", "message": str(exc)})

FILE: backend/api/routes/app_credentials.py
================================================
"""
api/routes/app_credentials.py

Per-user application login credentials.

Every Kavach user who works on an application stores THEIR OWN login for that
application (so a crawl/generation/execution they trigger signs in as them,
not as a shared account). These endpoints only ever read or write the
CALLER'S credential:

    GET    /v1/app-credentials/{application_id}          — the caller's saved
                                                            username + whether a
                                                            password is stored
                                                            (password masked)
    PUT    /v1/app-credentials/{application_id}          — save/replace the
                                                            caller's credential
    POST   /v1/app-credentials/{application_id}/reveal   — reveal the caller's
                                                            own password
    DELETE /v1/app-credentials/{application_id}          — delete the caller's
                                                            credential

ISOLATION
    The owning user is NEVER taken from the request body — it is resolved
    server-side from the caller's identity (auth/identity.resolve_user_id) and
    every query goes through the single door
    core.db.queries.app_credentials.get_credential(application_id, user_id),
    which always filters by BOTH keys. There is no endpoint that lists all
    users' credentials for an application and none that accepts an arbitrary
    user_id. So one user can never see or change another user's credential
    through this router.
"""

import logging

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel

from auth.identity import resolve_user_id
from core.db.queries import app_credentials as creds_db

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()

# Mirror the mask the test-data route uses, so the UI treats "a stored secret"
# the same way everywhere and never has to special-case this screen.
MASKED_SECRET = "********"


class CredentialBody(BaseModel):
    username: str
    # When the password comes back as the mask (the user edited only the
    # username and never retyped the secret), we keep the stored password
    # instead of overwriting it with "********".
    password: str


def _status_payload(application_id: int, user_id: int) -> dict:
    """The non-secret view of the caller's credential for this application."""
    stored = creds_db.get_credential(application_id, user_id)
    if stored is None:
        return {
            "application_id": application_id,
            "username": "",
            "has_password": False,
            "password": "",
        }
    return {
        "application_id": application_id,
        "username": stored["username"],
        "has_password": bool(stored["password"]),
        # Never leak the real password on a plain GET — only the reveal
        # endpoint returns plaintext, and only for the caller themselves.
        "password": MASKED_SECRET if stored["password"] else "",
    }


@router.get("/app-credentials/{application_id}")
def get_app_credential(application_id: int, request: Request):
    """Return the caller's own saved credential (password masked)."""
    user_id = resolve_user_id(request)
    try:
        return _status_payload(application_id, user_id)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        # Encryption key missing/rotated — surface clearly rather than 500.
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e)) from e


@router.put("/app-credentials/{application_id}")
def save_app_credential(application_id: int, body: CredentialBody, request: Request):
    """Create or replace the caller's credential for this application."""
    user_id = resolve_user_id(request)

    username = (body.username or "").strip()
    if not username:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Username is required.")

    password = body.password or ""
    if not password or password == MASKED_SECRET:
        # The user left the password untouched. Keep whatever is already
        # stored; only update the username.
        existing = creds_db.get_credential(application_id, user_id)
        if existing is None or not existing["password"]:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=400,
                detail="A password is required the first time you save this credential.",
            )
        password = existing["password"]

    try:
        creds_db.upsert_credential(application_id, user_id, username, password)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e)) from e
    return _status_payload(application_id, user_id)


class RevealResponse(BaseModel):
    application_id: int
    username: str
    password: str


@router.post("/app-credentials/{application_id}/reveal")
def reveal_app_credential(application_id: int, request: Request):
    """Return the caller's OWN password in plaintext (deliberate reveal)."""
    user_id = resolve_user_id(request)
    try:
        stored = creds_db.get_credential(application_id, user_id)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e)) from e
    if stored is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail="You have not saved a credential for this application.",
        )
    return {
        "application_id": application_id,
        "username": stored["username"],
        "password": stored["password"],
    }


@router.delete("/app-credentials/{application_id}")
def delete_app_credential(application_id: int, request: Request):
    """Delete the caller's own credential for this application."""
    user_id = resolve_user_id(request)
    removed = creds_db.delete_credential(application_id, user_id)
    return {"application_id": application_id, "deleted": removed}

"""
api/routes/applications.py

GET  /v1/applications                         — list all applications
POST /v1/applications                         — create or find by URL (idempotent)
GET  /v1/applications/{id}                    — get one application
PATCH /v1/applications/{id}/sso-gateway       — toggle SSO flag
POST /v1/applications/{id}/crawl              — start App Map crawl (SSE stream)
GET  /v1/applications/{id}/maps/latest        — latest completed App Map summary
"""

import asyncio
import logging
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Form, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

from api.sse import event_stream, make_progress_queue, queue_to_stream
from api.routes.workflows import WorkflowRoute
from core.db.queries import applications as apps_db
from service.context_resolver import normalize_url

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(route_class=WorkflowRoute)


class CreateApplicationRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str
    base_url: Optional[str] = None
    owner: Optional[str] = None
    requires_sso_gateway: bool = False


class UpdateSsoGatewayRequest(BaseModel):
    requires_sso_gateway: bool


@router.get("/applications")
def list_applications():
    """Returns all active (non-archived) applications."""
    logger.debug("list_applications: request received")
    result = apps_db.list_all(include_archived=False)
    logger.info("list_applications: returning %d application(s)", len(result) if isinstance(result, list) else 1)
    return result


@router.post("/applications")
def create_or_find_application(body: CreateApplicationRequest):
    """
    Creates a new application, or returns an existing one if the URL matches.
    Idempotent by normalized URL.
    """
    logger.info(
        "create_or_find_application: name=%r  base_url=%r  sso=%s",
        body.name, body.base_url, body.requires_sso_gateway,
    )
    normalized = normalize_url(body.base_url) if body.base_url else None

    if normalized:
        existing = apps_db.find_by_normalized_url(normalized, include_archived=True)
        if existing:
            if existing.get("is_archived"):
                logger.info(
                    "create_or_find_application: restoring archived application id=%d",
                    existing["id"],
                )
                restored = apps_db.unarchive(
                    application_id=existing["id"],
                    name=body.name,
                    base_url=body.base_url,
                    owner=body.owner,
                )
                restored = apps_db.set_requires_sso_gateway(
                    restored["id"],
                    body.requires_sso_gateway,
                ) or restored
                return {**restored, "created": False, "restored": True}
            logger.info(
                "create_or_find_application: found existing application id=%d",
                existing["id"],
            )
            updated = apps_db.set_requires_sso_gateway(
                existing["id"],
                body.requires_sso_gateway,
            ) or existing
            return {**updated, "created": False}

    application = apps_db.create(
        name=body.name,
        base_url=body.base_url,
        normalized_url=normalized,
        application_type=None,
        owner=body.owner,
        requires_sso_gateway=body.requires_sso_gateway,
    )
    logger.info(
        "create_or_find_application: created new application id=%d  name=%r",
        application.get("id"), body.name,
    )
    return {**application, "created": True}


@router.get("/applications/{application_id}")
def get_application(application_id: int):
    """Returns one application by ID."""
    logger.debug("get_application: id=%d", application_id)
    application = apps_db.find_by_id(application_id)
    if not application:
        logger.warning("get_application: not found  id=%d", application_id)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail={"code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": f"Application {application_id} not found."})
    logger.debug("get_application: found  id=%d  name=%r", application_id, application.get("name"))
    return application


@router.patch("/applications/{application_id}/sso-gateway")
def set_application_sso_gateway(application_id: int, body: UpdateSsoGatewayRequest):
    """Enable or disable SSO gateway enforcement for an existing application."""
    logger.info(
        "set_application_sso_gateway: id=%d  requires_sso_gateway=%s",
        application_id, body.requires_sso_gateway,
    )
    updated = apps_db.set_requires_sso_gateway(application_id, body.requires_sso_gateway)
    if not updated:
        logger.warning("set_application_sso_gateway: not found  id=%d", application_id)
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail={"code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": f"Application {application_id} not found."},
        )
    logger.debug("set_application_sso_gateway: updated  id=%d", application_id)
    return updated


# ── App Map crawler ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@router.post("/applications/{application_id}/crawl")
async def start_crawl(
    application_id: int,
    request: Request,
    username: Optional[str] = Form(None, description="Username/email for authenticated crawl"),
    password: Optional[str] = Form(None, description="Password for authenticated crawl"),
):
    """
    Start an App Map crawl for this application.

    Streams live progress via SSE while the crawler visits pages and
    records interactive elements. The map is persisted in the
    application_maps table when complete.

    Credentials are optional. If provided, the crawler detects the login
    form at the landing page, fills it, and maps the authenticated session.

    Final SSE event (type='complete'):
        map_id, page_count, element_count, message

    Returns:
        SSE stream (text/event-stream)

    Raises:
        404: If the application is not found or has no base_url.
    """
    app = apps_db.find_by_id(application_id)
    if not app:
        logger.warning("start_crawl: application not found  id=%d", application_id)
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail={"code": "NOT_FOUND",
                    "message": f"Application {application_id} not found."},
        )
    base_url = app.get("base_url")
    if not base_url:
        logger.warning("start_crawl: application %d has no base_url", application_id)
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail={"code": "NO_URL",
                    "message": "Application has no base_url — set one before crawling."},
        )
    logger.info(
        "start_crawl: application_id=%d  base_url=%s  authenticated=%s",
        application_id, base_url, bool(username or password),
    )

    credentials = None
    if username or password:
        credentials = {
            "username": username or "",
            "password": password or "",
        }

    queue, progress_callback = make_progress_queue()
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()

    async def run():
        from service.app_map_crawler import crawl_application

        def sync_progress(event_type: str, data: dict) -> None:
            asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(
                progress_callback(event_type, data), loop
            )

        try:
            await asyncio.to_thread(
                crawl_application,
                application_id,
                base_url,
                credentials,
                None,       # brd_text — not available at crawl-only route; survey runner passes it
                sync_progress,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.exception("Crawl failed for application %d", application_id)
            await progress_callback("error", {"message": str(exc)})

    asyncio.create_task(run())

    return StreamingResponse(
        event_stream(queue_to_stream(queue)),
        media_type="text/event-stream",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
    )


@router.get("/applications/{application_id}/maps/latest")
def get_latest_map(application_id: int):
    """
    Return summary of the most recent completed App Map for this application.

    Used by the UI to show crawl status and by the generation pipeline to
    check whether a fresh crawl is needed.

    Returns:
        {id, crawled_at, page_count, element_count, was_authenticated}
        or 404 if no crawl has been completed for this application.
    """
    from service.app_map_crawler import get_latest_map as _get_latest_map
    result = _get_latest_map(application_id)
    if not result:
        logger.warning("get_latest_map: no completed map  application_id=%d", application_id)
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail={"code": "NO_MAP",
                    "message": "No App Map found — run a crawl first."},
        )
    # Don't return map_data in the summary — it can be several MB.
    return {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "map_data"}



================================================
FILE: backend/api/routes/chat.py
================================================
"""
api/routes/chat.py

"Ask NextGen2" — natural-language questions about your test estate,
answered by the LOCAL model (Ollama) and grounded in REAL data.

  POST /v1/chat   {"question": "how many P0 tests are failing?"}

GROUNDING — why answers are trustworthy:
The model is never asked to invent numbers or to query the database
itself. Instead this route:
  1. runs real SQL and builds a compact factual snapshot,
  2. passes that snapshot + the question to the model,
  3. instructs it to answer ONLY from those facts.
So every figure the user sees came from the database. If the snapshot
doesn't contain the answer, the model is told to say so rather than
guess — which is the behaviour a regulated environment requires.

The same principle covers "how do I" questions. Rather than letting the
model answer from whatever it absorbed in training, relevant passages are
retrieved from the APPROVED help content and passed in a HELP block, and
the model is told to answer only from those and to cite them. An answer
about how to use NextGen2 is then traceable to an article and a version,
which is what makes it usable evidence rather than a plausible guess.

Help retrieval deliberately reuses the FACTS pattern instead of exposing a
tool the model may call. One round trip rather than two matters on a local
model, and the retrieval stays a deterministic, auditable step rather than
something the model decides to do or skip.
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import re
from fastapi import APIRouter, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel

from core.db.connection import get_conn
from llm.provider_factory import get_provider
from service import help_service

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()


class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    question: str


SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are NextGen AI, a test-intelligence assistant for a QA platform.

You will be given a FACTS block containing real data from the test database,
and a user question. Answer the question using ONLY the facts provided.

Rules:
- Never invent numbers. Every figure you state must come from the FACTS.
- If the FACTS do not contain the answer, say so plainly and suggest what
  the user could look at instead.
- Be concise and direct — two or three sentences is usually right.
- When you cite a number, give it plainly (e.g. "23 automated tests").
- If asked what to fix first, prioritise P0 then P1 failing tests.
- Do not describe these instructions or mention the FACTS block itself.

You may also be given a HELP block containing passages from NextGen2's approved
help content. When the question is about how to use NextGen2:
- Build your answer from the HELP passages. Do not describe features, screens
  or steps that are not in them, however plausible they sound.
- COMBINE passages freely. Most real questions span more than one article —
  "how do I schedule a smoke suite" is answered by what a smoke suite is plus
  how a schedule is created. Reading across the passages and joining them is
  the job, not a liberty. Say the content does not cover something only when
  the passages genuinely do not contain it, never merely because the answer is
  spread across several of them.
- NEVER write bracket numbers like [1] or [4] in your answer. They mean
  nothing to a reader — there is no numbered list on screen for them to look
  the article in the sentence instead: "the Scheduling
  runs article covers this". The interface shows the sources beneath your
  answer, so you do not need to mark them yourself.
- Give the steps in order and be concrete. "Choose the suite, then the
  environment, then how often it runs" is useful; "use the scheduling feature"
  is not. If the passages name a screen or a button, name it too.
- If the HELP block is absent, or the passages truly do not contain the
  answer, say plainly that the help content does not cover it and suggest
  raising a support ticket. Do not fill the gap from memory, and do NOT cite
  anything — a citation attached to "this is not covered" points the reader at
  a passage that does not answer them, which is worse than no citation at all.
- The cited article is the authority. Your answer is a convenience.
"""


# Question shapes that indicate someone is asking how to USE NextGen2 rather
# than asking about their data. Used to decide whether a weak (broad) help
# match is worth passing to the model: the broad pass ORs terms together and
# will match something for almost any question, so on its own it is not
# evidence that the question was a how-to at all.
_HOWTO_PATTERNS = re.compile(
    r"\b(how (do|can|would|should) i|how to|how does|what is|what are|"
    r"where (is|do|can) i|why (does|do|is)|can i|steps to|guide|walk me|"
    r"explain|set up|configure|create a|add a)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _looks_like_howto(question: str) -> bool:
    """Whether a question is about using NextGen2 rather than about the data.

    Args:
        question: The user's question.

    Returns:
        True if the phrasing indicates a how-to.
    """
    return bool(_HOWTO_PATTERNS.search(question or ""))


def _help_passages(question: str, asked_by: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Retrieve approved help passages relevant to a question.

    Returns nothing rather than something weak. A passage is included when
    either the precise pass matched — every term present, which is strong
    evidence on its own — or the question is shaped like a how-to and the
    broad pass found something. Passing broad matches indiscriminately would
    attach help text to "how many tests failed", which makes the answer worse
    and wastes context the local model needs elsewhere.

    Args:
        question: The user's question.
        asked_by: Who asked, recorded against any documentation gap.

    Returns:
        Passage dicts, best first, or an empty list.
    """
    looks_like_howto = _looks_like_howto(question)
    try:
        passages = help_service.search(question, asked_by=asked_by, source="chat")
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - help is an enhancement, not the answer
        logger.exception("Help retrieval failed for chat question")
        return []

    if not passages:
        return []
    if passages[0].get("match_type") == "precise" or looks_like_howto:
        return passages
    return []


def _help_block(passages: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Render retrieved passages for the prompt.

    Args:
        passages: Passage dicts from _help_passages.

    Returns:
        A numbered HELP block, or an empty string if there is nothing to show.
        The numbering is what the model cites, and it matches the order of the
        sources returned to the UI so a citation resolves to a real article.
    """
    if not passages:
        return ""
    lines = ["HELP (approved NextGen2 help content — build how-to answers from "
             "these, combining them where the answer spans more than one. Do "
             "not write bracket numbers in your reply):"]
    for p in passages:
        heading = f" — {p['heading']}" if p.get("heading") else ""
        lines.append(f"From “{p['citation']}”{heading}:")
        lines.append(p["body"])
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _snapshot() -> dict:
    """
    Build a compact factual snapshot of the test estate from real SQL.

    Returns:
        dict of real figures the model may quote — counts, coverage per
        application, failing tests, flaky count, recent activity.
    """
    facts: dict = {}
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM applications")
            facts["applications_total"] = cur.fetchone()[0]

            cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM test_case_proposals")
            facts["scenarios_total"] = cur.fetchone()[0]

            cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM generations WHERE script_path IS NOT NULL")
            facts["automated_scripts"] = cur.fetchone()[0]

            cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM executions")
            facts["executions_total"] = cur.fetchone()[0]

            # overall + critical pass rates
            cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE result='pass'), COUNT(*) FROM executions")
            p, t = cur.fetchone()
            facts["overall_pass_rate_pct"] = round(100 * (p or 0) / (t or 1))

            cur.execute("""
                SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE e.result='pass'), COUNT(*)
                FROM executions e
                JOIN generations g ON g.id = e.generation_id
                JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.id = g.test_case_proposal_id
                WHERE p.priority IN ('P0','P1')""")
            cp, ct = cur.fetchone()
            facts["critical_p0_p1_pass_rate_pct"] = round(100 * (cp or 0) / (ct or 1))

            # flaky = has both a pass and a fail in its history
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
                    SELECT generation_id FROM executions GROUP BY generation_id
                    HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE result='pass') > 0
                       AND COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE result='fail') > 0
                ) f""")
            facts["flaky_tests"] = cur.fetchone()[0]

            # per-application coverage
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT a.name,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS scenarios,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT g.test_case_proposal_id) AS automated
                FROM applications a
                LEFT JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.application_id = a.id
                LEFT JOIN generations g ON g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                     AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                GROUP BY a.name ORDER BY a.name""")
            facts["applications"] = [
                {
                    "name": n,
                    "scenarios": s or 0,
                    "automated": au or 0,
                    "coverage_pct": round(100 * (au or 0) / (s or 1)) if s else 0,
                }
                for n, s, au in cur.fetchall()
            ]

            # currently failing tests (latest run per script), P0 first
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT DISTINCT ON (g.id)
                       p.title, p.priority, p.test_type, a.name AS app, e.result
                FROM executions e
                JOIN generations g ON g.id = e.generation_id
                JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.id = g.test_case_proposal_id
                JOIN applications a ON a.id = p.application_id
                ORDER BY g.id, e.executed_at DESC""")
            latest = cur.fetchall()
            failing = [
                {"test": r[0], "priority": r[1], "type": r[2], "application": r[3]}
                for r in latest if r[4] in ("fail", "error")
            ]
            order = {"P0": 0, "P1": 1, "P2": 2, "P3": 3}
            failing.sort(key=lambda x: order.get(x["priority"], 9))
            facts["failing_tests_count"] = len(failing)
            facts["failing_tests"] = failing[:8]

            # test type mix
            cur.execute("SELECT test_type, COUNT(*) FROM test_case_proposals GROUP BY test_type")
            facts["test_types"] = {r[0]: r[1] for r in cur.fetchall()}

            # recent activity
            cur.execute("""
                SELECT p.title, e.result, e.executed_at
                FROM executions e
                JOIN generations g ON g.id = e.generation_id
                JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.id = g.test_case_proposal_id
                ORDER BY e.executed_at DESC LIMIT 3""")
            facts["recent_runs"] = [
                {"test": r[0], "result": r[1], "at": str(r[2])[:16]} for r in cur.fetchall()
            ]

    return facts


@router.post("/chat")
def chat(body: ChatRequest, request: Request):
    """
    Answer a natural-language question about the test estate or about using
    NextGen2.

    Args:
        body: {"question": "..."} from the chat panel.
        request: The incoming request, for the caller's identity. Used when
            recording a question the help content could not answer.

    Returns:
        {"answer": str, "facts_used": dict, "sources": list} — facts_used and
        sources are returned so the UI, or an auditor, can see exactly what
        the answer was based on. Nothing is hidden. sources[n-1] corresponds
        to the [n] citation in the answer.
    """
    question = (body.question or "").strip()
    if not question:
        return {"answer": "Ask me something about your tests — coverage, failures, or health.",
                "facts_used": {}, "sources": [], "help_gap": False}

    who = request.headers.get("X-Triggered-By", "chat")
    passages = _help_passages(question, who)

    # A how-to question that retrieved nothing is a documentation gap, and the
    # UI uses this to offer a ticket at the moment the user is stuck rather
    # than telling them to go and find the Help screen. It is set from
    # retrieval, not from the wording of the answer: parsing "I don't know"
    # out of model prose would be guesswork.
    help_gap = bool(_HOWTO_PATTERNS.search(question)) and not passages

    # A snapshot of the test estate has nothing to do with "how do I schedule
    # a suite". Sending it anyway spent context a local model needs elsewhere,
    # and put a panel of unrelated JSON under the answer that read as though
    # the answer came from it. So the snapshot is skipped — including the SQL
    # behind it — once the question is a how-to that help content can answer.
    answering_from_help = bool(passages) and _looks_like_howto(question)

    facts = {}
    if not answering_from_help:
        try:
            facts = _snapshot()
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Could not build data snapshot for chat")
            return {"answer": f"I couldn't read the test data just now ({e}).",
                    "facts_used": {}, "sources": [], "help_gap": False}

    help_block = _help_block(passages)
    prompt = (
        (f"FACTS (real data from the test database):\n"
         f"{json.dumps(facts, default=str)}\n\n" if facts else "")
        + (f"{help_block}\n" if help_block else "")
        + f"QUESTION: {question}"
    )

    try:
        provider = get_provider()
        # Chat is interactive, so it can use a smaller/faster model than
        # generation. Set LLM_CHAT_MODEL in .env to override; otherwise the
        # normal LLM_MODEL is used.
        chat_model = os.environ.get("LLM_CHAT_MODEL")
        if chat_model and hasattr(provider, "model"):
            provider.model = chat_model
            logger.info("Chat using model: %s", chat_model)

        tool = provider.build_tool([])          # no tools — plain answer
        contents = [provider.user_text_content(prompt)]
        response = provider.call_model(SYSTEM_PROMPT, tool, contents)

        # take the text parts of the reply
        parts = response.candidates[0].content.parts
        answer = " ".join(p.text for p in parts if getattr(p, "text", "")).strip()
        if not answer:
            answer = "I couldn't form an answer from the current data."

        # Surfaced in the UI so cost/latency is visible, not hidden in logs.
        usage = getattr(response, "usage", {}) or {}
        stats = {
            "model": getattr(response, "model", ""),
            "latency_ms": getattr(response, "latency_ms", 0),
            "input_tokens": usage.get("input_tokens"),
            "output_tokens": usage.get("output_tokens"),
        }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Chat model call failed")
        provider_name = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER_TYPE", "unknown")
        return {
            "answer": (
                "The configured model provider is not responding. "
                f"Current provider: {provider_name}. "
                "Check LLM_PROVIDER_TYPE, LLM_API_URL, LLM_MODEL and LLM_API_KEY in backend/.env. "
                f"({e})"
            ),
            "facts_used": facts,
            "sources": _sources(passages),
            "help_gap": help_gap,
        }

    return {"answer": _strip_citation_markers(answer), "facts_used": facts or None,
            "sources": _sources(passages), "help_gap": help_gap,
            "stats": stats}


def _strip_citation_markers(answer: str) -> str:
    """Remove bracket citation markers from an answer.

    The prompt tells the model not to write them; this is the guarantee. A
    small model follows an instruction most of the time, and "most of the
    time" is not good enough for something a reader sees. [4] with nothing
    numbered on screen is noise, and the sources are shown beneath the answer
    anyway.

    Args:
        answer: The model's reply.

    Returns:
        The reply with markers removed and spacing tidied.
    """
    if not answer:
        return answer
    # [1], [2][3], [1, 2] — but not [something] that carries meaning.
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\s*\[\s*\d+(?:\s*[,;]\s*\d+)*\s*\]", "", answer)
    # Tidy the space a removed marker leaves before punctuation.
    cleaned = re.sub(r"\s+([.,;:!?])", r"\1", cleaned)
    return cleaned.strip()


def _sources(passages: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Describe the cited passages for the UI.

    Args:
        passages: Passage dicts passed to the model, in prompt order.

    Returns:
        One entry per passage, numbered to match the [n] citations in the
        answer, carrying enough to link to the article and to show which
        version was cited. Body text is omitted — the UI links to the source
        rather than reproducing it.
    """
    return [
        {
            "n": i,
            "citation": p["citation"],
            "source_type": p["source_type"],
            "label": p["label"],
            "title": p["title"],
            "heading": p.get("heading"),
            "version": p.get("version"),
        }
        for i, p in enumerate(passages, start=1)
    ]


@router.get("/chat/suggestions")
def suggestions():
    """Starter questions shown in the empty chat panel."""
    return {
        "suggestions": [
            {"title": "What should I fix first?", "sub": "Failing tests by priority"},
            {"title": "What's our automation coverage?", "sub": "Across all applications"},
            {"title": "Which tests are flaky?", "sub": "Inconsistent pass/fail"},
            {"title": "How healthy is Netra?", "sub": "Coverage and recent results"},
        ]
    }

FILE: backend/api/routes/chat_actions.py

"""
api/routes/chat_actions.py

Letting the assistant act, with a confirmation in between.

  POST /v1/chat/interpret    instruction -> proposal. Executes nothing.
  POST /v1/chat/resummarise  rebuild the sentence after the user edits a field
  POST /v1/chat/execute      carry out a confirmed proposal

Three endpoints rather than one with flags, so executing by accident is not
possible: interpreting cannot change anything, and executing accepts only a
proposal that was already produced and shown.

The question endpoint in chat.py is untouched, so asking something can never
mutate state.
"""

import logging

from fastapi import APIRouter, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel

from service import actions

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()

# A wide filter, not a decision. It exists only so plainly conversational
# messages do not pay for a model call; anything that might be an
# instruction is passed on and the MODEL decides — it can reply that this is
# a question. A false positive costs one call; a false negative costs the
# feature, so the net is loose on purpose.
ACTION_HINTS = (
    "run", "execute", "schedule", "scheduled", "scheduling", "pause", "paused",
    "resume", "stop", "start", "create", "set up", "setup", "kick off",
    "kickoff", "trigger", "disable", "enable", "fire off", "launch",
    "every day", "every weekday", "every morning", "every week", "daily",
    "nightly", "weekly", "hourly", "each morning", "tonight", "tomorrow",
    # Raising a ticket. Without these, "can you raise a ticket for me" fails
    # this gate and is answered as a question — the request never reaches the
    # interpreter at all. Every word added here must also be recognised by
    # service/actions/runner.py::_prefilter, or a message passes this gate
    # only to be judged conversational one layer down.
    "ticket", "raise", "escalate", "file a", "log a", "report a", "open a",
)

QUESTION_OPENERS = (
    "how ", "what ", "which ", "why ", "when ", "who ", "is ", "are ",
    "do we", "does ", "show me", "tell me", "can i see", "list ",
)


def might_be_instruction(text: str) -> bool:
    """Whether a message is worth showing to the interpreter as an action.

    A filter, not a decision: anything that could plausibly be an instruction
    is passed on, and the interpreter decides. A false positive costs one
    model call; a false negative costs the feature silently, which is far
    worse and much harder to notice — the user simply gets an answer instead
    of the thing they asked for, with nothing logged to say why.

    Args:
        text: What the user typed.

    Returns:
        True if it should be interpreted.
    """
    t = (text or "").strip().lower()
    if not t:
        return False
    if t.startswith(QUESTION_OPENERS):
        return False
    return any(w in t for w in ACTION_HINTS)


class InterpretRequest(BaseModel):
    instruction: str


class ResummariseRequest(BaseModel):
    proposal: dict


class ExecuteRequest(BaseModel):
    proposal: dict


@router.get("/chat/actions")
def list_actions():
    """
    Everything the assistant is allowed to do.

    Exposed deliberately: in a validated environment "what can an LLM
    trigger?" needs an answer you can read, and this is it.
    """
    return {
        "actions": [
            {"name": n, "description": a.description,
             "parameters": a.parameters, "editable": list(a.confirm_fields)}
            for n, a in actions.ACTIONS.items()
        ]
    }


@router.post("/chat/interpret")
def interpret(body: InterpretRequest):
    """Turn an instruction into a proposal. Nothing is executed."""
    text = (body.instruction or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return {"error": "Nothing to interpret."}
    if not might_be_instruction(text):
        return {"not_an_action": True}

    try:
        from llm.provider_factory import get_provider
        provider = get_provider()
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("No model available to interpret instructions: %s", e)
        return {"error": "The model is not available."}

    try:
        return actions.interpret(text, provider)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Interpretation failed")
        return {"error": str(e)}


@router.post("/chat/resummarise")
def resummarise(body: ResummariseRequest):
    """Rebuild the confirmation sentence after an edit, so it stays truthful."""
    return {"summary": actions.resummarise(body.proposal or {})}


@router.post("/chat/execute")
def execute(body: ExecuteRequest, request: Request):
    """Carry out a proposal the user has confirmed."""
    who = request.headers.get("X-Triggered-By", "chat")
    if not body.proposal or not body.proposal.get("action"):
        return {"error": "No action to carry out."}
    try:
        return actions.execute(body.proposal, triggered_by=who)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Action failed")
        return {"error": str(e)}

FILE: backend/api/routes/dashboard.py
