"""
api/routes/imports.py

Import manual test cases from a spreadsheet.

  POST /v1/applications/{id}/import-preview   upload, detect, parse — saves nothing
  (accepting is the existing /v1/test-suites/accept-proposals)

Preview and accept are separate on purpose. The importer guesses what the
columns mean, and a wrong guess would otherwise put hundreds of malformed
rows into the repository before anyone noticed. So it shows what it worked
out, you confirm, and only then does the same approval gate that AI proposals
go through actually write anything.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import os
import tempfile
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, File, Form, UploadFile

from service import test_case_import as importer
from api.routes.workflows import WorkflowRoute
from service.workflow_control import checkpoint, current_operation

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(route_class=WorkflowRoute)

ALLOWED = (".xlsx", ".xlsm", ".csv")



def _existing_titles(application_id: int) -> dict:
    """
    Titles already in this application, so import can flag duplicates.

    Also reports whether each has a script — a duplicate with a broken
    script is exactly the one worth replacing, and the reviewer should be
    able to see that.
    """
    from core.db.connection import get_conn

    out = {}
    try:
        with get_conn() as conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    """SELECT p.id, p.title,
                              EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                                       WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                         AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                         AND g.is_stale = FALSE) AS has_script
                       FROM test_case_proposals p
                       WHERE p.application_id = %s AND p.status != 'archived'""",
                    (application_id,),
                )
                for pid, title, has_script in cur.fetchall():
                    out[(title or "").strip().lower()] = {
                        "id": pid, "title": title, "has_script": has_script,
                    }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("Could not load existing titles for duplicate check: %s", e)
    return out


@router.post("/applications/{application_id}/import-preview")
async def import_preview(
    application_id: int,
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    sheet: Optional[str] = Form(None),
    title_column: Optional[str] = Form(None),
    step_column: Optional[str] = Form(None),
    expected_column: Optional[str] = Form(None),
    row_mode: Optional[str] = Form(None),
):
    """
    Read a spreadsheet and return what it contains — without saving anything.

    Called twice in practice: once to see the detected mapping, and again
    with corrected columns if the detection was wrong. Nothing is written
    either time.

    Args:
        application_id: Which application these test cases belong to.
        file: .xlsx, .xlsm or .csv.
        sheet: Optional sheet name.
        title_column / step_column / expected_column / row_mode: supplied on
            the second call to override what was detected.

    Returns:
        headers, the mapping used, the parsed test cases, and a sample of
        rows so the UI can show what it read.
    """
    name = (file.filename or "").lower()
    if not name.endswith(ALLOWED):
        return {"error": f"Unsupported file type. Use {', '.join(ALLOWED)}."}

    suffix = os.path.splitext(name)[1]
    tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=suffix)
    try:
        tmp.write(await file.read())
        tmp.close()

        if current_operation():
            headers, rows = await asyncio.to_thread(importer.read_sheet, tmp.name, sheet)
        else:
            headers, rows = importer.read_sheet(tmp.name, sheet)
        checkpoint()
        if not headers:
            return {"error": "That file appears to be empty."}

        if title_column:
            # The reviewer corrected the mapping — use theirs, do not detect again.
            mapping = {
                "title_column": title_column,
                "step_column": step_column,
                "expected_column": expected_column,
                "priority_column": None, "requirement_column": None, "module_column": None,
                "row_mode": row_mode or "one_row_per_case",
                "blank_title_continues": (row_mode == "one_row_per_step"),
                "confidence": "high",
                "reasoning": "Set by hand.",
                "source": "set by hand",
            }
        else:
            provider = None
            try:
                from llm.provider_factory import get_provider
                provider = get_provider()
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning("No model available for column detection: %s", e)
            if current_operation():
                mapping = await asyncio.to_thread(importer.detect_mapping, headers, rows, provider)
            else:
                mapping = importer.detect_mapping(headers, rows, provider)

        checkpoint()
        cases = importer.parse_test_cases(headers, rows, mapping)

        # Flag anything that already exists so the reviewer can decide
        # whether to skip it or replace it — the same choice the survey
        # offers. Deciding silently either way would be wrong: a duplicate
        # might be the one with a broken script.
        existing = _existing_titles(application_id)
        for p_ in cases:
            prior = existing.get(p_["title"].strip().lower())
            p_["duplicate_of"] = prior["id"] if prior else None
            p_["duplicate_title"] = prior["title"] if prior else None
            p_["duplicate_has_script"] = bool(prior and prior["has_script"])
        logger.info("Import preview: %d row(s) -> %d test case(s) from %s",
                    len(rows), len(cases), file.filename)

        return {
            "filename": file.filename,
            "headers": headers,
            "row_count": len(rows),
            "mapping": mapping,
            "proposals": cases,
            "sample_rows": rows[:8],
        }
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Import preview failed")
        return {"error": f"Could not read that file: {e}"}
    finally:
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp.name)
        except OSError:
            pass

FILE: backend/api/routes/proposals.py

"""
api/routes/proposals.py

GET   /v1/applications/{id}/proposals  — list proposals for an application
PATCH /v1/proposals/{id}/priority      — set priority after review
PATCH /v1/proposals/{id}/status        — update status
PATCH /v1/proposals/{id}/steps         — edit the steps of an accepted test case
POST  /v1/proposals/{id}/archive       — archive a proposal
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

from core.db.queries import proposals as proposals_db

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()


class PriorityRequest(BaseModel):
    priority: str  # P0, P1, P2, P3, P4


class StatusRequest(BaseModel):
    status: str


class StepInput(BaseModel):
    step: str
    expected: Optional[str] = None
    matched: bool = True
    element_hint: Optional[str] = None
    # Preserved so re-saving steps from the review UI (even when only
    # unrelated steps changed) doesn't silently strip data the survey or
    # the deterministic trace compiler already produced. See the matching
    # fields on api.routes.run.AcceptedStep.
    data_input: Optional[str] = None
    wait_condition: Optional[str] = None
    action: Optional[str] = None


class StepsRequest(BaseModel):
    steps: list[StepInput]
    edited_by: Optional[str] = None


@router.get("/applications/{application_id}/proposals")
def list_proposals(application_id: int, status: Optional[str] = None):
    """
    Returns all proposals for an application, optionally filtered by status.

    Each proposal is enriched with script_count and run_count so the UI can
    show at a glance which test cases actually have automation behind them.
    Without this, a scenario with a working script looked identical to an
    empty one until you expanded it.
    """
    logger.info("Listing proposals app_id=%s status=%s", application_id, status)
    proposals = proposals_db.list_for_application(application_id, status_filter=status)
    if not proposals:
        logger.info("No proposals found for app_id=%s status=%s", application_id, status)
        return proposals

    from core.db.connection import get_conn
    counts = {}
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT p.id,
                       -- Retired versions are kept as a record but must not be
                       -- counted as scripts you have: the list hides them, so a
                       -- count that includes them reads as a contradiction
                       -- ("3 scripts" above a single row).
                       COUNT(DISTINCT g.id) FILTER (
                           WHERE g.script_path IS NOT NULL AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                       ) AS scripts,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT g.id) FILTER (
                           WHERE g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                             AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                             AND g.generation_status = 'success'
                       ) AS success_scripts,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT g.id) FILTER (
                           WHERE g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                             AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                             AND g.generation_status = 'incomplete'
                       ) AS incomplete_scripts,
                       -- Runs DO include those from retired scripts. They
                       -- happened, and that history is the audit evidence.
                       COUNT(e.id) AS runs,
                       -- The result of this test case's MOST RECENT run, so the
                       -- UI can show a "failing" count and a per-row status dot.
                       -- 'pass' | 'fail' | 'skip' | 'error', or NULL if never run.
                       (SELECT e2.result
                          FROM executions e2
                          JOIN generations g2 ON g2.id = e2.generation_id
                         WHERE g2.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                         ORDER BY e2.executed_at DESC
                                                 LIMIT 1) AS last_result,
                                             (SELECT g3.generation_status
                                                    FROM generations g3
                                                 WHERE g3.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                                     AND g3.is_stale = FALSE
                                                 ORDER BY g3.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, g3.id DESC
                                                 LIMIT 1) AS latest_generation_status,
                                             (SELECT g4.notes
                                                    FROM generations g4
                                                 WHERE g4.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                                     AND g4.is_stale = FALSE
                                                 ORDER BY g4.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, g4.id DESC
                                                 LIMIT 1) AS latest_generation_notes
                FROM test_case_proposals p
                LEFT JOIN generations g ON g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                LEFT JOIN executions  e ON e.generation_id = g.id
                WHERE p.application_id = %s
                GROUP BY p.id
                """,
                (application_id,),
            )
            counts = {
                r[0]: {
                    "script_count": r[1],
                    "success_script_count": r[2],
                    "incomplete_script_count": r[3],
                    "run_count": r[4],
                    "last_result": r[5],
                    "latest_generation_status": r[6],
                    "latest_generation_notes": r[7],
                }
                for r in cur.fetchall()
            }

    for p in proposals:
        info = counts.get(p["id"], {})
        p["script_count"] = info.get("script_count", 0)
        p["success_script_count"] = info.get("success_script_count", 0)
        p["incomplete_script_count"] = info.get("incomplete_script_count", 0)
        p["run_count"] = info.get("run_count", 0)
        p["last_result"] = info.get("last_result")  # 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'|'error'|None
        p["latest_generation_status"] = info.get("latest_generation_status")
        p["latest_generation_notes"] = info.get("latest_generation_notes")
    logger.info("Listed %s proposals for app_id=%s", len(proposals), application_id)
    return proposals


@router.patch("/proposals/{proposal_id}/priority")
def set_priority(proposal_id: int, body: PriorityRequest):
    """Sets the priority level (P0–P4) after human review."""
    valid = {"P0", "P1", "P2", "P3", "P4"}
    if body.priority not in valid:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail={"code": "INVALID_PRIORITY", "message": f"Priority must be one of {valid}."})
    proposals_db.update_priority(proposal_id, body.priority)
    return {"ok": True}


@router.patch("/proposals/{proposal_id}/status")
def update_status(proposal_id: int, body: StatusRequest):
    """Updates a proposal's status."""
    proposals_db.update_status(proposal_id, body.status)
    return {"ok": True}


@router.patch("/proposals/{proposal_id}/steps")
def update_steps(proposal_id: int, body: StepsRequest):
    """
    Replace the steps of an accepted test case.

    An accepted test case is the audit artefact — it is what a person
    approved. Editing its steps afterwards is a recorded event, not a silent
    update: the previous steps are written to proposal_edits along with who
    made the change.

    The description is re-derived from the steps in the same transaction.
    Callers cannot set it independently; it is a projection of the steps, and
    letting the two drift would mean generation reads something the reviewer
    never approved.

    Args:
        proposal_id: The test case to edit.
        body: The new steps, in order, and who is making the change.

    Returns:
        {"ok": True, "proposal": {...}, "step_count": int}

    Raises:
        400: If every step is blank — a test case with no steps should be
            edited to have steps, or archived, not silently emptied.
        404: If the proposal does not exist.
    """
    from service.test_case_import import flatten_steps

    steps = [s.model_dump() for s in body.steps]
    steps = [s for s in steps if (s.get("step") or "").strip()]
    if not steps:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail={
                "code": "NO_STEPS",
                "message": "At least one step with an action is required.",
            },
        )

    # Numbered here, from array order — never taken from the client, so
    # reordering in the UI cannot produce gaps or duplicate numbers.
    for i, s in enumerate(steps, 1):
        s["n"] = i

    updated = proposals_db.update_steps(
        proposal_id=proposal_id,
        steps=steps,
        description=flatten_steps(steps),
        edited_by=body.edited_by,
    )
    if updated is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail={"code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": f"Test case {proposal_id} not found."},
        )

    return {"ok": True, "proposal": updated, "step_count": len(steps)}


@router.post("/proposals/{proposal_id}/archive")
def archive_proposal(proposal_id: int):
    """Archives a proposal — reversible, stops it counting in coverage."""
    proposals_db.update_status(proposal_id, "archived")
    return {"ok": True}

# ── Report artefacts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Appended, not rewritten: the two endpoints above are in use by the
# dashboard and there is no reason to touch them.
#
# The distinction these draw is between a dashboard and a report. A
# dashboard answers "what is the state right now" and is consumed on screen.
# A report is parameterised — you choose the scope and the period — and is
# produced to be sent to someone. Every test management tool draws that
# line, and it is why this is not a second dashboard.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta          # noqa: E402
from typing import Optional                       # noqa: E402
from core.db.connection import get_conn           # noqa: E402


def _report_rows(cur):
    cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]


@router.get("/reports/traceability")
def traceability(application_id: Optional[int] = None):
    """
    Requirement to test to result to evidence.

    The artefact a regulated environment asks for. Requirements come from the
    tags recorded when a scenario was ACCEPTED, so this reflects what a person
    approved rather than what a document claimed.

    Test cases with no requirement are listed separately rather than dropped.
    An untraced test is a finding, and hiding it would defeat the purpose.
    """
    where, params = ["p.status != 'archived'"], []
    if application_id:
        where.append("p.application_id = %s")
        params.append(application_id)
    clause = "WHERE " + " AND ".join(where)

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                f"""
                SELECT p.id, p.title, p.priority,
                       p.tags->>'requirement_id' AS requirement_id,
                       p.tags->>'scenario'       AS scenario,
                       p.tags->>'accepted_by'    AS accepted_by,
                       p.tags->>'accepted_at'    AS accepted_at,
                       a.name AS application_name, a.id AS application_id,
                       (SELECT e.result FROM executions e
                         JOIN generations g ON g.id = e.generation_id
                         WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                         ORDER BY e.executed_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_result,
                       (SELECT e.executed_at FROM executions e
                         JOIN generations g2 ON g2.id = e.generation_id
                         WHERE g2.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                         ORDER BY e.executed_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_run_at,
                       (SELECT e.environment FROM executions e
                         JOIN generations g3 ON g3.id = e.generation_id
                         WHERE g3.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                         ORDER BY e.executed_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS environment,
                       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM executions e
                         JOIN generations g4 ON g4.id = e.generation_id
                         WHERE g4.test_case_proposal_id = p.id) AS run_count,
                       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g5
                                WHERE g5.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                  AND g5.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                  AND g5.is_stale = FALSE) AS automated
                FROM test_case_proposals p
                JOIN applications a ON a.id = p.application_id
                {clause}
                ORDER BY p.tags->>'requirement_id' NULLS LAST, p.title
                """,
                tuple(params),
            )
            rows = _report_rows(cur)

    traced = [r for r in rows if r["requirement_id"]]
    untraced = [r for r in rows if not r["requirement_id"]]

    grouped: dict = {}
    for r in traced:
        grouped.setdefault(r["requirement_id"], []).append(r)

    requirements = [
        {"requirement_id": req, "tests": tests,
         "verified": any(t["last_result"] == "pass" for t in tests)}
        for req, tests in sorted(grouped.items())
    ]

    return {
        "requirements": requirements,
        "untraced_tests": untraced,
        "counts": {
            "requirements": len(grouped),
            "verified": sum(1 for r in requirements if r["verified"]),
            "unverified": sum(1 for r in requirements if not r["verified"]),
            "tests_traced": len(traced),
            "tests_untraced": len(untraced),
        },
        "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
    }


@router.get("/reports/executions")
def execution_report(application_id: Optional[int] = None, days: int = 30,
                     environment: Optional[str] = None):
    """
    Everything that ran in a period, with where and what started it.

    The report a team sends after a release.
    """
    since = datetime.now() - timedelta(days=days)
    where, params = ["e.executed_at >= %s"], [since]
    if application_id:
        where.append("p.application_id = %s"); params.append(application_id)
    if environment:
        where.append("e.environment = %s"); params.append(environment)
    clause = "WHERE " + " AND ".join(where)

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                f"""SELECT e.id, e.result, e.executed_at, e.duration_ms,
                           e.triggered_by, e.environment,
                           p.title AS test_title, p.priority,
                           p.tags->>'requirement_id' AS requirement_id,
                           p.tags->>'scenario' AS scenario,
                           a.name AS application_name
                    FROM executions e
                    JOIN generations g ON g.id = e.generation_id
                    JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.id = g.test_case_proposal_id
                    JOIN applications a ON a.id = p.application_id
                    {clause}
                    ORDER BY e.executed_at DESC""",
                tuple(params),
            )
            runs = _report_rows(cur)

    passed = sum(1 for r in runs if r["result"] == "pass")
    scheduled = sum(1 for r in runs if r["triggered_by"] == "scheduler")
    return {
        "runs": runs,
        "period": {"days": days, "from": since.isoformat(),
                   "to": datetime.now().isoformat()},
        "counts": {"total": len(runs), "passed": passed,
                   "failed": len(runs) - passed,
                   "pass_rate_pct": round(100 * passed / len(runs)) if runs else None,
                   "scheduled": scheduled, "manual": len(runs) - scheduled},
        "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
    }


@router.get("/reports/coverage")
def coverage_report():
    """
    Coverage per application, with the automation gap stated beside it.

    A coverage percentage alone invites the wrong conclusion. How many
    critical tests have no script is the number worth acting on, so it is
    reported rather than left to be inferred.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT a.id, a.name, a.base_url,
                       COUNT(p.id) AS test_cases,
                       COUNT(p.id) FILTER (
                           WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                                          WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                            AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                            AND g.is_stale = FALSE)) AS automated,
                       COUNT(p.id) FILTER (
                           WHERE p.priority IN ('P0','P1')
                             AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                                              WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                                AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                                AND g.is_stale = FALSE)) AS critical_gap,
                       COUNT(p.id) FILTER (WHERE p.source = 'bulk_import') AS imported,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT p.tags->>'requirement_id')
                           FILTER (WHERE p.tags->>'requirement_id' IS NOT NULL) AS requirements
                FROM applications a
                LEFT JOIN test_case_proposals p
                       ON p.application_id = a.id AND p.status != 'archived'
                WHERE a.is_archived = FALSE
                GROUP BY a.id, a.name, a.base_url
                ORDER BY a.name
                """
            )
            apps = _report_rows(cur)

    for a in apps:
        a["coverage_pct"] = (round(100 * a["automated"] / a["test_cases"])
                             if a["test_cases"] else 0)
    return {
        "applications": apps,
        "totals": {"test_cases": sum(a["test_cases"] for a in apps),
                   "automated": sum(a["automated"] for a in apps),
                   "critical_gap": sum(a["critical_gap"] for a in apps),
                   "imported": sum(a["imported"] for a in apps)},
        "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
    }


# ── AI token usage and cost ──────────────────────────────────────────────

from decimal import Decimal                                  # noqa: E402
from fastapi import Query                                    # noqa: E402

from core.db.queries import reports as reports_db            # noqa: E402

    days: int = Query(30, ge=1, le=365, description="Look-back window in days"),
    application_id: Optional[int] = Query(None, ge=1, description="Limit to one application"),
):
    """Token usage (input/output) and cost for each AI activity."""
    return reports_db.get_ai_usage_summary(days=days, application_id=application_id)


@router.get("/reports/ai-cost/items")
def ai_cost_items(application_id: int = Query(..., ge=1, description="Application to price")):
    """
    test_cases: estimated share of the survey run that produced each test case (keyed by proposal id).
    scripts: exact cost of generating each test case's script, including repairs and regenerations.
    Items generated before cost tracking are left out so the UI can show "-" instead of a false $0.
    """
    test_cases = {
        pid: {"cost_usd": cost, "estimated": True}
        for pid, cost in ai_calls_db.get_test_case_costs(application_id).items()
    }

    # Adds up every generation of the same test case, so regenerating a script shows the running total.
    scripts = {}
    for r in ai_calls_db.get_script_costs(application_id):
        entry = scripts.setdefault(str(r["proposal_id"]), {"cost_usd": Decimal("0"), "generations": []})
        entry["cost_usd"] += Decimal(r["cost_usd"])
        entry["generations"].append({"generation_id": r["generation_id"], "cost_usd": r["cost_usd"]})
    for entry in scripts.values():
        entry["cost_usd"] = str(entry["cost_usd"])   # string keeps the exact value

    return {"application_id": application_id, "test_cases": test_cases, "scripts": scripts}

"""
api/routes/repository.py

The test repository, across every application.

  GET /v1/repository/test-cases    filtered list plus the counts behind it
  GET /v1/repository/summary       just the counts

The application page answers "tell me about Netra". This answers "tell me
about our testing" — how much of the estate is automated, which P1s have no
script, what came from an import versus what the AI proposed. Those are
questions you cannot answer by clicking through four applications one at a
time.

Read-only. Acting on a selection reuses the endpoints that already exist —
adding to a suite, generating scripts — so there is no second way to do
anything.
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter

from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()


def _rows(cur):
    cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]


@router.get("/repository/test-cases")
def list_test_cases(
    application_id: Optional[int] = None,
    priority: Optional[str] = None,
    automated: Optional[str] = None,      # "yes" | "no"
    source: Optional[str] = None,         # author_agent | bulk_import | brd | crawl | jira | alm
    scenario: Optional[str] = None,
    search: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: int = 500,
):
    """
    Every test case that matches, with enough context to be acted on.

    Args:
        application_id: Restrict to one application.
        priority: P0-P3.
        automated: "yes" for those with a current script, "no" for those without.
        source: Where the test case came from.
        scenario: The feature grouping it belongs to.
        search: Matches the title.
        limit: Safety cap; the UI shows the count so a truncated list is visible.

    Returns:
        {"test_cases": [...], "total": int, "counts": {...}}
    """
    where, params = [], []
    if application_id:
        where.append("p.application_id = %s"); params.append(application_id)
    if priority:
        where.append("p.priority = %s"); params.append(priority)
    if source:
        # Backward compatible filter:
        # - ingestion source: author_agent | bulk_import (column p.source)
        # - provenance source: brd | crawl | jira | alm (column p.origin)
        if source in {"brd", "crawl", "jira", "alm"}:
            where.append("p.origin = %s"); params.append(source)
        else:
            where.append("p.source = %s"); params.append(source)
    if scenario:
        where.append("p.tags->>'scenario' = %s"); params.append(scenario)
    if search:
        where.append("p.title ILIKE %s"); params.append(f"%{search}%")
    if automated == "yes":
        where.append("EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id "
                     "AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL AND g.is_stale = FALSE)")
    elif automated == "no":
        where.append("NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id "
                     "AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL AND g.is_stale = FALSE)")

    where.append("p.status != 'archived'")
    clause = "WHERE " + " AND ".join(where)

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                f"""SELECT p.id, p.title, p.priority, p.category, p.source, p.origin,
                           p.tags->>'scenario'       AS scenario,
                           p.tags->>'requirement_id' AS requirement_id,
                           a.id   AS application_id,
                           a.name AS application_name,
                           EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                                    WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                      AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                      AND g.is_stale = FALSE) AS automated,
                           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM executions e
                             JOIN generations g2 ON g2.id = e.generation_id
                             WHERE g2.test_case_proposal_id = p.id) AS run_count,
                           (SELECT e.result FROM executions e
                             JOIN generations g3 ON g3.id = e.generation_id
                             WHERE g3.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                             ORDER BY e.executed_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_result
                    FROM test_case_proposals p
                    JOIN applications a ON a.id = p.application_id
                    {clause}
                    ORDER BY a.name, p.priority NULLS LAST, p.title
                    LIMIT %s""",
                tuple(params) + (limit,),
            )
            cases = _rows(cur)

            cur.execute(
                f"""SELECT COUNT(*) FROM test_case_proposals p
                    JOIN applications a ON a.id = p.application_id
                    {clause}""",
                tuple(params),
            )
            total = cur.fetchone()[0]

    return {"test_cases": cases, "total": total, "shown": len(cases)}


@router.get("/repository/summary")
def summary():
    """
    The estate in numbers.

    Deliberately the same shape the dashboard would want: coverage is only
    meaningful next to what is missing, so the automation gap is reported
    rather than left to be worked out from two other figures.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """SELECT COUNT(*) AS total,
                          COUNT(*) FILTER (
                              WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                                             WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                               AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                               AND g.is_stale = FALSE)) AS automated,
                          COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.source = 'bulk_import') AS imported,
                          COUNT(*) FILTER (
                              WHERE p.priority IN ('P0','P1')
                                AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                                                 WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                                   AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                                   AND g.is_stale = FALSE)) AS critical_gap
                   FROM test_case_proposals p
                   WHERE p.status != 'archived'"""
            )
            total, automated, imported, gap = cur.fetchone()

            cur.execute(
                """SELECT a.id, a.name, COUNT(p.id) AS test_cases,
                          COUNT(p.id) FILTER (
                              WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                                             WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                                               AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                               AND g.is_stale = FALSE)) AS automated
                   FROM applications a
                   LEFT JOIN test_case_proposals p
                          ON p.application_id = a.id AND p.status != 'archived'
                   WHERE a.is_archived = FALSE
                   GROUP BY a.id, a.name
                   ORDER BY a.name"""
            )
            per_app = _rows(cur)

            cur.execute(
                """SELECT DISTINCT p.tags->>'scenario' AS scenario
                   FROM test_case_proposals p
                   WHERE p.status != 'archived' AND p.tags->>'scenario' IS NOT NULL
                   ORDER BY 1"""
            )
            scenarios = [r[0] for r in cur.fetchall()]

    return {
        "total": total,
        "automated": automated,
        "imported": imported,
        "critical_gap": gap,          # P0/P1 with no script — the number that matters
        "coverage_pct": round(100 * automated / total) if total else 0,
        "applications": per_app,
        "scenarios": scenarios,
    }

"""
api/routes/schedules.py

Scheduled runs — test suites and Jira change-detection.

  GET    /v1/schedules
  POST   /v1/schedules
  PATCH  /v1/schedules/{id}
  DELETE /v1/schedules/{id}
  POST   /v1/schedules/{id}/run          run it now
  GET    /v1/schedules/{id}/runs         its run history

A schedule's job_type decides what running it does. 'suite_run' executes a
test suite (the original behaviour); 'jira_sync' runs one Jira change-detection
pass. Both ride the same runner and the same "Run now" path — the route layer
only differs in what a create request must supply.
"""

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel

from core.db.connection import get_conn
from service import scheduler as scheduler_service

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()


class ScheduleIn(BaseModel):
    application_id: int
    name: str
    job_type: str = "suite_run"                 # 'suite_run' | 'jira_sync'
    suite_id: Optional[int] = None              # required for suite_run
    jira_project_key: Optional[str] = None      # required for jira_sync
    frequency: str = "daily"
    run_at: str                                 # ISO datetime of the first occurrence
    environment: Optional[str] = None
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None
    recipients: Optional[str] = None
    enabled: bool = True


class SchedulePatch(BaseModel):
    name: Optional[str] = None
    frequency: Optional[str] = None
    run_at: Optional[str] = None
    environment: Optional[str] = None
    webhook_url: Optional[str] = None
    recipients: Optional[str] = None
    enabled: Optional[bool] = None


def _rows(cur):
    cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]


@router.get("/schedules/summary")
def schedules_summary():
    """
    What is due next, and how the last automated run went.

    For the dashboard. The question a team asks first each morning is "did
    last night's run pass, and when do I next get fresh data" — and if
    nothing is scheduled at all, that absence is itself worth showing.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """SELECT s.id, s.name, s.frequency, s.next_run_at, s.environment,
                          ts.name AS suite_name, a.name AS application_name
                   FROM schedules s
                   LEFT JOIN test_suites ts ON ts.id = s.suite_id
                   JOIN applications a ON a.id = s.application_id
                   WHERE s.enabled = TRUE AND s.next_run_at IS NOT NULL
                   ORDER BY s.next_run_at LIMIT 3""",
            )
            upcoming = _rows(cur)

            cur.execute(
                """SELECT r.id, r.started_at, r.total, r.passed, r.failed, r.skipped,
                          r.triggered_by, s.name AS schedule_name,
                          ts.name AS suite_name, a.name AS application_name
                   FROM schedule_runs r
                   JOIN schedules s ON s.id = r.schedule_id
                   LEFT JOIN test_suites ts ON ts.id = s.suite_id
                   JOIN applications a ON a.id = s.application_id
                   WHERE r.finished_at IS NOT NULL
                   ORDER BY r.started_at DESC LIMIT 3""",
            )
            recent = _rows(cur)

            cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schedules")
            total = cur.fetchone()[0]
            cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schedules WHERE enabled = TRUE")
            active = cur.fetchone()[0]

    return {
        "upcoming": upcoming,
        "recent": recent,
        "total": total,
        "active": active,
        "server_time": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    }


@router.get("/schedules")
def list_schedules(application_id: Optional[int] = None):
    """
    All schedules, newest first, with enough context to render the list
    without a second call per row.

    s.* carries job_type and jira_project_key, so the UI can tell a suite
    schedule from a Jira one and show the right detail. member_count is a
    suite notion; for a Jira schedule (no suite) it comes back 0 and the UI
    simply does not show it.
    """
    where, params = "", []
    if application_id:
        where = "WHERE s.application_id = %s"
        params.append(application_id)

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                f"""SELECT s.*, a.name AS application_name, ts.name AS suite_name,
                           ts.kind AS suite_kind,
                           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM test_suite_members m
                             WHERE m.suite_id = s.suite_id) AS member_count
                    FROM schedules s
                    JOIN applications a ON a.id = s.application_id
                    LEFT JOIN test_suites ts ON ts.id = s.suite_id
                    {where}
                    ORDER BY s.enabled DESC, s.next_run_at NULLS LAST, s.created_at DESC""",
                tuple(params),
            )
            schedules = _rows(cur)

            for s in schedules:
                cur.execute(
                    """SELECT passed, failed, skipped, started_at
                       FROM schedule_runs WHERE schedule_id = %s
                       ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 7""",
                    (s["id"],),
                )
                s["recent_runs"] = _rows(cur)
    return {"schedules": schedules, "server_time": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}


@router.post("/schedules")
def create_schedule(body: ScheduleIn, request: Request):
    """
    Create a schedule.

    run_at is the first occurrence, and is also stored as next_run_at so the
    UI can count down to it and the scheduler can find it with one query.

    What a create must supply depends on job_type:
      suite_run  → a suite_id (which suite to run).
      jira_sync  → a jira_project_key (which project to check). No suite.
    Everything else (cadence, run_at, webhook, recipients) is shared.
    """
    who = request.headers.get("X-Triggered-By", "anonymous")

    job_type = (body.job_type or "suite_run").strip()
    if job_type not in ("suite_run", "jira_sync"):
        return {"error": f"Unknown job_type '{job_type}'."}

    # Type-specific requirements — mirror the runner's own validate() so a bad
    # schedule is rejected at creation, not discovered at run time.
    if job_type == "suite_run" and not body.suite_id:
        return {"error": "A suite is required for a suite-run schedule."}
    project_key = (body.jira_project_key or "").strip() or None
    if job_type == "jira_sync" and not project_key:
        return {"error": "A Jira project is required for a Jira-sync schedule."}

    # A Jira schedule has no suite; store NULL rather than whatever was sent.
    suite_id = body.suite_id if job_type == "suite_run" else None

    try:
        run_at = datetime.fromisoformat(body.run_at.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return {"error": "run_at must be an ISO datetime."}

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """INSERT INTO schedules
                   (application_id, suite_id, name, frequency, run_at, next_run_at,
                    environment, webhook_url, recipients, enabled, created_by,
                    job_type, jira_project_key)
                   VALUES (%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s) RETURNING *""",
                (body.application_id, suite_id, body.name.strip(), body.frequency,
                 run_at, run_at, body.environment, body.webhook_url, body.recipients,
                 body.enabled, who, job_type, project_key),
            )
            sched = _rows(cur)[0]
        conn.commit()
    logger.info("Created %s schedule '%s' (%s) first run %s",
                job_type, body.name, body.frequency, run_at)
    return {"schedule": sched}


@router.patch("/schedules/{schedule_id}")
def update_schedule(schedule_id: int, body: SchedulePatch):
    """Update a schedule. Changing run_at also moves the next occurrence."""
    sets, vals = [], []
    for field in ("name", "frequency", "environment", "webhook_url", "recipients"):
        v = getattr(body, field)
        if v is not None:
            sets.append(f"{field} = %s"); vals.append(v)
    if body.enabled is not None:
        sets.append("enabled = %s"); vals.append(body.enabled)
    if body.run_at:
        try:
            dt = datetime.fromisoformat(body.run_at.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        except ValueError:
            return {"error": "run_at must be an ISO datetime."}
        sets += ["run_at = %s", "next_run_at = %s"]; vals += [dt, dt]
    if not sets:
        return {"error": "Nothing to update."}
    sets.append("updated_at = now()")
    vals.append(schedule_id)

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(f"UPDATE schedules SET {', '.join(sets)} WHERE id = %s RETURNING *",
                        tuple(vals))
            rows = _rows(cur)
        conn.commit()
    return {"schedule": rows[0]} if rows else {"error": "Schedule not found."}


@router.delete("/schedules/{schedule_id}")
def delete_schedule(schedule_id: int):
    """Delete a schedule and its run records. Test results are untouched."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM schedule_runs WHERE schedule_id = %s", (schedule_id,))
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM schedules WHERE id = %s", (schedule_id,))
            deleted = cur.rowcount
        conn.commit()
    return {"deleted": bool(deleted), "schedule_id": schedule_id}


@router.post("/schedules/{schedule_id}/run")
def run_now(schedule_id: int):
    """
    Run a schedule immediately.

    Deliberately the same function the background scheduler calls, so this is
    a genuine rehearsal of the scheduled run rather than a lookalike. The
    returned dict is whatever the job produced — a suite result for a suite
    schedule, a change-detection summary for a Jira one.
    """
    return scheduler_service.run_schedule(schedule_id, triggered_by="manual")


@router.get("/schedules/{schedule_id}/runs")
def schedule_runs(schedule_id: int, limit: int = 20):
    """Recent runs for a schedule."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """SELECT id, started_at, finished_at, total, passed, failed, skipped,
                          triggered_by, webhook_status, summary
                   FROM schedule_runs WHERE schedule_id = %s
                   ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT %s""",
                (schedule_id, limit),
            )
            return {"runs": _rows(cur)}

"""
api/routes/suites.py

Test suites — a named, curated selection of existing test cases.

  GET    /v1/applications/{id}/suites
  POST   /v1/applications/{id}/suites
  GET    /v1/suites/{suite_id}
  PATCH  /v1/suites/{suite_id}
  DELETE /v1/suites/{suite_id}
  PUT    /v1/suites/{suite_id}/members
  GET    /v1/applications/{id}/suite-candidates?kind=smoke

A suite selects tests that already exist; it never generates new ones.
"Smoke" and "regression" describe WHICH tests run and when, not a kind of
test — and the same test case belongs in both, so membership is
many-to-many.
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel

from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()


class SuiteIn(BaseModel):
    name: str
    kind: str = "custom"
    description: Optional[str] = None
    member_ids: list[int] = []


class SuitePatch(BaseModel):
    name: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None


class MembersIn(BaseModel):
    member_ids: list[int]


def _rows(cur):
    cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]


@router.get("/applications/{application_id}/suites")
def list_suites(application_id: int):
    """Suites for an application, with member and automation counts."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT s.*,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT m.test_case_proposal_id) AS member_count,
                       COUNT(DISTINCT m.test_case_proposal_id) FILTER (
                           WHERE EXISTS (
                               SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                               WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = m.test_case_proposal_id
                                 AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL
                                 AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                           )
                       ) AS automated_count
                FROM test_suites s
                LEFT JOIN test_suite_members m ON m.suite_id = s.id
                WHERE s.application_id = %s
                GROUP BY s.id
                ORDER BY s.kind, s.name
                """,
                (application_id,),
            )
            return {"suites": _rows(cur)}


@router.get("/applications/{application_id}/suite-candidates")
def suite_candidates(application_id: int, kind: str = "custom"):
    """
    Every test case that could go in a suite, with a sensible pre-selection.

    Defaults are a starting point, not a decision:
        smoke       P0 and P1 that are automated — the critical path, minutes
        regression  everything automated — "did anything break"
        custom      nothing pre-selected

    Un-automated test cases are included deliberately. Choosing what belongs
    in a suite and choosing what to automate are separate decisions, and you
    should be able to put a test in the smoke suite and script it afterwards.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT p.id, p.title, p.priority, p.category, p.tags,
                       EXISTS (
                           SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                           WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                             AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                       ) AS automated
                FROM test_case_proposals p
                WHERE p.application_id = %s AND p.status != 'archived'
                ORDER BY p.priority NULLS LAST, p.title
                """,
                (application_id,),
            )
            rows = _rows(cur)

    k = (kind or "custom").lower()
    for r in rows:
        if k == "smoke":
            r["suggested"] = bool(r["automated"]) and r.get("priority") in ("P0", "P1")
        elif k == "regression":
            r["suggested"] = bool(r["automated"])
        else:
            r["suggested"] = False

    return {
        "candidates": rows,
        "kind": k,
        "suggested_count": sum(1 for r in rows if r["suggested"]),
    }


@router.post("/applications/{application_id}/suites")
def create_suite(application_id: int, body: SuiteIn, request: Request):
    """Create a suite and set its members."""
    name = (body.name or "").strip()
    if not name:
        return {"error": "A suite name is required."}

    who = request.headers.get("X-Triggered-By", "anonymous")
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM test_suites WHERE application_id=%s AND lower(name)=lower(%s)",
                (application_id, name),
            )
            if cur.fetchone():
                return {"error": f"A suite called '{name}' already exists."}

            cur.execute(
                """INSERT INTO test_suites (application_id, name, kind, description, created_by)
                   VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s) RETURNING *""",
                (application_id, name, body.kind, body.description, who),
            )
            suite = _rows(cur)[0]

            for pid in body.member_ids:
                cur.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO test_suite_members (suite_id, test_case_proposal_id) "
                    "VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
                    (suite["id"], pid),
                )
        conn.commit()

    logger.info("Created %s suite '%s' with %d member(s) for application %s",
                body.kind, name, len(body.member_ids), application_id)
    suite["member_count"] = len(body.member_ids)
    return {"suite": suite}


@router.get("/suites/{suite_id}")
def get_suite(suite_id: int):
    """A suite with its members, each showing whether it is automated."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT * FROM test_suites WHERE id = %s", (suite_id,))
            suites = _rows(cur)
            if not suites:
                return {"error": "Suite not found."}
            suite = suites[0]

            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT p.id, p.title, p.priority, p.category,
                       EXISTS (
                           SELECT 1 FROM generations g
                           WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                             AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                       ) AS automated
                FROM test_suite_members m
                JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.id = m.test_case_proposal_id
                WHERE m.suite_id = %s AND p.status != 'archived'
                ORDER BY p.priority NULLS LAST, p.title
                """,
                (suite_id,),
            )
            suite["members"] = _rows(cur)
    return {"suite": suite}


@router.patch("/suites/{suite_id}")
def update_suite(suite_id: int, body: SuitePatch):
    """Rename a suite or change its description."""
    sets, vals = [], []
    if body.name is not None:
        sets.append("name = %s"); vals.append(body.name.strip())
    if body.description is not None:
        sets.append("description = %s"); vals.append(body.description)
    if not sets:
        return {"error": "Nothing to update."}
    sets.append("updated_at = now()")
    vals.append(suite_id)

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(f"UPDATE test_suites SET {', '.join(sets)} WHERE id = %s RETURNING *",
                        tuple(vals))
            rows = _rows(cur)
        conn.commit()
    return {"suite": rows[0]} if rows else {"error": "Suite not found."}


@router.put("/suites/{suite_id}/members")
def set_members(suite_id: int, body: MembersIn):
    """
    Replace a suite's membership.

    A whole-set update rather than add/remove calls: the UI edits the
    selection as one thing, so sending the final list avoids the two ever
    disagreeing.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM test_suite_members WHERE suite_id = %s", (suite_id,))
            for pid in body.member_ids:
                cur.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO test_suite_members (suite_id, test_case_proposal_id) "
                    "VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
                    (suite_id, pid),
                )
            cur.execute("UPDATE test_suites SET updated_at = now() WHERE id = %s", (suite_id,))
        conn.commit()
    logger.info("Suite %s now has %d member(s)", suite_id, len(body.member_ids))
    return {"suite_id": suite_id, "member_count": len(body.member_ids)}


@router.delete("/suites/{suite_id}")
def delete_suite(suite_id: int):
    """
    Delete a suite.

    Only the grouping is removed — the test cases, their scripts and their
    run history are untouched. A suite is a view over tests, not their owner.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM test_suite_members WHERE suite_id = %s", (suite_id,))
            cur.execute("DELETE FROM test_suites WHERE id = %s", (suite_id,))
            deleted = cur.rowcount
        conn.commit()
    if not deleted:
        return {"error": "Suite not found."}
    return {"deleted": True, "suite_id": suite_id}


class RunSuiteRequest(BaseModel):
    headed: bool = False
    environment: Optional[str] = None
    target_url: Optional[str] = None
    triggered_by: Optional[str] = "ui"


@router.post("/suites/{suite_id}/run")
def run_suite(suite_id: int, body: RunSuiteRequest):
    """
    Run every automated test case in a suite.

    This is the ONE path a suite is executed by — the UI's Run button and the
    scheduler both call it. Keeping them on the same code means what you
    demonstrate by hand is exactly what runs at 6am.

    Members without a script are reported as skipped rather than ignored: a
    suite that silently drops half its tests is worse than one that says so.
    """
    from api.routes.environments import resolve_url
    from api.routes.run import _record, _test_env_for
    from service.selenium_runner import run_script_file

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """SELECT s.name, s.kind, s.application_id, a.name AS app_name
                   FROM test_suites s JOIN applications a ON a.id = s.application_id
                   WHERE s.id = %s""",
                (suite_id,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                return {"error": "Suite not found."}
            suite_name, kind, application_id, app_name = row

            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT p.id, p.title,
                       (SELECT g.id FROM generations g
                         WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                           AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                         ORDER BY g.id DESC LIMIT 1) AS generation_id,
                       (SELECT g.script_path FROM generations g
                         WHERE g.test_case_proposal_id = p.id
                           AND g.script_path IS NOT NULL AND g.is_stale = FALSE
                         ORDER BY g.id DESC LIMIT 1) AS script_path
                FROM test_suite_members m
                JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.id = m.test_case_proposal_id
                WHERE m.suite_id = %s AND p.status != 'archived'
                ORDER BY p.priority NULLS LAST, p.title
                """,
                (suite_id,),
            )
            members = _rows(cur)

    url, env_label = resolve_url(application_id, body.environment, body.target_url)
    logger.info("Running suite '%s' (%d member(s)) against %s [%s]",
                suite_name, len(members), url, env_label)

    results, passed, failed, skipped = [], 0, 0, []

    for m in members:
        if not m["generation_id"] or not m["script_path"]:
            skipped.append(m["title"])
            results.append({"test": m["title"], "result": "skipped",
                            "reason": "no script generated yet"})
            continue

        r = run_script_file(
            m["script_path"],
            headed=body.headed,
            target_url=url,
            extra_env=_test_env_for(m["generation_id"], body.environment),
        )
        r["environment"] = env_label
        try:
            _record(m["generation_id"], r)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Could not record execution for %s: %s", m["title"], e)

        if r.get("result") == "pass":
            passed += 1
        else:
            failed += 1
        results.append({
            "test": m["title"],
            "result": r.get("result"),
            "duration_ms": r.get("duration_ms"),
            "output": (r.get("output") or "")[-1200:] if r.get("result") != "pass" else "",
        })

    summary = {
        "suite_id": suite_id, "suite": suite_name, "kind": kind,
        "application": app_name, "application_id": application_id,
        "environment": env_label, "target_url": url,
        "total": len(members), "passed": passed, "failed": failed,
        "skipped": len(skipped), "skipped_tests": skipped,
        "results": results,
        "triggered_by": body.triggered_by,
    }
    logger.info("Suite '%s' finished: %d passed, %d failed, %d skipped",
                suite_name, passed, failed, len(skipped))
    return summary

"""
api/routes/support.py

Raising and tracking support tickets from inside NextGen2.

  GET  /v1/support/config              which provider is active, and is it usable
  GET  /v1/support/categories          the plain-English categories the form offers
  GET  /v1/support/tickets             tickets, newest first
  POST /v1/support/tickets             raise one
  GET  /v1/support/tickets/{id}        one ticket

Nothing in this file names Jira. It calls service.ticketing, which resolves
the configured provider — so moving to ServiceNow changes no route, no
response shape and no screen.

The ordering rule from help.py applies here too: literal paths are declared
before '/support/tickets/{ticket_id}', or 'config' and 'categories' would be
matched as ticket ids.

The write order is the part worth understanding. The row is inserted BEFORE
the external system is called, and updated after. If Jira is unreachable, or the
the project key is wrong, or the token expired, the ticket still exists in
NextGen2 with status='failed' and the reason recorded. A user who has just
described a problem should never be told to type it again because the
integration was down.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from typing import Any, Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel

from core.db.connection import get_conn
from core.settings import settings
from service.ticketing import TicketingError, TicketRequest, create_ticket, get_provider

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter()


# The categories the form offers. A bounded, enumerable list rather than free
# text: each provider maps these onto its own object model — a Jira label
# today, a ServiceNow incident-versus-request decision later — and that
# mapping is only possible if the set is known in advance. The user is never
# asked to understand either model.
CATEGORIES = [
    {"key": "how-to",   "label": "How do I…?",
     "hint": "Using a feature, or finding where something lives."},
    {"key": "bug",      "label": "Something is broken",
     "hint": "A screen, run or report is not behaving as expected."},
    {"key": "data",     "label": "The data looks wrong",
     "hint": "Results, coverage or a report do not match what you expected."},
    {"key": "access",   "label": "Access or permissions",
     "hint": "You cannot reach an application, environment or integration."},
    {"key": "request",  "label": "Feature or change request",
     "hint": "Something NextGen2 does not do yet."},
]

_CATEGORY_KEYS = {c["key"] for c in CATEGORIES}


class TicketIn(BaseModel):
    """A support request submitted from the Help screen.

    Attributes:
        category: One of CATEGORIES. An unknown value is accepted rather than
            rejected — see create_ticket — because losing a written-out
            problem report over a vocabulary mismatch is the worse outcome.
        summary: One-line title.
        description: The user's account of the problem.
        context: Technical detail captured by the UI — route, application_id,
            execution_id, browser, last error.
    """

    category: str = "how-to"
    summary: str
    description: str = ""
    context: dict[str, Any] = {}


def _rows(cur) -> list[dict]:
    """Read all rows from an open cursor as dicts.

    Args:
        cur: A cursor positioned after a SELECT.

    Returns:
        Rows as dicts.
    """
    cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]


def _who(request: Request) -> str:
    """Identify the caller.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request.

    Returns:
        The X-Triggered-By header value, or 'anonymous'.
    """
    return request.headers.get("X-Triggered-By", "anonymous")


# ── literal paths, before any parameterised path ─────────────────────────

@router.get("/support/config")
def support_config():
    """Report which ticketing provider is active and whether it is usable.

    A preflight check, so a missing project key surfaces here rather than at
    the moment a user is trying to report a problem.

    Returns:
        The provider name, whether its configuration validates, and the
        reason if it does not.
    """
    provider_name = settings.ticketing.provider
    try:
        provider = get_provider()
        provider.check_config()
        return {"provider": provider.name, "configured": True, "reason": None}
    except TicketingError as e:
        logger.warning("Ticketing provider is not usable: %s", e)
        return {"provider": provider_name, "configured": False, "reason": str(e)}


@router.get("/support/categories")
def list_categories():
    """Return the categories the support form offers.

    Returns:
        The bounded category list, each with a label and a hint.
    """
    return CATEGORIES


@router.get("/support/tickets")
def list_tickets(raised_by: Optional[str] = None, limit: int = 50):
    """List tickets raised from NextGen2, newest first.

    Args:
        raised_by: Restrict to one person, or None for everyone.
        limit: Maximum rows.

    Returns:
        Ticket rows including their external reference and link.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """SELECT id, provider, external_ref, external_url, raised_by,
                          category, summary, description, context, status,
                          external_status, submit_error, created_at
                   FROM support_tickets
                   WHERE (%s IS NULL OR raised_by = %s)
                   ORDER BY created_at DESC
                   LIMIT %s""",
                (raised_by, raised_by, limit),
            )
            return _rows(cur)


@router.post("/support/tickets")
def raise_ticket(body: TicketIn, request: Request):
    """Raise a support ticket in the configured external system.

    Args:
        body: The support request from the form.
        request: The incoming request, for the caller's identity.

    Returns:
        The stored ticket. On failure the response still carries the ticket,
        with status 'failed' and an error explaining what went wrong.
    """
    return create_support_ticket(
        category=body.category,
        summary=body.summary,
        description=body.description,
        context=body.context,
        raised_by=_who(request),
    )


def create_support_ticket(category: str, summary: str, description: str = "",
                          context: Optional[dict] = None,
                          raised_by: str = "anonymous") -> dict:
    """Create a support ticket, whatever asked for it.

    Shared by the Help screen's form and by the assistant's raise_ticket
    action, so a ticket raised in conversation is identical to one raised on
    the form — same validation, same stored row, same failure handling. Two
    code paths would have drifted, and the one used less often would have
    been the one that was wrong.

    The local row is written FIRST and updated afterwards, so a failure to
    reach the external system loses nothing: the ticket exists in NextGen2 with
    the reason recorded, and can be retried or picked up manually. A user who
    has just described a problem should never be told to type it again
    because an integration was down.

    Args:
        category: Plain-English kind of request. An unknown value is filed as
            'how-to' rather than rejected.
        summary: One-line title. Required.
        description: The user's account of the problem.
        context: Technical detail to attach.
        raised_by: Who is asking.

    Returns:
        The stored ticket, with an `error` key added when the external system
        rejected it.
    """
    summary = (summary or "").strip()
    if not summary:
        return {"error": "A summary is required."}

    who = raised_by
    category = category if category in _CATEGORY_KEYS else "how-to"
    body = TicketIn(category=category, summary=summary,
                    description=description or "", context=context or {})
    provider_name = settings.ticketing.provider

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """INSERT INTO support_tickets
                       (provider, raised_by, category, summary, description,
                        context, status)
                   VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, 'open')
                   RETURNING id""",
                (provider_name, who, category, summary,
                 (body.description or "").strip(), json.dumps(body.context or {})),
            )
            ticket_id = cur.fetchone()[0]

    logger.info("Support ticket %s recorded for %s (category=%s)",
                ticket_id, who, category)

    try:
        ref = create_ticket(TicketRequest(
            category=category,
            summary=summary,
            description=(body.description or "").strip(),
            raised_by=who,
            context=body.context or {},
        ))
    except TicketingError as e:
        _mark_failed(ticket_id, str(e))
        logger.error("Support ticket %s could not be filed: %s", ticket_id, e)
        return {
            **_get(ticket_id),
            "error": (
                f"Your request was saved in NextGen2 but could not be filed "
                f"externally: {e}"
            ),
        }

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """UPDATE support_tickets
                   SET provider = %s, external_ref = %s, external_url = %s,
                       external_status = %s, status = 'submitted',
                       last_synced_at = now(), updated_at = now()
                   WHERE id = %s""",
                (ref.provider, ref.external_ref, ref.external_url,
                 ref.external_status, ticket_id),
            )

    logger.info("Support ticket %s filed as %s", ticket_id, ref.external_ref)
    return _get(ticket_id)


# ── parameterised paths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

@router.get("/support/tickets/{ticket_id}")
def get_ticket(ticket_id: int):
    """Return one ticket.

    Args:
        ticket_id: support_tickets.id.

    Returns:
        The ticket row, or an error if it does not exist.
    """
    row = _get(ticket_id)
    return row or {"error": f"Ticket {ticket_id} not found."}


# ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _get(ticket_id: int) -> dict:
    """Read one ticket.

    Args:
        ticket_id: support_tickets.id.

    Returns:
        The row as a dict, or an empty dict if there is none.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """SELECT id, provider, external_ref, external_url, raised_by,
                          category, summary, description, context, status,
                          external_status, submit_error, created_at
                   FROM support_tickets WHERE id = %s""",
                (ticket_id,),
            )
            rows = _rows(cur)
            return rows[0] if rows else {}


def _mark_failed(ticket_id: int, reason: str) -> None:
    """Record that a ticket could not be filed externally.

    Args:
        ticket_id: support_tickets.id.
        reason: The provider's message, truncated to a sane length.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """UPDATE support_tickets
                   SET status = 'failed', submit_error = %s, updated_at = now()
                   WHERE id = %s""",
                (reason[:2000], ticket_id),
            )

FILE: backend/api/routes/test_data.py
