"""
core/settings.py

Loads all configuration at startup from environment variables and YAML
config files. Validates that every required value is present before the
application accepts any requests — a missing setting is caught immediately,
not discovered mid-request.

All other modules import from here. Nothing reads os.environ directly.
"""

from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()  # read .env before any env var is accessed

import os
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional


CONFIG_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "config"


@dataclass
class LLMSettings:
    api_url: str
    api_key: str
    model: str
    max_retries: int
    timeout_per_step: int
    aws_secret: Optional[str]
    aws_region: Optional[str]
    langfuse_url: Optional[str]
    langfuse_api_key: Optional[str]
    provider_type: str = "gemini"
    azure_api_version: Optional[str] = None
    azure_deployment_name: Optional[str] = None


@dataclass
class DatabaseSettings:
    url: str


@dataclass
class AppSettings:
    port: int
    cors_origins: list[str]
    selenium_headed: bool


@dataclass
class JiraSettings:
    """
    Jira connection settings for the Jira source adapter.

    Optional: the credentials are read with _optional_env so the application
    still starts when Jira is not configured. The adapter raises a clear error
    only if a Jira-sourced run is actually attempted without them.
    """
    base_url: str
    email: str
    api_token: str
    project_key: str
    issue_type: str


@dataclass
class ALMSettings:
    """
    ALM connection settings for read-only requirements ingestion.

    base_url is optional at startup so environments that do not use ALM are
    not blocked. The ALM routes require either this setting or a request-time
    override.
    """
    base_url: str
    connect_timeout_sec: int
    read_timeout_sec: int
    max_retries: int
    retry_backoff_base_ms: int
    ssl_verify: bool


@dataclass
class HelpSettings:
    """
    Help & Support behaviour.

    search_strategy selects which implementation in service/help_search/
    answers a query. It is a setting rather than a code path so retrieval can
    move from keyword matching to embeddings without any caller changing:
    everything above SearchStrategy.search() is identical either way.

    Attributes:
        search_strategy: Key into service.help_search.registry.STRATEGIES.
            'fts' is Postgres full-text search over help_chunks — the only
            strategy implemented today. A vector or hybrid strategy plugs in
            here later without touching the routes, the chat tool or the UI.
        min_score: Absolute relevance floor. Zero for full-text search,
            because ts_rank_cd is a cover-density measure rather than a
            calibrated score: a precise all-terms match can score far LOWER
            than a loose any-term one, so any fixed threshold discards good
            results. Retained because a vector strategy's cosine similarity IS
            calibrated 0-1, and there an absolute floor is the right tool.
        relative_floor: Fraction of the best result's score, within the same
            retrieval pass, below which a passage is treated as noise. Within
            one pass the scores ARE comparable, so this is the filter that
            actually works for full-text search. It matters because a local
            model given two good passages and one irrelevant one answers worse
            than one given two. 0.0 disables it.
        max_passages: How many passages are returned to the model. Kept small
            deliberately — a local model given ten passages answers worse than
            one given three.
        content_dir: Where the authored markdown articles live, relative to
            the backend directory. Article text is authored in files and
            seeded into the database; it is never embedded in Python.
        training_dir: Where uploaded training documents are stored, relative
            to the backend directory. Unlike a BRD — which is read once during
            a survey and can live in a temp directory — a training document
            stays downloadable for as long as the training record referencing
            it must remain readable, so it needs a persistent home.
        chunk_target_words: Approximate size of a retrievable passage. Chunks
            are created at write time and are the unit a future vector store
            would embed, so this value shapes retrieval quality later as well
            as now.
    """
    search_strategy: str
    min_score: float
    relative_floor: float
    max_passages: int
    content_dir: str
    training_dir: str
    chunk_target_words: int


@dataclass
class TicketingSettings:
    """
    Where a support ticket raised inside NextGen2 is created.

    provider names an implementation in service/ticketing/registry.py. NextGen2
    itself never references a specific ticketing system: moving from Jira to
    ServiceNow is a new provider class plus this one value, with no schema
    change and no change to any route or screen.

    The Jira fields here are deliberately separate from JiraSettings above.
    That block is the requirements SOURCE (read-only, a different project);
    this is the support DESTINATION (write). Pointing both at one project
    would let support tickets be picked up by the requirements sync as if they
    were requirements in NextGen2.

    Attributes:
        provider: Key into service.ticketing.registry.PROVIDERS, e.g. 'jira'.
        jira_project_key: Jira project support tickets are created in. Must
            NOT be the requirements project.
        jira_issue_type: Issue type to create, e.g. 'Task' or 'Bug'.
    """
    provider: str
    jira_project_key: str
    jira_issue_type: str


@dataclass
class Settings:
    llm: LLMSettings
    db: DatabaseSettings
    app: AppSettings
    jira: JiraSettings
    alm: ALMSettings
    help: HelpSettings
    ticketing: TicketingSettings
    applications_config: dict
    import_aliases: dict


def _require_env(name: str) -> str:
    """Reads a required environment variable. Raises clearly if missing."""
    value = os.environ.get(name)
    if not value:
        raise EnvironmentError(
            f"Required environment variable '{name}' is not set. "
            f"Copy .env.example to .env and fill in the value."
        )
    return value


def _optional_env(name: str, default: str = "") -> str:
    return os.environ.get(name, default)


def _load_yaml(filename: str) -> dict:
    path = CONFIG_DIR / filename
    with open(path) as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}


def load_settings() -> Settings:
    """
    Loads and validates all configuration.
    Called once at startup in api/main.py.
    Raises EnvironmentError with a clear message if anything is missing.
    """
    applications_config = _load_yaml("applications.yaml")
    import_aliases = _load_yaml("import_aliases.yaml")

    llm = LLMSettings(
        api_url=_require_env("LLM_API_URL"),
        api_key=_require_env("LLM_API_KEY"),
        model=_require_env("LLM_MODEL"),
        max_retries=int(_optional_env("LLM_MAX_RETRIES", "3")),
        timeout_per_step=int(_optional_env("LLM_TIMEOUT_PER_STEP", "180")),
        aws_secret=_optional_env("LLM_AWS_SECRET") or None,
        aws_region=_optional_env("LLM_AWS_REGION", "us-east-1"),
        langfuse_url=_optional_env("LANGFUSE_URL") or None,
        langfuse_api_key=_optional_env("LANGFUSE_API_KEY") or None,
        provider_type=_optional_env("LLM_PROVIDER_TYPE", "gemini").lower(),
        azure_api_version=_optional_env("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION") or None,
        azure_deployment_name=_optional_env("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME") or None,
    )

    db = DatabaseSettings(url=_require_env("DATABASE_URL"))

    cors_raw = _optional_env("CORS_ORIGINS", "http://localhost:9000")
    cors_origins = [o.strip() for o in cors_raw.split(",") if o.strip()]

    app = AppSettings(
        port=int(_optional_env("APP_PORT", "9090")),
        cors_origins=cors_origins,
        selenium_headed=_optional_env("SELENIUM_HEADED", "true").lower() == "true",
    )

    jira = JiraSettings(
        base_url=_optional_env("JIRA_BASE_URL").rstrip("/"),
        email=_optional_env("JIRA_EMAIL"),
        api_token=_optional_env("JIRA_API_TOKEN"),
        project_key=_optional_env("JIRA_PROJECT_KEY", "KAN"),
        issue_type=_optional_env("JIRA_ISSUE_TYPE", "Feature"),
    )

    alm = ALMSettings(
        base_url=_optional_env("ALM_BASE_URL", "https://baxter.alm.saas.microfocus.com/qcbin").rstrip("/"),
        connect_timeout_sec=int(_optional_env("ALM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SEC", "10")),
        read_timeout_sec=int(_optional_env("ALM_READ_TIMEOUT_SEC", "30")),
        max_retries=int(_optional_env("ALM_MAX_RETRIES", "3")),
        retry_backoff_base_ms=int(_optional_env("ALM_RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE_MS", "250")),
        ssl_verify=_optional_env("ALM_SSL_VERIFY", "true").lower() == "true",
    )

    help_settings = HelpSettings(
        search_strategy=_optional_env("HELP_SEARCH_STRATEGY", "fts").lower(),
        min_score=float(_optional_env("HELP_MIN_SCORE", "0.0")),
        relative_floor=float(_optional_env("HELP_RELATIVE_FLOOR", "0.2")),
        max_passages=int(_optional_env("HELP_MAX_PASSAGES", "3")),
        content_dir=_optional_env("HELP_CONTENT_DIR", "content/help"),
        training_dir=_optional_env("HELP_TRAINING_DIR", "storage/training"),
        chunk_target_words=int(_optional_env("HELP_CHUNK_TARGET_WORDS", "300")),
    )

    ticketing = TicketingSettings(
        provider=_optional_env("TICKETING_PROVIDER", "jira").lower(),
        # No default project key on purpose. Falling back to the requirements
        # project would silently file support tickets into the project the
        # sync engine reads requirements from. The provider raises a clear
        # error if this is unset when a ticket is actually raised.
        jira_project_key=_optional_env("JIRA_SUPPORT_PROJECT_KEY"),
        jira_issue_type=_optional_env("JIRA_SUPPORT_ISSUE_TYPE", "Task"),
    )

    return Settings(
        llm=llm,
        db=db,
        app=app,
        jira=jira,
        alm=alm,
        help=help_settings,
        ticketing=ticketing,
        applications_config=applications_config,
        import_aliases=import_aliases,
    )


# Singleton — loaded once, imported everywhere
settings: Settings = load_settings()

FILE: backend/core/db/connection.py
================================================
"""
core/db/connection.py

Opens and manages the database connection pool.
Every query module imports `get_conn()` from here — nothing else
constructs its own connection.

Uses psycopg2 with a simple connection pool. For production scale,
swap the pool implementation here without touching any query module.
"""

import logging
import psycopg2
from psycopg2 import pool
from contextlib import contextmanager
from core.settings import settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_pool: pool.ThreadedConnectionPool | None = None


def init_pool() -> None:
    """
    Initialises the connection pool.
    Called once at startup from api/main.py.

    Uses explicit keyword arguments instead of a DSN string because
    psycopg2 on Windows ignores the host in a DSN and attempts a
    Unix socket connection, which Windows does not support.
    """
    global _pool
    logger.info("Initialising database connection pool")

    from urllib.parse import urlparse
    parsed = urlparse(settings.db.url)
    _pool = pool.ThreadedConnectionPool(
        minconn=2,
        maxconn=10,
        host=parsed.hostname,
        port=parsed.port or 5432,
        dbname=parsed.path.lstrip("/"),
        user=parsed.username,
        password=parsed.password,
    )
    logger.info("Database connection pool ready")


@contextmanager
def get_conn():
    """
    Context manager that yields a database connection from the pool
    and returns it when the block exits, whether or not an exception
    was raised.

    Usage:
        with get_conn() as conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(...)

    Raises: RuntimeError if init_pool() has not been called yet.
    """
    if _pool is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Database pool is not initialised. "
            "Call init_pool() during application startup."
        )
    conn = _pool.getconn()
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    except Exception:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        _pool.putconn(conn)

FILE: backend/core/db/queries/ai_calls.py
================================================
"""
core/db/queries/ai_calls.py

Records every LLM API call for cost and performance tracking.
The reporting dashboards calculate token usage and cost from this data.

Token counts come from the provider's response at the time of the call.
They are never estimated afterward.
"""

import logging
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
from typing import Optional

from core.db.connection import get_conn
from llm.usage_context import get_usage_context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Prices are stored per 1 million tokens. Costs are rounded to 6 decimals,
# which matches the NUMERIC(14,6) database column.
_ONE_MILLION = Decimal("1000000")
_COST_PRECISION = Decimal("0.000001")

# Maps the purpose labels to the original related_to_type column,
# so existing code that reads related_to_type keeps working.
_PURPOSE_TO_RELATED_TYPE = {
    "test_case_generation": "survey",
    "script_generation": "generation",
    "healing": "heal",
    "chat": "chat",
    "crawl": "other",
    "other": "other",
}


def record(
    related_to_type: str,
    related_to_id: Optional[int],
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    input_tokens: Optional[int],
    output_tokens: Optional[int],
    cost_usd: Optional[Decimal],
    latency_ms: Optional[int],
    purpose: str = "other",
    application_id: Optional[int] = None,
    user_id: Optional[int] = None,
    pricing_found: bool = False,
    run_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> None:
    """
    Inserts one row into ai_calls. Raises on database errors,
    so providers should call record_llm_call(), which never raises.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO ai_calls
                    (related_to_type, related_to_id, provider, model,
                     input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, latency_ms,
                     purpose, application_id, user_id, pricing_found, run_id)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                """,
                (related_to_type, related_to_id, provider, model,
                 input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, latency_ms,
                 purpose, application_id, user_id, pricing_found, run_id),
            )


def _lookup_pricing(provider, model):
    """Returns the current (input, output) price per 1M tokens, or None if no price is set."""
    # Takes the newest price row that is already in effect for this provider and model.
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT input_usd_per_1m, output_usd_per_1m
                FROM llm_model_pricing
                WHERE provider = %s AND model = %s AND effective_from <= NOW()
                ORDER BY effective_from DESC
                LIMIT 1
                """,
                (provider, model),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
    return (Decimal(row[0]), Decimal(row[1])) if row else None


def _calculate_cost(pricing, input_tokens, output_tokens):
    """Calculates the cost in USD with exact Decimal math. Returns None when no price is set."""
    # No price configured for this model: return None so the cost is saved as unknown, not $0.
    if pricing is None:
        return None
    input_price, output_price = pricing
    # Prices are per 1M tokens, so multiply the tokens by the price and divide by one million.
    cost = (
        Decimal(input_tokens or 0) * input_price
        + Decimal(output_tokens or 0) * output_price
    ) / _ONE_MILLION
    # Round to 6 decimals to match the NUMERIC(14,6) database column.
    return cost.quantize(_COST_PRECISION, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def record_llm_call(
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    input_tokens: Optional[int],
    output_tokens: Optional[int],
    latency_ms: Optional[int],
) -> None:
    """
    Called by every provider after a successful LLM response.
    Reads the active label, calculates the cost, and saves the row.
    Never raises, so a tracking failure can't break test or script generation.
    """
    try:
        ctx = get_usage_context()
        pricing = _lookup_pricing(provider, model)
        if pricing is None:
            # Logged so a missing price gets noticed. The call is still saved, with cost left empty.
            logger.warning("No pricing configured for %s/%s; cost recorded as NULL", provider, model)

        record(
            related_to_type=_PURPOSE_TO_RELATED_TYPE.get(ctx.purpose, "other"),
            related_to_id=ctx.related_to_id,
            provider=provider,
            model=model,
            input_tokens=input_tokens,
            output_tokens=output_tokens,
            cost_usd=_calculate_cost(pricing, input_tokens, output_tokens),
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            purpose=ctx.purpose,
            application_id=ctx.application_id,
            user_id=ctx.user_id,
            pricing_found=pricing is not None,
            run_id=ctx.run_id,
        )
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to record LLM usage (non-fatal) for %s/%s", provider, model)


def sum_cost_for_run(run_id: str) -> Decimal:
    """Total cost of every AI call in one survey run. Unpriced calls (NULL cost) count as zero."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM ai_calls WHERE run_id = %s", (run_id,))
            return Decimal(cur.fetchone()[0])


def get_script_costs(application_id: int) -> list:
    """
    Cost of each script generation for one application, as exact sums of the AI
    calls linked to that generation (including verify-and-repair attempts).
    Generations with no recorded calls, such as older ones, are left out rather than shown as $0.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT g.test_case_proposal_id, g.id,
                       COALESCE(SUM(c.cost_usd), 0) AS cost_usd,
                       COUNT(c.id)                  AS ai_calls
                FROM generations g
                JOIN test_case_proposals p ON p.id = g.test_case_proposal_id
                JOIN ai_calls c ON c.purpose = 'script_generation' AND c.related_to_id = g.id
                WHERE p.application_id = %s
                GROUP BY g.test_case_proposal_id, g.id
                ORDER BY g.id
                """,
                (application_id,),
            )
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [
        {"proposal_id": r[0], "generation_id": r[1], "cost_usd": str(r[2]), "ai_calls": r[3]}
        for r in rows
    ]


def save_survey_run(run_id, application_id, proposal_count, total_cost, per_case_cost):
    """
    Stores the total AI cost of one survey run and each test case's even share of it.
    Never raises: cost bookkeeping must not break the survey.
    """
    try:
        with get_conn() as conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO survey_runs
                        (run_id, application_id, proposal_count, total_cost_usd, per_case_cost_usd)
                    VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                    ON CONFLICT (run_id) DO NOTHING
                    """,
                    (run_id, application_id, proposal_count, total_cost, per_case_cost),
                )
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Could not save survey run cost (non-fatal)")


def get_survey_run(application_id, run_id=None):
    """
    Finds the survey run a test case's cost share comes from. Needs the run id:
    with none (file or ALM imports) it returns None, so no cost is attached.
    """
    if not run_id:
        return None
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT run_id, per_case_cost_usd FROM survey_runs WHERE run_id = %s AND application_id = %s",
                (run_id, application_id),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
    return {"run_id": row[0], "per_case_cost_usd": Decimal(row[1])} if row else None


def get_test_case_costs(application_id):
    """Estimated AI cost per test case of one application, as {proposal id (string): cost (string)}."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, ai_cost_usd FROM test_case_proposals
                WHERE application_id = %s AND ai_cost_usd IS NOT NULL AND status != 'archived'
                """,
                (application_id,),
            )
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return {str(r[0]): str(r[1]) for r in rows}



================================================
FILE: backend/core/db/queries/app_credentials.py
================================================
"""
core/db/queries/app_credentials.py

All database reads and writes for the `app_credentials` table — one login
credential per (application, user). No other module touches this table
directly.

THE SINGLE DOOR
    get_credential(application_id, user_id) is the ONLY way any stage
    (crawl, generation, execution) obtains a stored password. It always
    filters by BOTH application_id AND user_id, so a run can only ever read
    the credential of the user who initiated it — never another user's. There
    is deliberately no function that returns "all credentials for an
    application", and no function that accepts a password back out in bulk.

SECRECY
    The password is encrypted at rest with Fernet, using the SAME key as the
    existing test-data store (TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY). The plaintext is only
    ever held in memory, at save time and at the moment of use. The username
    is stored in clear (it is not a secret and callers routinely need to
    display it); only the password is encrypted.
"""

import logging
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from cryptography.fernet import Fernet, InvalidToken
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SECRET_ALG = "fernet"


def _fernet() -> Fernet:
    """Build a Fernet from TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY — the same key the
    test-data store uses, so one key decrypts every stored secret.

    Raises RuntimeError with an actionable message if the key is missing or
    malformed, rather than failing obscurely deep inside a save.
    """
    key = (os.environ.get("TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY") or "").strip()
    if not key:
        # Some processes start from the repo root rather than backend/, so
        # implicit dotenv discovery can miss backend/.env. Load it directly.
        backend_env = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / ".env"
        if backend_env.exists():
            load_dotenv(dotenv_path=backend_env, override=False)
        key = (os.environ.get("TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY") or "").strip()
    if not key:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Configure it before saving "
            "or reading per-user application credentials."
        )
    try:
        return Fernet(key.encode("utf-8"))
    except Exception as e:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is invalid. It must be a valid Fernet key."
        ) from e


def upsert_credential(application_id: int, user_id: int, username: str, password: str) -> dict:
    """Save (or replace) THIS user's credential for THIS application.

    The password is encrypted before it ever reaches the database. A second
    call for the same (application, user) updates the existing row — enforced
    by the UNIQUE(application_id, user_id) constraint via ON CONFLICT.

    Args:
        application_id: The application this credential logs into.
        user_id: The internal users.id of the credential's owner.
        username: The login username (stored in clear — not a secret).
        password: The login password (encrypted at rest, never stored plain).

    Returns:
        A dict of the row's non-secret metadata (id, application_id, user_id,
        username, created_at, updated_at). Never returns the password.
    """
    cipher = _fernet().encrypt(password.encode("utf-8")).decode("utf-8")
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO app_credentials
                    (application_id, user_id, username, secret_alg, secret_cipher)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                ON CONFLICT (application_id, user_id) DO UPDATE
                    SET username      = EXCLUDED.username,
                        secret_alg    = EXCLUDED.secret_alg,
                        secret_cipher = EXCLUDED.secret_cipher,
                        updated_at    = now()
                RETURNING id, application_id, user_id, username, created_at, updated_at
                """,
                (application_id, user_id, username, SECRET_ALG, cipher),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    logger.info(
        "app_credentials: saved credential app=%s user=%s", application_id, user_id
    )
    return dict(zip(cols, row))


def get_credential(application_id: int, user_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
    """THE SINGLE DOOR. Return THIS user's decrypted credential for THIS
    application, or None if they have not saved one.

    Always scoped by BOTH application_id and user_id. There is no fallback to
    any other user's row: if this user has no credential for this application,
    the result is None — never someone else's credential.

    Args:
        application_id: The application being logged into.
        user_id: The internal users.id of the run's initiator.

    Returns:
        {"username": str, "password": str} with the password decrypted in
        memory, or None if no row exists for this exact (application, user).
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT username, secret_cipher
                FROM app_credentials
                WHERE application_id = %s AND user_id = %s
                """,
                (application_id, user_id),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return None
    username, cipher = row[0], row[1]
    try:
        password = _fernet().decrypt(cipher.encode("utf-8")).decode("utf-8")
    except InvalidToken as e:
        # A wrong/rotated key, or a tampered row, must fail loudly — never
        # silently return a bad or empty password that a stage would type.
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Could not decrypt stored credential with current "
            "TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY (app=%s user=%s)." % (application_id, user_id)
        ) from e
    return {"username": username, "password": password}


def has_credential(application_id: int, user_id: int) -> bool:
    """True if THIS user has a saved credential for THIS application.

    Lets a caller check presence (e.g. to show "you haven't added your login
    for this app yet") without decrypting the secret.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT 1 FROM app_credentials
                WHERE application_id = %s AND user_id = %s
                """,
                (application_id, user_id),
            )
            return cur.fetchone() is not None


def delete_credential(application_id: int, user_id: int) -> bool:
    """Delete THIS user's credential for THIS application.

    Returns True if a row was removed, False if there was nothing to remove.
    Scoped by both keys, so a user can only ever delete their own credential.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                DELETE FROM app_credentials
                WHERE application_id = %s AND user_id = %s
                """,
                (application_id, user_id),
            )
            removed = cur.rowcount > 0
    if removed:
        logger.info(
            "app_credentials: deleted credential app=%s user=%s",
            application_id, user_id,
        )
    return removed

"""
core/db/queries/applications.py

All database reads and writes for the `applications` table.
No other module touches this table directly.
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional
from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def find_by_normalized_url(normalized_url: str, include_archived: bool = False) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Finds an existing application by its normalised URL.

    Args:
        normalized_url: The URL after normalisation (lowercase host,
            stripped trailing slash, stripped default port).
        include_archived: When True, archived rows are eligible matches.

    Returns:
        A dict with all application fields, or None if not found.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                                SELECT id, name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner,
                       is_archived, created_at
                FROM applications
                WHERE normalized_url = %s
                  AND (%s OR is_archived = FALSE)
                """,
                (normalized_url, include_archived),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return dict(zip(cols, row))


def unarchive(application_id: int, name: Optional[str], base_url: Optional[str], owner: Optional[str]) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Restores an archived application to active state.

    Args:
        application_id: Row ID to restore.
        name: Optional replacement display name.
        base_url: Optional replacement base URL.
        owner: Optional replacement owner.

    Returns:
        Restored row as dict, or None when ID is not found.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE applications
                SET is_archived = FALSE,
                    name = COALESCE(%s, name),
                    base_url = COALESCE(%s, base_url),
                    owner = COALESCE(%s, owner)
                WHERE id = %s
                RETURNING id, name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner,
                          is_archived, created_at
                """,
                (name, base_url, owner, application_id),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            result = dict(zip(cols, row))
            logger.info("Restored archived application id=%s", application_id)
            return result


def find_by_id(application_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Fetches one application by primary key.

    Args:
        application_id: The application's database ID.

    Returns:
        A dict with all application fields, or None if not found.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                  SELECT id, name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner,
                       is_archived, created_at
                FROM applications
                WHERE id = %s
                """,
                (application_id,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return dict(zip(cols, row))


def create(name: str, base_url: Optional[str], normalized_url: Optional[str],
           application_type: Optional[str], owner: Optional[str],
           requires_sso_gateway: bool = False) -> dict:
    """
    Inserts a new application row.

    Args:
        name: Display name, required.
        base_url: Raw URL as provided by the user, optional.
        normalized_url: Normalised form of the URL, optional.
        application_type: e.g. "web", "enterprise_erp", optional.
        owner: Name of the person responsible, optional.

    Returns:
        The newly created application as a dict.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO applications (name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                RETURNING id, name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner,
                          is_archived, created_at
                """,
                (name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            result = dict(zip(cols, row))
            logger.info("Created application id=%s name=%s", result["id"], name)
            return result


def list_all(include_archived: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Returns all applications, ordered by name.

    Args:
        include_archived: When True, includes archived applications.
            Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        A list of application dicts.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            where = "" if include_archived else "WHERE is_archived = FALSE"
            cur.execute(
                f"""
                SELECT id, name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner,
                       is_archived, created_at
                FROM applications
                {where}
                ORDER BY name
                """
            )
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return [dict(zip(cols, row)) for row in cur.fetchall()]


def set_requires_sso_gateway(application_id: int, requires_sso_gateway: bool) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Sets whether this application should enforce SSO prechecks."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE applications
                SET requires_sso_gateway = %s
                WHERE id = %s
                RETURNING id, name, base_url, requires_sso_gateway, normalized_url, owner,
                          is_archived, created_at
                """,
                (requires_sso_gateway, application_id),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return dict(zip(cols, row))

"""
core/db/queries/batches.py

All database reads and writes for the `batches` table.
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional
from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def create(application_id: int, environment: str,
           triggered_by: Optional[str], trigger_type: str) -> dict:
    """
    Creates a new batch run record.

    Args:
        application_id: FK to applications.
        environment: Which environment this batch runs against.
        triggered_by: Who or what started it.
        trigger_type: 'manual' or 'scheduled'.

    Returns:
        The newly created batch row as a dict.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO batches
                    (application_id, environment, triggered_by, trigger_type)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (application_id, environment, triggered_by, trigger_type),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return dict(zip(cols, row))


def update_status(batch_id: int, status: str) -> None:
    """
    Updates a batch's status.

    Args:
        batch_id: The batch's database ID.
        status: One of 'running', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled'.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE batches
                SET status = %s,
                    completed_at = CASE WHEN %s != 'running' THEN now() ELSE NULL END
                WHERE id = %s
                """,
                (status, status, batch_id),
            )

"""
core/db/queries/executions.py

All database reads and writes for the `executions` table.

Every run is additive — results are never overwritten. Re-running a test
adds a new row; it does not update the previous one. This preserves the
complete execution history every proposal carries.
"""

import json
import logging
from typing import Optional
from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def create(
    generation_id: int,
    result: str,
    output: Optional[str],
    duration_ms: Optional[int],
    screenshot_path: Optional[str],
    triggered_by: Optional[str],
    batch_id: Optional[int] = None,
    environment: Optional[str] = None,
    step_results: Optional[list] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Inserts a new execution result row.

    Args:
        generation_id: FK to generations.
        result: One of 'pass', 'fail', 'skip', 'error'.
        output: Full pytest output text.
        duration_ms: How long the execution took in milliseconds.
        screenshot_path: Path to a failure screenshot, or None.
        triggered_by: Who or what ran this execution.
        batch_id: FK to batches if this execution was part of a batch.
        environment: Which environment this ran against. "It passed" is
            not auditable without saying where.
        step_results: Per-step ledger from the run — what each numbered step
            did, when, how long it took and which screenshot evidences it.
            None for scripts generated before step recording existed, which
            correctly reads as "no step detail" rather than "no steps".

    Returns:
        The newly created execution row as a dict.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO executions
                    (generation_id, result, output, duration_ms,
                     screenshot_path, triggered_by, batch_id, environment,
                     step_results)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (generation_id, result, output, duration_ms,
                 screenshot_path, triggered_by, batch_id, environment,
                 json.dumps(step_results) if step_results else None),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            result_row = dict(zip(cols, row))
            logger.info(
                "Recorded execution id=%s generation=%s result=%s",
                result_row["id"], generation_id, result,
            )
            return result_row


def list_for_generation(generation_id: int) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Returns all execution history for one generation, newest first.

    Args:
        generation_id: FK to generations.

    Returns:
        List of execution dicts, ordered by executed_at descending.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT * FROM executions
                WHERE generation_id = %s
                ORDER BY executed_at DESC
                """,
                (generation_id,),
            )
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return [dict(zip(cols, row)) for row in cur.fetchall()]

"""Read-only, application-scoped captured maps for generation coverage."""

from core.db.connection import get_conn


def list_complete(application_id):
    with get_conn() as conn, conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute('''SELECT id, crawled_at, map_data
                       FROM application_maps
                       WHERE application_id=%s AND status='complete'
                       ORDER BY crawled_at DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC''', (application_id,))
        columns = [column[0] for column in cur.description]
        return [dict(zip(columns, row)) for row in cur.fetchall()]

FILE: backend/core/db/queries/generations.py
================================================
"""
core/db/queries/generations.py

All database reads and writes for the `generations` table.

Key design decisions:
    - script_content is the source of truth, not script_path.
      The file on disk is derived from the database. If the file is
      ever lost, regenerate it from script_content — never the reverse.
    - generation_status starts as 'running' at insert time and is
      updated to 'success' or 'incomplete' when the agent finishes.
      This means a crashed/interrupted generation is detectable —
      its row stays in 'running' state indefinitely, which is honest
      and recoverable, unlike leaving the column null.
"""

import json
import logging
from typing import Optional

from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def create(
    test_case_proposal_id: int,
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    triggered_by: Optional[str] = None,
    attempt_number: int = 1,
    app_map_id: Optional[int] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Inserts a new generation attempt row with generation_status='running'.

    Called at the START of a generation, before the agent runs. The row
    records that work is in progress. If the process crashes after this
    point, the row stays in 'running' state — detectable as an
    interrupted generation, not silently lost.

    Args:
        test_case_proposal_id: FK to test_case_proposals.
        provider: The LLM provider name, e.g. 'gemini', 'bedrock'.
        model: The exact model identifier used, e.g. 'gemini-2.5-flash'.
        triggered_by: Who or what started this — a person's name or
            'scheduled' for an unattended run. Nullable for MVP.
        attempt_number: Which attempt this is. 1 for first, 2 for a
            retry after a previous incomplete attempt, etc.

    Returns:
        The newly created generation row as a dict, including its id
        which the orchestrator uses to call complete() afterward.

    Raises:
        psycopg2.DatabaseError: On any database write failure.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO generations (
                    test_case_proposal_id,
                    provider,
                    model,
                    triggered_by,
                    attempt_number,
                    generation_status,
                    app_map_id
                )
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, 'running', %s)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (
                    test_case_proposal_id,
                    provider,
                    model,
                    triggered_by,
                    attempt_number,
                    app_map_id,
                ),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            result = dict(zip(cols, row))
            logger.info(
                "Started generation id=%s proposal=%s attempt=%s provider=%s",
                result["id"],
                test_case_proposal_id,
                attempt_number,
                provider,
            )
            return result


def complete(
    generation_id: int,
    generation_status: str,
    test_verdict: Optional[str],
    script_content: Optional[str],
    script_path: Optional[str],
    steps_taken: Optional[int],
    trace: Optional[dict],
    notes: Optional[str],
    *,
    replace_existing: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """
    Updates a generation row when the agent finishes — success or incomplete.

    Called at the END of a generation. Transitions generation_status from
    'running' to either 'success' or 'incomplete'.

    Args:
        generation_id: The generation's database ID, from create().
        generation_status: Final status — 'success' or 'incomplete'.
            'incomplete' means the agent gave up or an infrastructure
            error occurred. The compiled script will contain pytest.skip()
            rather than real assertions, so it never reports a false failure.
        test_verdict: 'pass', 'fail', or None. Only meaningful when
            generation_status='success'. Keeping these two columns separate
            prevents infrastructure failures from being reported as genuine
            test failures — a real bug caught during development.
        script_content: The full script text. This is the source of truth.
            script_path is derived from this, not the other way around.
        script_path: Path to the file written on disk for pytest to run.
        steps_taken: Number of agent loop iterations executed.
        trace: Full raw trace as a Python dict — stored as JSONB for
            audit and debugging. May be large.
        notes: Human-readable explanation of the outcome, especially
            useful when generation_status='incomplete'.
        replace_existing: Atomically retire prior usable scripts only after
            a successful replacement. Failed attempts preserve existing scripts.
            The parent proposal lock serializes replacements: the last successful
            completion wins, regardless of generation ID or start order.

    Returns:
        None

    Raises:
        psycopg2.DatabaseError: On any database write failure.
        ValueError: If a replacement is missing, no longer running/active,
            or has an invalid final status or missing successful script.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            if replace_existing:
                # Read the parent ID without locking the child. Every replacement
                # takes the parent lock FIRST, avoiding cross-attempt deadlocks.
                cur.execute(
                    "SELECT test_case_proposal_id FROM generations WHERE id = %s",
                    (generation_id,),
                )
                candidate = cur.fetchone()
                if not candidate:
                    raise ValueError("Replacement generation does not exist")
                proposal_id = candidate[0]
                cur.execute(
                    "SELECT id FROM test_case_proposals WHERE id = %s FOR UPDATE",
                    (proposal_id,),
                )
                if not cur.fetchone():
                    raise ValueError("Replacement proposal does not exist")
                cur.execute(
                    """SELECT generation_status, is_stale, superseded_by
                       FROM generations WHERE id = %s FOR UPDATE""",
                    (generation_id,),
                )
                candidate = cur.fetchone()
                if (not candidate or candidate[0] != "running"
                        or candidate[1] or candidate[2] is not None):
                    raise ValueError("Replacement generation is no longer running and active")
                if generation_status not in ("success", "incomplete"):
                    raise ValueError("Replacement requires a final generation status")
                if generation_status == "success" and (
                    not script_content or not script_content.strip()
                    or not script_path or not script_path.strip()
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Successful replacement requires script content and path")

            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE generations
                SET generation_status = %s,
                    test_verdict      = %s,
                    script_content    = %s,
                    script_path       = %s,
                    steps_taken       = %s,
                    trace             = %s,
                    notes             = %s,
                    completed_at      = now()
                WHERE id = %s
                """,
                (
                    generation_status,
                    test_verdict,
                    script_content,
                    script_path,
                    steps_taken,
                    json.dumps(trace) if trace else None,
                    notes,
                    generation_id,
                ),
            )
            if replace_existing:
                if generation_status == "success":
                    cur.execute(
                        """UPDATE generations SET is_stale = TRUE
                           WHERE test_case_proposal_id = %s AND id <> %s
                             AND generation_status = 'success'
                             AND is_stale = FALSE AND superseded_by IS NULL
                             AND BTRIM(script_content) <> ''
                             AND BTRIM(script_path) <> ''""",
                        (proposal_id, generation_id),
                    )
                # Include the newly completed row and any surviving valid script.
                # get_conn commits all writes together or rolls them all back.
                cur.execute(
                    """UPDATE test_case_proposals
                       SET status = CASE WHEN EXISTS (
                           SELECT 1 FROM generations
                           WHERE test_case_proposal_id = %s
                             AND generation_status = 'success'
                             AND is_stale = FALSE AND superseded_by IS NULL
                             AND BTRIM(script_content) <> ''
                             AND BTRIM(script_path) <> ''
                       ) THEN 'generated' ELSE 'queued' END
                       WHERE id = %s""",
                    (proposal_id, proposal_id),
                )
            logger.info(
                "Completed generation id=%s status=%s verdict=%s steps=%s",
                generation_id,
                generation_status,
                test_verdict,
                steps_taken,
            )


def get_latest_for_proposal(proposal_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Returns the most recent non-superseded generation for a proposal.

    Used by the orchestrator to check current state before deciding
    whether to regenerate or just re-execute an existing script.

    Args:
        proposal_id: FK to test_case_proposals.

    Returns:
        The latest generation as a dict, or None if no generation
        exists yet for this proposal.

    Raises:
        psycopg2.DatabaseError: On any database read failure.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT *
                FROM   generations
                WHERE  test_case_proposal_id = %s
                  AND  superseded_by IS NULL
                ORDER  BY attempt_number DESC
                LIMIT  1
                """,
                (proposal_id,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                logger.debug("No generation found for proposal id=%s", proposal_id)
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return dict(zip(cols, row))

"""
core/db/queries/healing.py

All database reads and writes for the `healing_proposals` table.
Healing proposals are never applied automatically — they always
require explicit human approval.
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional
from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def create(execution_id: int, old_selector: str, proposed_role: str,
           proposed_name: str, confidence: str, reasoning: str) -> dict:
    """
    Creates a new healing proposal from the Healer Agent's output.

    Args:
        execution_id: FK to executions (the failed run that triggered healing).
        old_selector: The CSS selector that stopped working.
        proposed_role: The role of the replacement element.
        proposed_name: The name/label of the replacement element.
        confidence: 'high', 'medium', or 'low'.
        reasoning: The agent's explanation for its proposal.

    Returns:
        The newly created healing_proposals row as a dict.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO healing_proposals
                    (execution_id, old_selector, proposed_role,
                     proposed_name, confidence, reasoning)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (execution_id, old_selector, proposed_role,
                 proposed_name, confidence, reasoning),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return dict(zip(cols, row))


def approve(proposal_id: int, decided_by: Optional[str]) -> None:
    """
    Marks a proposal as approved. The actual script patching is
    handled by the service layer after calling this.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE healing_proposals
                SET status = 'approved', decided_at = now(), decided_by = %s
                WHERE id = %s
                """,
                (decided_by, proposal_id),
            )


def reject(proposal_id: int, decided_by: Optional[str]) -> None:
    """Marks a proposal as rejected."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE healing_proposals
                SET status = 'rejected', decided_at = now(), decided_by = %s
                WHERE id = %s
                """,
                (decided_by, proposal_id),

"""
core/db/queries/proposals.py

All database reads and writes for the `test_case_proposals` table.
"""

import json
import logging
from typing import Optional
from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def create(
    application_id: int,
    title: str,
    description: str,
    source: str,
    test_type: str = "functional",
    category: Optional[str] = None,
    import_batch_id: Optional[int] = None,
    source_document_id: Optional[int] = None,
    steps: Optional[list] = None,
    derivation: Optional[str] = None,
    origin: Optional[str] = None,
    source_version: Optional[str] = None,
    source_updated_at: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Inserts a new test case proposal.

    Args:
        application_id: FK to applications.
        title: One-line scenario name.
        description: Full steps/content the Explorer Agent will carry out.
        source: One of 'author_agent', 'bulk_import', 'brd_frd'.
        test_type: Defaults to 'functional'.
        category: One of 'positive', 'negative', 'edge', 'boundary',
            'wrong_data', 'missing_field', 'security', or None.
        import_batch_id: FK to import_batches, if sourced from a file.
        source_document_id: FK to documents, if grounded in a BRD/FRD.
        steps: Optional structured steps, [{"n", "step", "expected",
            "matched", "element_hint"}]. When present, `description` must
            already be the flattened projection of it — see
            service.test_case_import.flatten_steps. None means a one-line
            test case, which is what every pre-006 row is.

    Returns:
        The newly created proposal as a dict.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO test_case_proposals
                    (application_id, title, description, source, test_type,
                     category, import_batch_id, source_document_id, steps,
                     derivation, origin, source_version, source_updated_at)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (application_id, title, description, source, test_type,
                 category, import_batch_id, source_document_id,
                 json.dumps(steps) if steps else None,
                 derivation, origin, source_version, source_updated_at),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            result = dict(zip(cols, row))
            logger.info(
                "Created proposal id=%s title=%s app=%s",
                result["id"], title, application_id,
            )
            return result


def list_for_application(application_id: int,
                         status_filter: Optional[str] = None) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Returns all proposals for an application, newest first.

    Args:
        application_id: FK to applications.
        status_filter: Optional status to filter by (e.g. 'generated').

    Returns:
        List of proposal dicts.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            if status_filter:
                cur.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT * FROM test_case_proposals
                    WHERE application_id = %s AND status = %s
                    ORDER BY created_at DESC
                    """,
                    (application_id, status_filter),
                )
            else:
                cur.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT * FROM test_case_proposals
                    WHERE application_id = %s AND status != 'archived'
                    ORDER BY created_at DESC
                    """,
                    (application_id,),
                )
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return [dict(zip(cols, row)) for row in cur.fetchall()]

    """

                """
                UPDATE test_case_proposals

                """,

            )
            logger.info("Proposal id=%s → status=%s", proposal_id, status)

            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE test_case_proposals

                """,
                (priority, proposal_id),
            )


def update_steps(proposal_id: int, steps: list, description: str,
                 edited_by: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Replace a test case's steps and re-derive its description, in one
    transaction, recording the change in proposal_edits.

    Two invariants live here:

    1. steps, description and tags.step_count are written TOGETHER. Both
       of the latter are projections of steps, so updating one without the
       others leaves the row saying two different things — and generation
       reads description, while list screens read step_count.
    2. the previous value is recorded first. An approved test case is the
       audit artefact; changing its steps after approval is exactly the
       event proposal_edits exists to capture, and until now nothing had
       ever written to that table.

    Args:
        proposal_id: The test case being edited.
        steps: The new steps, already validated and numbered by the caller.
        description: flatten_steps(steps) — passed in rather than computed
            here so the query layer keeps no opinion about the format.
        edited_by: Who made the change.

    Returns:
        The updated proposal row, or None if the id does not exist.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT steps FROM test_case_proposals WHERE id = %s",
                (proposal_id,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                logger.warning("Cannot edit steps: proposal id=%s not found", proposal_id)
                return None
            # description is not recorded: it is derived from steps, so the
            # steps before and after are the whole of the change.
            previous_steps = row[0]

            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO proposal_edits
                    (test_case_proposal_id, field_edited, previous_value,
                     new_value, edited_by)
                VALUES (%s, 'steps', %s, %s, %s)
                """,
                (
                    proposal_id,
                    # NOT NULL in the schema — a test case that had no steps
                    # before still needs an honest previous value.
                    json.dumps(previous_steps) if previous_steps else "[]",
                    json.dumps(steps),
                    edited_by,
                ),
            )

            cur.execute(
                """
                UPDATE test_case_proposals
                SET steps       = %s,
                    description = %s,
                    -- tags.step_count is a cached count that list screens
                    -- read instead of parsing the JSONB. It has to move with
                    -- the steps or it silently reports the old number.
                    tags        = jsonb_set(
                                      COALESCE(tags, '{}'::jsonb),
                                      '{step_count}',
                                      to_jsonb(%s::int)
                                  ),
                    updated_at  = now()
                WHERE id = %s
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (json.dumps(steps), description, len(steps), proposal_id),
            )
            updated = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]

    logger.info(
        "Proposal id=%s steps edited by %s (%d step(s), was %d)",
        proposal_id, edited_by or "unknown", len(steps),
        len(previous_steps or []),
    )
    return dict(zip(cols, updated))


def get(proposal_id: int):
    """
    Return one proposal by id, including its category and priority.
    Used by the scripts endpoint to show category/priority badges.
    """
    from core.db.connection import get_conn
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT * FROM test_case_proposals WHERE id = %s", (proposal_id,))
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if not row:
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return dict(zip(cols, row))

def get_ai_usage_summary(days: int, application_id: Optional[int] = None) -> dict:
    """
    Totals token usage and cost for each AI activity over the last `days` days,
    plus how many test cases were generated and how many tests were automated.
    Powers the dashboard's Tokens & Cost card.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            # Script calls are only counted when the script they belong to was generated successfully,
            # so the Tests automated row shows the tokens and cost of working tests only. Calls from
            # failed or incomplete scripts, and old calls not linked to a script, are left out.
            # Every other activity (test case generation, etc.) is counted as before.
            # unpriced_calls counts calls whose model had no price set.
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT c.purpose,
                       COUNT(*)                                     AS calls,
                       COALESCE(SUM(c.input_tokens), 0)             AS input_tokens,
                       COALESCE(SUM(c.output_tokens), 0)            AS output_tokens,
                       COALESCE(SUM(c.cost_usd), 0)                 AS cost_usd,
                       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT c.pricing_found)  AS unpriced_calls
                FROM ai_calls c
                LEFT JOIN generations g
                       ON c.purpose = 'script_generation' AND g.id = c.related_to_id
                WHERE c.called_at >= NOW() - make_interval(days => %s)
                  AND (%s::int IS NULL OR c.application_id = %s)
                  AND (c.purpose <> 'script_generation' OR g.generation_status = 'success')
                GROUP BY c.purpose
                ORDER BY c.purpose
                """,
                (days, application_id, application_id),
            )
            rows = cur.fetchall()

            # Test cases generated: how many test cases the survey runs in this period produced.
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT COALESCE(SUM(proposal_count), 0)
                FROM survey_runs
                WHERE created_at >= NOW() - make_interval(days => %s)
                  AND (%s::int IS NULL OR application_id = %s)
                """,
                (days, application_id, application_id),
            )
            test_cases_generated = int(cur.fetchone()[0])

            # Tests automated: test cases with a successfully generated script in this period.
            # A test case is counted once, however many times its script was regenerated.
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT g.test_case_proposal_id)
                FROM ai_calls c
                JOIN generations g ON g.id = c.related_to_id
                WHERE c.purpose = 'script_generation'
                  AND g.generation_status = 'success'
                  AND c.called_at >= NOW() - make_interval(days => %s)
                  AND (%s::int IS NULL OR c.application_id = %s)
                """,
                (days, application_id, application_id),
            )
            tests_automated = int(cur.fetchone()[0])

    # Cost is sent as a string so the exact Decimal value reaches the frontend unchanged.
    by_purpose = [
        {
            "purpose": r[0],
            "calls": r[1],
            "input_tokens": int(r[2]),
            "output_tokens": int(r[3]),
            "cost_usd": str(r[4]),
            "unpriced_calls": r[5],
        }
        for r in rows
    ]

    # Grand totals across all activities, for the card's Total row.
    totals = {
        "calls": sum(p["calls"] for p in by_purpose),
        "input_tokens": sum(p["input_tokens"] for p in by_purpose),
        "output_tokens": sum(p["output_tokens"] for p in by_purpose),
        "cost_usd": str(sum((Decimal(p["cost_usd"]) for p in by_purpose), Decimal("0"))),
        "unpriced_calls": sum(p["unpriced_calls"] for p in by_purpose),
    }
    return {
        "period_days": days,
        "application_id": application_id,
        "by_purpose": by_purpose,
        "totals": totals,
        "counts": {
            "test_cases_generated": test_cases_generated,
            "tests_automated": tests_automated,
        },
    }


def get_ai_cost_summary(application_id: int) -> dict:
    """Kept for existing callers. Returns all-time usage for one application."""
    return get_ai_usage_summary(days=3650, application_id=application_id)

FILE: backend/core/db/queries/users.py

"""
core/db/queries/users.py

All database reads and writes for the `users` table — the internal Kavach
user identity introduced in migration 016. One module per table: nothing
else touches `users` directly.

The `users` row is the stable, internal identity that every per-user feature
keys off (per-application ownership, access grants, and per-user application
credentials). It is intentionally decoupled from Microsoft Entra: the
`entra_object_id` column is the join point to Entra's stable "oid" claim, but
this module never talks to Entra itself.

DEV / INTERIM NOTE
    Until the Phase 1 backend token validation is in place, the only identity
    signal the backend receives is the caller's email (the `X-Triggered-By`
    header the frontend already stamps on every request). `get_or_create_by_
    email` therefore provisions a `users` row keyed on the email, storing the
    email itself in `entra_object_id` as a stable placeholder. When real Entra
    validation is wired up, the resolver in `auth/identity.py` will supply the
    genuine `oid` and this is the only module that needs to change — callers
    continue to receive an internal `users.id` exactly as they do today.
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional

from core.db.connection import get_conn

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def get_or_create_by_email(email: str, display_name: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
    """Return the internal `users` row for this email, creating it if needed.

    Keyed on `entra_object_id` so exactly one row ever exists per identity
    (the UNIQUE constraint enforces it via ON CONFLICT). In this interim
    phase the email doubles as the `entra_object_id`; see the module
    docstring.

    Never overwrites `is_admin` (that flag is managed manually in the DB per
    the Phase 2 Option C design) and never blanks an existing `display_name`.

    Args:
        email: The caller's email / UPN (from the identity header).
        display_name: Optional human-friendly name to seed on first sight.

    Returns:
        A dict with id, entra_object_id, email, display_name, is_admin.
    """
    normalized = (email or "").strip().lower()
    if not normalized:
        raise ValueError("email is required to resolve a user")

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO users (entra_object_id, email, display_name)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s)
                ON CONFLICT (entra_object_id) DO UPDATE
                    SET email        = EXCLUDED.email,
                        display_name = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.display_name, users.display_name),
                        updated_at   = now()
                RETURNING id, entra_object_id, email, display_name, is_admin
                """,
                (normalized, normalized, (display_name or "").strip() or None),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return dict(zip(cols, row))


def get_by_id(user_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Return a `users` row by its internal id, or None if it does not exist."""
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, entra_object_id, email, display_name, is_admin
                FROM users
                WHERE id = %s
                """,
                (user_id,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if row is None:
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return dict(zip(cols, row))


def get_by_email(email: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Return an EXISTING `users` row for this email, or None — never creates.

    Used on the run path (crawl/generation/execution) to map the initiator's
    email to their internal id WITHOUT provisioning a row: a run must never
    create users as a side effect. By the time a run uses a per-user
    credential, the user already exists (they created it by saving that
    credential through the Stage 2a route).

    Email is not unique at the schema level, so the lowest id is returned for
    determinism in the unlikely event of duplicates.
    """
    normalized = (email or "").strip().lower()
    if not normalized:
        return None
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, entra_object_id, email, display_name, is_admin
                FROM users
                WHERE email = %s
                ORDER BY id
                LIMIT 1
                """,
                (normalized,),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()
            if row is None:
                return None
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return dict(zip(cols, row))



================================================
FILE: backend/db/query.py
================================================
"""
db/query.py

Runs one ad-hoc SQL statement against the configured database and prints the
result as a simple table.

A development and verification convenience, not part of the application. It
exists so a schema check does not require psql on PATH or a fragile shell
one-liner, and so the connection details still come from one place
(core.settings) rather than being typed each time.

Usage (from the backend directory). Wrap the SQL in DOUBLE quotes so any
single quotes inside it survive PowerShell:

    python db/query.py "SELECT id, slug, status FROM help_articles ORDER BY id"
    python db/query.py "SELECT count(*) FROM help_chunks"

Reads only what you give it — it will happily run a write statement, so treat
it as you would a psql prompt.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse

# Make the backend package importable when this script is run directly.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import psycopg2  # noqa: E402

from core.settings import settings  # noqa: E402


def run(sql: str) -> None:
    """Execute one SQL statement and print any rows it returns.

    Args:
        sql: The SQL statement to execute.

    Raises:
        psycopg2.Error: If the statement fails. The error is printed plainly
            first so the cause is readable without a stack trace.
    """
    parsed = urlparse(settings.db.url)
    conn = psycopg2.connect(
        host=parsed.hostname,
        port=parsed.port or 5432,
        dbname=parsed.path.lstrip("/"),
        user=parsed.username,
        password=parsed.password,
    )
    try:
        with conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(sql)

                if cur.description is None:
                    print(f"OK ({cur.rowcount} row(s) affected)")
                    return

                cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
                rows = cur.fetchall()
                _print_table(cols, rows)
                print(f"\n({len(rows)} row(s))")
    except psycopg2.Error as e:
        print("FAILED")
        print(f"  {e.pgerror or e}".rstrip())
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


def _print_table(cols: list[str], rows: list[tuple]) -> None:
    """Print columns and rows aligned, truncating very wide values.

    Args:
        cols: Column names from the cursor description.
        rows: The fetched rows.
    """
    def cell(v) -> str:
        s = "NULL" if v is None else str(v)
        return s if len(s) <= 60 else s[:57] + "..."

    table = [cols] + [[cell(v) for v in r] for r in rows]
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in table) for i in range(len(cols))]

    print("  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(cols, widths)))
    print("  ".join("-" * w for w in widths))
    for r in table[1:]:
        print("  ".join(v.ljust(w) for v, w in zip(r, widths)))


def main() -> None:
    """Command-line entry point."""
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print('Usage: python db/query.py "SELECT ..."')
        sys.exit(2)

    try:
        run(" ".join(sys.argv[1:]))
    except Exception:
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()



================================================
FILE: backend/db/run_migration.py
================================================
"""
db/run_migration.py

Applies a .sql migration file to the configured database.

Exists because psql is not always on PATH on Windows, and because the
connection details should come from one place. The database URL is read from
core.settings (the single config entry point) — nothing is typed on the
command line and nothing is hardcoded here.

The whole file is sent as one statement to the server, so dollar-quoted
DO $$ ... $$ blocks and multi-statement migrations run exactly as psql would
run them. The migration is wrapped in a single transaction: if any statement
fails, nothing is applied and the database is left as it was.

Usage (from the backend directory):
    python db/run_migration.py db/migrations/012_help_and_support.sql
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse

# Make the backend package importable when this script is run directly.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import psycopg2  # noqa: E402

from core.settings import settings  # noqa: E402


def apply_migration(sql_path: Path) -> None:
    """Apply one .sql file to the configured database in a single transaction.

    Args:
        sql_path: Path to the .sql migration file to run.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the migration file does not exist.
        psycopg2.Error: If any statement in the migration fails. The
            transaction is rolled back before the error propagates, so a
            failed migration never leaves the schema half-applied.
    """
    if not sql_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Migration file not found: {sql_path}")

    sql = sql_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    # Explicit keyword arguments rather than the DSN string, for the same
    # reason core/db/connection.py does it: psycopg2 on Windows ignores the
    # host in a DSN and attempts a Unix socket connection.
    parsed = urlparse(settings.db.url)
    conn = psycopg2.connect(
        host=parsed.hostname,
        port=parsed.port or 5432,
        dbname=parsed.path.lstrip("/"),
        user=parsed.username,
        password=parsed.password,
    )

    print(f"Database : {parsed.path.lstrip('/')} on {parsed.hostname}:{parsed.port or 5432}")
    print(f"Migration: {sql_path.name}")

    try:
        with conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(sql)
        print("Applied successfully.")
    except psycopg2.Error as e:
        # psycopg2 puts the useful detail on the diagnostics object; print it
        # plainly so the failure is actionable rather than a stack trace.
        print("FAILED — nothing was applied.")
        print(f"  {e.pgerror or e}".rstrip())
        if getattr(e, "diag", None) and e.diag.message_detail:
            print(f"  detail: {e.diag.message_detail}")
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


def main() -> None:
    """Command-line entry point."""
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: python db/run_migration.py <path-to-.sql>")
        sys.exit(2)

    try:
        apply_migration(Path(sys.argv[1]))
    except Exception:
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
