-- NextGen2 Database Schema
-- Run once to initialise:
--   psql -U postgres -d nextgen2 -f db/schema.sql

-- Internal Kavach users mapped to Microsoft Entra object IDs.
-- is_admin is managed in the database; access enforcement lives in application code.
CREATE TABLE users (
    id                SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    entra_object_id   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    email             TEXT NOT NULL,
    display_name      TEXT,
    is_admin          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per application under test.
CREATE TABLE applications (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name            TEXT NOT NULL,
    base_url        TEXT,
    requires_sso_gateway BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    normalized_url  TEXT UNIQUE,
    owner           TEXT,
    -- Nullable until assigned; the existing owner text remains informational.
    owner_user_id   INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),
    is_archived     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Per-application, per-user permission grants. Matches migration 016.
CREATE TABLE application_access (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    can_view        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    can_edit        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    can_run         BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    can_schedule    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    can_delete      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    granted_by      INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),
    granted_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, user_id)
);

-- Per-user application login credentials. Matches migration 017.
-- One credential row per (application, user); the password is encrypted at
-- rest with Fernet using TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY (never stored in plaintext).
CREATE TABLE app_credentials (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    username        TEXT NOT NULL,
    secret_alg      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'fernet',
    secret_cipher   TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, user_id)
);

-- App Map: persistent record of every page and interactive element crawled
-- from an application session (authenticated or not).
-- One row per crawl run. Old rows are kept for audit history.
CREATE TABLE application_maps (
    id                SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    crawled_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    page_count        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    element_count     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    map_data          JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    -- True if the crawl authenticated (elements behind login wall are included).
    was_authenticated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    -- 'running' while in progress; 'complete'; 'failed'.
    status            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'complete'
                          CHECK (status IN ('running', 'complete', 'failed')),
    error_message     TEXT
);

-- Stores uploaded documents: BRD/FRD requirements, existing test case files,
-- and knowledge base standards. Keeps both original file and extracted text.
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id     INTEGER REFERENCES applications(id),
    document_type      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (document_type IN ('requirements', 'existing_test_cases', 'standard', 'training')),
    original_filename  TEXT NOT NULL,
    storage_path       TEXT NOT NULL,
    extracted_text     TEXT,
    -- Which requirements a survey read and which produced no test case.
    -- Append-only: see 006_test_case_steps.sql.
    requirement_index  JSONB,
    uploaded_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per file-upload import operation.
CREATE TABLE import_batches (
    id                  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    document_id         INTEGER REFERENCES documents(id),
    file_name           TEXT NOT NULL,
    file_type           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (file_type IN ('csv', 'xlsx', 'json')),
    imported_row_count  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    status              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'completed'
                            CHECK (status IN ('completed', 'partial_failure', 'failed')),
    imported_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per proposed test scenario.
CREATE TABLE test_case_proposals (
    id                  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    import_batch_id     INTEGER REFERENCES import_batches(id),
    source_document_id  INTEGER REFERENCES documents(id),
    title               TEXT NOT NULL,
    description         TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- Structured steps: [{"n":1,"step":...,"expected":...,"matched":bool}]
    -- description is a flattened projection of this when it is non-null.
    -- NULL means a one-line test case, which is what all pre-006 rows are.
    steps               JSONB,
    test_type           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'functional',
    category            TEXT CHECK (category IN ('positive', 'negative', 'edge', 'boundary', 'wrong_data', 'missing_field', 'security', NULL)),
    source              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('author_agent', 'bulk_import', 'brd_frd')),
    priority            TEXT CHECK (priority IN ('P0', 'P1', 'P2', 'P3', 'P4', NULL)),
    derivation          TEXT CHECK (derivation IN ('stated', 'inferred') OR derivation IS NULL),
    origin              TEXT CHECK (origin IN ('brd', 'crawl', 'jira', 'alm') OR origin IS NULL),
    source_version      TEXT,
    source_updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    source_sync_status  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'current'
                            CHECK (source_sync_status IN ('current', 'requirement_changed', 'requirement_deleted')),
    tags                JSONB,
    should_automate     BOOLEAN,
    status              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'proposed'
                            CHECK (status IN ('proposed', 'queued', 'generating', 'generated', 'stale', 'manual_only', 'archived')),
    raw_import_row      JSONB,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Version history for edits to a scenario's text.
CREATE TABLE proposal_edits (
    id                      SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    test_case_proposal_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES test_case_proposals(id),
    field_edited            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (field_edited IN ('title', 'description', 'steps')),
    previous_value          TEXT NOT NULL,
    new_value               TEXT NOT NULL,
    edited_at               TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    edited_by               TEXT
);

-- One row per automation attempt for a proposal.
-- script_content is the source of truth — script_path is derived from it.
CREATE TABLE generations (
    id                      SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    test_case_proposal_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES test_case_proposals(id),
    attempt_number          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    provider                TEXT NOT NULL,
    model                   TEXT NOT NULL,
    triggered_by            TEXT,
    -- 'running' is written at insert time, before the agent runs, so an
    -- interrupted generation stays detectable rather than absent.
    generation_status       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (generation_status IN ('running', 'success', 'incomplete')),
    test_verdict            TEXT CHECK (test_verdict IN ('pass', 'fail', NULL)),
    script_content          TEXT,
    script_path             TEXT,
    steps_taken             INTEGER,
    trace                   JSONB,
    -- Which numbered test-case step each pytest block implements, so
    -- per-step screenshots attach to the step they evidence.
    step_map                JSONB,
    notes                   TEXT,
    is_stale                BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    is_manually_edited      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    edited_by               TEXT,
    edited_at               TIMESTAMPTZ,
    superseded_by           INTEGER REFERENCES generations(id),
    -- Which App Map snapshot was current when this script was generated.
    -- NULL for generations that pre-date this column or that fell back to
    -- live-page extraction (no crawled map existed for the app).
    -- The healer uses this to retrieve the before-state and compare with
    -- the current snapshot when proposing a selector replacement.
    app_map_id              INTEGER REFERENCES application_maps(id),
    started_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    completed_at            TIMESTAMPTZ
);

-- One row per batch run.
CREATE TABLE batches (
    id                  SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    environment         TEXT NOT NULL,
    triggered_by        TEXT,
    trigger_type        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (trigger_type IN ('manual', 'scheduled')),
    status              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running' CHECK (status IN ('running', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled')),
    notification_sent   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    started_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    completed_at        TIMESTAMPTZ
);

-- One row per actual test run.
CREATE TABLE executions (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    generation_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES generations(id),
    batch_id        INTEGER REFERENCES batches(id),
    suite_id        INTEGER,
    triggered_by    TEXT,
    environment     TEXT,
    result          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (result IN ('pass', 'fail', 'skip', 'error')),
    output          TEXT,
    screenshot_path TEXT,
    -- Per-step ledger for the run: what each numbered step did, when, how
    -- long it took and which screenshot evidences it. NULL for runs that
    -- predate step-level recording. See 007_execution_step_results.sql.
    step_results    JSONB,
    duration_ms     INTEGER,
    executed_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per AI-proposed fix for a broken test.
CREATE TABLE healing_proposals (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    execution_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES executions(id),
    old_selector    TEXT NOT NULL,
    proposed_role   TEXT NOT NULL,
    proposed_name   TEXT NOT NULL,
    confidence      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (confidence IN ('high', 'medium', 'low')),
    reasoning       TEXT NOT NULL,
    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'superseded')),
    proposed_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    decided_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    decided_by      TEXT
);

-- One row per LLM API call, for cost and performance tracking.
CREATE TABLE ai_calls (
    id                SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    related_to_type   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (related_to_type IN ('survey', 'generation', 'heal')),
    related_to_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    provider          TEXT NOT NULL,
    model             TEXT NOT NULL,
    input_tokens      INTEGER,
    output_tokens     INTEGER,
    cost_usd          NUMERIC(10, 6),
    latency_ms        INTEGER,
    called_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One or more test datasets per scenario.
CREATE TABLE proposal_data_sets (
    id                      SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    test_case_proposal_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES test_case_proposals(id),
    data                    JSONB NOT NULL,
    tried                   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    result                  TEXT CHECK (result IN ('pass', 'fail', NULL)),
    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Per-application execution environments (dev/test/stage/prod).
CREATE TABLE application_environments (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    name            TEXT NOT NULL,
    base_url        TEXT NOT NULL,
    is_default      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    notes           TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, name)
);

-- Named sets of test cases (smoke/regression/custom).
CREATE TABLE test_suites (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    name            TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'custom'
                    CHECK (kind IN ('smoke', 'regression', 'custom')),
    description     TEXT,
    created_by      TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, name)
);

CREATE TABLE test_suite_members (
    suite_id                INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES test_suites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    test_case_proposal_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES test_case_proposals(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    added_at                TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (suite_id, test_case_proposal_id)
);

-- Scheduled suite runs and periodic jobs.
CREATE TABLE schedules (
    id                SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    suite_id          INTEGER REFERENCES test_suites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name              TEXT NOT NULL,
    frequency         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'daily'
                      CHECK (frequency IN ('once', 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekdays', 'weekly')),
    run_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    next_run_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    environment       TEXT,
    webhook_url       TEXT,
    recipients        TEXT,
    enabled           BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    last_run_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    last_status       TEXT,
    last_summary      JSONB,
    job_type          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'suite_run'
                      CHECK (job_type IN ('suite_run', 'jira_sync')),
    jira_project_key  TEXT,
    created_by        TEXT,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CHECK (job_type <> 'jira_sync' OR jira_project_key IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE schedule_runs (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    schedule_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES schedules(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    started_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    total           INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    passed          INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    failed          INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    skipped         INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    triggered_by    TEXT DEFAULT 'scheduler',
    webhook_status  TEXT,
    summary         JSONB
);

-- Jira sync cursor per application/project.
CREATE TABLE jira_sync_state (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER REFERENCES applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    project_key     TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_synced_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, project_key)
);

-- Versioned help content.
CREATE TABLE help_articles (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    slug            TEXT NOT NULL,
    title           TEXT NOT NULL,
    category        TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary         TEXT,
    body_md         TEXT NOT NULL,
    version         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
                    CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'approved', 'retired')),
    author          TEXT,
    approved_by     TEXT,
    approved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    effective_from  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    sort_order      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,
    is_stale        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    superseded_by   INTEGER REFERENCES help_articles(id),
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Searchable passages from help content and training docs.
CREATE TABLE help_chunks (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    source_type     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source_type IN ('article', 'training_doc')),
    article_id      INTEGER REFERENCES help_articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    document_id     INTEGER REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    chunk_index     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    heading         TEXT,
    body            TEXT NOT NULL,
    search_vector   tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
                      to_tsvector('english'::regconfig,
                          coalesce(heading, '') || ' ' || coalesce(body, ''))
                    ) STORED,
    is_stale        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    CHECK (
        (source_type = 'article' AND article_id IS NOT NULL AND document_id IS NULL)
        OR
        (source_type = 'training_doc' AND document_id IS NOT NULL AND article_id IS NULL)
    )
);

-- Read/ack evidence for help/training.
CREATE TABLE help_views (
    id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    article_id         INTEGER REFERENCES help_articles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    document_id        INTEGER REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    article_version    INTEGER,
    viewed_by          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anonymous',
    viewed_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    acknowledged       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    acknowledged_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    CHECK (
        (article_id IS NOT NULL AND document_id IS NULL)
        OR
        (document_id IS NOT NULL AND article_id IS NULL)
    )
);

-- Provider-agnostic local mirror of support tickets.
CREATE TABLE support_tickets (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    provider        TEXT NOT NULL,
    external_ref    TEXT,
    external_url    TEXT,
    raised_by       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anonymous',
    category        TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary         TEXT NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT,
    context         JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'
                    CHECK (status IN ('open', 'submitted', 'failed', 'resolved', 'closed')),
    external_status TEXT,
    last_synced_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    submit_error    TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Search queries that returned no useful help results.
CREATE TABLE help_search_misses (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    query           TEXT NOT NULL,
    source          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'help_search'
                    CHECK (source IN ('help_search', 'chat')),
    result_count    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    asked_by        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anonymous',
    asked_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

ALTER TABLE executions
    ADD CONSTRAINT executions_suite_id_fkey
    FOREIGN KEY (suite_id) REFERENCES test_suites(id);

FILE: backend/db/seed_database.py
================================================
"""
seed_database.py

Populates the database with demo data for the NextGen2 dashboard.

WHY THIS EXISTS (read before editing):
This is NOT throwaway code. The demo data lives in seed_data.json — a
plain, editable file. This script reads that JSON and inserts it into
Postgres using the real schema. To change what apps/scenarios appear,
edit seed_data.json ONLY. Never hardcode data in components or here.

Baxter developers can:
  - edit seed_data.json to add real apps/scenarios
  - re-run this script any time to reset demo data
  - delete it entirely for production — nothing depends on it

It inserts a full, realistic chain per app:
  application -> proposals (scenarios) -> generations -> a batch ->
  executions (pass/fail history), so coverage %, pass rates, the trend
  chart and the donut all populate.

Usage (from the backend folder, with .env configured):
    python seed_database.py
    python seed_database.py --reset      # wipe seeded data first
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import random
from pathlib import Path

import psycopg2
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()

DATA_FILE = Path(__file__).parent / "seed_data.json"


def get_conn():
    url = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL")
    if not url:
        print("ERROR: DATABASE_URL not set (check your .env).")
        sys.exit(1)
    return psycopg2.connect(url)


def reset(cur):
    """Remove previously seeded rows (keeps schema intact)."""
    # Order matters for FKs: executions -> batches/generations -> proposals -> apps
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM executions")
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM batches")
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM generations")
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM test_case_proposals")
    cur.execute("DELETE FROM applications")
    print("  Cleared existing data.")


def normalize(url: str) -> str:
    return (url or "").replace("https://", "").replace("http://", "").rstrip("/")


def seed(cur, data: dict):
    apps = data["applications"]
    total_scen = total_exec = 0

    for app in apps:
        # 1. application
        cur.execute(
            """INSERT INTO applications (name, base_url, normalized_url, owner)
               VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s) RETURNING id""",
            (app["name"], app["base_url"], normalize(app["base_url"]), app["owner"]),
        )
        app_id = cur.fetchone()[0]

        # 2. one batch per app (a run grouping)
        cur.execute(
            """INSERT INTO batches (application_id, environment, trigger_type, status, completed_at)
               VALUES (%s, %s, 'manual', 'completed', now() - (random() * interval '3 days'))
               RETURNING id""",
            (app_id, app.get("environment", "default")),
        )
        batch_id = cur.fetchone()[0]

        for scen in app["scenarios"]:
            # 3. proposal (scenario)
            cur.execute(
                """INSERT INTO test_case_proposals
                   (application_id, title, description, test_type, category, source, priority, should_automate, status)
                   VALUES (%s, %s, %s, 'functional', %s, 'author_agent', %s, TRUE, %s)
                   RETURNING id""",
                (app_id, scen["title"], scen["title"], scen.get("category"),
                 scen.get("priority"), scen["status"]),
            )
            proposal_id = cur.fetchone()[0]
            total_scen += 1

            # 4. generation + execution only for 'generated' scenarios
            if scen["status"] == "generated":
                verdict = scen.get("verdict") or "pass"
                cur.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO generations
                       (test_case_proposal_id, provider, model, generation_status, test_verdict,
                        script_content, script_path, steps_taken, completed_at)
                       VALUES (%s, 'simulation', 'sim-1.0', 'success', %s, %s, %s, %s,
                               now() - (random() * interval '3 days'))
                       RETURNING id""",
                    (proposal_id, verdict,
                     f"# Simulated pytest+selenium script for: {scen['title']}",
                     f"generated_tests/test_{proposal_id}.py",
                     random.randint(5, 14)),
                )
                gen_id = cur.fetchone()[0]

                cur.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO executions
                       (generation_id, batch_id, result, output, duration_ms, executed_at)
                       VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, now() - (random() * interval '3 days'))""",
                    (gen_id, batch_id, verdict,
                     f"Simulated run output for {scen['title']}",
                     random.randint(1200, 7000)),
                )
                total_exec += 1

        print(f"  {app['name']}: {len(app['scenarios'])} scenarios inserted.")

    return len(apps), total_scen, total_exec


def main():
    do_reset = "--reset" in sys.argv
    data = json.loads(DATA_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    conn = get_conn()
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            if do_reset:
                reset(cur)
            n_apps, n_scen, n_exec = seed(cur, data)
        conn.commit()
        print(f"\nDone. Seeded {n_apps} applications, {n_scen} scenarios, {n_exec} executions.")
        print("Refresh the dashboard to see them.")
    except psycopg2.Error as e:
        conn.rollback()
        print(f"\nDatabase error: {e}")
        print("If it's a duplicate error, run:  python seed_database.py --reset")
        sys.exit(1)
    finally:
        conn.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()



================================================
FILE: backend/db/seed_help.py
================================================
"""
db/seed_help.py

Loads the authored help articles from markdown files into the database.

Article text lives in backend/content/help/*.md, not in Python and not typed
into a screen. Three reasons:

  - It is reviewable. A change to help content shows up as a diff.
  - It is re-runnable. Seeding is idempotent: unchanged content produces no
    new version, so running this script does not invalidate training records.
  - It separates authoring from approval. Seeding creates drafts; a person
    approves them. That gate is the point, not an obstacle to route around.

Each file begins with YAML front matter between --- markers:

    ---
    slug: scheduling-runs
    title: Scheduling runs
    category: Running tests
    summary: Running suites unattended
    sort_order: 10
    ---

    # markdown body follows

Usage, from the backend directory:

    python db/seed_help.py                      # load as drafts
    python db/seed_help.py --approve ""         # load and approve
    python db/seed_help.py --dry-run            # report, change nothing
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

# Make the backend package importable when run directly.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from core.db.connection import init_pool  # noqa: E402
from core.settings import settings  # noqa: E402
from service import help_service  # noqa: E402


REQUIRED = ("slug", "title", "category")


def parse_article(path: Path) -> dict:
    """Read one markdown file and split its front matter from its body.

    Args:
        path: Path to the .md file.

    Returns:
        A dict of the front-matter fields plus 'body_md'.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the front matter is missing, malformed, or lacks a
            required field. Failing loudly is deliberate — a silently skipped
            article is a gap nobody notices until a user cannot find it.
    """
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    if not raw.lstrip().startswith("---"):
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: missing YAML front matter")

    stripped = raw.lstrip()
    parts = stripped.split("---", 2)
    if len(parts) < 3:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: front matter is not closed with ---")

    meta = yaml.safe_load(parts[1]) or {}
    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: front matter is not a mapping")

    missing = [f for f in REQUIRED if not meta.get(f)]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: front matter missing {', '.join(missing)}")

    body = parts[2].strip()
    if not body:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: body is empty")

    meta["body_md"] = body
    return meta


def main() -> int:
    """Load every article file and report what changed.

    Returns:
        0 on success, 1 if any file could not be read.
    """
    approve_as = None
    if "--approve" in sys.argv:
        i = sys.argv.index("--approve")
        if i + 1 >= len(sys.argv):
            print('Usage: python db/seed_help.py --approve "Your Name"')
            return 1
        approve_as = sys.argv[i + 1]
    dry_run = "--dry-run" in sys.argv

    content_dir = Path(settings.help.content_dir)
    if not content_dir.is_absolute():
        content_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / content_dir

    if not content_dir.exists():
        print(f"No help content directory at {content_dir}")
        return 1

    files = sorted(content_dir.glob("*.md"))
    if not files:
        print(f"No .md files found in {content_dir}")
        return 1

    print(f"Content: {content_dir}")
    print(f"Files  : {len(files)}")
    print(f"Mode   : {'dry run' if dry_run else 'seeding'}"
          f"{f', approving as {approve_as}' if approve_as else ', as drafts'}\n")

    init_pool()

    created = versioned = unchanged = 0
    errors: list[str] = []

    for path in files:
        try:
            meta = parse_article(path)
        except ValueError as e:
            errors.append(str(e))
            print(f"  ERROR    {path.name}: {e}")
            continue

        if dry_run:
            print(f"  would load {meta['slug']}  ({meta['category']})")
            continue

        before = help_service.get_article(meta["slug"], include_drafts=True)
        article = help_service.upsert_article(
            slug=meta["slug"],
            title=meta["title"],
            category=meta["category"],
            body_md=meta["body_md"],
            summary=meta.get("summary"),
            author=meta.get("author", "NextGen2 team"),
            status=meta.get("status", "draft"),
            sort_order=int(meta.get("sort_order", 100)),
        )

        if before is None:
            created += 1
            state = f"created  v{article['version']}"
        elif before["id"] == article["id"]:
            unchanged += 1
            state = f"unchanged v{article['version']}"
        else:
            versioned += 1
            state = f"updated  v{article['version']} (was v{before['version']})"

        if approve_as and article["status"] != "approved":
            help_service.approve_article(article["id"], approved_by=approve_as)
            state += ", approved"

        print(f"  {state:28} {meta['slug']}")

    if dry_run:
        print("\nDry run — nothing was written.")
        return 0

    print(f"\n{created} created, {versioned} updated, {unchanged} unchanged.")

    if not approve_as:
        print(
            "\nArticles were loaded as DRAFTS. NextGen2 AI will not cite a draft "
            "and it does not count as training material.\n"
            'Approve them with: python db/seed_help.py --approve "Your Name"'
        )

    if errors:
        print(f"\n{len(errors)} file(s) could not be read.")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FILE: backend/db/migrations/002_environments.sql

-- 002_environments.sql
--
-- Applications are tested against several environments (dev, test, stage,
-- production). A test case must not know which one — it is written once and
-- run anywhere — so the URL belongs to the environment, not the test.
--
-- Purely additive: no existing column changes, no data migration needed.
-- Applications that already have a base_url are given a "default"
-- environment from it, so nothing breaks.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS application_environments (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    name            TEXT NOT NULL,
    base_url        TEXT NOT NULL,
    is_default      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    notes           TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, name)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_app_env_application
    ON application_environments (application_id);

-- Which environment a run actually used. "This test passed" means nothing
-- without it, and an auditor will ask.
ALTER TABLE executions
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS environment TEXT;

-- Seed a default environment for every application that already has a URL.
INSERT INTO application_environments (application_id, name, base_url, is_default)
SELECT a.id, 'default', a.base_url, TRUE
FROM applications a
WHERE a.base_url IS NOT NULL
  AND a.base_url <> ''
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM application_environments e WHERE e.application_id = a.id
  );

FILE: backend/db/migrations/003_suites.sql
================================================
-- 003_suites.sql
--
-- Test suites: a named, curated selection of existing test cases.
--
-- A suite is NOT a new set of tests. "Smoke" and "regression" are not kinds
-- of test — they are decisions about WHICH tests to run and when:
--
--   smoke       is this build worth testing?   a handful, minutes, every build
--   regression  did anything break?            everything, nightly
--
-- The same test case belongs in both, so membership is many-to-many. That is
-- why a single test_type column could not express it.
--
-- Additive: nothing existing is changed.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_suites (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    name            TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'custom'
                    CHECK (kind IN ('smoke', 'regression', 'custom')),
    description     TEXT,
    created_by      TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, name)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_suite_members (
    suite_id                INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES test_suites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    test_case_proposal_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES test_case_proposals(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    added_at                TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (suite_id, test_case_proposal_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_suite_application ON test_suites (application_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_suite_members_suite ON test_suite_members (suite_id);

-- Which suite a run belonged to, so results can be reported per suite.
ALTER TABLE executions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS suite_id INTEGER REFERENCES test_suites(id);



================================================
FILE: backend/db/migrations/004_schedules.sql
================================================
-- 004_schedules.sql
--
-- Scheduled suite runs, and a record of each one.
--
-- next_run_at is stored rather than computed on the fly so the UI can show a
-- live countdown and the scheduler can find due work with a single indexed
-- query instead of evaluating every schedule every tick.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schedules (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    suite_id        INTEGER REFERENCES test_suites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name            TEXT NOT NULL,

    -- 'once' fires a single time, which is what you want when demonstrating
    -- it live; the recurring options are the real-world use.
    frequency       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'daily'
                    CHECK (frequency IN ('once', 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekdays', 'weekly')),
    run_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,        -- first/next occurrence
    next_run_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,                 -- NULL once a 'once' schedule has fired

    environment     TEXT,
    webhook_url     TEXT,                        -- posted to on completion (n8n)
    recipients      TEXT,                        -- informational; n8n decides delivery
    enabled         BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,

    last_run_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    last_status     TEXT,
    last_summary    JSONB,

    created_by      TEXT,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_schedules_due
    ON schedules (enabled, next_run_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schedule_runs (
    id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    schedule_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES schedules(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    started_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    finished_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    total         INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    passed        INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    failed        INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    skipped       INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    triggered_by  TEXT DEFAULT 'scheduler',
    webhook_status TEXT,
    summary       JSONB
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_schedule_runs ON schedule_runs (schedule_id, started_at DESC);

FILE: backend/db/migrations/005_generation_status.sql
================================================
-- 005_generation_status.sql
--
-- generations.generation_status is written THREE times in a row's life, not
-- two. core/db/queries/generations.py inserts 'running' at the START of a
-- generation, before the agent runs, so a process that dies mid-way leaves a
-- row that is detectably interrupted rather than silently missing. Only later
-- does complete() move it to 'success' or 'incomplete'.
--
-- The original CHECK allowed only the two end states, so every insert failed
-- on a database built from schema.sql. This widens it to the set the code
-- actually writes.
--
-- Purely additive: the new set is a superset of the old one, so no existing
-- row can violate it and no data migration is needed.

ALTER TABLE generations
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS generations_generation_status_check;

ALTER TABLE generations
    ADD CONSTRAINT generations_generation_status_check
    CHECK (generation_status IN ('running', 'success', 'incomplete'));



================================================
FILE: backend/db/migrations/006_test_case_steps.sql
================================================
-- 006_test_case_steps.sql
--
-- A test case is a title AND the steps that carry it out. Until now the only
-- place steps existed was as flattened text inside description, produced by
-- the spreadsheet importer (service/test_case_import.py). The script
-- generator reads description, so that flattening stays — but the structured
-- form has to live somewhere it can be edited, exported and traced back to a
-- requirement.
--
-- Purely additive:
--   * every new column is NULLABLE with no default, so Postgres adds a
--     catalog entry and rewrites no rows. Existing rows keep their exact
--     current meaning: steps IS NULL means "one-line test case", which is
--     precisely what they are.
--   * the widened CHECK is a strict superset of the old one, so no existing
--     row can violate it — the same reasoning as 005_generation_status.sql.
--
-- Nothing is deleted, rewritten or backfilled.

-- The structured source of truth for a test case's steps.
--   [{"n": 1, "step": "Click Settings", "expected": "The menu opens",
--     "matched": true, "element_hint": "aria-label='Settings'"}]
-- description is DERIVED from this (flattened) whenever it is non-null, and
-- must never be edited independently of it.
ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS steps JSONB;

-- Which numbered step each part of the generated pytest file implements, so
-- a per-step screenshot can be attached to the step it is evidence for.
--   {"1": {"label": "open_settings", "screenshot_prefix": "step_01"}}
-- Deliberately NOT folded into generations.trace: trace is the Explorer
-- Agent's raw audit record and means something different.
ALTER TABLE generations
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS step_map JSONB;

-- Which requirements a survey read, and which produced no test case at all.
-- Append-only array of runs: a regulated environment cannot have the previous
-- run's coverage gap silently overwritten by the next one.
--   {"runs": [{"at": "...", "requirements": ["NET-020"],
--              "zero_coverage": ["NET-031"], "chunks": 12,
--              "not_surveyed": ["NET-044"]}]}
ALTER TABLE documents
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS requirement_index JSONB;

-- proposal_edits can now record a step edit. The table has existed since the
-- first schema but has never been written to — only deleted from. "Who
-- changed step 3, and when" is exactly the question it was created to answer.
ALTER TABLE proposal_edits
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS proposal_edits_field_edited_check;

ALTER TABLE proposal_edits
    ADD CONSTRAINT proposal_edits_field_edited_check
    CHECK (field_edited IN ('title', 'description', 'steps'));

-- Find the test cases that carry structure without scanning every row.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_proposals_with_steps
    ON test_case_proposals (application_id)
    WHERE steps IS NOT NULL;

FILE: backend/db/migrations/007_execution_step_results.sql
================================================
-- 007_execution_step_results.sql
--
-- Per-step results for a run.
--
-- Until now an execution recorded one verdict and a folder of screenshots.
-- That answers "did it pass" but not "which step failed, when, and what did
-- the screen look like at that moment" — which is the question actually
-- asked when a nightly run goes red, and the one an auditor asks about a
-- test case that has approved steps.
--
--   [{"n": 1, "action": "Click the Login button",
--     "expected": "The catalogue opens", "status": "pass",
--     "started_at": "2026-07-29T14:22:07+05:30", "duration_ms": 412,
--     "screenshot": "step_01_Click_the_Login_button.png", "error": ""}]
--
-- status is one of: pass, fail, not_automated, running. 'running' survives
-- in the ledger when a run is killed mid-step, which is honest and tells you
-- exactly where it stopped.
--
-- Purely additive: one nullable column, no default, no backfill. Existing
-- executions keep step_results NULL, which correctly means "this run predates
-- step-level recording" rather than "this run had no steps".

ALTER TABLE executions
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS step_results JSONB;

-- Find runs that carry step detail without scanning the whole table.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_executions_with_steps
    ON executions (generation_id)
    WHERE step_results IS NOT NULL;



================================================
FILE: backend/db/migrations/008_test_case_provenance.sql
================================================
-- 008_test_case_provenance.sql
--
-- Traceability metadata for a test case: WHERE it came from, and WHETHER a
-- human/document specified it or the AI reasoned it. In a regulated context an
-- auditor asks exactly this — "this test, who or what authored it, and what
-- did it derive from" — so it has to be stored on the record, not inferred.
--
-- Note on naming: the existing `source` column already means the INTERNAL
-- producer ('author_agent' | 'bulk_import' | 'brd_frd') and is left untouched.
-- `origin` is the REAL-WORLD provenance (a BRD document, a crawl, a Jira
-- story, an ALM record). Two different concepts, two columns — overloading
-- `source` would break its CHECK and conflate the two meanings.
--
-- Purely additive, same reasoning as 006:
--   * every new column is NULLABLE with no default, so Postgres adds a catalog
--     entry and rewrites no rows. Existing rows keep their exact meaning
--     (NULL derivation/origin = "recorded before provenance was tracked").
--   * the CHECKs allow NULL, so no existing row can violate them.
--
-- Nothing is deleted, rewritten or backfilled. created_at / updated_at already
-- exist and are reused as generated-at / last-updated — no new timestamp
-- columns are added.

-- Did the requirement STATE this case, or did the model REASON it?
--   'stated'   — written in the requirement text or its acceptance criterion.
--   'inferred' — the AI derived it from the behaviour type; the document did
--                not spell it out. This is the governance flag: it lets a
--                human see, and reject, the AI's guesses.
ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS derivation TEXT;

ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS test_case_proposals_derivation_check;

ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD CONSTRAINT test_case_proposals_derivation_check
    CHECK (derivation IN ('stated', 'inferred') OR derivation IS NULL);

-- The real-world artifact this test case traces back to. 'brd' today; the
-- other values become live as their source adapters are built.
ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS origin TEXT;

ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS test_case_proposals_origin_check;

ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD CONSTRAINT test_case_proposals_origin_check
    CHECK (origin IN ('brd', 'crawl', 'jira', 'alm') OR origin IS NULL);

-- Which version of the source this was generated from — a BRD version string
-- ("v0.9"), a document hash, or a Jira story version. NULL when unknown.
-- Sources change over time; without this you cannot tell whether a test was
-- generated from the current requirement or a superseded one.
ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_version TEXT;

FILE: backend/db/migrations/009_source_updated_at.sql
================================================
-- 009_source_updated_at.sql
--
-- Adds source_updated_at to test_case_proposals.
--
-- For a Jira-sourced test case, this stores the Jira issue's own `updated`
-- timestamp AT THE MOMENT the test case was generated from it. It is the
-- anchor for change-detection: a scheduled poll (Stage 3) compares the Jira
-- issue's current `updated` against this value — if Jira's is newer, the
-- requirement changed after the test was written, and the linked test cases
-- are flagged for human re-review (never auto-regenerated, per GxP).
--
-- NULL for BRD/crawl-sourced rows, and for every pre-009 row — the column is
-- additive and nullable, so it does not touch existing data.
--
-- Deliberately a separate column from source_version: source_version means
-- "which revision of the source spec" (e.g. a BRD "v2.1"), a different fact
-- from "when the source last changed". Overloading one column with both would
-- be a trap for the next reader and for an auditor.

ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

COMMENT ON COLUMN test_case_proposals.source_updated_at IS
    'For jira-sourced cases: the source issue''s updated timestamp at generation time. Anchor for change-detection. NULL for other sources.';

FILE: backend/db/migrations/010_jira_sync.sql
================================================
-- 010_jira_sync.sql
--
-- Stage 3 (Jira change-detection / scheduled poll) schema.
--
-- Two additions:
--
-- 1. test_case_proposals.source_sync_status — the flag the poll sets and the
--    UI (Stage 4) reads. For a jira-sourced test case:
--       'current'              — the linked Jira issue has not changed since
--                                this test was generated (the default).
--       'requirement_changed'  — the Jira issue was updated AFTER this test
--                                was generated; a human must re-review it.
--       'requirement_deleted'  — the Jira issue no longer exists / left the
--                                requirement set (reserved; not set in v1).
--    The poll only FLAGS. It never regenerates or edits a test case — that
--    would be an unreviewed AI change to a validated artefact, which GxP
--    forbids. A human decides what to do with a flagged case.
--
-- 2. jira_sync_state — remembers when each application/project was last
--    synced, so the poll asks Jira only for issues updated since then
--    (JQL: updated >= last_synced_at) rather than re-reading everything.
--
-- Both are additive; nothing existing is touched. source_sync_status
-- defaults to 'current' so pre-010 rows read as not-flagged.

ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_sync_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'current';

-- Guard the allowed values, matching the pattern of the other status columns.
DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE test_case_proposals
        ADD CONSTRAINT test_case_proposals_source_sync_status_check
        CHECK (source_sync_status IN
               ('current', 'requirement_changed', 'requirement_deleted'));
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

COMMENT ON COLUMN test_case_proposals.source_sync_status IS
    'Change-detection flag for jira-sourced cases: current | requirement_changed | requirement_deleted. Set by the sync poll; flag-only, never auto-regenerated.';


CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS jira_sync_state (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER REFERENCES applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    project_key     TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- The high-water mark: the poll next asks Jira for issues updated at or
    -- after this. NULL means "never synced" — the first poll seeds it.
    last_synced_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    -- One sync cursor per application+project pair.
    UNIQUE (application_id, project_key)
);

COMMENT ON TABLE jira_sync_state IS
    'Per application+project high-water mark for the Jira change-detection poll (Stage 3).';

FILE: backend/db/migrations/011_schedule_job_type.sql
================================================
-- migrations/011_schedule_job_type.sql
--
-- Adds two columns to `schedules` so one scheduler can run more than one kind
-- of job:
--   job_type          discriminator the runner dispatches on ('suite_run' | 'jira_sync')
--   jira_project_key  the Jira project a jira_sync schedule targets (per-schedule
--                     data, NOT a hardcoded literal)
--
-- Existing rows become 'suite_run' automatically via the column default, so no
-- backfill is needed. Safe to re-run (IF NOT EXISTS + guarded constraint).

ALTER TABLE schedules
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS job_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'suite_run'
    CHECK (job_type IN ('suite_run', 'jira_sync'));

ALTER TABLE schedules
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS jira_project_key TEXT;

-- A jira_sync schedule must name a project. Guarded because Postgres has no
-- "ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS" for CHECK constraints.
DO $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'schedules_jira_project_required'
    ) THEN
        ALTER TABLE schedules
            ADD CONSTRAINT schedules_jira_project_required
            CHECK (job_type <> 'jira_sync' OR jira_project_key IS NOT NULL);
    END IF;
END$$;

FILE: backend/db/migrations/012_help_and_support.sql
================================================
-- migrations/012_help_and_support.sql
--
-- Help & Support schema — the in-product resource centre.
--
-- Five additions, all new tables plus one widened CHECK. Nothing existing is
-- altered or dropped, so this migration cannot affect the generation, sync,
-- execution or scheduling paths.
--
-- 1. help_articles        Versioned how-to content, authored as markdown and
--                         seeded from backend/content/help/*.md. Treated as a
--                         CONTROLLED DOCUMENT: an article is never edited in
--                         place. A change inserts a new row at version+1 and
--                         marks the previous one is_stale with superseded_by
--                         pointing forward — the same soft-delete discipline
--                         used for test cases, for the same GxP reason (an
--                         auditor must be able to see what the text said on
--                         the day someone read it).
--
-- 2. help_chunks          One row per retrievable passage, from EITHER an
--                         article OR an uploaded training document. This is
--                         the retrieval unit: search ranks chunks, not whole
--                         documents, so NextGen2 AI receives the three relevant
--                         paragraphs instead of a twelve-page PDF.
--
--                         Chunking at write time is deliberate. Today the
--                         chunks are ranked by Postgres full-text search. When
--                         embeddings are introduced later (Qdrant or any other
--                         vector store), the SAME chunk rows become the points
--                         that get embedded — chunk_id is the join key. That
--                         makes the vector step additive rather than a
--                         re-derivation of the corpus.
--
-- 3. help_views           The training record: who opened which article or
--                         training document, when, and whether they
--                         acknowledged having read it. This is the audit
--                         artefact — training evidence, exportable as CSV.
--
-- 4. support_tickets      Local mirror of a ticket raised from inside NextGen2.
--                         Deliberately PROVIDER-AGNOSTIC: `provider` plus an
--                         opaque `external_ref`/`external_url`, never a
--                         jira_key column. Moving from Jira to ServiceNow is
--                         then a new provider class and a config change, with
--                         no schema migration and no data rewrite.
--
-- 5. help_search_misses   Every query that returned nothing useful. This is
--                         the documentation backlog captured as data rather
--                         than guessed at.
--
-- Plus: documents.document_type gains 'training', so an uploaded training PDF
-- reuses the existing documents table, storage path and text extraction
-- (service/orchestrator.py::_extract_text_from_document) rather than
-- introducing a parallel upload path.
--
-- Requires PostgreSQL 12+ (uses a GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED column for the
-- tsvector). Safe to re-run: IF NOT EXISTS throughout and guarded constraints.


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. help_articles
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS help_articles (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Stable human-readable id, e.g. 'scheduling-a-run'. Carried across
    -- versions: every version of an article shares its slug, and exactly one
    -- of them is live at a time (enforced by ux_help_articles_live below).
    slug            TEXT NOT NULL,
    title           TEXT NOT NULL,
    category        TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary         TEXT,
    body_md         TEXT NOT NULL,

    -- Controlled-document fields. An article is only retrievable by NextGen2 AI
    -- and only counts as training material once status = 'approved'; a draft
    -- is visible in the UI, clearly marked, but is never cited as authority.
    version         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    status          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
    author          TEXT,
    approved_by     TEXT,
    approved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    effective_from  TIMESTAMPTZ,

    -- Ordering within a category, so the navigation reads in a teaching order
    -- rather than alphabetically.
    sort_order      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,

    -- Soft delete / supersede. History is retained, never removed.
    is_stale        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    superseded_by   INTEGER REFERENCES help_articles(id),

    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE help_articles
        ADD CONSTRAINT help_articles_status_check
        CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'approved', 'retired'));
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

-- Exactly one live version per slug. Superseded versions stay in the table
-- with is_stale = TRUE and do not collide.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_help_articles_live
    ON help_articles (slug) WHERE is_stale = FALSE;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_help_articles_category
    ON help_articles (category, sort_order) WHERE is_stale = FALSE;

COMMENT ON TABLE help_articles IS
    'Versioned help content, treated as a controlled document: never edited in place, superseded via is_stale/superseded_by.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN help_articles.status IS
    'draft | approved | retired. Only approved articles are cited by NextGen2 AI or counted as training material.';


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. help_chunks — the retrieval unit
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS help_chunks (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Which kind of source this passage came from. Both kinds are searched
    -- together so a user's question is answered from whichever explains it
    -- best, article or training deck.
    source_type     TEXT NOT NULL,

    -- Exactly one of these is set, matching source_type (see the CHECK below).
    article_id      INTEGER REFERENCES help_articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    document_id     INTEGER REFERENCES documents(id)     ON DELETE CASCADE,

    chunk_index     INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- position within its source
    heading         TEXT,                  -- nearest heading, shown as the citation label
    body            TEXT NOT NULL,         -- the passage itself

    -- Full-text index over heading + body. A stored generated column rather
    -- than a trigger: it cannot drift out of step with the text.
    search_vector   tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
                        to_tsvector('english'::regconfig,
                                    coalesce(heading, '') || ' ' || coalesce(body, ''))
                    ) STORED,

    -- Chunks are rebuilt wholesale when their source is re-seeded or a
    -- document is re-extracted; the old set is marked stale rather than
    -- deleted so a citation recorded in help_views still resolves.
    is_stale        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,

    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE help_chunks
        ADD CONSTRAINT help_chunks_source_type_check
        CHECK (source_type IN ('article', 'training_doc'));
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

-- A chunk belongs to exactly one source, and that source matches source_type.
-- Without this it is possible to insert an orphan chunk that search would
-- return but no citation could resolve.
DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE help_chunks
        ADD CONSTRAINT help_chunks_one_source
        CHECK (
            (source_type = 'article'      AND article_id IS NOT NULL AND document_id IS NULL)
         OR (source_type = 'training_doc' AND document_id IS NOT NULL AND article_id IS NULL)
        );
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_help_chunks_fts
    ON help_chunks USING GIN (search_vector);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_help_chunks_article
    ON help_chunks (article_id, chunk_index) WHERE is_stale = FALSE;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_help_chunks_document
    ON help_chunks (document_id, chunk_index) WHERE is_stale = FALSE;

COMMENT ON TABLE help_chunks IS
    'One retrievable passage per row, from an article or a training document. Ranked by full-text search today; the same rows become vector points when embeddings are added.';


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. help_views — the training record
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS help_views (
    id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Exactly one of these is set — the article or the training document that
    -- was opened.
    article_id         INTEGER REFERENCES help_articles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    document_id        INTEGER REFERENCES documents(id)     ON DELETE SET NULL,

    -- The version that was actually on screen. Recorded as a value, not a
    -- lookup, so the record still reads true after the article is superseded.
    article_version    INTEGER,

    viewed_by          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anonymous',
    viewed_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

    -- An explicit "I have read and understood" action. A view alone is not
    -- training evidence; an acknowledgement is.
    acknowledged       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    acknowledged_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
);

DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE help_views
        ADD CONSTRAINT help_views_one_source
        CHECK (
            (article_id IS NOT NULL AND document_id IS NULL)
         OR (document_id IS NOT NULL AND article_id IS NULL)
        );
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_help_views_by_user
    ON help_views (viewed_by, viewed_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_help_views_acknowledged
    ON help_views (acknowledged, acknowledged_at DESC) WHERE acknowledged = TRUE;

COMMENT ON TABLE help_views IS
    'Training record: who opened which help article or training document, at which version, and whether they acknowledged reading it.';


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. support_tickets — provider-agnostic
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS support_tickets (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,

    -- Which ticketing system this was raised into. The value matches a key in
    -- service/ticketing/registry.py. There is deliberately no jira_key column:
    -- the external system is a runtime choice, not a schema commitment.
    provider        TEXT NOT NULL,
    external_ref    TEXT,          -- e.g. 'KVSUP-14' (Jira) or 'INC0012345' (ServiceNow)
    external_url    TEXT,          -- deep link back to the ticket

    raised_by       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anonymous',

    -- Plain-English category chosen by the user. The provider maps this onto
    -- its own object model (Jira issue type, ServiceNow incident vs request),
    -- so the user is never asked to understand ITIL.
    category        TEXT NOT NULL,
    summary         TEXT NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT,

    -- Automatically captured technical context: route, application_id,
    -- execution_id, browser, last error. Collected by the UI so the ticket is
    -- actionable without a follow-up conversation.
    context         JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,

    -- Local lifecycle mirror. The external system remains the system of
    -- record; this exists so the user can see their tickets inside NextGen2.
    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
    external_status TEXT,
    last_synced_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,

    -- Set when the provider call fails, so a ticket is never silently lost:
    -- the row is written either way and the failure is visible.
    submit_error    TEXT,

    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE support_tickets
        ADD CONSTRAINT support_tickets_status_check
        CHECK (status IN ('open', 'submitted', 'failed', 'resolved', 'closed'));
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_support_tickets_by_user
    ON support_tickets (raised_by, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_support_tickets_external
    ON support_tickets (provider, external_ref);

COMMENT ON TABLE support_tickets IS
    'Local mirror of tickets raised from NextGen2. Provider-agnostic by design: switching Jira to ServiceNow is a new provider class and a config change, not a migration.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN support_tickets.context IS
    'Auto-captured technical context (route, application_id, execution_id, browser, last error) so the ticket is actionable on arrival.';


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 5. help_search_misses — the documentation backlog, as data
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS help_search_misses (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    query           TEXT NOT NULL,

    -- Where the question was asked: the Help search box, or NextGen2 AI.
    source          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'help_search',

    -- 0 means nothing matched at all; a small number means the results existed
    -- but scored below the usefulness threshold. Both are content gaps.
    result_count    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

    asked_by        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anonymous',
    asked_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE help_search_misses
        ADD CONSTRAINT help_search_misses_source_check
        CHECK (source IN ('help_search', 'chat'));
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_help_search_misses_recent
    ON help_search_misses (asked_at DESC);

COMMENT ON TABLE help_search_misses IS
    'Queries that returned nothing useful — the documentation gap list, captured rather than guessed.';


-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 6. documents.document_type gains 'training'
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
--
-- Training PDFs and decks reuse the existing documents table: same storage
-- path, same extraction (_extract_text_from_document already handles PDF via
-- PyMuPDF and DOCX via python-docx), same lifecycle. Only the CHECK widens.
--
-- The constraint was declared inline in schema.sql, so PostgreSQL auto-named
-- it documents_document_type_check. Dropped by that name and re-added.

ALTER TABLE documents
    DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS documents_document_type_check;

DO $$
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE documents
        ADD CONSTRAINT documents_document_type_check
        CHECK (document_type IN
               ('requirements', 'existing_test_cases', 'standard', 'training'));
EXCEPTION
    WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
END $$;

COMMENT ON COLUMN documents.document_type IS
    'requirements | existing_test_cases | standard | training. training = help/onboarding material shown in Help & Support and retrieved by NextGen2 AI.';

-- 014_application_maps.sql
-- App Map: persistent record of every page and interactive element crawled
-- from an application session (authenticated or not).
--
-- One row per crawl run. Old rows are kept for audit history — they record
-- what the application's UI surface looked like at that point in time. The
-- healer uses the map stored at generation time to compare before/after states.
--
-- map_data column schema:
--   {
--     "base_url": "https://...",
--     "crawled_at": "ISO-8601",
--     "page_count": N,
--     "pages": [
--       {
--         "url": "...",
--         "title": "...",
--         "depth": N,
--         "element_count": N,
--         "iframe_count": N,
--         "elements": [
--           {tag, id, name, aria_label, placeholder, text, data_test,
--            css_class, frame_index (if inside iframe)}
--         ]
--       }
--     ]
--   }

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS application_maps (
    id                SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id),
    crawled_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    page_count        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    element_count     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    map_data          JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    -- True if the crawl authenticated (elements behind login wall are included).
    was_authenticated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    -- 'running' while in progress; 'complete'; 'failed'.
    -- Used to detect abandoned in-progress rows after a server restart.
    status            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'complete'
                          CHECK (status IN ('running', 'complete', 'failed')),
    error_message     TEXT
);

-- Retrieve the latest map for an application without a full table scan.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_maps_app_crawled
    ON application_maps (application_id, crawled_at DESC);

================================================
-- 015_generations_map_id.sql
--
-- Track which App Map was used to generate each script.
--
-- CLAUDE.md requirement:
--   "Write the map ID used for generation into the generations row so there
--   is a permanent record of which element map each script was generated from.
--   The healer reads the map stored at generation time so it can compare old
--   state vs new state when proposing a replacement."
--
-- Without this column the healer has no way to retrieve the element snapshot
-- that was current when the script was written, making before/after comparison
-- impossible.  NULL means the generation pre-dates this migration or ran
-- without a crawled map (live-page extraction fallback).

ALTER TABLE generations
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS app_map_id INTEGER REFERENCES application_maps(id);

COMMENT ON COLUMN generations.app_map_id IS
    'FK to application_maps — the element map snapshot used when this script '
    'was generated.  NULL for generations that pre-date this column or that '
    'fell back to live-page extraction (no crawled map existed for the app).';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_generations_app_map
    ON generations (app_map_id)
    WHERE app_map_id IS NOT NULL;

FILE: backend/db/migrations/016_user_ownership_access.sql
================================================
-- 016_user_ownership_access.sql
-- Phase 2: Internal user identity (mapped from Microsoft Entra), per-application
-- ownership, and per-user access grants.
--
-- Run once:
--   python db/run_migration.py db/migrations/016_user_ownership_access.sql
--
-- Existing applications get owner_user_id = NULL, meaning they become
-- invisible to regular users until an Admin assigns an owner or grants
-- access via application_access. Admins (users.is_admin = true) can see
-- all applications regardless of ownership -- enforced in application code,
-- not in this schema.

-- Internal Kavach user, mapped from the Microsoft Entra token's stable
-- object ID (the "oid" claim). is_admin is managed manually for now
-- (Option C) -- see .github/copilot-instructions.md.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id                SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    entra_object_id   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    email             TEXT NOT NULL,
    display_name      TEXT,
    is_admin          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Real, enforceable owner. Nullable so existing applications are not
-- destructively altered -- they simply have no owner until one is assigned.
-- The existing free-text `owner` column is untouched and remains purely
-- informational.
ALTER TABLE applications
    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS owner_user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id);

-- Per-application, per-user permission grants. A row here means "this user
-- has been given access to this application, with these specific rights."
-- The owner (applications.owner_user_id) implicitly has all rights and does
-- not need a row here. Admins (users.is_admin) implicitly have all rights
-- on every application and also do not need a row here.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS application_access (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    can_view        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    can_edit        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    can_run         BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    can_schedule    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    can_delete      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    granted_by      INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),
    granted_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (application_id, user_id)
);

-- Indexes for the access checks that will run on nearly every application,
-- test suite, execution, report, and schedule request going forward.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_entra_object_id ON users(entra_object_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_applications_owner ON applications(owner_user_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_access_app ON application_access(application_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_application_access_user ON application_access(user_id);

FILE: backend/db/migrations/017_app_credentials.sql
================================================
-- 017_app_credentials.sql
-- Phase 2: Per-user application login credentials.
--
-- Run once (from the backend directory):
--   python db/run_migration.py db/migrations/017_app_credentials.sql
--
-- WHY THIS TABLE EXISTS
-- Today an application's login username/password lives in a single
-- test_data/applications/app_<id>.json file, owned (via _created_by) by
-- whoever saved it first. That is "one owner per application", which cannot
-- express the real requirement: a single application may be used by several
-- Kavach users, and each user must supply and use THEIR OWN credentials,
-- never a shared one.
--
-- This table stores one credential row per (application, user). Retrieval is
-- always scoped by BOTH keys, so a stage can only ever obtain the credential
-- belonging to the user who initiated that run -- never anyone else's.
--
-- SECRECY
-- The password is encrypted at rest with Fernet, using the SAME key as the
-- existing test-data store (TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY) -- no new key, no new
-- algorithm. The Fernet token already carries its own IV and HMAC, so a
-- single ciphertext column is sufficient. The plaintext is never stored.
--
-- BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY
-- This migration only ADDS a table. It changes no existing row and no
-- existing column. Applications continue to work exactly as before until a
-- user saves a per-user credential here.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_credentials (
    id              SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    application_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES applications(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    username        TEXT NOT NULL,
    secret_alg      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'fernet',
    secret_cipher   TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    -- One credential per user per application. A second save by the same
    -- user for the same application updates the existing row (see the
    -- ON CONFLICT upsert in core/db/queries/app_credentials.py).
    UNIQUE (application_id, user_id)
);

-- The lookup every stage performs: "this application, this user".
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_app_credentials_app_user
    ON app_credentials(application_id, user_id);

-- 018_ai_usage_tracking.sql
-- Extends ai_calls so every LLM call can be attributed to an activity,
-- an application and a user, and priced from a configurable pricing table.
-- Safe to re-run: every statement checks before it changes anything.

-- Which product activity triggered the call. The dashboard splits cost by this.
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS purpose TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'other';

-- Lets the dashboard filter by application and, later, by user.
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS application_id INTEGER;
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS user_id INTEGER;

-- FALSE means no price was configured for this model, so cost_usd is NULL.
-- This keeps "unknown cost" separate from a real $0.
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pricing_found BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;

-- More room for cost values. NUMERIC keeps money exact (no float rounding).
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ALTER COLUMN cost_usd TYPE NUMERIC(14,6);

-- Some calls (e.g. chat) have no single parent row, so the link is now optional.
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ALTER COLUMN related_to_id DROP NOT NULL;

-- Allow the new related types alongside the original three.
ALTER TABLE ai_calls DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS ai_calls_related_to_type_check;
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ADD CONSTRAINT ai_calls_related_to_type_check
    CHECK (related_to_type IN ('survey', 'generation', 'heal', 'chat', 'other'));

-- Only known activity names can be stored, so typos can't create new dashboard rows.
ALTER TABLE ai_calls DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS ai_calls_purpose_check;
ALTER TABLE ai_calls ADD CONSTRAINT ai_calls_purpose_check
    CHECK (purpose IN ('test_case_generation', 'script_generation', 'healing',
                       'chat', 'crawl', 'other'));

-- Indexes for the dashboard query (filtered by date, purpose and application).
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ai_calls_called_at   ON ai_calls (called_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ai_calls_purpose_at  ON ai_calls (purpose, called_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ai_calls_app_at      ON ai_calls (application_id, called_at);

-- Price per 1 million tokens for each provider and model.
-- When a price changes, add a new row instead of editing the old one, so past
-- calls keep the price that applied at the time.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_model_pricing (
    id                 SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    provider           TEXT          NOT NULL,
    model              TEXT          NOT NULL,
    input_usd_per_1m   NUMERIC(12,6) NOT NULL CHECK (input_usd_per_1m  >= 0),
    output_usd_per_1m  NUMERIC(12,6) NOT NULL CHECK (output_usd_per_1m >= 0),
    effective_from     TIMESTAMPTZ   NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (provider, model, effective_from)
);

-- Speeds up "latest price for this model" lookups.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pricing_lookup
    ON llm_model_pricing (provider, model, effective_from DESC);
