"""
service/help_service.py

The business logic behind Help & Support.

Four responsibilities, kept in one module because they share the versioning
rules and would drift if separated:

  1. Articles     Authored as markdown, seeded into help_articles, and treated
                  as controlled documents — never edited in place.
  2. Chunking     Turning an article or an uploaded training document into the
                  passages retrieval actually ranks.
  3. Training     Recording who read what, at which version, and who
                  acknowledged it.
  4. Search       Delegating to service/help_search and recording the misses.

The versioning rule is the part worth understanding, because it drives
everything else. Changing an article does not update a row. It inserts a new
row at version+1 and marks the previous one is_stale with superseded_by
pointing forward. That is the same soft-delete discipline used for test cases,
for the same reason: a training record saying "read v2 on 4 August" has to
still mean something after v3 is published, and an auditor has to be able to
see the text as it stood that day.

A consequence worth stating plainly: a new version arrives as a draft. NextGen2
AI will not cite it and it does not count as training material until a person
approves it. Content changing under an approval is exactly what the approval
was supposed to prevent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from typing import Any, Optional

from core.db.connection import get_conn
from core.settings import settings
from service.help_search import search as retrieve

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# Fields that define an article's content. If none of these differ, an upsert
# is a no-op rather than a new version — re-running the seed script must not
# manufacture version churn and invalidate every training record.
_CONTENT_FIELDS = ("title", "category", "summary", "body_md", "sort_order")


# ── articles ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def list_articles(category: Optional[str] = None,
                  include_drafts: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """List the live articles, ordered for reading rather than alphabetically.

    Args:
        category: Restrict to one category, or None for all.
        include_drafts: When True, unapproved articles are included. The Help
            screen passes True and marks them visibly as drafts; NextGen2 AI
            never does.

    Returns:
        Article rows without their body text, which is fetched per article.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT id, slug, title, category, summary, version, status,
               author, approved_by, approved_at, sort_order, updated_at
        FROM help_articles
        WHERE is_stale = FALSE
          AND (%(include_drafts)s OR status = 'approved')
          AND (%(category)s IS NULL OR category = %(category)s)
        ORDER BY category ASC, sort_order ASC, title ASC
    """
    return _rows(sql, {"category": category, "include_drafts": include_drafts})


def get_article(slug: str, include_drafts: bool = True) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Fetch one live article by slug, including its body.

    Args:
        slug: The article's stable identifier.
        include_drafts: When False, an unapproved article reads as absent.

    Returns:
        The article row, or None if there is no live article with that slug.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT *
        FROM help_articles
        WHERE slug = %(slug)s
          AND is_stale = FALSE
          AND (%(include_drafts)s OR status = 'approved')
    """
    rows = _rows(sql, {"slug": slug, "include_drafts": include_drafts})
    return rows[0] if rows else None


def get_article_by_id(article_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Fetch any article by id, including superseded versions.

    Used when resolving a citation recorded against an older version, which
    must still resolve after the article has moved on.

    Args:
        article_id: help_articles.id.

    Returns:
        The article row, or None.
    """
    rows = _rows("SELECT * FROM help_articles WHERE id = %(id)s", {"id": article_id})
    return rows[0] if rows else None


def list_categories(include_drafts: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """Count live articles per category, for the navigation.

    Args:
        include_drafts: Whether unapproved articles are counted.

    Returns:
        One row per category with an article_count, ordered by the lowest
        sort_order in each so the navigation follows a teaching order.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT category,
               COUNT(*)          AS article_count,
               MIN(sort_order)   AS first_sort_order
        FROM help_articles
        WHERE is_stale = FALSE
          AND (%(include_drafts)s OR status = 'approved')
        GROUP BY category
        ORDER BY first_sort_order ASC, category ASC
    """
    return _rows(sql, {"include_drafts": include_drafts})


def upsert_article(slug: str, title: str, category: str, body_md: str,
                   summary: Optional[str] = None,
                   author: Optional[str] = None,
                   status: str = "draft",
                   sort_order: int = 100) -> dict:
    """Create an article, or supersede it with a new version if it changed.

    Never updates in place. If the live article's content is identical the
    call is a no-op, so re-seeding is safe and does not churn versions.

    The whole operation runs in one transaction because the unique index on
    live slugs means the old row must be marked stale before the new one is
    inserted; a failure between the two would leave the article missing.

    Args:
        slug: Stable identifier, shared across every version.
        title: Human title.
        category: Navigation grouping.
        body_md: Markdown body.
        summary: One-line description for the article list.
        author: Who wrote it.
        status: 'draft' or 'approved'. A new version defaults to draft — a
            change to approved content requires a person to approve it again.
        sort_order: Position within its category.

    Returns:
        The live article row, whether newly created, newly versioned, or
        unchanged.
    """
    incoming = {
        "title": title,
        "category": category,
        "summary": summary,
        "body_md": body_md,
        "sort_order": sort_order,
    }

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM help_articles WHERE slug = %s AND is_stale = FALSE",
                (slug,),
            )
            existing = _one(cur)

            if existing and all(existing.get(f) == incoming[f] for f in _CONTENT_FIELDS):
                logger.debug("Help article '%s' unchanged at v%s", slug, existing["version"])
                return existing

            version = (existing["version"] + 1) if existing else 1

            if existing:
                # Free the unique live-slug index before inserting the
                # replacement, and take the old version's chunks out of
                # retrieval at the same time.
                cur.execute(
                    "UPDATE help_articles SET is_stale = TRUE, updated_at = now() "
                    "WHERE id = %s",
                    (existing["id"],),
                )
                cur.execute(
                    "UPDATE help_chunks SET is_stale = TRUE WHERE article_id = %s",
                    (existing["id"],),
                )

            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO help_articles
                    (slug, title, category, summary, body_md, version, status,
                     author, sort_order, effective_from)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s,
                        CASE WHEN %s = 'approved' THEN now() ELSE NULL END)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (slug, title, category, summary, body_md, version, status,
                 author, sort_order, status),
            )
            created = _one(cur)

            if existing:
                cur.execute(
                    "UPDATE help_articles SET superseded_by = %s WHERE id = %s",
                    (created["id"], existing["id"]),
                )

            _write_article_chunks(cur, created["id"], title, body_md)

    logger.info("Help article '%s' saved at v%s (%s)", slug, created["version"], status)
    return created


def approve_article(article_id: int, approved_by: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Mark an article approved, making it citable and countable as training.

    Args:
        article_id: help_articles.id.
        approved_by: Who approved it.

    Returns:
        The updated row, or None if the article does not exist or is stale.
    """
    sql = """
        UPDATE help_articles
        SET status = 'approved',
            approved_by = %(approved_by)s,
            approved_at = now(),
            effective_from = COALESCE(effective_from, now()),
            updated_at = now()
        WHERE id = %(id)s AND is_stale = FALSE
        RETURNING *
    """
    rows = _rows(sql, {"id": article_id, "approved_by": approved_by})
    if rows:
        logger.info("Help article %s approved by %s", article_id, approved_by)
    return rows[0] if rows else None


# ── training documents ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

def list_training_documents() -> list[dict]:
    """List uploaded training documents with their indexed passage counts.

    Returns:
        One row per training document, newest first. chunk_count reveals a
        document whose text never extracted — a scanned PDF with no text
        layer indexes as zero passages and would otherwise look fine.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT d.id, d.original_filename, d.storage_path, d.uploaded_at,
               length(d.extracted_text) AS text_length,
               COUNT(c.id) FILTER (WHERE c.is_stale = FALSE) AS chunk_count
        FROM documents d
        LEFT JOIN help_chunks c ON c.document_id = d.id
        WHERE d.document_type = 'training'
        GROUP BY d.id
        ORDER BY d.uploaded_at DESC
    """
    return _rows(sql, {})


def index_training_document(document_id: int) -> int:
    """Chunk a training document's extracted text so it becomes searchable.

    Uploading only stores the file and its text. Nothing is retrievable until
    it has been chunked, which is what this does. Safe to re-run: existing
    chunks for the document are retired first.

    Args:
        document_id: documents.id, which must be of type 'training'.

    Returns:
        The number of passages indexed. Zero means the document carried no
        extractable text — most often a scanned PDF with no text layer, which
        the caller should surface rather than treat as success.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the document does not exist or is not a training
            document.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT id, document_type, original_filename, extracted_text "
                "FROM documents WHERE id = %s",
                (document_id,),
            )
            doc = _one(cur)
            if not doc:
                raise ValueError(f"Document {document_id} does not exist.")
            if doc["document_type"] != "training":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Document {document_id} is of type '{doc['document_type']}', "
                    "not 'training'."
                )

            cur.execute(
                "UPDATE help_chunks SET is_stale = TRUE WHERE document_id = %s",
                (document_id,),
            )

            pieces = _split_text(doc["extracted_text"] or "")
            for i, (heading, body) in enumerate(pieces):
                cur.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO help_chunks
                           (source_type, document_id, chunk_index, heading, body)
                       VALUES ('training_doc', %s, %s, %s, %s)""",
                    (document_id, i, heading, body),
                )

    if not pieces:
        logger.warning(
            "Training document %s (%s) produced no passages — it may be a "
            "scanned PDF with no text layer.",
            document_id, doc["original_filename"],
        )
    else:
        logger.info("Indexed %d passage(s) from training document %s",
                    len(pieces), document_id)
    return len(pieces)


# ── training record ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def record_view(article_id: Optional[int] = None,
                document_id: Optional[int] = None,
                viewed_by: str = "anonymous") -> dict:
    """Record that someone opened an article or training document.

    The article's version is stored as a value rather than a reference, so the
    record still reads true after the article is superseded.

    Args:
        article_id: help_articles.id, if an article was opened.
        document_id: documents.id, if a training document was opened.
        viewed_by: Who opened it.

    Returns:
        The created help_views row.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If neither or both ids are given.
    """
    if (article_id is None) == (document_id is None):
        raise ValueError("Exactly one of article_id or document_id is required.")

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            version = None
            if article_id is not None:
                cur.execute("SELECT version FROM help_articles WHERE id = %s",
                            (article_id,))
                row = cur.fetchone()
                version = row[0] if row else None

            cur.execute(
                """INSERT INTO help_views
                       (article_id, document_id, article_version, viewed_by)
                   VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s)
                   RETURNING *""",
                (article_id, document_id, version, viewed_by),
            )
            return _one(cur)


def acknowledge(view_id: int, viewed_by: str = "anonymous") -> Optional[dict]:
    """Record an explicit "I have read and understood" against a view.

    A view alone is not training evidence — it says a page was opened. An
    acknowledgement is the assertion that carries weight in an audit, which is
    why it is a separate deliberate act rather than a side effect of reading.

    Args:
        view_id: help_views.id to acknowledge.
        viewed_by: Who is acknowledging. Must match the recorded viewer; an
            acknowledgement made on someone else's behalf would be worthless
            as evidence.

    Returns:
        The updated row, or None if no matching unacknowledged view exists.
    """
    sql = """
        UPDATE help_views
        SET acknowledged = TRUE, acknowledged_at = now()
        WHERE id = %(id)s AND viewed_by = %(viewed_by)s
        RETURNING *
    """
    rows = _rows(sql, {"id": view_id, "viewed_by": viewed_by})
    if not rows:
        logger.warning("Acknowledgement rejected for view %s by %s", view_id, viewed_by)
    return rows[0] if rows else None


def training_records(viewed_by: Optional[str] = None,
                     acknowledged_only: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """The training record, joined to what was actually read.

    Args:
        viewed_by: Restrict to one person, or None for everyone.
        acknowledged_only: When True, only acknowledged views are returned —
            the subset that constitutes training evidence.

    Returns:
        One row per view, newest first, naming the article or document, the
        version read, and whether it was acknowledged.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT v.id, v.viewed_by, v.viewed_at, v.acknowledged, v.acknowledged_at,
               v.article_version,
               COALESCE(a.title, d.original_filename) AS source_title,
               COALESCE(a.slug, d.original_filename)  AS source_label,
               CASE WHEN v.article_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'article'
                    ELSE 'training_doc' END           AS source_type,
               a.category                             AS category
        FROM help_views v
        LEFT JOIN help_articles a ON a.id = v.article_id
        LEFT JOIN documents     d ON d.id = v.document_id
        WHERE (%(viewed_by)s IS NULL OR v.viewed_by = %(viewed_by)s)
          AND (NOT %(acknowledged_only)s OR v.acknowledged = TRUE)
        ORDER BY v.viewed_at DESC
    """
    return _rows(sql, {"viewed_by": viewed_by, "acknowledged_only": acknowledged_only})


# ── search ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def search(query: str, asked_by: str = "anonymous", source: str = "help_search",
           approved_only: bool = True, limit: Optional[int] = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Search help content and record the question if nothing useful came back.

    The recording is the point as much as the search. A question that finds
    nothing is a documentation gap, and capturing it as data means the backlog
    of articles still to write is measured rather than guessed at.

    Args:
        query: The user's question, in their own words.
        asked_by: Who asked.
        source: 'help_search' or 'chat' — where the question came from.
        approved_only: When True, drafts are excluded. NextGen2 AI always passes
            True; an unapproved article is not authority.
        limit: Maximum passages. Defaults to settings.help.max_passages.

    Returns:
        Passages as plain dicts, best first. Empty means nothing matched.
    """
    passages = retrieve(query, limit=limit, approved_only=approved_only)

    if not passages:
        _log_miss(query, asked_by, source, 0)
        return []

    return [p.as_dict() for p in passages]


def search_misses(limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]:
    """The questions that found nothing, most frequent first.

    Args:
        limit: Maximum rows to return.

    Returns:
        Distinct queries with how often they were asked and when last asked —
        the ranked list of articles still to write.
    """
    sql = """
        SELECT lower(query)      AS query,
               COUNT(*)          AS times_asked,
               MAX(asked_at)     AS last_asked,
               COUNT(DISTINCT asked_by) AS distinct_askers
        FROM help_search_misses
        GROUP BY lower(query)
        ORDER BY times_asked DESC, last_asked DESC
        LIMIT %(limit)s
    """
    return _rows(sql, {"limit": limit})


def _log_miss(query: str, asked_by: str, source: str, result_count: int) -> None:
    """Record a question that found nothing useful.

    Failing to log must never fail the request: the user asked a question and
    is owed an answer, or an honest "I don't know", regardless of whether the
    gap was recorded.

    Args:
        query: The question asked.
        asked_by: Who asked.
        source: 'help_search' or 'chat'.
        result_count: How many results were returned, usually zero.
    """
    if source not in ("help_search", "chat"):
        source = "help_search"
    try:
        with get_conn() as conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO help_search_misses
                           (query, source, result_count, asked_by)
                       VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s)""",
                    (query[:1000], source, result_count, asked_by),
                )
        logger.info("Help search miss recorded: %r (from %s)", query, source)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - logging a gap must not break the answer
        logger.exception("Failed to record help search miss for %r", query)


# ── chunking ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _write_article_chunks(cur, article_id: int, title: str, body_md: str) -> None:
    """Split an article body into passages and insert them.

    Args:
        cur: An open cursor, so chunking joins the caller's transaction — an
            article must never exist without its chunks.
        article_id: The article the chunks belong to.
        title: Used as the heading for text appearing before the first
            markdown heading, so an intro paragraph is still citable.
        body_md: The markdown body.
    """
    for i, (heading, body) in enumerate(_split_markdown(body_md, title)):
        cur.execute(
            """INSERT INTO help_chunks
                   (source_type, article_id, chunk_index, heading, body)
               VALUES ('article', %s, %s, %s, %s)""",
            (article_id, i, heading, body),
        )


def _split_markdown(body_md: str, default_heading: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Split markdown into passages, one per section, subdividing long ones.

    Sections are the natural retrieval unit: a heading states what the text
    below answers, which is precisely the signal a question needs to match
    against. The heading is stored with each passage and indexed alongside it.

    Args:
        body_md: The markdown body.
        default_heading: Heading for content before the first '#' heading.

    Returns:
        (heading, body) pairs in document order.
    """
    if not (body_md or "").strip():
        return []

    sections: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = [(default_heading, [])]
    for line in body_md.split("\n"):
        match = re.match(r"^\s{0,3}(#{1,6})\s+(.*\S)\s*$", line)
        if match:
            sections.append((match.group(2).strip(), []))
        else:
            sections[-1][1].append(line)

    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for heading, lines in sections:
        text = "\n".join(lines).strip()
        if not text:
            continue
        for part in _subdivide(text):
            out.append((heading, part))
    return out


def _split_text(text: str) -> list[tuple[Optional[str], str]]:
    """Split unstructured extracted text into passages.

    Used for training documents, whose text comes out of a PDF or DOCX with no
    reliable heading structure. Paragraphs are accumulated to the target size
    instead.

    Args:
        text: Extracted plain text.

    Returns:
        (heading, body) pairs, heading always None.
    """
    if not (text or "").strip():
        return []
    return [(None, part) for part in _subdivide(text)]


def _subdivide(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Break text into pieces of roughly the configured passage size.

    Splits on blank lines and accumulates paragraphs until the target word
    count is reached, so a passage never ends mid-sentence. A single paragraph
    longer than the target is left whole rather than cut arbitrarily —
    truncating one would produce a passage that answers half a question.

    Args:
        text: The text to divide.

    Returns:
        Non-empty pieces in order.
    """
    target = max(50, settings.help.chunk_target_words)
    paragraphs = [p.strip() for p in re.split(r"\n\s*\n", text) if p.strip()]
    if not paragraphs:
        return []

    pieces: list[str] = []
    buffer: list[str] = []
    words = 0

    for para in paragraphs:
        para_words = len(para.split())
        if buffer and words + para_words > target:
            pieces.append("\n\n".join(buffer))
            buffer, words = [], 0
        buffer.append(para)
        words += para_words

    if buffer:
        pieces.append("\n\n".join(buffer))
    return pieces


# ── row helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _rows(sql: str, params: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict]:
    """Run a query and return its rows as dicts.

    Args:
        sql: SQL with named placeholders.
        params: Values for those placeholders.

    Returns:
        Rows as dicts, empty if the statement returned none.
    """
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(sql, params)
            if cur.description is None:
                return []
            cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]


def _one(cur) -> dict:
    """Read a single row from an open cursor as a dict.

    Args:
        cur: A cursor positioned after a statement returning at most one row.

    Returns:
        The row as a dict, or an empty dict if there was none.
    """
    row = cur.fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return {}
    return dict(zip([d[0] for d in cur.description], row))

"""
service/hint_resolver.py

Handles:
  - Extracting element hints from steps
  - Formatting hints for LLM clarity
  - Generating CSS selectors from hints (optional)
  - Selector validation and testing
"""

import logging
import re
from typing import Optional, Dict, Any, Tuple

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def extract_hint(step: dict) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Extract and normalize element hint from a step.
    
    Args:
        step: Step dict potentially containing element_hint field
        
    Returns:
        Normalized hint string (e.g., "aria-label='Settings'") or None
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If step is not a dict or hint format is invalid
    """
    if not isinstance(step, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected dict, got {type(step).__name__}")
    
    hint = step.get("element_hint")
    if not hint:
        logger.debug("extract_hint: no element_hint in step")
        return None
    
    if not isinstance(hint, str):
        logger.warning("extract_hint: element_hint not string, got %s", type(hint).__name__)
        return None
    
    hint = hint.strip()
    if not hint:
        logger.debug("extract_hint: element_hint is empty string")
        return None
    
    logger.debug("extract_hint: extracted hint=%s", hint)
    return hint


def format_hint_for_step(hint: Optional[str], max_length: int = 60) -> str:
    """
    Format a hint for inclusion in step text.
    
    Args:
        hint: Raw hint string or None
        max_length: Maximum formatted hint length
        
    Returns:
        Formatted hint like "[aria-label='Settings']" or ""
    """
    if not hint:
        return ""
    
    if len(hint) > max_length:
        # Truncate long hints gracefully
        hint = hint[:max_length-3] + "..."
        logger.debug("format_hint_for_step: truncated hint to %d chars", max_length)
    
    formatted = f" [{hint}]"
    logger.debug("format_hint_for_step: formatted_hint=%s", formatted)
    return formatted


def parse_hint_attribute(hint: str) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str]]:
    """
    Parse hint into attribute and value.
    
    Args:
        hint: Hint string like "aria-label='Settings'" or "name='username'"
        
    Returns:
        (attribute, value) tuple or (None, None) if unparseable
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If hint format is invalid
    """
    if not isinstance(hint, str):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected string, got {type(hint).__name__}")
    
    # Pattern: attr='value' or attr="value"
    match = re.match(r"(\w[\w\-]*)\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]*)['\"]", hint.strip())
    
    if not match:
        logger.warning("parse_hint_attribute: could not parse hint=%s", hint)
        return None, None
    
    attr, value = match.groups()
    logger.debug("parse_hint_attribute: attr=%s  value=%s", attr, value)
    return attr, value


def hint_to_selector(hint: str, tag: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Convert a hint to a CSS selector.
    
    Args:
        hint: Hint like "aria-label='Settings'" or "name='username'"
        tag: Optional tag to restrict selector (e.g., "button", "input")
        
    Returns:
        CSS selector like "button[aria-label='Settings']" or None
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If hint format invalid
    """
    attr, value = parse_hint_attribute(hint)
    if not attr or not value:
        logger.warning("hint_to_selector: could not parse hint=%s", hint)
        return None
    
    # Special handling for certain attributes
    if attr == "id":
        selector = f"#{value}"
        logger.debug("hint_to_selector: id hint → selector=%s", selector)
        return selector
    
    if attr == "class":
        # Handle class names carefully (can have spaces)
        classes = ".".join(value.split())
        selector = f".{classes}" if classes else None
        logger.debug("hint_to_selector: class hint → selector=%s", selector)
        return selector
    
    if attr == "name":
        # Name hints often for input/textarea
        selector = f"input[{attr}='{value}'], textarea[{attr}='{value}'], select[{attr}='{value}']"
        logger.debug("hint_to_selector: name hint → selector=%s", selector)
        return selector
    
    if attr == "aria-label":
        # aria-label hints for buttons, links, etc.
        # If tag specified, use it; otherwise be flexible
        if tag:
            selector = f"{tag}[{attr}='{value}']"
        else:
            selector = f"[{attr}='{value}']"
        logger.debug("hint_to_selector: aria-label hint → selector=%s", selector)
        return selector
    
    # Generic: just build the attribute selector
    selector = f"[{attr}='{value}']"
    if tag:
        selector = f"{tag}{selector}"
    logger.debug("hint_to_selector: generic hint → selector=%s", selector)
    return selector


def validate_selector_from_hint(selector: str) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[str]]:
    """
    Validate that a selector is well-formed CSS.
    
    Args:
        selector: CSS selector to validate
        
    Returns:
        (is_valid, error_message) tuple
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If selector not a string
    """
    if not isinstance(selector, str):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected string, got {type(selector).__name__}")
    
    if not selector.strip():
        return False, "Selector is empty"
    
    # Basic validation: check for balanced brackets
    if selector.count("[") != selector.count("]"):
        logger.warning("validate_selector_from_hint: unbalanced brackets in %s", selector)
        return False, "Unbalanced brackets in selector"
    
    if selector.count("(") != selector.count(")"):
        logger.warning("validate_selector_from_hint: unbalanced parens in %s", selector)
        return False, "Unbalanced parentheses in selector"
    
    # Check for unclosed quotes
    single_quotes = selector.count("'") % 2
    double_quotes = selector.count('"') % 2
    if single_quotes != 0 or double_quotes != 0:
        logger.warning("validate_selector_from_hint: unclosed quotes in %s", selector)
        return False, "Unclosed quotes in selector"
    
    logger.debug("validate_selector_from_hint: selector valid: %s", selector)
    return True, None


def get_hint_confidence(hint: str) -> float:
    """
    Rate how confident we should be in a hint for selector generation.
    
    Args:
        hint: Hint string to rate
        
    Returns:
        Confidence score 0.0-1.0
        
    Raises:
        ValueError: If hint not a string
    """
    if not isinstance(hint, str):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected string, got {type(hint).__name__}")
    
    score = 0.5  # Base confidence
    
    # High-confidence attributes
    if "id=" in hint:
        score = 0.95
        logger.debug("get_hint_confidence: id hint → high confidence")
    elif "data-test" in hint or "data-testid" in hint:
        score = 0.9
        logger.debug("get_hint_confidence: data-test hint → high confidence")
    elif "aria-label=" in hint or "name=" in hint:
        score = 0.8
        logger.debug("get_hint_confidence: aria-label/name hint → medium-high confidence")
    elif "placeholder=" in hint:
        score = 0.7
        logger.debug("get_hint_confidence: placeholder hint → medium confidence")
    elif "class=" in hint:
        score = 0.6
        logger.debug("get_hint_confidence: class hint → medium-low confidence")
    else:
        score = 0.5
        logger.debug("get_hint_confidence: generic hint → low confidence")
    
    return score


def annotate_hint(hint: Optional[str], matched: bool) -> str:
    """
    Annotate a hint based on step match status.
    
    Args:
        hint: Element hint or None
        matched: Whether step's element was found
        
    Returns:
        Annotated hint string for step text
    """
    if not hint:
        return ""
    
    if not matched:
        # Unmatched steps: hint is informational only
        return f" [{hint} — not found on page]"
    else:
        # Matched steps: hint is reliable selector
        return f" [{hint}]"


def collect_hints_from_steps(steps: Optional[list[dict]]) -> Dict[int, str]:
    """
    Collect all hints from a set of steps.
    
    Args:
        steps: List of step dicts
        
    Returns:
        Dict mapping step index → hint string
    """
    hints = {}
    
    if not steps:
        logger.debug("collect_hints_from_steps: no steps provided")
        return hints
    
    for i, step in enumerate(steps):
        try:
            hint = extract_hint(step)
            if hint:
                hints[i] = hint
                logger.debug("collect_hints_from_steps: step %d has hint=%s", i, hint)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("collect_hints_from_steps: error on step %d: %s", i, e)
    
    logger.info("collect_hints_from_steps: collected %d hints from %d steps",
                len(hints), len(steps))
    return hints


def validate_hint_coverage(steps: Optional[list[dict]], min_coverage: float = 0.8) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Validate that most steps have element hints.
    
    Args:
        steps: List of step dicts
        min_coverage: Minimum fraction of steps that should have hints (0.0-1.0)
        
    Returns:
        Validation result dict:
        {
            "valid": bool,
            "total_steps": int,
            "steps_with_hints": int,
            "coverage_percent": float,
            "message": str,
        }
    """
    if not steps:
        logger.debug("validate_hint_coverage: no steps")
        return {
            "valid": True,
            "total_steps": 0,
            "steps_with_hints": 0,
            "coverage_percent": 0.0,
            "message": "No steps to validate",
        }
    
    hints = collect_hints_from_steps(steps)
    total = len(steps)
    with_hints = len(hints)
    coverage = with_hints / total if total > 0 else 0.0
    is_valid = coverage >= min_coverage
    
    result = {
        "valid": is_valid,
        "total_steps": total,
        "steps_with_hints": with_hints,
        "coverage_percent": round(coverage * 100, 1),
        "message": f"Hint coverage: {with_hints}/{total} steps ({coverage*100:.1f}%)",
    }
    
    if not is_valid:
        logger.warning("validate_hint_coverage: %s", result["message"])
    else:
        logger.info("validate_hint_coverage: %s", result["message"])
    
    return result

FILE: backend/service/iframe_helper.py

"""
service/iframe_helper.py

Iframe detection and exploration helper for the crawler.

When get_snapshot() encounters iframes, this module provides utilities to:
  1. Detect all iframes on the current page (main document)
  2. Switch to each iframe, capture its elements
  3. Return to main document
  4. Annotate elements with the iframe they came from

Iframes require special handling because Selenium's find_elements() only
searches within the current context (main document or current iframe).
To capture elements inside an iframe, we must call driver.switch_to.frame()
first, then find_elements(), then switch back.

Usage:
    elements = get_snapshot(driver)  # Already handles iframes internally
    # Elements from iframes will have iframe_context: "frame_name"
"""

import logging
from typing import Optional
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.common.exceptions import WebDriverException

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# JDE's editable grids (e.g. the Sales Order Entry line-item grid) render
# every column's <input> identically — no aria-label, placeholder, name, or
# title. The only place a column's real label ("Item Number", "Unit Price",
# ...) exists is a SEPARATE header <table>, correlated to the data cell only
# through a shared column index: the data cell's ancestor <td colindex="N">
# and the header's <span id="GC<gridid>.N">. Confirmed against a live grid
# DOM sample on 2026-09-09 — data-row inputs carry no name of their own at
# all. Without this lookup, every editable cell in a grid row looks
# identical to the agent (same empty name), so "Enter Item Number" / "Enter
# Unit Price" steps ended up typing into every textbox in the row instead of
# the right one.
#
# The header lookup also returns rowIndex now, in addition to the header
# text. The header text alone is enough to LABEL the cell for a human/LLM
# reading the crawl (resolve_jde_grid_header_name, unchanged below), but
# re-FINDING that exact cell later (from a generated script, on a fresh
# page load) additionally needs to know which data row it was in — see
# resolve_jde_grid_cell_locator. Neither value is ever the grid's own
# jdeGridData<gridid> id: that id is regenerated by JDE on every page load,
# so nothing derived from this lookup is allowed to depend on it — only the
# column header TEXT and the row's POSITION are stable across a refresh.
#
# ROW POSITION — fixed 2026-09-18. JDE renders EACH grid row as its own,
# separate nested <table id="jdeGridData<gridid>.<rownum>"> (confirmed
# against a live multi-row grid DOM sample), not one shared table with
# multiple <tr> rows. The previous approach — count td[colindex="N"]
# siblings within table.closest('table[id^="jdeGridData"]') — always
# resolves to that single-row table (closest() finds the innermost match),
# which only ever contains ONE row, so rowIndex was always computed as 0
# for every row on every screen. This was invisible on a brand-new "Add"
# entry form (exactly one row, so 0 happened to be correct) and only
# breaks once a grid has more than one line item. Fixed by reading the
# `realrow` attribute JDE already puts directly on the data <tr> itself
# (e.g. <tr id="G0_1_R0" realrow="0">), with the old sibling-count kept
# only as a fallback for a grid variant that might lack that attribute.
_JDE_GRID_HEADER_JS = """
var el = arguments[0];
var td = el.closest('td[colindex]');
if (!td) { return null; }
var colindex = td.getAttribute('colindex');
var table = el.closest('table[id^="jdeGridData"]');
if (!table || !table.id) { return null; }
var m = table.id.match(/^jdeGridData(.+)\\.\\d+$/);
if (!m) { return null; }
var gridId = m[1];
var header = document.getElementById('GC' + gridId + '.' + colindex);
if (!header) { return null; }
var headerText = (header.innerText || header.textContent || '');
var rowEl = el.closest('tr[realrow]');
var rowIndex = 0;
if (rowEl && rowEl.getAttribute('realrow') !== null) {
    rowIndex = parseInt(rowEl.getAttribute('realrow'), 10);
    if (isNaN(rowIndex)) { rowIndex = 0; }
} else {
    var rows = Array.from(table.querySelectorAll('td[colindex="' + colindex + '"]'));
    rowIndex = rows.indexOf(td);
}
return {headerText: headerText, rowIndex: rowIndex};
"""


def _resolve_jde_grid_cell(driver, el) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Shared lookup behind resolve_jde_grid_header_name and
    resolve_jde_grid_cell_locator — runs the DOM script once and returns
    both pieces of information it produces.

    Returns {"header": "Item Number", "row_index": 0}, or None if el is
    not inside a recognizable JDE grid data cell.
    """
    try:
        raw = driver.execute_script(_JDE_GRID_HEADER_JS, el)
    except WebDriverException as e:
        logger.debug("_resolve_jde_grid_cell: script failed: %s", e)
        return None
    if not raw or not raw.get("headerText"):
        return None
    return {
        "header": " ".join(raw["headerText"].split()),
        "row_index": raw.get("rowIndex", 0),
    }


def resolve_jde_grid_header_name(driver, el) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Look up the real column label for a JDE editable-grid cell, e.g. an
    <input> inside the Sales Order Entry line-item grid.

    Returns the header text (e.g. "Item Number") with embedded newlines
    (from a <br> in the header, e.g. "Item\\nNumber") normalized to a
    single space, or None if el is not inside a recognizable JDE grid
    data cell (in which case the caller's existing name-fallback chain
    is unaffected).
    """
    result = _resolve_jde_grid_cell(driver, el)
    return result["header"] if result else None


def resolve_jde_grid_cell_locator(driver, el) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Build a reusable, refresh-safe "recipe" for re-finding this exact grid
    cell later, e.g. from a generated Selenium script on a fresh page load.

    Deliberately excludes the grid's own DOM id (jdeGridData<gridid>) —
    JDE regenerates that id every page load, so a recipe built from it
    would break on the very next run. Only the column header TEXT and the
    cell's ROW POSITION are included, both of which are stable across a
    refresh; whatever re-derives the cell from this recipe must re-look-up
    the current gridId/colindex live, the same way this function just did.

    Returns {"strategy": "jde_grid_header", "column": "Item Number",
    "row_index": 0}, or None if el is not a recognizable JDE grid cell.
    """
    result = _resolve_jde_grid_cell(driver, el)
    if not result:
        return None
    return {
        "strategy": "jde_grid_header",
        "column": result["header"],
        "row_index": result["row_index"],
    }


def detect_iframes(driver) -> list[tuple[str, str, object]]:
    """
    Find all iframes in the main document.

    This function operates in the main document context. It finds all <iframe>
    and <frame> elements visible on the page and returns metadata about each.

    Args:
        driver: A live Selenium WebDriver instance (must be in main document).

    Returns:
        List of tuples: (frame_name_or_id, iframe_title, iframe_element).
        Each tuple represents one iframe found.
        Empty list if no iframes detected or if an error occurs.

    Note:
        Does NOT switch context. Caller must manage driver.switch_to as needed.
    """
    try:
        # Find both <iframe> and <frame> elements (legacy HTML)
        iframes = driver.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR, "iframe, frame")
        logger.debug("detect_iframes: found %d iframe(s) on page", len(iframes))

        result = []
        for iframe_el in iframes:
            try:
                # Try to get a meaningful identifier for the iframe
                frame_id = (
                    iframe_el.get_attribute("id")
                    or iframe_el.get_attribute("name")
                    or f"frame_{len(result)}"
                )
                frame_title = iframe_el.get_attribute("title") or frame_id
                result.append((frame_id, frame_title, iframe_el))
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning("detect_iframes: could not read iframe metadata: %s", e)
                continue

        return result

    except WebDriverException as e:
        logger.warning("detect_iframes: could not search for iframes: %s", e)
        return []


def snapshot_iframe_contents(
    driver,
    iframe_element: object,
    frame_name: str,
    selector: str,
    poll_timeout: float = 0.5,
    min_elements: int = 1,
) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Switch to an iframe, read its interactive elements, and return to main.

    This function encapsulates the full iframe exploration cycle:
    1. Switch to the iframe context
    2. Poll briefly for at least min_elements matching element(s) to appear
       (the iframe's content may still be loading asynchronously at the
       moment we switch in)
    3. Find all interactive elements matching the given selector
    4. Annotate each element with iframe_context = frame_name
    5. Switch back to main document
    6. Return the annotated elements

    Args:
        driver: A live Selenium WebDriver instance (should be in main context).
        iframe_element: The <iframe> WebElement returned by detect_iframes.
        frame_name: Identifier for the iframe (id, name, or synthetic name).
        selector: CSS selector to find interactive elements (e.g., INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR).
        poll_timeout: Max seconds to wait for the iframe's content to render
            before accepting whatever is currently present (default 2.0).
            Frames that never gain matching elements (e.g. genuinely empty
            hidden/utility iframes) simply wait out this timeout once and
            return empty, same as before.
        min_elements: Minimum element count to wait for before accepting the
            result as final (default 1 — unchanged prior behavior). Callers
            that know a click just navigated this specific frame can pass a
            higher value (with a longer poll_timeout) to avoid capturing the
            frame mid-transition — see explore_iframes' just_clicked handling.

    Returns:
        List of element dicts with "iframe_context" field added.
        Example: {"ref": "ifr-el-0", "role": "button", "name": "Submit", "iframe_context": "frame_1"}
        Empty list if iframe is unreachable or has no matching elements.
    """
    from selenium.webdriver.support.wait import WebDriverWait
    from selenium.common.exceptions import TimeoutException

    elements = []
    try:
        # Switch into the iframe
        driver.switch_to.frame(iframe_element)
        logger.debug("snapshot_iframe_contents: switched to iframe '%s'", frame_name)

        # The iframe's content may still be loading asynchronously right
        # after switching in. Give it a short, bounded chance to render
        # before treating an empty (or too-small, see min_elements) result
        # as final.
        try:
            WebDriverWait(driver, poll_timeout).until(
                lambda d: len(d.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR, selector)) >= min_elements
            )
        except TimeoutException:
            pass  # Genuinely empty/small (or slower than poll_timeout) — proceed as before.

        # Find interactive elements within the iframe
        iframe_elements = driver.find_elements(By.CSS_SELECTOR, selector)
        logger.debug(
            "snapshot_iframe_contents: found %d elements in iframe '%s'",
            len(iframe_elements),
            frame_name,
        )

        # Process each element: read its properties and annotate
        for i, el in enumerate(iframe_elements):
            try:
                if not el.is_displayed():
                    continue
                if el.get_attribute("aria-hidden") == "true":
                    continue

                # Use a different ref namespace to distinguish iframe elements from main doc
                ref = f"ifr-{frame_name}-el-{i}"
                role = el.get_attribute("role") or el.tag_name

                # locator records WHICH real attribute actually produced the
                # name below (or the JDE grid recipe, for a cell that has no
                # real attribute at all) — a generated script transcribes a
                # selector straight from this instead of re-guessing one from
                # the flattened name text. See service.trace_compiler.
                # Preserves the exact original name-precedence order:
                # aria-label, placeholder, visible text, title.
                name = ""
                locator: Optional[dict] = None
                for attr, getter in (
                    ("aria-label", lambda: el.get_attribute("aria-label")),
                    ("placeholder", lambda: el.get_attribute("placeholder")),
                    ("text", lambda: el.text),
                    ("title", lambda: el.get_attribute("title")),
                ):
                    value = (getter() or "").strip()
                    if value:
                        name = value
                        locator = {"strategy": "attribute", "attr": attr, "value": value}
                        break

                if not name and el.tag_name.lower() in ("input", "textarea", "select"):
                    # See resolve_jde_grid_cell_locator — editable grid cells
                    # (e.g. Item Number / Unit Price in the Sales Order Entry
                    # line-item grid) carry no name of their own. locator here
                    # is a recipe (column header + row position), never the
                    # grid's own DOM id — JDE regenerates that id every page
                    # load, so nothing recorded here may depend on it.
                    grid_locator = resolve_jde_grid_cell_locator(driver, el)
                    if grid_locator:
                        name = grid_locator["column"]
                        locator = grid_locator

                # Same decorative-placeholder noise filtered in
                # core.tools.get_snapshot — see comment there. Applies here
                # too since iframe content can contain the same kind of
                # leftover no-iframe-support fallback text.
                if "iframe support is required" in name.lower():
                    continue

                element_dict = {
                    "ref": ref,
                    "role": role,
                    "name": name,
                    "iframe_context": frame_name,  # Key annotation
                    "locator": locator,
                }
                elements.append(element_dict)

            except Exception as e:
                logger.debug("snapshot_iframe_contents: skipped element in iframe: %s", e)
                continue

        logger.info(
            "snapshot_iframe_contents: captured %d elements from iframe '%s'",
            len(elements),
            frame_name,
        )

    except WebDriverException as e:
        logger.warning(
            "snapshot_iframe_contents: could not access iframe '%s': %s", frame_name, e
        )

    finally:
        # Always return to main document
        try:
            driver.switch_to.default_content()
            logger.debug("snapshot_iframe_contents: returned to main document")
        except WebDriverException as e:
            logger.error("snapshot_iframe_contents: failed to return to main document: %s", e)

    return elements


# Per-URL cache of consecutive "empty" results for each iframe. A frame
# that reliably comes back empty (e.g. LOGOUT_IFRAME, RunAppHiddenIframe —
# hidden/utility iframes JDE always includes) does not need a full
# switch-in + poll + switch-out cycle on every single snapshot. Cleared
# implicitly whenever the URL changes (a new dict is created per URL).
# Because some apps (e.g. JDE) can replace a frame's content under the
# SAME url, a skipped frame is still re-probed eventually rather than being
# skipped forever — but the interval backs off exponentially (3, 6, 12, ...
# capped at MAX_RECHECK_INTERVAL) instead of a fixed "every 3rd call"
# forever. A frame that has genuinely been empty every time for the whole
# session (JDE's structural shell iframes almost always are) quickly stops
# costing a full rescan on a tight fixed schedule, while still eventually
# being re-checked in case content really does appear later.
INITIAL_RECHECK_INTERVAL = 3
MAX_RECHECK_INTERVAL = 30
# Backward-compat alias — some callers/tests may still reference the old name.
RECHECK_INTERVAL = INITIAL_RECHECK_INTERVAL
_empty_streak_by_url: dict[str, dict[str, dict]] = {}

# The one iframe JDE actually renders real application screens into (menu,
# forms, grids). Confirmed via a live debugging session on 2026-09-11: right
# after clicking a final menu leaf (e.g. "Standard Order SO"), this frame
# briefly still shows its prior near-empty placeholder state (as few as 1
# element) while the real form is still rendering — the default 0.5s poll is
# nowhere near enough for that transition. Every other iframe on the page is
# either a fixed structural shell frame or a utility/hidden frame that does
# not need this extra patience, so the extra wait below is scoped to just
# this one frame_id rather than applied broadly.
MAIN_CONTENT_IFRAME_ID = "e1menuAppIframe"
# Bounded extra wait applied only to MAIN_CONTENT_IFRAME_ID, only on the
# snapshot taken immediately after a click (see just_clicked below).
_POST_CLICK_POLL_TIMEOUT = 3.0
_POST_CLICK_MIN_ELEMENTS = 2


def explore_iframes(driver, iframes: list, selector: str, just_clicked: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Snapshot a pre-detected list of iframes (as returned by detect_iframes),
    skipping frames that have reliably come back empty on recent calls for
    the current URL.

    Use this when the caller already has the iframe list, to avoid querying
    the DOM for iframes a second time in the same snapshot. Use
    explore_all_iframes when it doesn't.

    Args:
        driver: A live Selenium WebDriver instance (must be in main document).
        iframes: List of (frame_id, frame_title, iframe_element) as returned
            by detect_iframes.
        selector: CSS selector for interactive elements.
        just_clicked: When True, MAIN_CONTENT_IFRAME_ID is given extra time
            (and a minimum-element threshold) to finish rendering before its
            snapshot is accepted, instead of the default quick poll. Every
            other iframe is unaffected. Defaults to False, which reproduces
            the exact prior behavior for all callers that don't pass it.

    Returns:
        List of element dicts from all iframes, each annotated with iframe_context.
    """
    all_elements: list[dict] = []
    if not iframes:
        return all_elements

    try:
        url = driver.current_url
    except Exception:
        url = ""
    streaks = _empty_streak_by_url.setdefault(url, {}) if url else {}

    skipped = 0
    for frame_id, frame_title, iframe_el in iframes:
        state = streaks.get(frame_id)
        if state and 0 < state["streak"] < state["interval"]:
            logger.debug(
                "explore_iframes: skipping known-empty frame '%s' (streak=%d/%d)",
                frame_id, state["streak"], state["interval"],
            )
            state["streak"] += 1
            skipped += 1
            continue

        if just_clicked and frame_id == MAIN_CONTENT_IFRAME_ID:
            elements = snapshot_iframe_contents(
                driver, iframe_el, frame_id, selector,
                poll_timeout=_POST_CLICK_POLL_TIMEOUT,
                min_elements=_POST_CLICK_MIN_ELEMENTS,
            )
        else:
            elements = snapshot_iframe_contents(driver, iframe_el, frame_id, selector)
        all_elements.extend(elements)
        if elements:
            # Content found — reset fully, next empty streak (if any) starts
            # the backoff over from INITIAL_RECHECK_INTERVAL.
            streaks[frame_id] = {"streak": 0, "interval": INITIAL_RECHECK_INTERVAL}
        else:
            # Empty again — double how long we'll wait before the next full
            # recheck (capped), instead of rechecking on the same fixed
            # schedule forever.
            prev_interval = state["interval"] if state else INITIAL_RECHECK_INTERVAL
            next_interval = (
                min(prev_interval * 2, MAX_RECHECK_INTERVAL) if state else INITIAL_RECHECK_INTERVAL
            )
            streaks[frame_id] = {"streak": 1, "interval": next_interval}

    logger.info(
        "explore_iframes: captured %d total elements from %d iframe(s) (%d skipped as known-empty)",
        len(all_elements), len(iframes), skipped,
    )
    return all_elements


def explore_all_iframes(driver, selector: str) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Convenience function: detect all iframes, snapshot each, return all elements.

    This is a higher-level API that chains detect_iframes + explore_iframes
    for cases where the caller does not already have the iframe list (see
    explore_iframes for the empty-frame skip/recheck behaviour).

    Args:
        driver: A live Selenium WebDriver instance (must be in main document).
        selector: CSS selector for interactive elements.

    Returns:
        List of element dicts from all iframes, each annotated with iframe_context.
        Empty list if no iframes found or if all fail.
    """
    try:
        iframes = detect_iframes(driver)
        if not iframes:
            logger.debug("explore_all_iframes: no iframes found on page")
            return []
        return explore_iframes(driver, iframes, selector)

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error("explore_all_iframes: unexpected error: %s", e)
        return []


# Backward compatibility: a simple cache so the crawl agent and tools
# can annotate elements with their iframe context when needed later.
_IFRAME_ELEMENT_CACHE: dict[str, dict] = {}


def store_iframe_element(ref: str, context: dict) -> None:
    """Store metadata about an iframe element for later lookup.

    Args:
        ref: Element reference (e.g., "ifr-frame_1-el-5").
        context: Dict with iframe metadata (frame_name, frame_title, etc.).
    """
    _IFRAME_ELEMENT_CACHE[ref] = context
    logger.debug("store_iframe_element: stored context for ref=%s", ref)


def get_iframe_context(ref: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Retrieve stored iframe context for an element.

    Args:
        ref: Element reference.

    Returns:
        Dict with iframe metadata, or None if not found.
    """
    return _IFRAME_ELEMENT_CACHE.get(ref)
