"""
service/help_search/base.py

The contract every help-search implementation satisfies, and the shape of a
result.

This module is the seam. Retrieval today is Postgres full-text search over
help_chunks. It will later be embeddings in a vector store (Qdrant or
otherwise), and most likely both at once with the ranks fused. None of that is
visible above this line: the route, the chat tool and the UI call
`search(query, limit)` and receive a list of Passage. Changing how matching
works means adding a file next to fts.py and changing one setting.

Nothing here imports psycopg2, a vector client, or anything else
implementation-specific. That is deliberate — it is what keeps the seam real
rather than nominal.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional, Protocol


@dataclass
class Passage:
    """
    One retrieved passage, with everything needed to cite it.

    Citation is not decoration here. An answer from NextGen2 AI is advisory; the
    approved article or training document is the authority. So every passage
    carries enough identity for the reader to go and check the source, and for
    an auditor to see which version of which document an answer came from.

    Attributes:
        chunk_id: help_chunks.id — the retrieval unit's primary key. This is
            also the join key a future vector store would carry in its point
            payload, so a passage retrieved by either method is the same row.
        source_type: 'article' or 'training_doc'.
        source_id: help_articles.id or documents.id, per source_type.
        label: Stable identifier shown to the user — an article slug, or a
            training document's original filename.
        title: The source's human title.
        heading: Nearest heading within the source, or None.
        body: The passage text itself. This is what the model is given.
        version: Article version, or None for a training document.
        score: Relevance from the pass that produced it. Comparable ONLY
            against passages from the same pass — see match_type. For
            full-text search this is ts_rank_cd, a cover-density measure whose
            magnitude depends on how many terms were required and how far
            apart they sit, so it carries no absolute meaning and is never
            compared against a fixed threshold.
        match_type: Which pass produced this passage: 'precise' when every
            term had to be present, 'broad' when the terms were ORed after the
            precise pass found nothing. Recorded because the two run on
            different numeric scales — a 0.009 precise hit is a better match
            than a 0.500 broad one — and because a future hybrid strategy
            needs to know which retriever produced a result in order to fuse
            ranks.
    """

    chunk_id: int
    source_type: str
    source_id: int
    label: str
    title: str
    heading: Optional[str]
    body: str
    version: Optional[int]
    score: float
    match_type: str = "precise"

    def citation(self) -> str:
        """Build the short source reference shown alongside an answer.

        Returns:
            A string such as 'Scheduling a run (v2)' for an article, or
            'NextGen2 onboarding.pdf' for a training document.
        """
        if self.source_type == "article":
            return f"{self.title} (v{self.version})" if self.version else self.title
        return self.label or self.title

    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
        """Serialise for an API response or a chat tool result.

        Returns:
            A plain dict; no database types, safe to hand to FastAPI or to
            embed in a tool result string.
        """
        return {
            "chunk_id": self.chunk_id,
            "source_type": self.source_type,
            "source_id": self.source_id,
            "label": self.label,
            "title": self.title,
            "heading": self.heading,
            "body": self.body,
            "version": self.version,
            "score": round(self.score, 5),
            "match_type": self.match_type,
            "citation": self.citation(),
        }


class SearchStrategy(Protocol):
    """
    The contract a retrieval implementation satisfies.

    Duck-typed via typing.Protocol, matching the pattern already used for
    scheduler jobs: a strategy class inherits nothing, it just provides these
    members. Adding vector or hybrid retrieval is a new class plus one entry
    in registry.py.
    """

    name: str

    def search(self, query: str, limit: int = 3,
               approved_only: bool = True) -> list[Passage]:
        """Return the most relevant passages for a query, best first.

        Args:
            query: The user's question, in their own words.
            limit: Maximum number of passages to return.
            approved_only: When True, draft and retired articles are excluded.
                NextGen2 AI always calls with True — an unapproved article is
                not authority and must never be cited as if it were. The Help
                screen may pass False so an author can find their own draft.

        Returns:
            Passages ordered by descending relevance, already filtered to
            those the strategy considers good enough to answer from. An empty
            list means nothing matched well enough, which the caller records
            as a documentation gap rather than answering anyway.

            Relevance gating belongs to the strategy, not to its callers: what
            counts as a good enough match is specific to how the strategy
            matches, and a threshold that suits keyword ranking is meaningless
            for cosine distance.
        """
        ...


================================================
FILE: backend/service/help_search/fts.py
================================================
"""
service/help_search/fts.py

Postgres full-text search over help_chunks — the retrieval strategy in use
today.

Why this and not embeddings, for now: the corpus is small and its vocabulary
is largely the product's own (schedule, suite, requirement, sync, execution).
Keyword matching handles that well, needs no model, no extra service and no
extension, and runs against an index that already exists. Embeddings raise
recall on paraphrased questions, which matters as the corpus grows — that is a
separate strategy alongside this one, not a replacement. Production retrieval
usually keeps both and fuses the ranks, because exact terms like 'jira_sync'
or 'requirement_changed' are precisely where keyword search beats a vector.

Two passes, in order:

    precise  every term must appear (websearch_to_tsquery ANDs them)
    broad    terms ORed, run only if the precise pass found nothing

The broad pass exists because on a small corpus a user's phrasing routinely
shares few words with the article that answers them. It is a fallback, not a
peer: the precise pass runs first so a well-worded question is never diluted.

A caution that cost us a round of debugging, recorded here so it is not
rediscovered: ts_rank_cd is a cover-density measure, NOT a calibrated score.
Its magnitude depends on how many terms were required and how far apart they
sit, so the two passes land on completely different scales — a precise match
was measured at 0.009 while a loose broad match on the same corpus scored
0.500. Comparing a score from one pass against a score from the other, or
against any fixed threshold, is meaningless. That is why every Passage carries
match_type, and why filtering happens relative to the best result within a
single pass (see registry.py).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re

from core.db.connection import get_conn
from service.help_search.base import Passage

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# One SELECT, parameterised on the tsquery expression. Written once and reused
# by both passes so the two cannot drift apart.
#
# The source is joined in so a passage can be cited without a second query,
# and so article state is filtered here rather than by the caller — a draft or
# superseded article must not reach the model by accident.
_SQL = """
SELECT
    c.id                AS chunk_id,
    c.source_type       AS source_type,
    c.heading           AS heading,
    c.body              AS body,
    a.id                AS article_id,
    a.slug              AS article_slug,
    a.title             AS article_title,
    a.version           AS article_version,
    d.id                AS document_id,
    d.original_filename AS document_filename,
    ts_rank_cd(c.search_vector, q.query) AS score
FROM help_chunks c
CROSS JOIN {tsquery_expr} AS q(query)
LEFT JOIN help_articles a ON a.id = c.article_id
LEFT JOIN documents     d ON d.id = c.document_id
WHERE c.is_stale = FALSE
  AND c.search_vector @@ q.query
  AND (
        c.source_type <> 'article'
        OR (a.is_stale = FALSE AND (NOT %(approved_only)s OR a.status = 'approved'))
      )
ORDER BY score DESC, c.chunk_index ASC
LIMIT %(limit)s
"""

# Precise pass. websearch_to_tsquery understands ordinary typed input — quoted
# phrases, 'or', a leading '-' to exclude — and never raises on punctuation,
# unlike to_tsquery. Terms are ANDed, so every word must appear.
_PRECISE = "websearch_to_tsquery('english'::regconfig, %(query)s)"

# Broad pass. Terms ORed, so a passage matching most of them still surfaces.
_BROAD = "to_tsquery('english'::regconfig, %(query)s)"

# Words carried by almost every question. They add no signal but do drag the
# broad pass toward irrelevant passages, so they are stripped before ORing.
_NOISE = {
    "how", "do", "does", "did", "i", "we", "you", "to", "the", "a", "an",
    "is", "are", "was", "were", "can", "could", "should", "would", "what",
    "which", "where", "when", "why", "who", "in", "on", "at", "of", "for",
    "and", "or", "my", "me", "it", "this", "that", "please", "help", "with",
    "from", "there", "any", "get", "got", "NextGen2",
}


class PostgresFTS:
    """
    Keyword retrieval over help_chunks using Postgres full-text search.

    Satisfies the SearchStrategy protocol. Holds no state, so the single
    instance in the registry is safe to share across requests.
    """

    name = "fts"

    def search(self, query: str, limit: int = 3,
               approved_only: bool = True) -> list[Passage]:
        """Return the most relevant passages for a query, best first.

        Args:
            query: The user's question, in their own words.
            limit: Maximum number of passages to return.
            approved_only: When True, draft and retired articles are excluded.

        Returns:
            Passages ordered by descending relevance, each stamped with the
            pass that produced it. Empty means neither pass matched, which the
            caller records as a documentation gap rather than answering anyway.
        """
        q = (query or "").strip()
        if not q:
            return []

        rows = self._run(_PRECISE, q, limit, approved_only)
        if rows:
            return [self._to_passage(r, "precise") for r in rows]

        broad = self._broaden(q)
        if not broad:
            logger.info("Help search: %r contained no usable terms", q)
            return []

        rows = self._run(_BROAD, broad, limit, approved_only)
        if not rows:
            logger.info("Help search found nothing for %r (broadened to %r)", q, broad)
        return [self._to_passage(r, "broad") for r in rows]

    def _run(self, tsquery_expr: str, query: str, limit: int,
             approved_only: bool) -> list[dict]:
        """Execute one search pass.

        Args:
            tsquery_expr: SQL fragment producing the tsquery — _PRECISE or
                _BROAD. A module constant, never user input, so it is safe to
                format into the statement; the query text itself is always
                bound as a parameter.
            query: Text bound into the tsquery function.
            limit: Row limit.
            approved_only: Whether to exclude non-approved articles.

        Returns:
            Rows as dicts, ordered by descending score.
        """
        sql = _SQL.format(tsquery_expr=tsquery_expr)
        params = {"query": query, "limit": limit, "approved_only": approved_only}

        with get_conn() as conn:
            with conn.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(sql, params)
                cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
                return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]

    @staticmethod
    def _broaden(query: str) -> str:
        """Turn a question into an OR-joined tsquery expression.

        Strips punctuation and common question words, then joins what remains
        with '|'. Only word characters survive, so nothing the user types can
        reach to_tsquery as syntax — a stray ':' or '&' would otherwise raise.

        Args:
            query: The user's raw question.

        Returns:
            An expression such as 'schedule | jira | sync', or '' if the
            question carried no usable words at all.
        """
        words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+", query.lower())
        terms = [w for w in words if w not in _NOISE and len(w) > 2]
        if not terms:
            # Everything was filtered out — fall back to the raw words rather
            # than giving up on a question made entirely of common ones.
            terms = [w for w in words if len(w) > 2]

        seen: set[str] = set()
        ordered: list[str] = []
        for t in terms:
            if t not in seen:
                seen.add(t)
                ordered.append(t)
        return " | ".join(ordered)

    @staticmethod
    def _to_passage(row: dict, match_type: str) -> Passage:
        """Map one result row onto a Passage.

        Args:
            row: A row from _run, with the source columns joined in.
            match_type: 'precise' or 'broad' — which pass produced the row.
                Carried through because the two passes score on different
                scales and must never be compared against one another.

        Returns:
            A Passage carrying enough identity to cite its source.
        """
        is_article = row["source_type"] == "article"
        return Passage(
            chunk_id=row["chunk_id"],
            source_type=row["source_type"],
            source_id=(row["article_id"] if is_article else row["document_id"]) or 0,
            label=(row["article_slug"] if is_article else row["document_filename"]) or "",
            title=(row["article_title"] if is_article else row["document_filename"]) or "",
            heading=row["heading"],
            body=row["body"] or "",
            version=row["article_version"] if is_article else None,
            score=float(row["score"] or 0.0),
            match_type=match_type,
        )


================================================
FILE: backend/service/help_search/registry.py
================================================
"""
service/help_search/registry.py

The bounded set of retrieval strategies, and the one place a caller resolves
which is active.

Mirrors service/scheduler_jobs.py deliberately: an explicit dict rather than
an if/else, so what can run is enumerable and adding a strategy touches this
file only. Nothing above this line imports fts directly — that is what makes
a later move to vector retrieval a configuration change.

Adding vector search later:
    1. write service/help_search/qdrant.py with a class exposing
       `name` and `search(query, limit, approved_only)`
    2. add it to STRATEGIES below
    3. set HELP_SEARCH_STRATEGY=qdrant in .env
No route, service, chat tool or screen changes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

from core.settings import settings
from service.help_search.base import Passage, SearchStrategy
from service.help_search.fts import PostgresFTS

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# The explicit, bounded set. Keeping it a literal is itself a control: no
# retrieval path exists that is not listed here.
STRATEGIES: dict[str, SearchStrategy] = {
    strategy.name: strategy
    for strategy in (PostgresFTS(),)
}

# What to fall back to if the configured name is not registered — the one
# strategy with no external dependency, so help search degrades to working
# rather than to broken.
_DEFAULT = PostgresFTS.name


def get_strategy(name: str | None = None) -> SearchStrategy:
    """Resolve the active retrieval strategy.

    Args:
        name: Strategy key to use. Defaults to settings.help.search_strategy.

    Returns:
        The matching strategy. If the configured name is not registered, a
        warning is logged and the default is returned rather than raising —
        a mistyped setting should not take Help & Support offline.
    """
    key = (name or settings.help.search_strategy or _DEFAULT).lower()
    strategy = STRATEGIES.get(key)
    if strategy is None:
        logger.warning(
            "Help search strategy '%s' is not registered; falling back to '%s'. "
            "Registered strategies: %s",
            key, _DEFAULT, ", ".join(sorted(STRATEGIES)),
        )
        return STRATEGIES[_DEFAULT]
    return strategy


def search(query: str, limit: int | None = None,
           approved_only: bool = True) -> list[Passage]:
    """Search help content using the configured strategy.

    The single entry point every caller uses.

    Two filters are applied to what the strategy returns, in this order:

    1. min_score — an absolute floor. Zero by default, because full-text
       ranking is not calibrated: ts_rank_cd measures cover density, so a
       precise all-terms-required match scores an order of magnitude LOWER
       than a loose any-term match on the same corpus. Comparing either to a
       fixed number discards good results. The setting is retained because a
       vector strategy's cosine similarity IS calibrated 0-1, and there an
       absolute floor is exactly the right instrument.

    2. relative_floor — a proportion of the best result in this set. Within a
       single pass the scores ARE comparable, so a passage scoring a fraction
       of the top hit matched on one weak term and is noise. Dropping it
       matters: a local model given two good passages and one irrelevant one
       answers worse than a model given two.

    Args:
        query: The user's question, in their own words.
        limit: Maximum passages to return. Defaults to
            settings.help.max_passages.
        approved_only: When True, draft and retired articles are excluded.

    Returns:
        Passages ordered by descending relevance. Empty means nothing matched,
        which the caller records as a documentation gap rather than answering
        anyway.
    """
    strategy = get_strategy()
    passages = strategy.search(
        query,
        limit=limit or settings.help.max_passages,
        approved_only=approved_only,
    )
    if not passages:
        return []

    floor = settings.help.min_score
    kept = [p for p in passages if p.score >= floor]
    if not kept:
        logger.info(
            "Help search: %d result(s) for %r all scored below min_score %.4f "
            "(best %.6f) - treating as no answer",
            len(passages), query, floor, passages[0].score,
        )
        return []

    kept = _drop_weak_tail(kept, settings.help.relative_floor)

    logger.debug(
        "Help search %r -> %d passage(s), match_type=%s, top score %.6f",
        query, len(kept), kept[0].match_type, kept[0].score,
    )
    return kept


def _drop_weak_tail(passages: list[Passage], relative_floor: float) -> list[Passage]:
    """Remove passages scoring far below the best one in the same pass.

    Only compares passages sharing a match_type, since the precise and broad
    passes score on different scales and a cross-pass ratio would be
    meaningless. In practice a strategy returns one pass's results at a time,
    so this is a guard against a future strategy that mixes them.

    Args:
        passages: Results ordered by descending score.
        relative_floor: Fraction of the top score below which a passage is
            treated as noise. 0.0 disables the filter entirely.

    Returns:
        The passages worth showing, order preserved. The best result is always
        kept, whatever its absolute score.
    """
    if relative_floor <= 0 or not passages:
        return passages

    best_by_type: dict[str, float] = {}
    for p in passages:
        if p.score > best_by_type.get(p.match_type, 0.0):
            best_by_type[p.match_type] = p.score

    kept = [
        p for p in passages
        if p.score >= best_by_type[p.match_type] * relative_floor
    ]

    dropped = len(passages) - len(kept)
    if dropped:
        logger.debug(
            "Help search dropped %d weak passage(s) below %.0f%% of the top score",
            dropped, relative_floor * 100,
        )
    return kept

FILE: backend/service/ticketing/base.py

"""
service/ticketing/base.py

The contract every ticketing provider satisfies, and the shapes passed across
it.

This module is the seam that keeps NextGen2 independent of any one ticketing
system. Baxter runs ServiceNow; the demo runs Jira; a future deployment might
run neither. None of that reaches the routes, the database or the UI: they
deal in TicketRequest and TicketRef, and the provider is resolved at runtime
from configuration.

Nothing here imports urllib, a Jira client, or anything else
implementation-specific. That is deliberate — it is what makes the seam real
rather than nominal. If a provider-specific import ever appears above this
line, the abstraction has quietly stopped working, and test_ticketing.py
exists to catch exactly that.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Optional, Protocol


class TicketingError(RuntimeError):
    """
    Raised when a ticket cannot be created.

    Carries a message fit to show a user. The caller records the failure on
    the support_tickets row (status='failed', submit_error set) rather than
    discarding it, so a ticket that could not be filed is still visible
    afterwards instead of silently lost.
    """


@dataclass
class TicketRequest:
    """
    What the user is asking for, in NextGen2's own terms.

    Deliberately free of any provider's vocabulary. There is no issue type, no
    incident-versus-request, no priority scheme here — those are each
    provider's own model, and translating into them is the provider's job.
    The user picks a plain-English category and is never asked to understand
    ITIL or Jira's schema.

    Attributes:
        category: Plain-English kind of request, e.g. 'how-to', 'bug',
            'access', 'data'. Providers map this onto their own object model.
        summary: One-line title.
        description: The user's own account of the problem.
        raised_by: Who is asking. Currently supplied by the caller and
            defaulting to 'anonymous', matching how accepted_by works
            elsewhere in NextGen2; it becomes a real identity when SSO lands.
        context: Automatically captured technical detail — route,
            application_id, execution_id, browser, last error. Collected by
            the UI so the ticket is actionable without a follow-up
            conversation. Rendered into the ticket body by the provider.
    """

    category: str
    summary: str
    description: str = ""
    raised_by: str = "anonymous"
    context: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class TicketRef:
    """
    Where the created ticket lives, in the external system.

    Intentionally opaque: an identifier and a link, with no assumption about
    their format. 'KVSUP-14' and 'INC0012345' are both just strings here,
    which is why moving between ticketing systems needs no schema migration.

    Attributes:
        provider: Which provider created it — matches a key in registry.py.
        external_ref: The external identifier, as that system displays it.
        external_url: Deep link to the ticket, or None if the provider cannot
            construct one.
        external_status: The external system's own status at creation time,
            if it reports one.
        raw: The provider's unmodified response, kept for diagnostics. Never
            parsed by callers — anything callers need is promoted to a field.
    """

    provider: str
    external_ref: str
    external_url: Optional[str] = None
    external_status: Optional[str] = None
    raw: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


class TicketProvider(Protocol):
    """
    The contract a ticketing implementation satisfies.

    Duck-typed via typing.Protocol, matching the pattern already used for
    scheduler jobs and help-search strategies: an implementation inherits
    nothing, it just provides these members. Adding ServiceNow is a new class
    plus one entry in registry.py.
    """

    name: str

    def create_ticket(self, request: TicketRequest) -> TicketRef:
        """Create a ticket in the external system.

        Args:
            request: What the user is asking for, in NextGen2's terms.

        Returns:
            A reference to the created ticket.

        Raises:
            TicketingError: If the provider is misconfigured or the external
                system rejected the request. The message is fit to show a
                user.
        """
        ...

    def check_config(self) -> None:
        """Validate configuration without creating anything.

        Lets a misconfiguration surface on a preflight check rather than at
        the moment a user is trying to report a problem — which is the worst
        possible time to discover that the project key is unset.

        Raises:
            TicketingError: If required configuration is missing or unusable.
        """
        ...

FILE: backend/service/ticketing/fake.py

"""
service/ticketing/fake.py

An in-memory ticketing provider.

Not a mock bolted on beside the code — a real implementation of the same
contract, registered alongside Jira. It earns its place twice:

1. It is the test that the abstraction is genuine. If any Jira-specific
   import, field or assumption has leaked upward into the route or the
   service layer, raising a ticket with TICKETING_PROVIDER=fake breaks, and
   the leak is found immediately rather than during a ServiceNow migration.

2. It makes the support flow demonstrable and testable with no Atlassian
   account, no network, and no risk of littering a real project with test
   issues.

It is safe to leave registered in production: selecting it requires setting
TICKETING_PROVIDER=fake explicitly, and it logs loudly that nothing left the
process.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from itertools import count

from service.ticketing.base import TicketRef, TicketRequest

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class FakeTicketProvider:
    """
    Records tickets in memory and returns plausible references.

    Attributes:
        created: Every request handled by this instance, in order. Tests read
            it to assert what the caller actually sent.
    """

    name = "fake"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initialise an empty in-memory ticket store."""
        self.created: list[TicketRequest] = []
        self._counter = count(1)

    def create_ticket(self, request: TicketRequest) -> TicketRef:
        """Record a ticket without contacting anything.

        Args:
            request: What the user is asking for, in NextGen2's terms.

        Returns:
            A reference with a synthetic identifier. external_url is None,
            because there is nothing to link to — callers must cope with a
            missing link, and this is what proves they do.
        """
        self.created.append(request)
        ref = f"FAKE-{next(self._counter)}"
        logger.warning(
            "FakeTicketProvider recorded %s in memory (category=%s, raised_by=%s). "
            "No ticket was created in any external system.",
            ref, request.category, request.raised_by,
        )
        return TicketRef(
            provider=self.name,
            external_ref=ref,
            external_url=None,
            external_status="recorded",
            raw={"summary": request.summary, "context": request.context},
        )

    def check_config(self) -> None:
        """Validate configuration. There is none, so this always succeeds."""
        return None

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Discard recorded tickets, so one test cannot affect the next."""
        self.created.clear()

FILE: backend/service/ticketing/jira.py
================================================
"""
service/ticketing/jira.py

Creates support tickets as Jira issues.

This is NextGen2's first WRITE to Jira. Everything before it — the source
adapter, the sync engine — only reads. Two consequences shape this file:

1. The description field on Jira Cloud is ADF (Atlassian Document Format), a
   nested JSON tree, not a string. service/jira_adapter.py flattens ADF on the
   way in; this builds it on the way out. Posting a plain string to
   /rest/api/3/issue fails with an unhelpful error, so _text_to_adf exists.

2. Support tickets must NOT land in the requirements project. The sync engine
   runs JQL over that project and treats what it finds as requirements: a
   support ticket filed there would be picked up and generate test cases from
   itself, and would appear in the traceability matrix an auditor reads. The
   project key therefore has no default, and _config() refuses to proceed if
   it matches the configured requirements project.

Credentials are shared with the source adapter — same Atlassian site, same
account — and read from settings.jira. The destination project and issue type
are separate, and come from settings.ticketing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import logging
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from service.ticketing.base import TicketingError, TicketRef, TicketRequest

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_TIMEOUT = 30

# Applied to every issue NextGen2 files, so support tickets raised from the
# product can be found, reported on, and excluded from other queries.
_BASE_LABEL = "NextGen2-support"


@dataclass
class _JiraTicketConfig:
    """Resolved configuration for the Jira write path.

    Attributes:
        base_url: Atlassian site URL, no trailing slash.
        email: Atlassian account email used for basic auth.
        api_token: Atlassian API token.
        project_key: Project support tickets are created in.
        issue_type: Issue type to create.
    """

    base_url: str
    email: str
    api_token: str
    project_key: str
    issue_type: str


class JiraTicketProvider:
    """
    Creates support tickets as issues in a Jira project.

    Holds no state — configuration is resolved per call, so a change to .env
    takes effect on restart without any cached client to invalidate.
    """

    name = "jira"

    def create_ticket(self, request: TicketRequest) -> TicketRef:
        """Create a Jira issue for a support request.

        Args:
            request: What the user is asking for, in NextGen2's terms.

        Returns:
            A reference carrying the Jira key and a browse URL.

        Raises:
            TicketingError: If Jira is not configured, the destination project
                is unsafe, or Jira rejected the request.
        """
        cfg = self._config()

        payload = {
            "fields": {
                "project": {"key": cfg.project_key},
                "issuetype": {"name": cfg.issue_type},
                "summary": self._summary(request),
                "description": _text_to_adf(self._body(request)),
                # The category is carried as a label rather than mapped onto a
                # Jira issue type. Mapping would mean assuming types like
                # 'Bug' and 'Service Request' exist in whichever project this
                # points at, and a missing type fails the create with a schema
                # error. A label always works, and the mapping can be made
                # explicit later once the destination project is fixed.
                "labels": [_BASE_LABEL, f"NextGen2-{_slug(request.category)}"],
            }
        }

        data = self._post(cfg, "/rest/api/3/issue", payload)

        key = data.get("key") or ""
        if not key:
            raise TicketingError(
                "Jira accepted the request but returned no issue key. "
                "The ticket may or may not have been created — check the "
                f"{cfg.project_key} project before retrying."
            )

        logger.info("Created Jira support ticket %s for %s", key, request.raised_by)
        return TicketRef(
            provider=self.name,
            external_ref=key,
            external_url=f"{cfg.base_url}/browse/{key}",
            raw=data,
        )

    def check_config(self) -> None:
        """Validate configuration without creating an issue.

        Raises:
            TicketingError: If credentials or the destination project are
                missing or unsafe.
        """
        self._config()

    # ── internals ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @staticmethod
    def _config() -> _JiraTicketConfig:
        """Resolve and sanity-check the write configuration.

        Returns:
            The resolved configuration.

        Raises:
            TicketingError: If credentials are missing, the support project
                key is unset, or it matches the requirements project.
        """
        from core.settings import settings

        j, t = settings.jira, settings.ticketing

        if not (j.base_url and j.email and j.api_token):
            raise TicketingError(
                "Jira is not configured. Set JIRA_BASE_URL, JIRA_EMAIL and "
                "JIRA_API_TOKEN in .env."
            )

        if not t.jira_project_key:
            raise TicketingError(
                "No Jira project is configured for support tickets. Set "
                "JIRA_SUPPORT_PROJECT_KEY in .env to a project separate from "
                "the requirements project."
            )

        # The guard that matters. Filing support tickets into the project the
        # sync engine reads would turn them into requirements.
        if t.jira_project_key.strip().upper() == (j.project_key or "").strip().upper():
            raise TicketingError(
                f"JIRA_SUPPORT_PROJECT_KEY is set to '{t.jira_project_key}', which "
                f"is also the requirements project. Support tickets filed there "
                f"would be read back as requirements by the Jira sync. Use a "
                f"separate project."
            )

        return _JiraTicketConfig(
            base_url=j.base_url.rstrip("/"),
            email=j.email,
            api_token=j.api_token,
            project_key=t.jira_project_key.strip(),
            issue_type=t.jira_issue_type,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _post(cfg: _JiraTicketConfig, path: str, payload: dict) -> dict:
        """POST JSON to Jira and return the decoded response.

        Args:
            cfg: Resolved configuration.
            path: API path beginning with '/'.
            payload: Request body.

        Returns:
            The decoded JSON response.

        Raises:
            TicketingError: On any HTTP or transport failure. Jira's own error
                messages are extracted and surfaced, because they name the
                actual problem ("issue type is required", "project not found")
                far better than a status code does.
        """
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{cfg.base_url}{path}",
            method="POST",
            data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
            headers={
                "Authorization": _auth_header(cfg),
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
                "Accept": "application/json",
            },
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=_TIMEOUT) as resp:
                body = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
                return json.loads(body) if body else {}
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            raise TicketingError(_http_error_message(e, cfg)) from e
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            raise TicketingError(
                f"Could not reach Jira at {cfg.base_url}: {e.reason}"
            ) from e

    @staticmethod
    def _summary(request: TicketRequest) -> str:
        """Build the issue title.

        Args:
            request: The support request.

        Returns:
            The user's summary, prefixed so NextGen2 tickets are recognisable in
            a shared queue, and truncated to Jira's 255-character limit.
        """
        text = (request.summary or "").strip() or "NextGen2 support request"
        prefixed = f"[NextGen2] {text}"
        return prefixed[:255]

    @staticmethod
    def _body(request: TicketRequest) -> str:
        """Build the issue description.

        Args:
            request: The support request.

        Returns:
            The user's description followed by the captured technical context,
            so whoever picks the ticket up has what they need without asking.
        """
        parts = [(request.description or "").strip() or "(no description given)"]

        parts.append("")
        parts.append("--- Raised from NextGen2 ---")
        parts.append(f"Category: {request.category}")
        parts.append(f"Raised by: {request.raised_by}")

        if request.context:
            parts.append("")
            parts.append("Context:")
            for key in sorted(request.context):
                value = request.context[key]
                if value in (None, "", [], {}):
                    continue
                parts.append(f"- {key}: {value}")

        return "\n".join(parts)


# ── module helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _auth_header(cfg: _JiraTicketConfig) -> str:
    """Build the basic auth header.

    Args:
        cfg: Resolved configuration.

    Returns:
        A 'Basic ...' header value.
    """
    raw = f"{cfg.email}:{cfg.api_token}".encode("utf-8")
    return "Basic " + base64.b64encode(raw).decode("ascii")


def _text_to_adf(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Convert plain text into an Atlassian Document Format document.

    Jira Cloud's v3 API will not accept a string for `description`; it expects
    an ADF tree. This produces the minimal valid shape: one paragraph per
    line, with blank lines preserved as empty paragraphs so the context block
    stays readable.

    Args:
        text: Plain text, newline-separated.

    Returns:
        An ADF document node suitable for the description field.
    """
    content: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for line in (text or "").split("\n"):
        if line.strip():
            content.append({
                "type": "paragraph",
                "content": [{"type": "text", "text": line}],
            })
        else:
            # An empty paragraph — ADF rejects a text node with an empty
            # string, so the paragraph carries no content at all.
            content.append({"type": "paragraph"})

    if not content:
        content = [{"type": "paragraph"}]

    return {"type": "doc", "version": 1, "content": content}


def _slug(value: str) -> str:
    """Reduce a category to a label-safe token.

    Jira labels cannot contain spaces, so a category like 'how to' would be
    rejected outright.

    Args:
        value: The plain-English category.

    Returns:
        A lowercase token containing only letters, digits and hyphens.
    """
    cleaned = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "-" for c in (value or "").lower())
    while "--" in cleaned:
        cleaned = cleaned.replace("--", "-")
    return cleaned.strip("-") or "general"


def _http_error_message(e: urllib.error.HTTPError, cfg: _JiraTicketConfig) -> str:
    """Turn a Jira HTTP error into a message that names the actual problem.

    Args:
        e: The raised HTTPError.
        cfg: Resolved configuration, for naming the project in the message.

    Returns:
        A message fit to show a user.
    """
    detail = ""
    try:
        payload = json.loads(e.read().decode("utf-8"))
        messages = list(payload.get("errorMessages") or [])
        messages += [f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in (payload.get("errors") or {}).items()]
        detail = "; ".join(m for m in messages if m)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the body may not be JSON at all
        detail = ""

    if e.code in (401, 403):
        return (
            "Jira rejected the credentials or the account lacks permission to "
            f"create issues in {cfg.project_key}." + (f" {detail}" if detail else "")
        )
    if e.code == 404:
        return (
            f"Jira project '{cfg.project_key}' was not found, or the account "
            "cannot see it." + (f" {detail}" if detail else "")
        )
    if e.code == 400:
        return (
            f"Jira rejected the ticket. This is usually an issue type that "
            f"does not exist in {cfg.project_key} — currently configured as "
            f"'{cfg.issue_type}'." + (f" Jira said: {detail}" if detail else "")
        )
    return f"Jira returned HTTP {e.code}." + (f" {detail}" if detail else "")

FILE: backend/service/ticketing/registry.py
================================================
"""
service/ticketing/registry.py

The bounded set of ticketing providers, and the one place a caller resolves
which is active.

Mirrors service/scheduler_jobs.py deliberately: an explicit dict rather than
an if/else, so what can run is enumerable and adding a provider touches this
file only. In a regulated environment that enumerability is a property worth
having — the set of external systems NextGen2 can write to is a short list
anyone can read, not something inferred from control flow.

Nothing above this line imports jira.py. That is what makes moving to
ServiceNow a configuration change:

    1. write service/ticketing/servicenow.py with a class exposing
       `name`, `create_ticket(request)` and `check_config()`
    2. add it to PROVIDERS below
    3. set TICKETING_PROVIDER=servicenow in .env

No schema migration, no route change, no UI change. support_tickets already
stores `provider` and an opaque `external_ref`, so existing rows stay valid
and readable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

from core.settings import settings
from service.ticketing.base import (
    TicketingError,
    TicketProvider,
    TicketRef,
    TicketRequest,
)
from service.ticketing.fake import FakeTicketProvider
from service.ticketing.jira import JiraTicketProvider

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# The explicit, bounded set. Keeping it a literal is itself a control: there
# is no path by which NextGen2 writes to a system not named here.
PROVIDERS: dict[str, TicketProvider] = {
    provider.name: provider
    for provider in (JiraTicketProvider(), FakeTicketProvider())
}


def get_provider(name: str | None = None) -> TicketProvider:
    """Resolve the active ticketing provider.

    Args:
        name: Provider key to use. Defaults to settings.ticketing.provider.

    Returns:
        The matching provider.

    Raises:
        TicketingError: If the configured name is not registered. Unlike help
            search — where an unknown strategy falls back to a working default
            — this raises. Silently filing a ticket somewhere other than where
            the operator configured it would be worse than not filing it, and
            the failure is recorded on the support_tickets row either way.
    """
    key = (name or settings.ticketing.provider or "").lower().strip()
    provider = PROVIDERS.get(key)
    if provider is None:
        raise TicketingError(
            f"Ticketing provider '{key}' is not registered. "
            f"Set TICKETING_PROVIDER to one of: {', '.join(sorted(PROVIDERS))}."
        )
    return provider


def create_ticket(request: TicketRequest,
                  provider_name: str | None = None) -> TicketRef:
    """Create a ticket using the configured provider.

    The single entry point callers use. Callers never import a provider
    module, never name Jira, and never branch on which system is in use.

    Args:
        request: What the user is asking for, in NextGen2's terms.
        provider_name: Override the configured provider. Used by tests; not
            exposed through the API, since letting a request choose where it
            is filed would defeat the point of configuring it.

    Returns:
        A reference to the created ticket.

    Raises:
        TicketingError: If the provider is unknown, misconfigured, or the
            external system rejected the request.
    """
    provider = get_provider(provider_name)
    logger.info(
        "Creating ticket via provider '%s' (category=%s)",
        provider.name, request.category,
    )
    return provider.create_ticket(request)


def check_config(provider_name: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Validate the active provider's configuration without creating anything.

    Intended for a preflight check, so a missing project key surfaces on
    startup or a health endpoint rather than at the moment a user is trying to
    report a problem.

    Args:
        provider_name: Override the configured provider.

    Raises:
        TicketingError: If the provider is unknown or misconfigured.
    """
    get_provider(provider_name).check_config()

"""
test_data/loader.py

Loads externalised test data for a script or crawl.

SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH, per application:

    test_data/applications/app_<application_id>.json

    {
      "application_id": 7,
      "environments": {
        "default": {
          "username": "...",
          "password": {"_encrypted": true, "alg": "fernet", "value": "..."},
          "ItemNumber": "48166329",
          "forms": {
            "Sales Order Entry":      {"ItemNumber": "1001-STAR"},
            "Inventory Adjustment":   {"ItemNumber": "2005-CHEM"}
          }
        }
      }
    }

Resolution for any key (e.g. "ItemNumber"), given a target_flow:
    1. environments.<env>.forms.<target_flow>.<key>   — most specific, wins
    2. environments.<env>.<key>                        — app-level default

MATCHING A target_flow TO A "forms" ENTRY — two supported styles:
    (a) Short destination style: target_flow IS the form name, e.g.
        target_flow = "Sales Order Entry". Matched by exact equality.
    (b) Ordered step-list style: target_flow is a full multi-line manual
        procedure, e.g. "Launch the url\nEnter SSO Username\n...Click on
        Sales Order Entry.\n...Enter Item Number in Item Number field...".
        This is what the New Test Suite wizard sends when a reviewer pastes
        one step per line rather than a short navigation phrase (see
        agents/crawl_agent.py's _is_step_list handling). An exact-equality
        match against a short form name like "Sales Order Entry" will NEVER
        succeed here, even though the procedure clearly targets that form
        — the saved override would be silently ignored, and the crawl
        would fall back to typing synthetic placeholder values instead of
        the real ones a reviewer already saved. This was confirmed live:
        a reviewer saved forms."Sales Order Entry".SoldTo, but a step-list
        target_flow caused SoldTo to resolve to nothing, and the crawl
        agent typed "1000" and failed JDE's address-type validation.

        To support this style too, when no exact match is found, this
        module falls back to a substring match: the LONGEST form name that
        appears anywhere inside target_flow (case-insensitive) is used.
        Longest wins so a more specific name (e.g. "Standard Order SO")
        is preferred over a shorter, more generic one (e.g. "Sales") if
        both happen to appear in the same procedure text.

    (c) Tolerant match (added after a live failure): reviewers rarely type
        the form name in the procedure exactly as it is saved in the Test
        Data screen. A saved form "Inventory Adjustment" never appeared
        verbatim in a step list that said "Click on Inventory Adjust" —
        the JDE menu label is shorter — so styles (a) and (b) both missed,
        the saved Branch/Plant/Quantity/Lot values were silently dropped,
        and the crawl typed synthetic values that JDE rejected. The form
        name is therefore also matched word-by-word, case/punctuation
        insensitive, with each word allowed to be a prefix of the word in
        the procedure (or vice-versa, minimum 4 letters), and the words
        must appear consecutively on ONE line of the procedure. No form
        names are hardcoded anywhere — it works for any form name.

    (d) Field-name match (no dependence on the form's name at all): if the
        form name is not recognisable in the procedure, each form is scored
        by how many of ITS OWN saved field names (e.g. "Branch/Plant",
        "ItemNumber", "Lot/Serial") are mentioned in the procedure, again
        word-tolerant and on a single line. The form with the clearly
        highest score wins. A tie, or a single weak hit, matches nothing —
        guessing wrong would type another form's values, which is worse
        than typing none. Field names come from the saved JSON, never from
        code, so this works for any scenario you add through the UI.

"forms" is popped off before returning, so nothing downstream (get_data(),
a crawl agent, _test_env_for()) ever sees nesting or the word "forms" —
every value that leaves this function is flat.

There is deliberately no second file, no test_data/scenarios/ directory,
and no "link this scenario to a file" step. Everything for one application
lives in this one file, edited through GET/PUT /v1/test-data/app. A form
that needs its own value is just another entry under "forms" — never a
new file, never a new mechanism.

MULTI-ACTOR PROCEDURES — "personas" block:
    A procedure that must run as more than one identity in the SAME
    continuous script/run (e.g. a requester creates a record, an
    approver later approves it, an admin performs a final override) needs
    more than one set of stored credentials for one application. These
    live under an optional "personas" block, alongside "forms":

    {
      "application_id": 7,
      "environments": {
        "default": {
          "username": "...",             <- unchanged: the DEFAULT identity,
          "password": {...},                used for the first login of any
                                             script, the SSO precheck, and
                                             every existing single-user flow
          "personas": {
            "requester": {"username": "...", "password": {...}},
            "approver":  {"username": "...", "password": {...}},
            "admin":     {"username": "...", "password": {...}}
          }
        }
      }
    }

    There is NO fixed list of role names anywhere in this module (or
    anywhere downstream) — "personas" is a plain dict, and any key is a
    valid persona name. A procedure needing a 4th, 5th or 10th role is
    purely a JSON edit here; no code change anywhere is required.

    Each persona's username/password is flattened into two plain keys
    before this function returns: "<persona>_username" and
    "<persona>_password" (e.g. "approver_username", "approver_password"),
    decrypting the password the same way a flat top-level password is
    decrypted. See _flatten_personas() below. These then flow through
    service/auth_gateway.py's existing *generic* TEST_<UPPER_KEY> export
    unchanged — that function has no special-case knowledge of personas
    at all, since every key it sees is already flat by the time it gets
    here.

    "personas" is popped off before returning, exactly like "forms" — it
    never reaches get_data() as a nested key.
"""
import json
import logging
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from cryptography.fernet import Fernet, InvalidToken

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
APP_DIR = HERE / "applications"
LEGACY_APP_DIR = HERE.parents[1] / "test_data" / "applications"
DEFAULT_ENV = "default"


def load_test_data(
    application_id: Optional[int] = None,
    environment: Optional[str] = None,
    target_flow: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Return this application's test data, resolved to one flat dict.

    Args:
        application_id: Which application's app_<id>.json to read. None
            returns {} — matches every existing caller's fallback pattern.
        environment: Which environment block to read. Defaults to "default".
        target_flow: The flow/screen this crawl or script belongs to — see
            the module docstring for the two supported styles (short
            destination name, or a full multi-line step-list procedure
            that mentions the form name somewhere in its text). When a
            "forms" entry resolves (exact or substring match), those
            values override the app-level ones on a shared key. No match
            (or target_flow=None) means the flat app-level values are
            used untouched — this keeps every existing app without a
            "forms" block working exactly as before.

    Returns:
        A flat dict of key -> value, secrets decrypted. Never contains a
        "forms" key.
    """
    if application_id is None:
        return {}
    env_key = (environment or "").strip() or DEFAULT_ENV
    doc = _read_app_file(application_id)
    env_data = dict((doc.get("environments") or {}).get(env_key) or {})
    forms = env_data.pop("forms", None)
    personas = env_data.pop("personas", None)
    override = _resolve_form_override(forms, target_flow)
    if override:
        env_data.update(override)
    flat = {k: _decrypt_if_needed(v) for k, v in env_data.items()}
    flat.update(_flatten_personas(personas))
    logger.info(
        "test_data: app=%s env=%s resolved keys=%s",
        application_id, env_key, sorted(str(k) for k in flat.keys()),
    )
    return flat


def _flatten_personas(personas) -> dict:
    """
    Flatten environments.<env>.personas.<name>.{username,password} into
    flat "<name>_username" / "<name>_password" keys.

    See the module docstring ("MULTI-ACTOR PROCEDURES") for the full
    shape. This function has no fixed list of role names — any key under
    "personas" is flattened the same way, so adding a new role to a
    procedure is purely a JSON edit, never a code change here or in any
    downstream caller (service/auth_gateway.py's TEST_* export already
    handles an arbitrary flat key generically).

    Args:
        personas: The environment's "personas" dict (already popped off
            of env_data by the caller), or None/empty if this application
            has no named personas configured at all — single-identity
            applications are completely unaffected and this returns {}.

    Returns:
        Flat dict, e.g. {"approver_username": "...", "approver_password":
        "...", ...}. Never contains a "personas" key, and never contains
        a bare "username"/"password" key (those remain the separate,
        unchanged default-identity keys this function does not touch).
    """
    if not isinstance(personas, dict) or not personas:
        return {}
    out = {}
    for name, creds in personas.items():
        if not isinstance(creds, dict):
            continue
        norm_name = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", str(name).strip()).strip("_").lower()
        if not norm_name:
            continue
        if "username" in creds:
            out[f"{norm_name}_username"] = creds.get("username")
        if "password" in creds:
            out[f"{norm_name}_password"] = _decrypt_if_needed(creds.get("password"))
    return out


def _tokens(text: str) -> list:
    """Lower-case alphanumeric words of text; punctuation/whitespace dropped."""
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", (text or "").lower())


def _word_match(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """
    True if two words are the same, or one is a prefix of the other.

    The prefix rule needs both sides to be at least 4 letters so short
    words ("so", "to", "po") can never match something unrelated. This is
    what lets "adjust" (menu label) match "adjustment" (saved form name).
    """
    if a == b:
        return True
    if min(len(a), len(b)) < 4:
        return False
    return a.startswith(b) or b.startswith(a)


def _form_match_score(form_name: str, flow_lines: list) -> Optional[tuple]:
    """
    Score how well form_name appears in the procedure, or None for no match.

    All words of form_name must appear consecutively (word_match-tolerant)
    on a single line. Returns (word_count, char_count, last_line_index) so
    the caller can prefer: more specific names first, then the occurrence
    closest to the end of the procedure.
    """
    want = _tokens(form_name)
    if not want:
        return None
    best_line = None
    for idx, line_tokens in enumerate(flow_lines):
        n = len(want)
        for i in range(0, len(line_tokens) - n + 1):
            if all(_word_match(want[j], line_tokens[i + j]) for j in range(n)):
                best_line = idx
                break
    if best_line is None:
        return None
    return (len(want), len("".join(want)), best_line)


def _key_tokens(key: str) -> list:
    """
    Words of a saved field name. Splits camelCase before lower-casing so
    "ItemNumber" -> ["item", "number"], "Branch/Plant" -> ["branch", "plant"],
    "TEST_UNIT_PRICE" -> ["test", "unit", "price"].
    """
    spaced = re.sub(r"(?<=[a-z0-9])(?=[A-Z])", " ", str(key or ""))
    return _tokens(spaced)


def _resolve_by_field_names(forms: dict, flow_lines: list) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Pick the form whose saved field names are mentioned most in the procedure.

    Returns the form name, or None when there is no clear winner: needs a
    strictly higher score than every other form, and either 2+ fields hit or
    at least half of that form's fields hit.
    """
    scores = {}
    for name, value in forms.items():
        if not isinstance(value, dict) or not value:
            continue
        hits = 0
        for key in value.keys():
            want = _key_tokens(key)
            if not want:
                continue
            n = len(want)
            found = any(
                all(_word_match(want[j], line[i + j]) for j in range(n))
                for line in flow_lines
                for i in range(0, len(line) - n + 1)
            )
            if found:
                hits += 1
        scores[name] = (hits, len(value))
    if not scores:
        return None
    ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1][0], reverse=True)
    top_name, (top_hits, top_total) = ranked[0]
    if top_hits == 0:
        return None
    if len(ranked) > 1 and ranked[1][1][0] == top_hits:
        return None  # tie -> ambiguous, do not guess
    if top_hits < 2 and top_hits * 2 < top_total:
        return None  # weak single hit
    return top_name


def _resolve_form_override(forms, target_flow: Optional[str]) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Find which forms.<name> block applies to this target_flow.

    See the module docstring ("MATCHING A target_flow TO A 'forms' ENTRY")
    for the three matching styles, tried in this order:
      (a) exact name, (b) case-insensitive substring, (c) tolerant
      word-by-word match.

    Args:
        forms: The environment's "forms" dict (already popped off of
            env_data by the caller), or None/empty if the app has no
            per-form overrides configured at all.
        target_flow: See load_test_data's docstring.

    Returns:
        The matching form's dict of overrides, or None if nothing matched
        (including when forms itself is empty/absent).
    """
    if not target_flow or not isinstance(forms, dict) or not forms:
        return None

    # (a) Short destination style — cheapest, most common case.
    exact = forms.get(target_flow)
    if isinstance(exact, dict):
        logger.info("test_data: form override matched exactly: %r", target_flow)
        return exact

    # (b) Form name appears verbatim somewhere in a longer procedure.
    # Longest name wins so "Standard Order SO" beats "Sales".
    flow_lower = target_flow.lower()
    best_name = None
    for name, value in forms.items():
        if not isinstance(value, dict):
            continue
        if name.lower() in flow_lower:
            if best_name is None or len(name) > len(best_name):
                best_name = name
    if best_name:
        logger.info("test_data: form override matched by substring: %r", best_name)
        return forms.get(best_name)

    # (c) Tolerant word-by-word match, per line of the procedure.
    flow_lines = [_tokens(line) for line in target_flow.splitlines()]
    best_name, best_score = None, None
    for name, value in forms.items():
        if not isinstance(value, dict):
            continue
        score = _form_match_score(name, flow_lines)
        if score is not None and (best_score is None or score > best_score):
            best_name, best_score = name, score
    if best_name:
        logger.info("test_data: form override matched by tolerant match: %r", best_name)
        return forms.get(best_name)

    # (d) Field-name match — independent of how the form itself is named.
    best_name = _resolve_by_field_names(forms, flow_lines)
    if best_name:
        logger.info("test_data: form override matched by field names: %r", best_name)
        return forms.get(best_name)

    logger.warning(
        "test_data: no 'forms' entry matched the target flow. Saved forms: %s. "
        "Only application-level values will be used.",
        sorted(str(k) for k in forms.keys()),
    )
    return None


def _read_app_file(application_id: int) -> dict:
    """Find and parse app_<id>.json, checking the legacy path as a fallback."""
    path = APP_DIR / f"app_{application_id}.json"
    if not path.exists():
        legacy = LEGACY_APP_DIR / f"app_{application_id}.json"
        path = legacy if legacy.exists() else None
    if not path:
        return {}
    return _read(path)


def _read(path: Path) -> dict:
    with open(path) as f:
        d = json.load(f)
    d.pop("_comment", None)
    return d


def _fernet() -> Optional[Fernet]:
    key = (os.environ.get("TEST_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY") or "").strip()
    if not key:
        return None
    return Fernet(key.encode("utf-8"))


def _decrypt_if_needed(value):
    """Decrypt a {"_encrypted": true, "alg": "fernet", "value": "..."} payload."""
    if not (
        isinstance(value, dict)
        and value.get("_encrypted") is True
        and value.get("alg") == "fernet"
        and "value" in value
    ):
        return value
    fernet = _fernet()
    if fernet is None:
        return value
    try:
        return fernet.decrypt(value["value"].encode("utf-8")).decode("utf-8")
    except InvalidToken:
        return value

import './globals.css'
// Self-hosted Tabler icons webfont. Served from our own bundle instead of the
// jsDelivr CDN, so corporate Tracking Prevention / proxies can't block it.
import '@tabler/icons-webfont/dist/tabler-icons.min.css'
import Providers from '../components/Providers/Providers'
import AppShell from '../components/AppShell/AppShell'

export const metadata = {
  title: 'NextGen2 — Test Intelligence',
  description: 'AI-powered test automation platform',
}

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    // suppressHydrationWarning: the inline script below rewrites data-theme
    // from localStorage before React hydrates, so the server value ("dark")
    // and the client value can differ by design. This silences only that
    // element's attribute mismatch, not real hydration bugs elsewhere.
    <html lang="en" data-theme="dark" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <head>
        {/* Apply saved theme before paint to avoid a flash */}
        <script
          dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
            __html: `(function(){try{var t=localStorage.getItem('kavach-theme')||'dark';document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme',t);}catch(e){}})();`,
          }}
        />
      </head>
      <body>
        {/*
          Providers wraps the entire application with:
            MsalProvider  — one PublicClientApplication, initialised once.
            AuthGuard     — redirects to Entra login if not authenticated;
                            covers every page without per-page logic.
        */}
        <Providers>
          <AppShell>{children}</AppShell>
        </Providers>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}

FILE: frontend/app/page.js

import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'

/**
 * app/page.js
 *
 * Root route ("/"). Kavach has no standalone home page — every visit to
 * "/" continues straight to "/dashboard", which opens on the Leadership
 * view by default (see app/dashboard/page.js).
 *
 * Why this also fixes the "not authenticated" case, not just the
 * logged-in one:
 *
 * AuthGuard (components/AuthGuard/AuthGuard.jsx) wraps every page via
 * the root layout and, when unauthenticated, triggers an Entra login
 * redirect using InteractionType.Redirect. MSAL then returns the user to
 * whatever URL originally triggered that redirect — navigateToLoginRequestUrl:
 * true in lib/msalConfig.js. Because this redirect() call runs on the
 * server before any client-side code (including AuthGuard) executes for
 * "/", an unauthenticated visit to "/" never actually reaches AuthGuard
 * at "/" — Next.js has already sent the browser to "/dashboard" by then.
 * AuthGuard therefore evaluates (and MSAL remembers) "/dashboard" as the
 * request URL, so a fresh login lands the user there directly instead of
 * back on "/".
 *
 * No 'use client' directive needed: redirect() from next/navigation is
 * designed to run in a Server Component and works via Next's routing
 * layer, not React state — nothing here touches MSAL or auth state
 * directly, so it can't conflict with AuthGuard's own logic.
 */
export default function RootPage() {
  redirect('/dashboard')
}

'use client'

/**
 * app/applications/page.js
 *
 * Real applications screen (replaces the stub).
 *   - Lists all applications from GET /v1/applications
 *   - "Add application" opens a form that POSTs to /v1/applications
 *   - Each row links to that application's detail
 *
 * Everything here is live against the backend — no placeholder data.
 */

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import Link from 'next/link'
import { getApplications, createApplication, setApplicationSsoGateway, archiveApplication, deleteApplication } from '../../lib/api'

export default function ApplicationsPage() {
  const [removing, setRemoving] = useState(null)
  const [apps, setApps]       = useState([])
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)
  const [error, setError]     = useState(null)

  // add-form state
  const [showForm, setShowForm]   = useState(false)
  const [name, setName]           = useState('')
  const [baseUrl, setBaseUrl]     = useState('')
  const [owner, setOwner]         = useState('')
  const [requiresSsoGateway, setRequiresSsoGateway] = useState(false)
  const [saving, setSaving]       = useState(false)
  const [ssoSavingId, setSsoSavingId] = useState(null)
  const [formError, setFormError] = useState(null)

  async function load() {
    setLoading(true)
    setError(null)
    try {
      const data = await getApplications()
      setApps(Array.isArray(data) ? data : [])
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err.message)
    } finally {
      setLoading(false)
    }
  }

  useEffect(() => { load() }, [])

  async function handleAdd() {
    if (!name.trim()) {
      setFormError('Application name is required.')
      return
    }
    setSaving(true)
    setFormError(null)
    try {
      await createApplication({
        name: name.trim(),
        base_url: baseUrl.trim() || null,
        owner: owner.trim() || null,
        requires_sso_gateway: requiresSsoGateway,
      })
      // reset + reload
      setName(''); setBaseUrl(''); setOwner(''); setRequiresSsoGateway(false)
      setShowForm(false)
      await load()
    } catch (err) {
      setFormError(err.message)
    } finally {
      setSaving(false)
    }
  }

  async function handleToggleSso(app, checked) {
    setSsoSavingId(app.id)
    try {
      await setApplicationSsoGateway(app.id, checked)
      await load()
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err.message)
    } finally {
      setSsoSavingId(null)
    }
  }

  return (
    <div style={{ padding: '32px' }}>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between', alignItems: 'flex-start', marginBottom: '24px' }}>
        <div>
          <h1 style={{ fontSize: '24px', fontWeight: 700, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>Applications</h1>
          <p style={{ color: 'var(--text-muted)', fontSize: '14px', marginTop: '4px' }}>
            {loading ? 'Loading…' : `${apps.length} application${apps.length !== 1 ? 's' : ''}`}
          </p>
        </div>
        <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={() => setShowForm(v => !v)}>
          <i className="ti ti-plus" aria-hidden="true" /> Add application
        </button>
      </div>

      {/* Add form */}
      {showForm && (
        <div className="card" style={{ marginBottom: '24px', padding: '20px' }}>
          <div className="card-title" style={{ marginBottom: '16px' }}>New application</div>
          <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: '12px', maxWidth: '480px' }}>
            <div>
              <label style={{ display: 'block', fontSize: '14px', color: 'var(--text-secondary)', marginBottom: '4px' }}>
                Name *
              </label>
              <input
                className="input" value={name} onChange={e => setName(e.target.value)}
                placeholder="e.g. FS, Netra, Baxter Portal"
                style={{ width: '100%' }}
              />
            </div>
            <div>
              <label style={{ display: 'block', fontSize: '14px', color: 'var(--text-secondary)', marginBottom: '4px' }}>
                Base URL
              </label>
              <input
                className="input" value={baseUrl} onChange={e => setBaseUrl(e.target.value)}
                placeholder="https://…"
                style={{ width: '100%' }}
              />
            </div>
            <div>
              <label style={{ display: 'block', fontSize: '14px', color: 'var(--text-secondary)', marginBottom: '4px' }}>
                Owner
              </label>
              <input
                className="input" value={owner} onChange={e => setOwner(e.target.value)}
                placeholder="Team or person"
                style={{ width: '100%' }}
              />
            </div>
            <label style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, fontSize: 14, color: 'var(--text-secondary)' }}>
              <input
                type="checkbox"
                checked={requiresSsoGateway}
                onChange={e => setRequiresSsoGateway(e.target.checked)}
              />
              This application requires SSO login gateway
            </label>
            {formError && (
              <div style={{ color: 'var(--red, #e5484d)', fontSize: '14px' }}>{formError}</div>
            )}
            <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '8px', marginTop: '4px' }}>
              <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={handleAdd} disabled={saving}>
                {saving ? 'Saving…' : 'Create application'}
              </button>
              <button className="btn btn-ghost" onClick={() => { setShowForm(false); setFormError(null) }}>
                Cancel
              </button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}

      {/* States */}
      {loading && (
        <div className="card" style={{ padding: '20px' }}>
          {[1,2,3].map(i => <div key={i} className="skeleton" style={{ height: '48px', marginBottom: '8px', borderRadius: '6px' }} />)}
        </div>
      )}

      {!loading && error && (
        <div className="card" style={{ padding: '20px', color: 'var(--amber, #f5a623)' }}>
          <i className="ti ti-alert-circle" aria-hidden="true" /> Could not load applications: {error}
        </div>
      )}

      {!loading && !error && apps.length === 0 && (
        <div className="card" style={{ padding: '40px', textAlign: 'center', color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>
          <i className="ti ti-apps" style={{ fontSize: '32px' }} aria-hidden="true" />
          <p style={{ margin: '12px 0' }}>No applications yet. Add your first one above.</p>
        </div>
      )}

      {!loading && !error && apps.length > 0 && (
        <div className="card">
          <div className="table-wrapper">
            <table className="table">
              <thead>
                <tr><th>Application</th><th>Base URL</th><th>SSO</th><th>Owner</th><th></th></tr>
              </thead>
              <tbody>
                {apps.map(app => (
                  <tr key={app.id}>
                    <td style={{ fontWeight: 600, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>{app.name}</td>
                    <td className="text-muted">{app.base_url || '—'}</td>
                    <td className="text-secondary">
                      <label style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 6, cursor: 'pointer' }}>
                        <input
                          type="checkbox"
                          checked={!!app.requires_sso_gateway}
                          disabled={ssoSavingId === app.id}
                          onChange={e => handleToggleSso(app, e.target.checked)}
                        />
                        {app.requires_sso_gateway ? 'Enabled' : 'Disabled'}
                      </label>
                    </td>
                    <td className="text-secondary">{app.owner || '—'}</td>
                    <td style={{ textAlign: 'right', whiteSpace: 'nowrap' }}>
                      <Link href={`/applications/${app.id}`}
                            style={{ color: 'var(--accent)', fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 14, marginRight: 14 }}>
                        Open
                      </Link>
                      <Link href={`/applications/${app.id}/credentials`}
                            title="Set your own login for this application"
                            style={{ color: 'var(--accent)', fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 13, marginRight: 14 }}>
                        My login
                      </Link>
                      <button
                        onClick={() => setRemoving(app)}
                        title="Retire or delete this application"
                        style={{
                          background: 'none', border: '1px solid var(--border)',
                          color: 'var(--text-muted)', borderRadius: 7,
                          padding: '5px 11px', fontSize: 12, cursor: 'pointer',
                          fontFamily: 'var(--font-body)',
                        }}
                      >
                        Retire
                      </button>
                    </td>
                  </tr>
                ))}
              </tbody>
            </table>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
      {removing && (
        <RetireDialog
          app={removing}
          onClose={() => setRemoving(null)}
          onDone={() => { setRemoving(null); load() }}
        />
      )}
    </div>
  )
}


/**
 * Retire an application.
 *
 * Archiving is offered first: a decommissioned system still needs its
 * test evidence retained. Deleting removes the application, every
 * scenario and script beneath it, and all execution history — so it is
 * the deliberate, secondary choice.
 */
function RetireDialog({ app, onClose, onDone }) {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(null)
  const [error, setError] = useState(null)

  async function run(action) {
    setBusy(action); setError(null)
    try {
      await (action === 'archive' ? archiveApplication(app.id) : deleteApplication(app.id))
      onDone()
    } catch (e) { setError(e.message); setBusy(null) }
  }

  const box = { background: 'var(--bg-card)', border: '1px solid var(--border)',
                borderRadius: 12, padding: 22, width: 'min(520px, 100%)' }
  const opt = { border: '1px solid var(--border)', borderRadius: 10, padding: 14,
                marginBottom: 12, display: 'grid', gap: 6 }

  return (
    <div onClick={onClose}
         style={{ position: 'fixed', inset: 0, background: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.55)',
                  display: 'grid', placeItems: 'center', zIndex: 300, padding: 40 }}>
      <div style={box} onClick={e => e.stopPropagation()}>
        <h3 style={{ marginBottom: 4 }}>Retire application?</h3>
        <p className="text-secondary" style={{ marginBottom: 18 }}>{app.name} · {app.base_url}</p>

        <div style={opt}>
          <strong style={{ fontSize: 14 }}>Archive</strong>
          <span className="text-muted" style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 1.5 }}>
            Removes it from the active list but keeps every scenario, script and
            execution record. Recommended when a system is decommissioned but its
            test evidence must be retained.
          </span>
          <button className="btn btn-secondary" style={{ justifySelf: 'start', marginTop: 6 }}
                  onClick={() => run('archive')} disabled={!!busy}>
            {busy === 'archive' ? 'Archiving…' : 'Archive'}
          </button>
        </div>

        <div style={{ ...opt, borderColor: 'var(--red-bg)' }}>
          <strong style={{ fontSize: 14 }}>Delete permanently</strong>
          <span className="text-muted" style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 1.5 }}>
            Deletes the application, every scenario and script beneath it, and all
            execution history and screenshots. This cannot be undone.
          </span>
          <button style={{ justifySelf: 'start', marginTop: 6, background: 'var(--red)',
                           color: '#fff', border: 'none', padding: '7px 14px',
                           borderRadius: 8, fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 600, cursor: 'pointer' }}
                  onClick={() => run('delete')} disabled={!!busy}>
            {busy === 'delete' ? 'Deleting…' : 'Delete permanently'}
          </button>
        </div>

        {error && <div style={{ color: 'var(--red)', fontSize: 12, marginBottom: 10 }}>{error}</div>}
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'flex-end' }}>
          <button className="btn btn-ghost" onClick={onClose} disabled={!!busy}>Cancel</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
