'use client'

/**
 * app/help/page.js
 *
 * Help and support.
 *
 * Four things sit behind one screen, in the order someone in trouble
 * actually needs them:
 *
 *   Browse    the articles, by category
 *   Search    articles and uploaded training documents together
 *   Training  the documents, and the record of who has read what
 *   Support   raise a ticket, and see the ones you have raised
 *
 * Search is first in the layout rather than buried, because a person who
 * opens Help already has a question — making them navigate a taxonomy to
 * reach a search box is the most common way an in-product help centre fails.
 *
 * Two behaviours worth knowing while reading this file:
 *
 *   Opening an article records a view. That record is the training evidence,
 *   so it is written by reading rather than by a separate action. An explicit
 *   acknowledgement is offered on top, because "opened the page" and "read
 *   and understood" are not the same claim.
 *
 *   A search that finds nothing is not a dead end. The backend records it as
 *   a documentation gap and the UI offers to raise a ticket, carrying the
 *   question across so it does not have to be typed twice.
 */

import { useState, useEffect, useCallback, useMemo, useRef } from 'react'
import {
  Search, BookOpen, GraduationCap, LifeBuoy, Upload, Download, Check,
  FileText, AlertTriangle, ExternalLink, ChevronLeft, Loader2, ShieldCheck,
  Inbox, CircleDot, CircleCheck, Users,
} from 'lucide-react'
import {
  getHelpCategories, getHelpArticles, getHelpArticle, acknowledgeHelpView,
  searchHelp, getTrainingDocuments, uploadTrainingDocument,
  trainingDocumentUrl, getTrainingRecords, getSupportConfig,
  getSupportCategories, getSupportTickets, raiseSupportTicket,
  collectSupportContext, getCurrentUser,
} from '../../lib/api'
import Markdown from '../../components/Markdown/Markdown'
import styles from './Help.module.css'

const TABS = [
  { key: 'browse',   label: 'Articles', icon: BookOpen },
  { key: 'training', label: 'Training', icon: GraduationCap },
  { key: 'support',  label: 'Support',  icon: LifeBuoy },
]

export default function HelpPage() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState('browse')
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
  const [results, setResults] = useState(null)   // null = not searching
  const [searching, setSearching] = useState(false)
  const [deepSlug, setDeepSlug] = useState(null)

  // NextGen2 AI cites an article and links here, so a citation has to open the
  // article rather than dropping the reader on a category list to find it
  // themselves. Read from window.location rather than useSearchParams to
  // avoid forcing this page into a Suspense boundary for one query string.
  useEffect(() => {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
    const slug = params.get('article')
    const wanted = params.get('tab')
    if (slug) setDeepSlug(slug)
    if (wanted && TABS.some(t => t.key === wanted)) setTab(wanted)
  }, [])

  // Search is owned by the page rather than the Browse tab, so a result can
  // be opened without losing the query, and so the empty-result path can
  // hand the question to the support form.
  const runSearch = useCallback(async (q) => {
    const text = (q ?? query).trim()
    if (!text) { setResults(null); return }
    setSearching(true)
    try {
      const data = await searchHelp(text)
      setResults(data)
    } catch (e) {
      setResults({ query: text, results: [], error: e.message })
    } finally {
      setSearching(false)
    }
  }, [query])

  function clearSearch() {
    setQuery('')
    setResults(null)
  }

  if (deepSlug) {
    return (
      <div className={styles.page}>
        <ArticleReader slug={deepSlug} onBack={() => {
          setDeepSlug(null)
          window.history.replaceState({}, '', '/help')
        }} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className={styles.page}>
      <div className={styles.head}>
        <div>
          <h1 className={styles.title}>Help and support</h1>
          <p className={styles.sub}>
            Search the guides, read the training material, or raise a ticket
            when neither covers it.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <SearchBar
        query={query} setQuery={setQuery} onSearch={runSearch}
        onClear={clearSearch} searching={searching}
      />

      {results ? (
        <SearchResults
          data={results} searching={searching}
          onClear={clearSearch}
          onRaiseTicket={() => { setTab('support') }}
        />
      ) : (
        <>
          <div className={styles.tabs} role="tablist">
            {TABS.map(t => {
              const Icon = t.icon
              return (
                <button key={t.key} role="tab" aria-selected={tab === t.key}
                  className={`${styles.tab} ${tab === t.key ? styles.tabOn : ''}`}
                  onClick={() => setTab(t.key)}>
                  <Icon size={14} strokeWidth={2} /> {t.label}
                </button>
              )
            })}
          </div>

          {tab === 'browse' && <BrowseTab />}
          {tab === 'training' && <TrainingTab />}
          {tab === 'support' && <SupportTab seedSummary={results?.query} />}
        </>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}


/* ── search ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

function SearchBar({ query, setQuery, onSearch, onClear, searching }) {
  return (
    <div className={styles.searchRow}>
      <div className={styles.searchBox}>
        <Search size={15} strokeWidth={2} />
        <input
          value={query}
          onChange={e => setQuery(e.target.value)}
          onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') onSearch() }}
          placeholder="How do I schedule a suite? What does a sync flag mean?"
          aria-label="Search help"
        />
        {query && (
          <button className={styles.clearBtn} onClick={onClear} aria-label="Clear search">
            Clear
          </button>
        )}
      </div>
      <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={() => onSearch()} disabled={searching || !query.trim()}>
        {searching ? <Loader2 size={15} className={styles.spin} /> : <Search size={15} />}
        Search
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

function SearchResults({ data, searching, onClear, onRaiseTicket }) {
  const [openSlug, setOpenSlug] = useState(null)

  if (searching) return <div className={styles.empty}>Searching…</div>
  if (openSlug) {
    return <ArticleReader slug={openSlug} onBack={() => setOpenSlug(null)} />
  }

  const hits = data.results || []

  return (
    <div className={styles.panel}>
      <div className={styles.resultHead}>
        <span>
          {hits.length
            ? `${hits.length} passage${hits.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} for “${data.query}”`
            : `Nothing found for “${data.query}”`}
        </span>
        <button className={styles.linkBtn} onClick={onClear}>Back to articles</button>
      </div>

      {data.error && <div className={styles.errorBox}>{data.error}</div>}

      {hits.length === 0 && !data.error && (
        // A dead end is where an in-product help centre loses people, so the
        // no-result path is a route onward rather than an apology.
        <div className={styles.noResult}>
          <AlertTriangle size={18} strokeWidth={1.8} />
          <div>
            <strong>The help content does not cover this yet.</strong>
            <p>
              Your question has been recorded so the missing article can be
              written. If you need an answer now, raise a ticket — the question
              is carried across.
            </p>
            <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={onRaiseTicket}>
              <LifeBuoy size={15} /> Raise a ticket
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}

      {hits.map(hit => (
        <button key={hit.chunk_id} className={styles.hit}
          onClick={() => hit.source_type === 'article' && setOpenSlug(hit.label)}
          disabled={hit.source_type !== 'article'}>
          <div className={styles.hitTop}>
            <span className={styles.hitTitle}>{hit.heading || hit.title}</span>
            <span className={styles.hitSource}>
              {hit.source_type === 'article'
                ? <><BookOpen size={11} /> {hit.citation}</>
                : <><FileText size={11} /> {hit.title}</>}
            </span>
          </div>
          <p className={styles.hitBody}>{hit.body}</p>
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}


/* ── browse ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

function BrowseTab() {
  const [categories, setCategories] = useState(null)
  const [articles, setArticles] = useState(null)
  const [slug, setSlug] = useState(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    getHelpCategories().then(setCategories).catch(() => setCategories([]))
    getHelpArticles().then(setArticles).catch(() => setArticles([]))
  }, [])

  const grouped = useMemo(() => {
    const map = new Map()
    for (const a of articles || []) {
      if (!map.has(a.category)) map.set(a.category, [])
      map.get(a.category).push(a)
    }
    // Follow the category order the backend returned, which is a teaching
    // order rather than alphabetical.
    return (categories || []).map(c => [c.category, map.get(c.category) || []])
  }, [articles, categories])

  if (slug) return <ArticleReader slug={slug} onBack={() => setSlug(null)} />

  if (!articles) return <div className={styles.empty}>Loading…</div>
  if (articles.length === 0) {
    return (
      <div className={styles.empty}>
        No help articles have been published yet.
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className={styles.catGrid}>
      {grouped.map(([category, items]) => (
        <section key={category} className={styles.catCard}>
          <h2 className={styles.catTitle}>{category}</h2>
          <ul className={styles.artList}>
            {items.map(a => (
              <li key={a.id}>
                <button className={styles.artItem} onClick={() => setSlug(a.slug)}>
                  <span className={styles.artName}>
                    {a.title}
                    {a.status !== 'approved' && (
                      <span className={styles.draftTag}>Draft</span>
                    )}
                  </span>
                  {a.summary && <span className={styles.artSub}>{a.summary}</span>}
                </button>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </section>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}


/* ── article reader ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

function ArticleReader({ slug, onBack }) {
  const [article, setArticle] = useState(null)
  const [error, setError] = useState(null)
  const [ack, setAck] = useState(false)
  const [acking, setAcking] = useState(false)

  useEffect(() => {
    setArticle(null); setError(null); setAck(false)
    getHelpArticle(slug)
      .then(a => (a.error ? setError(a.error) : setArticle(a)))
      .catch(e => setError(e.message))
  }, [slug])

  async function acknowledge() {
    if (!article?.view_id) return
    setAcking(true)
    try {
      const r = await acknowledgeHelpView(article.view_id)
      if (!r.error) setAck(true)
    } catch { /* the article is still readable; the record simply is not written */ }
    finally { setAcking(false) }
  }

  if (error) return <div className={styles.panel}><div className={styles.errorBox}>{error}</div></div>
  if (!article) return <div className={styles.empty}>Loading…</div>

  return (
    <article className={styles.reader}>
      <button className={styles.backBtn} onClick={onBack}>
        <ChevronLeft size={15} /> Back
      </button>

      <header className={styles.readerHead}>
        <h1>{article.title}</h1>
        <div className={styles.readerMeta}>
          <span>{article.category}</span>
          <span>·</span>
          <span>Version {article.version}</span>
          {article.status === 'approved' ? (
            <span className={styles.approvedTag}>
              <ShieldCheck size={12} /> Approved
            </span>
          ) : (
            <span className={styles.draftTag}>Draft — not yet approved</span>
          )}
        </div>
      </header>

      <Markdown text={article.body_md} className={styles.prose} />

      {/* Reading records a view. This is the separate, deliberate claim that
          the reader understood it — which is what an audit asks for. */}
      <footer className={styles.ackBox}>
        {ack ? (
          <div className={styles.ackDone}>
            <Check size={15} strokeWidth={2.4} />
            Recorded — you have acknowledged version {article.version} of this article.
          </div>
        ) : (
          <>
            <div>
              <strong>Confirm you have read this</strong>
              <p>
                Opening an article records that you viewed it. Acknowledging
                records that you read and understood version {article.version},
                which is what appears in the training record.
              </p>
            </div>
            <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={acknowledge}
              disabled={acking || !article.view_id}>
              {acking ? <Loader2 size={15} className={styles.spin} /> : <Check size={15} />}
              I have read and understood
            </button>
          </>
        )}
      </footer>
    </article>
  )
}


/* ── training ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

function TrainingTab() {
  const [docs, setDocs] = useState(null)
  const [records, setRecords] = useState(null)
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)
  const [notice, setNotice] = useState(null)
  const [mine, setMine] = useState(true)

  const load = useCallback(() => {
    getTrainingDocuments().then(setDocs).catch(() => setDocs([]))
  }, [])

  useEffect(load, [load])
  useEffect(() => {
    getTrainingRecords(mine ? { viewedBy: getCurrentUser() } : {})
      .then(setRecords).catch(() => setRecords([]))
  }, [mine])

  async function onUpload(e) {
    const file = e.target.files?.[0]
    if (!file) return
    setBusy(true); setNotice(null)
    try {
      const res = await uploadTrainingDocument(file)
      setNotice(res.warning
        ? { kind: 'warn', text: res.warning }
        : { kind: 'ok', text: `${file.name} indexed as ${res.chunks_indexed} searchable passage${res.chunks_indexed === 1 ? '' : 's'}.` })
      load()
    } catch (err) {
      setNotice({ kind: 'warn', text: err.message })
    } finally {
      setBusy(false)
      e.target.value = ''      // allow re-uploading the same file
    }
  }

  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.panel}>
        <div className={styles.panelHead}>
          <div>
            <h2 className={styles.panelTitle}>Training material</h2>
            <p className={styles.panelSub}>
              Uploaded documents are searched alongside the articles and can be
              cited by NextGen2 AI.
            </p>
          </div>
          <label className={`btn btn-secondary ${styles.uploadBtn}`}>
            {busy ? <Loader2 size={15} className={styles.spin} /> : <Upload size={15} />}
            Upload
            <input type="file" accept=".pdf,.docx,.doc,.txt,.md"
              onChange={onUpload} disabled={busy} hidden />
          </label>
        </div>

        {notice && (
          <div className={notice.kind === 'ok' ? styles.okBox : styles.errorBox}>
            {notice.text}
          </div>
        )}

        {!docs ? <div className={styles.empty}>Loading…</div>
          : docs.length === 0 ? <div className={styles.empty}>No training documents uploaded yet.</div>
          : (
            <table className="table">
              <thead>
                <tr><th>Document</th><th>Indexed</th><th>Uploaded</th><th /></tr>
              </thead>
              <tbody>
                {docs.map(d => (
                  <tr key={d.id}>
                    <td><FileText size={13} className={styles.rowIcon} /> {d.original_filename}</td>
                    <td>
                      {d.chunk_count > 0
                        ? <span className="badge badge-green">{d.chunk_count} passages</span>
                        /* Zero passages means no text could be extracted —
                           usually a scanned PDF. Saying so beats letting the
                           upload look successful while answering nothing. */
                        : <span className="badge badge-amber">Not searchable</span>}
                    </td>
                    <td>{fmtDate(d.uploaded_at)}</td>
                    <td className={styles.rowRight}>
                      <a className={styles.linkBtn} href={trainingDocumentUrl(d.id)}
                         target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
                        <Download size={13} /> Download
                      </a>
                    </td>
                  </tr>
                ))}
              </tbody>
            </table>
          )}
      </div>

      <div className={styles.panel}>
        <div className={styles.panelHead}>
          <div>
            <h2 className={styles.panelTitle}>Training record</h2>
            <p className={styles.panelSub}>
              What was read, at which version, and what was acknowledged.
            </p>
          </div>
          <label className={styles.toggle}>
            <input type="checkbox" checked={mine} onChange={e => setMine(e.target.checked)} />
            Only mine
          </label>
        </div>

        {!records ? <div className={styles.empty}>Loading…</div>
          : records.length === 0 ? <div className={styles.empty}>Nothing recorded yet.</div>
          : (
            <table className="table">
              <thead>
                <tr><th>Read</th><th>Who</th><th>Version</th><th>Acknowledged</th><th>When</th></tr>
              </thead>
              <tbody>
                {records.slice(0, 100).map(r => (
                  <tr key={r.id}>
                    <td>{r.source_title}</td>
                    <td>{r.viewed_by}</td>
                    <td>{r.article_version ? `v${r.article_version}` : '—'}</td>
                    <td>
                      {r.acknowledged
                        ? <span className="badge badge-green">Yes</span>
                        : <span className="badge badge-gray">Viewed only</span>}
                    </td>
                    <td>{fmtDate(r.acknowledged_at || r.viewed_at)}</td>
                  </tr>
                ))}
              </tbody>
            </table>
          )}
      </div>
    </>
  )
}


/* ── support ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

function SupportTab({ seedSummary }) {
  const [config, setConfig] = useState(null)
  const [categories, setCategories] = useState([])
  const [tickets, setTickets] = useState(null)
  // Defaults to everyone. NextGen2 is a shared platform with a handful of
  // users, so the useful first view is what has been reported at all — a
  // personal list that reads "you have not raised any tickets" tells a new
  // user nothing and hides tickets someone else already raised about the
  // problem they are about to report.
  const [scope, setScope] = useState('all')          // 'mine' | 'all'
  const [form, setForm] = useState({ category: 'how-to', summary: seedSummary || '', description: '' })
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)
  const [result, setResult] = useState(null)
  const [highlightId, setHighlightId] = useState(null)

  const resultRef = useRef(null)
  const me = getCurrentUser()

  const loadTickets = useCallback(() => {
    const opts = scope === 'mine' ? { raisedBy: me } : {}
    getSupportTickets(opts).then(setTickets).catch(() => setTickets([]))
  }, [scope, me])

  useEffect(() => {
    getSupportConfig().then(setConfig).catch(() => setConfig(null))
    getSupportCategories().then(setCategories).catch(() => setCategories([]))
  }, [])

  useEffect(loadTickets, [loadTickets])

  // Counts come from the rows already loaded rather than a second request:
  // one source, so a figure can never disagree with the table beneath it.
  const counts = useMemo(() => {
    const list = tickets || []
    return {
      total: list.length,
      open: list.filter(t => ['submitted', 'open'].includes(t.status)).length,
      failed: list.filter(t => t.status === 'failed').length,
      closed: list.filter(t => ['resolved', 'closed'].includes(t.status)).length,
    }
  }, [tickets])

  async function submit() {
    if (!form.summary.trim() || busy) return
    setBusy(true); setResult(null)
    try {
      const res = await raiseSupportTicket({
        category: form.category,
        summary: form.summary.trim(),
        description: form.description.trim(),
        context: collectSupportContext(),
      })
      setResult(res)
      if (!res.error) {
        setForm(f => ({ ...f, summary: '', description: '' }))
        setHighlightId(res.id)
        // A confirmation the user has to go looking for is not a
        // confirmation. Bring it into view and mark the new row, so pressing
        // the button visibly does something even when the table is below the
        // fold.
        setTimeout(() => resultRef.current?.scrollIntoView({
          behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center',
        }), 60)
        setTimeout(() => setHighlightId(null), 6000)
      }
      loadTickets()
    } catch (e) {
      setResult({ error: e.message })
    } finally {
      setBusy(false)
    }
  }

  const chosen = categories.find(c => c.key === form.category)

  return (
    <>
      {/* Counters sit above the form so the state of your tickets is the
          first thing on the tab, not something found by scrolling past it. */}
      <div className={styles.statRow}>
        <Stat icon={Inbox}       label={scope === 'mine' ? 'Your tickets' : 'All tickets'} value={counts.total} />
        <Stat icon={CircleDot}   label="Open"      value={counts.open} tone="accent" />
        <Stat icon={CircleCheck} label="Closed"    value={counts.closed} tone="green" />
        <Stat icon={AlertTriangle} label="Not filed" value={counts.failed}
              tone={counts.failed ? 'red' : undefined}
            hint={counts.failed ? 'Saved in NextGen2 but not created in the ticketing system' : undefined} />
      </div>

      <div className={styles.panel}>
        <div className={styles.panelHead}>
          <div>
            <h2 className={styles.panelTitle}>Raise a ticket</h2>
            <p className={styles.panelSub}>
              The screen you were on, your browser and the last error are
              attached automatically — you do not need to gather them.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>

        {/* A misconfigured ticketing system is worth saying before someone
            writes out a problem, not after they press Send. */}
        {config && !config.configured && (
          <div className={styles.errorBox}>
            <AlertTriangle size={14} /> Ticketing is not configured
            {config.reason ? `: ${config.reason}` : '.'} Your ticket will still
            be saved in NextGen2.
          </div>
        )}

        <div className={styles.formGrid}>
          <label className={styles.field}>
            <span>What kind of problem?</span>
            <select className="form-select" value={form.category}
              onChange={e => setForm(f => ({ ...f, category: e.target.value }))}>
              {categories.map(c => <option key={c.key} value={c.key}>{c.label}</option>)}
            </select>
            {chosen?.hint && <small className="form-hint">{chosen.hint}</small>}
          </label>

          <label className={styles.field}>
            <span>Summary</span>
            <input className="form-input" value={form.summary}
              onChange={e => setForm(f => ({ ...f, summary: e.target.value }))}
              placeholder="One line — what went wrong, or what you are trying to do" />
          </label>

          <label className={`${styles.field} ${styles.fieldWide}`}>
            <span>What happened?</span>
            <textarea className="form-textarea" rows={5} value={form.description}
              onChange={e => setForm(f => ({ ...f, description: e.target.value }))}
              placeholder="What you did, what you expected, and what happened instead." />
          </label>
        </div>

        <div className={styles.formFoot}>
          <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={submit}
            disabled={busy || !form.summary.trim()}>
            {busy ? <Loader2 size={15} className={styles.spin} /> : <LifeBuoy size={15} />}
            {busy ? 'Raising…' : 'Raise ticket'}
          </button>
          {config?.provider && (
            <span className={styles.footNote}>Filed in {config.provider}</span>
          )}
        </div>

        <div ref={resultRef}>
          {result && (
            <div className={result.error ? styles.errorBox : styles.okBox}>
              {result.error
                ? <>{result.error}</>
                : <>Ticket {result.external_ref || `#${result.id}`} raised.{' '}
                    {result.external_url && (
                      <a href={result.external_url} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
                        Open it <ExternalLink size={11} />
                      </a>
                    )}</>}
            </div>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className={styles.panel}>
        <div className={styles.panelHead}>
          <div>
            <h2 className={styles.panelTitle}>
              {scope === 'mine' ? 'Your tickets' : 'All tickets'}
            </h2>
            <p className={styles.panelSub}>
              {scope === 'mine'
                ? <>Raised from NextGen2 as <strong>{me}</strong>.</>
                : <>Everything raised from NextGen2 by anyone.</>}
            </p>
          </div>

          {/* A filter, not a permission. NextGen2 has no authentication, so
              this changes what is shown and nothing else — saying otherwise
              would imply a control that does not exist. */}
          <div className={styles.scopeSwitch} role="group" aria-label="Ticket scope">
            <button className={scope === 'mine' ? styles.scopeOn : ''}
              onClick={() => setScope('mine')}>Mine</button>
            <button className={scope === 'all' ? styles.scopeOn : ''}
              onClick={() => setScope('all')}>
              <Users size={12} /> Everyone
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>

        {scope === 'all' && (
          <p className={styles.scopeNote}>
            Showing everyone&rsquo;s tickets. This is a view filter — NextGen2 has
            no sign-in yet, so it is not access control.
          </p>
        )}

        {!tickets ? <div className={styles.empty}>Loading…</div>
          : tickets.length === 0 ? (
            <div className={styles.empty}>
              {scope === 'mine'
                ? 'You have not raised any tickets.'
                : 'No tickets have been raised yet.'}
            </div>
          ) : (
            <table className="table">
              <thead>
                <tr>
                  <th>Reference</th><th>Summary</th>
                  {scope === 'all' && <th>Raised by</th>}
                  <th>Kind</th><th>Status</th><th>Raised</th>
                </tr>
              </thead>
              <tbody>
                {tickets.map(t => (
                  <tr key={t.id} className={t.id === highlightId ? styles.newRow : undefined}>
                    <td>
                      {t.external_url
                        ? <a href={t.external_url} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
                            {t.external_ref} <ExternalLink size={11} />
                          </a>
                        : (t.external_ref || `#${t.id}`)}
                    </td>
                    <td>{t.summary}</td>
                    {scope === 'all' && <td>{t.raised_by}</td>}
                    <td>{t.category}</td>
                    <td>
                      {t.status === 'submitted' ? <span className="badge badge-green">Submitted</span>
                        : t.status === 'failed' ? <span className="badge badge-red" title={t.submit_error}>Not filed</span>
                        : ['resolved', 'closed'].includes(t.status) ? <span className="badge badge-gray">{t.status}</span>
                        : <span className="badge badge-amber">{t.status}</span>}
                    </td>
                    <td>{fmtDate(t.created_at)}</td>
                  </tr>
                ))}
              </tbody>
            </table>
          )}
      </div>
    </>
  )
}


/**
 * One counter above the support form.
 *
 * @param {object} props
 * @param {Function} props.icon - A lucide icon component.
 * @param {string} props.label - What is being counted.
 * @param {number} props.value - The count.
 * @param {string} [props.tone] - 'accent' | 'green' | 'red' for emphasis.
 * @param {string} [props.hint] - Tooltip explaining a figure that needs it.
 */
function Stat({ icon: Icon, label, value, tone, hint }) {
  return (
    <div className={`${styles.stat} ${tone ? styles['stat_' + tone] : ''}`} title={hint}>
      <div className={styles.statTop}>
        <Icon size={13} strokeWidth={2} />
        <span>{label}</span>
      </div>
      <div className={styles.statValue}>{value}</div>
    </div>
  )
}


/* ── helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

function fmtDate(value) {
  if (!value) return '—'
  const d = new Date(value)
  if (Number.isNaN(d.getTime())) return '—'
  return d.toLocaleString(undefined, {
    day: '2-digit', month: 'short', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit',
  })
}

FILE: frontend/app/reports/page.js

'use client'

/**
 * app/reports/page.js
 *
 * The artefacts that leave the tool.
 *
 * The dashboard answers "what is the state right now" and is consumed on
 * screen. A report is parameterised — you choose the scope and the period —
 * and is produced to be sent to someone or filed. That is the line every
 * test management tool draws, and it is why this is not a second dashboard.
 *
 * Three of them:
 *   Traceability   requirement -> test -> result -> evidence. The artefact a
 *                  regulated environment asks for.
 *   Executions     what ran in a period, where, and what started it.
 *   Coverage       per application, with the automation gap stated beside it.
 *
 * All three export to CSV, because a report nobody can send is a dashboard.
 */

import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react'
import Link from 'next/link'
import {
  FileText, Download, CheckCircle2, XCircle, MinusCircle, AlertTriangle,
  RefreshCw, CalendarClock, User,
} from 'lucide-react'
import {
  getTraceabilityReport, getExecutionReport, getCoverageReport, getApplications,
} from '../../lib/api'
import styles from './Reports.module.css'

const TABS = [
  { id: 'traceability', label: 'Traceability',
    blurb: 'Requirement to test to result to evidence' },
  { id: 'executions',   label: 'Execution report',
    blurb: 'What ran in a period, and where' },
  { id: 'coverage',     label: 'Coverage',
    blurb: 'By application, with the automation gap' },
]

export default function ReportsPage() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState('traceability')
  const [apps, setApps] = useState([])
  const [applicationId, setApplicationId] = useState('')
  const [days, setDays] = useState(30)
  const [data, setData] = useState(null)
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)

  useEffect(() => { getApplications().then(setApps).catch(() => setApps([])) }, [])

  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    setBusy(true); setData(null)
    try {
      if (tab === 'traceability') setData(await getTraceabilityReport(applicationId || undefined))
      else if (tab === 'executions') setData(await getExecutionReport({
        application_id: applicationId || undefined, days,
      }))
      else setData(await getCoverageReport())
    } catch {
      setData({ error: true })
    } finally { setBusy(false) }
  }, [tab, applicationId, days])

  useEffect(() => { load() }, [load])

  return (
    <div>
      <div className={styles.head}>
        <div>
          <h2 className={styles.title}>Reports</h2>
          <p className={styles.sub}>
            Evidence you can send. Choose the scope, generate, export.
          </p>
        </div>
        <button className={styles.refresh} onClick={load} disabled={busy}>
          <RefreshCw size={14} strokeWidth={2} className={busy ? styles.spin : ''} />
          Regenerate
        </button>
      </div>

      <div className={styles.tabs}>
        {TABS.map(t => (
          <button key={t.id}
                  className={`${styles.tab} ${tab === t.id ? styles.tabOn : ''}`}
                  onClick={() => setTab(t.id)}>
            <span className={styles.tabLabel}>{t.label}</span>
            <span className={styles.tabBlurb}>{t.blurb}</span>
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>

      <div className={styles.controls}>
        {tab !== 'coverage' && (
          <select className={styles.select} value={applicationId}
                  onChange={e => setApplicationId(e.target.value)}>
            <option value="">All applications</option>
            {apps.map(a => <option key={a.id} value={a.id}>{a.name}</option>)}
          </select>
        )}
        {tab === 'executions' && (
          <select className={styles.select} value={days}
                  onChange={e => setDays(Number(e.target.value))}>
            <option value={7}>Last 7 days</option>
            <option value={30}>Last 30 days</option>
            <option value={90}>Last 90 days</option>
          </select>
        )}
        {data && !data.error && (
          <button className={styles.export} onClick={() => exportCsv(tab, data)}>
            <Download size={14} strokeWidth={2} /> Export CSV
          </button>
        )}
      </div>

      {busy && <div className="skeleton" style={{ height: 260 }} />}
      {data?.error && <div className={styles.empty}>Could not generate that report.</div>}

      {!busy && data && !data.error && tab === 'traceability' && <Traceability data={data} />}
      {!busy && data && !data.error && tab === 'executions' && <Executions data={data} />}
      {!busy && data && !data.error && tab === 'coverage' && <Coverage data={data} />}

      {data?.generated_at && (
        <p className={styles.footNote}>
          Generated {new Date(data.generated_at).toLocaleString()}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

/** Requirement to test to result to evidence. */
function Traceability({ data }) {
  if (!data?.requirements) return <NotAvailable data={data} what="traceability report" />
  const c = data.counts || {}
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.stats}>
        <Stat label="Requirements" value={c.requirements} />
        <Stat label="Verified" value={c.verified} tone="good" />
        <Stat label="Not verified" value={c.unverified}
              tone={c.unverified ? 'warn' : undefined} />
        <Stat label="Tests without a requirement" value={c.tests_untraced}
              tone={c.tests_untraced ? 'warn' : undefined} />
      </div>

      {(data.requirements || []).length === 0 && (
        <div className={styles.empty}>
          No requirements recorded yet. They come from the requirement id captured
          when a scenario is accepted — upload a BRD when creating a test suite and
          they will appear here.
        </div>
      )}

      {(data.requirements || []).map(r => (
        <div key={r.requirement_id} className={styles.reqBlock}>
          <div className={styles.reqHead}>
            {r.verified
              ? <CheckCircle2 size={15} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.pass} />
              : <AlertTriangle size={15} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.warn} />}
            <span className={styles.reqId}>{r.requirement_id}</span>
            <span className={styles.reqState}>
              {r.verified ? 'verified' : 'not verified'}
            </span>
            <span className={styles.reqCount}>
              {r.tests.length} test{r.tests.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}
            </span>
          </div>
          {r.tests.map(t => (
            <div key={t.id} className={styles.testRow}>
              <ResultIcon result={t.last_result} automated={t.automated} />
              <span className={styles.testTitle}>{t.title}</span>
              <span className={styles.testMeta}>
                <Link href={`/applications/${t.application_id}`} className={styles.appLink}>
                  {t.application_name}
                </Link>
                {t.environment && <> · {t.environment}</>}
                {t.last_run_at && <> · {new Date(t.last_run_at).toLocaleDateString()}</>}
              </span>
              {t.accepted_by && (
                <span className={styles.approved} title={`Accepted ${t.accepted_at}`}>
                  approved by {t.accepted_by}
                </span>
              )}
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}

      {(data.untraced_tests || []).length > 0 && (
        <div className={styles.untraced}>
          <div className={styles.untracedHead}>
            {(data.untraced_tests || []).length} test case
            {(data.untraced_tests || []).length === 1 ? '' : 's'} with no requirement
          </div>
          <p className={styles.untracedNote}>
            Listed rather than omitted — a test that traces to nothing is a
            finding, not something to leave out of the report.
          </p>
          {(data.untraced_tests || []).slice(0, 20).map(t => (
            <div key={t.id} className={styles.testRow}>
              <ResultIcon result={t.last_result} automated={t.automated} />
              <span className={styles.testTitle}>{t.title}</span>
              <span className={styles.testMeta}>{t.application_name}</span>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </>
  )
}

/** What ran in a period. */
function Executions({ data }) {
  // A report page must not white-screen because an endpoint returned
  // something unexpected. Missing data is a message, not a crash.
  if (!data?.runs) return <NotAvailable data={data} what="execution report" />
  const c = data.counts || {}
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.stats}>
        <Stat label="Runs" value={c.total} />
        <Stat label="Passed" value={c.passed} tone="good" />
        <Stat label="Failed" value={c.failed} tone={c.failed ? 'warn' : undefined} />
        <Stat label="Pass rate" value={c.pass_rate_pct != null ? `${c.pass_rate_pct}%` : '—'} />
        <Stat label="Unattended" value={c.scheduled} />
      </div>

      {(data.runs || []).length === 0 && (
        <div className={styles.empty}>Nothing ran in this period.</div>
      )}

      {(data.runs || []).length > 0 && (
        <div className="card" style={{ padding: 0 }}>
          {(data.runs || []).map(r => (
            <div key={r.id} className={styles.runRow}>
              <ResultIcon result={r.result} automated />
              <span className={styles.testTitle}>{r.test_title}</span>
              <span className={styles.testMeta}>
                {r.application_name}
                {r.requirement_id && <> · <span className={styles.req}>{r.requirement_id}</span></>}
              </span>
              <span className={styles.env}>{r.environment || 'default'}</span>
              <span className={styles.trigger}>
                {r.triggered_by === 'scheduler'
                  ? <><CalendarClock size={11} strokeWidth={2} /> scheduled</>
                  : <><User size={11} strokeWidth={2} /> manual</>}
              </span>
              <span className={styles.when}>
                {new Date(r.executed_at).toLocaleString([], {
                  day: 'numeric', month: 'short', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit',
                })}
              </span>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </>
  )
}

/** Coverage per application. */
function Coverage({ data }) {
  if (!data?.applications) return <NotAvailable data={data} what="coverage report" />
  const t = data.totals || {}
  return (
    <>
      <div className={styles.stats}>
        <Stat label="Test cases" value={t.test_cases} />
        <Stat label="Automated" value={t.automated} tone="good" />
        <Stat label="P0/P1 without a script" value={t.critical_gap}
              tone={t.critical_gap ? 'warn' : undefined} />
        <Stat label="Imported" value={t.imported} />
      </div>

      <div className="card" style={{ padding: 0 }}>
        {(data.applications || []).map(a => (
          <div key={a.id} className={styles.covRow}>
            <Link href={`/applications/${a.id}`} className={styles.covName}>{a.name}</Link>
            <span className={styles.covBar}>
              <span className={styles.covFill} style={{ width: `${a.coverage_pct}%` }} />
            </span>
            <span className={styles.covPct}>{a.coverage_pct}%</span>
            <span className={styles.covMeta}>
              {a.automated} of {a.test_cases} automated
              {a.requirements > 0 && <> · {a.requirements} requirements</>}
            </span>
            {a.critical_gap > 0 && (
              <span className={styles.covGap}>{a.critical_gap} critical without a script</span>
            )}
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
    </>
  )
}


/**
 * Shown when an endpoint returned something the report cannot render.
 *
 * Says what came back rather than a bare failure: a missing endpoint and an
 * empty result look identical otherwise, and that ambiguity sent me looking
 * in the wrong place more than once already.
 */
function NotAvailable({ data, what }) {
  const detail = data?.detail || data?.error || data?.message
  return (
    <div className={styles.empty}>
      <p style={{ margin: '0 0 8px', color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>
        The {what} is not available.
      </p>
      <p style={{ margin: 0, fontSize: 12 }}>
        {detail
          ? String(detail)
          : 'The endpoint did not return the expected data. If the backend was ' +
            'not restarted after copying api/routes/reports.py, that is the ' +
            'likely cause.'}
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

function Stat({ label, value, tone }) {
  return (
    <div className={`${styles.stat} ${tone === 'warn' ? styles.statWarn : ''} ${tone === 'good' ? styles.statGood : ''}`}>
      <span className={styles.statValue}>{value}</span>
      <span className={styles.statLabel}>{label}</span>
    </div>
  )
}

function ResultIcon({ result, automated }) {
  if (result === 'pass') return <CheckCircle2 size={14} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.pass} />
  if (result) return <XCircle size={14} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.fail} />
  return <MinusCircle size={14} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.none}
                      // No result at all is different from a failure, and the
                      // report should not let them look alike.
                      title={automated ? 'Never run' : 'No script'} />
}

/**
 * Write the report to a CSV the browser downloads.
 *
 * Done client-side from data already fetched: a report that cannot leave the
 * screen is a dashboard, and this is the smallest honest way to make it
 * leave. A PDF with letterhead is the next step, not the first.
 */
function exportCsv(tab, data) {
  let rows = []
  if (tab === 'traceability') {
    rows.push(['Requirement', 'Verified', 'Test case', 'Application',
               'Last result', 'Last run', 'Environment', 'Approved by'])
    ;(data.requirements || []).forEach(r => (r.tests || []).forEach(t => rows.push([
      r.requirement_id, r.verified ? 'yes' : 'no', t.title, t.application_name,
      t.last_result || 'never run', t.last_run_at || '', t.environment || '',
      t.accepted_by || '',
    ])))
    ;(data.untraced_tests || []).forEach(t => rows.push([
      '(none)', '', t.title, t.application_name,
      t.last_result || 'never run', t.last_run_at || '', t.environment || '',
      t.accepted_by || '',
    ]))
  } else if (tab === 'executions') {
    rows.push(['Test case', 'Application', 'Requirement', 'Result',
               'Environment', 'Started by', 'When', 'Duration (s)'])
    ;(data.runs || []).forEach(r => rows.push([
      r.test_title, r.application_name, r.requirement_id || '', r.result,
      r.environment || '', r.triggered_by, r.executed_at,
      r.duration_ms ? (r.duration_ms / 1000).toFixed(1) : '',
    ]))
  } else {
    rows.push(['Application', 'Test cases', 'Automated', 'Coverage %',
               'P0/P1 without a script', 'Imported', 'Requirements'])
    ;(data.applications || []).forEach(a => rows.push([
      a.name, a.test_cases, a.automated, a.coverage_pct,
      a.critical_gap, a.imported, a.requirements,
    ]))
  }

  const csv = rows.map(r => r.map(cell => {
    const s = String(cell ?? '')
    return /[",\n]/.test(s) ? `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"` : s
  }).join(',')).join('\n')

  const stamp = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)
  const blob = new Blob([csv], { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8;' })
  const a = document.createElement('a')
  a.href = URL.createObjectURL(blob)
  a.download = `nextgen2-${tab}-${stamp}.csv`
  a.click()
  URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href)
}

FILE: frontend/app/scenarios/page.js

'use client'
/**
 * app/scenarios/page.js
 *
 * The test repository, across every application.
 *
 * The application page answers "tell me about Netra" — it has environments,
 * suites, run buttons and history, all scoped to one thing. This answers a
 * different kind of question, and one you cannot get at by clicking through
 * four applications in turn:
 *
 *     how much of the estate is automated
 *     which P0 and P1 tests still have no script
 *     what came from an import versus what the AI proposed
 *     which tests cover a given requirement
 *
 * Acting on a selection reuses the endpoints that already exist, so there is
 * no second way to add something to a suite or generate a script.
 */
import { useState, useEffect, useCallback, useMemo } from 'react'
import Link from 'next/link'
import {
  Search, CheckCircle2, XCircle, MinusCircle, Zap, Layers, RefreshCw,
  ExternalLink,
} from 'lucide-react'
import {
  listRepositoryTestCases, getRepositorySummary,
  getSuites, setSuiteMembers, getSuite, generateScriptsFor,
} from '../../lib/api'
import styles from './Scenarios.module.css'

export default function ScenariosPage() {
  const [summary, setSummary] = useState(null)
  const [cases, setCases] = useState(null)
  const [total, setTotal] = useState(0)
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(() => new Set())
  const [toast, setToast] = useState(null)
  const [adding, setAdding] = useState(false)
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState({
    application_id: '', priority: '', automated: '', source: '', scenario: '', search: '',
  })

  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    setBusy(true)
    try {
      const d = await listRepositoryTestCases(filters)
      setCases(d.test_cases || [])
      setTotal(d.total || 0)
    } catch {
      setCases([])
    } finally { setBusy(false) }
  }, [filters])

  useEffect(() => { load() }, [load])

  useEffect(() => {
    getRepositorySummary().then(setSummary).catch(() => setSummary(null))
  }, [])

  function set(k, v) {
    setFilters(f => ({ ...f, [k]: v }))
    setSelected(new Set())          // a filter change makes the old selection meaningless
  }

  function toggle(id) {
    setSelected(prev => {
      const n = new Set(prev)
      n.has(id) ? n.delete(id) : n.add(id)
      return n
    })
  }

  const chosen = useMemo(
    () => (cases || []).filter(c => selected.has(c.id)),
    [cases, selected]
  )

  // Suites belong to one application, so adding across applications is not a
  // thing that exists. Said plainly rather than silently doing something odd.
  const chosenApps = useMemo(
    () => Array.from(new Set(chosen.map(c => c.application_id))),
    [chosen]
  )
  const oneApplication = chosenApps.length === 1

  /**
   * Generate a script for everything selected.
   *
   * Generation is per application only because the endpoint takes an
   * application id — each test case already knows which one it belongs to,
   * so a selection spanning several is simply several calls. Blocking it
   * was a restriction I had no reason to impose; a suite is a different
   * matter, because a suite genuinely belongs to one application.
   */
  async function generateForSelected() {
    if (!chosen.length) return
    setBusy(true)
    const byApplication = chosen.reduce((acc, c) => {
      (acc[c.application_id] = acc[c.application_id] || []).push(c.id)
      return acc
    }, {})
    const failed = []
    for (const [appId, ids] of Object.entries(byApplication)) {
      try {
        await generateScriptsFor(Number(appId), ids)
      } catch (e) {
        const name = chosen.find(c => String(c.application_id) === appId)?.application_name || appId
        failed.push(`${name}: ${e.message}`)
      }
    }
    const apps = Object.keys(byApplication).length
    setToast(
      failed.length
        ? { message: `Some did not start — ${failed.join('; ')}`, tone: 'error' }
        : { message: `Generating ${chosen.length} script${chosen.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`
                     + (apps > 1 ? ` across ${apps} applications` : '')
                     + ' — about a minute each.' }
    )
    setSelected(new Set())
    setBusy(false)
    setTimeout(load, 2000)
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <div className={styles.head}>
        <div>
          <h2 className={styles.title}>Scenarios</h2>
          <p className={styles.sub}>
            Every test case across every application — what is covered, what
            is not, and where it came from.
          </p>
        </div>
        <button className={styles.refresh} onClick={load} disabled={busy}>
          <RefreshCw size={14} strokeWidth={2} className={busy ? styles.spin : ''} />
          Refresh
        </button>
      </div>

      {summary && <SummaryStrip summary={summary} onFilter={set} />}

      <div className={styles.filters}>
        <div className={styles.searchBox}>
          <Search size={14} strokeWidth={2} />
          <input
            placeholder="Search test cases…"
            value={filters.search}
            onChange={e => set('search', e.target.value)}
          />
        </div>
        <select className={styles.select} value={filters.application_id}
                onChange={e => set('application_id', e.target.value)}>
          <option value="">All applications</option>
          {(summary?.applications || []).map(a => (
            <option key={a.id} value={a.id}>{a.name}</option>
          ))}
        </select>
        <select className={styles.select} value={filters.priority}
                onChange={e => set('priority', e.target.value)}>
          <option value="">Any priority</option>
          {['P0', 'P1', 'P2', 'P3'].map(p => <option key={p} value={p}>{p}</option>)}
        </select>
        <select className={styles.select} value={filters.automated}
                onChange={e => set('automated', e.target.value)}>
          <option value="">Automated or not</option>
          <option value="yes">Automated</option>
          <option value="no">Not automated</option>
        </select>
        <select className={styles.select} value={filters.source}
                onChange={e => set('source', e.target.value)}>
          <option value="">Any source</option>
          <option value="author_agent">Proposed by AI</option>
          <option value="bulk_import">Imported</option>
          <option value="alm">ALM</option>
          <option value="jira">Jira</option>
          <option value="brd">BRD document</option>
          <option value="crawl">Crawl-only</option>
        </select>
        {(summary?.scenarios || []).length > 0 && (
          <select className={styles.select} value={filters.scenario}
                  onChange={e => set('scenario', e.target.value)}>
            <option value="">Any scenario</option>
            {summary.scenarios.map(s => <option key={s} value={s}>{s}</option>)}
          </select>
        )}
      </div>

      {cases === null && <div className="skeleton" style={{ height: 240 }} />}

      {cases && cases.length === 0 && (
        <div className={styles.empty}>Nothing matches these filters.</div>
      )}

      {cases && cases.length > 0 && (
        <>
          <div className={styles.countLine}>
            Showing {cases.length} of {total}
            {total > cases.length && ' — narrow the filters to see the rest'}
          </div>
          <div className="card" style={{ padding: 0 }}>
            {cases.map(c => (
              <label key={c.id} className={styles.row}>
                <input
                  type="checkbox"
                  className={styles.checkbox}
                  checked={selected.has(c.id)}
                  onChange={() => toggle(c.id)}
                />
                {c.priority && (
                  <span className={styles.prio} data-level={c.priority}>{c.priority}</span>
                )}
                <span className={styles.rowMain}>
                  <span className={styles.rowTitle}>{c.title}</span>
                  <span className={styles.rowMeta}>
                    <Link href={`/applications/${c.application_id}`} className={styles.appLink}>
                      {c.application_name}
                    </Link>
                    {c.scenario && <> · {c.scenario}</>}
                    {c.requirement_id && <> · <span className={styles.req}>{c.requirement_id}</span></>}
                    {c.source === 'bulk_import' && <> · <span className={styles.imported}>imported</span></>}
                    {c.origin && (
                      <>
                        {' '}· <span className={styles.origin} data-origin={String(c.origin).toLowerCase()}>
                          {String(c.origin).toLowerCase() === 'jira'
                            ? 'Jira'
                            : String(c.origin).toLowerCase() === 'brd'
                              ? 'BRD'
                              : String(c.origin).toLowerCase() === 'alm'
                                ? 'ALM'
                                : 'Crawl'}
                        </span>
                      </>
                    )}
                  </span>
                </span>
                {c.automated
                  ? <span className={styles.auto}><CheckCircle2 size={13} strokeWidth={2} /> automated</span>
                  : <span className={styles.notAuto}><MinusCircle size={13} strokeWidth={2} /> no script</span>}
                {c.run_count > 0 && (
                  <span className={styles.runs} data-result={c.last_result}>
                    {c.run_count} run{c.run_count === 1 ? '' : 's'}
                  </span>
                )}
              </label>
            ))}
          </div>
        </>
      )}

      {selected.size > 0 && (
        <div className={styles.actionBar}>
          <span className={styles.selCount}>
            {selected.size} selected
            {!oneApplication && (
              <span className={styles.selWarn}>
                {' '}across {chosenApps.length} applications — a suite belongs to one
              </span>
            )}
          </span>
          <button className={styles.barBtn} disabled={busy}
                  onClick={generateForSelected}
                  title="Generate a script for each selected test case">
            <Zap size={14} strokeWidth={2} /> Generate scripts
          </button>
          <button className={styles.barBtn} disabled={busy || !oneApplication}
                  onClick={() => setAdding(true)}
                  title={oneApplication
                    ? 'Add these to a suite'
                    : 'A suite belongs to one application — select from a single one'}>
            <Layers size={14} strokeWidth={2} /> Add to suite
          </button>
          <button className={styles.barGhost} onClick={() => setSelected(new Set())}>
            Clear
          </button>
        </div>
      )}

      {adding && oneApplication && (
        <AddToSuite
          applicationId={chosenApps[0]}
          caseIds={chosen.map(c => c.id)}
          onClose={() => setAdding(false)}
          onDone={(msg) => { setAdding(false); setSelected(new Set()); setToast({ message: msg }) }}
        />
      )}

      {toast && (
        <div className={`${styles.toast} ${toast.tone === 'error' ? styles.toastError : ''}`}>
          {toast.message}
          <button className={styles.toastClose} onClick={() => setToast(null)}>✕</button>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

/** Coverage at a glance, with each number acting as a filter. */
function SummaryStrip({ summary, onFilter }) {
  return (
    <div className={styles.summary}>
      <Stat label="Test cases" value={summary.total} />
      <Stat label="Automated" value={`${summary.automated} · ${summary.coverage_pct}%`}
            onClick={() => onFilter('automated', 'yes')} />
      <Stat label="Imported" value={summary.imported}
            onClick={() => onFilter('source', 'bulk_import')} />
      {/* The number that actually matters: critical tests with no automation. */}
      <Stat label="P0/P1 without a script" value={summary.critical_gap}
            tone={summary.critical_gap > 0 ? 'warn' : undefined}
            onClick={() => onFilter('automated', 'no')} />
    </div>
  )
}

function Stat({ label, value, tone, onClick }) {
  const Tag = onClick ? 'button' : 'div'
  return (
    <Tag className={`${styles.stat} ${tone === 'warn' ? styles.statWarn : ''}`} onClick={onClick}>
      <span className={styles.statValue}>{value}</span>
      <span className={styles.statLabel}>{label}</span>
    </Tag>
  )
}

/** Add the selection to one of that application's suites. */
function AddToSuite({ applicationId, caseIds, onClose, onDone }) {
  const [suites, setSuites] = useState(null)
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)
  const [error, setError] = useState(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    getSuites(applicationId)
      .then(d => setSuites(d.suites || []))
      .catch(() => setSuites([]))
  }, [applicationId])

  async function add(suite) {
    setBusy(true); setError(null)
    try {
      // Membership is set as a whole list, so the existing members have to be
      // read first — otherwise adding would quietly remove everything else.
      const full = await getSuite(suite.id)
      const existing = (full.suite?.members || []).map(m => m.id)
      const merged = Array.from(new Set([...existing, ...caseIds]))
      const res = await setSuiteMembers(suite.id, merged)
      if (res.error) { setError(res.error); return }
      const added = merged.length - existing.length
      onDone(`${added} test case${added === 1 ? '' : 's'} added to ${suite.name}.`)
    } catch (e) {
      setError(e.message)
    } finally { setBusy(false) }
  }

  return (
    <div className={styles.backdrop} onClick={onClose}>
      <div className={styles.modal} onClick={e => e.stopPropagation()}>
        <div className={styles.modalHead}>
          <span className={styles.modalTitle}>
            Add {caseIds.length} test case{caseIds.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} to a suite
          </span>
          <button className={styles.ghost} onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
        </div>
        <div className={styles.modalBody}>
          {suites === null && <div className="skeleton" style={{ height: 80 }} />}
          {suites && suites.length === 0 && (
            <p className={styles.hint}>
              This application has no suites yet. Create one on its page first.
            </p>
          )}
          {suites && suites.map(s => (
            <button key={s.id} className={styles.suiteOption} disabled={busy}
                    onClick={() => add(s)}>
              <span className={styles.suiteKind} data-kind={s.kind}>{s.kind}</span>
              <span className={styles.suiteName}>{s.name}</span>
              <span className={styles.hint}>{s.member_count} already in it</span>
            </button>
          ))}
          {error && <div className={styles.error}>{error}</div>}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
