'use client'

/**
 * app/schedules/page.js
 *
 * Scheduled runs — test suites and Jira change-detection.
 *
 * A scheduler is invisible by nature — you cannot watch a clock tick over in
 * a meeting. So this page makes the waiting visible: every schedule shows a
 * live countdown to its next run, the list refreshes itself, and a run that
 * fires appears without anyone touching the page.
 *
 * A schedule is one of two types:
 *   - Suite run: runs a test suite (smoke/regression/custom).
 *   - Jira sync: checks a Jira project for changed / new requirements and
 *     flags the affected test cases. It DETECTS only — generating tests from a
 *     flagged requirement stays a separate, human action.
 *
 * "Run now" uses the same code path as the scheduler, so demonstrating it by
 * hand is a genuine rehearsal rather than a lookalike.
 */

import { useState, useEffect, useCallback, useMemo } from 'react'
import Link from 'next/link'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import {
  Calendar, Clock, Play, Pause, Trash2, Plus, CheckCircle2, XCircle,
  MinusCircle, Mail, RefreshCw, ChevronRight,
} from 'lucide-react'
import {
  getSchedules, createSchedule, updateSchedule, deleteSchedule,
  runScheduleNow, getApplications, getApplication, getSuites, getSuite,
  getJiraPending, markTestCaseReviewed, archiveScenario,
} from '../../lib/api'
import styles from './Schedules.module.css'

const FREQUENCIES = [
  { value: 'once',     label: 'Once' },
  { value: 'hourly',   label: 'Hourly' },
  { value: 'daily',    label: 'Daily' },
  { value: 'weekdays', label: 'Weekdays' },
  { value: 'weekly',   label: 'Weekly' },
]

// A Jira run returns a change-detection summary rather than a suite result.
// This is the reliable way to tell them apart in the "Run now" response and in
// the stored last_summary, without depending on job_type being present.
function isJiraResult(x) {
  return !!x && (x.project_key !== undefined || 'changed_requirements' in x)
}

export default function SchedulesPage() {
  const [schedules, setSchedules] = useState(null)
  const [creating, setCreating] = useState(false)
  const [runningId, setRunningId] = useState(null)
  const [toast, setToast] = useState(null)
  const [tick, setTick] = useState(0)
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState('all')

  // Filter chips are built from what is actually present, so no empty chip is
  // ever shown: always "All", one per suite kind in use, and "Jira sync" if
  // any Jira schedule exists.
  const filters = useMemo(() => {
    const out = [{ key: 'all', label: 'All' }]
    if (!schedules) return out
    const kinds = new Set()
    let hasJira = false
    for (const s of schedules) {
      if (s.job_type === 'jira_sync') hasJira = true
      else if (s.suite_kind) kinds.add(s.suite_kind)
    }
    for (const k of ['smoke', 'regression', 'custom']) {
      if (kinds.has(k)) { out.push({ key: `kind:${k}`, label: cap(k) }); kinds.delete(k) }
    }
    for (const k of kinds) out.push({ key: `kind:${k}`, label: cap(k) })  // any others
    if (hasJira) out.push({ key: 'jira', label: 'Jira sync' })
    return out
  }, [schedules])

  const visible = (schedules || []).filter(s => {
    if (filter === 'all') return true
    if (filter === 'jira') return s.job_type === 'jira_sync'
    if (filter.startsWith('kind:')) return s.job_type !== 'jira_sync' && s.suite_kind === filter.slice(5)
    return true
  })

  const load = useCallback(async () => {
    try {
      const d = await getSchedules()
      const list = d.schedules || []
      setSchedules(list)
      return list
    } catch { setSchedules([]); return [] }
  }, [])

  // Jira review backlog per application. Fetched only on load and after
  // actions — never on the 1s countdown or the 15s list timer — so the
  // on-screen queue reflects the current standing state without polling Jira
  // on every tick.
  const [pendingByApp, setPendingByApp] = useState({})
  const loadPending = useCallback(async (list) => {
    const jiraApps = [...new Set(
      (list || []).filter(s => s.job_type === 'jira_sync').map(s => s.application_id)
    )]
    if (!jiraApps.length) return
    const entries = await Promise.all(jiraApps.map(async id => {
      try { return [id, await getJiraPending(id)] } catch { return [id, null] }
    }))
    setPendingByApp(prev => ({ ...prev, ...Object.fromEntries(entries) }))
  }, [])

  const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
    const list = await load()
    await loadPending(list)
  }, [load, loadPending])

  useEffect(() => { refresh() }, [refresh])

  // Two timers with different jobs: one drives the countdown text every
  // second, the other re-reads the list so a run that fires on the server
  // appears here on its own.
  useEffect(() => {
    const t = setInterval(() => setTick(n => n + 1), 1000)
    return () => clearInterval(t)
  }, [])
  useEffect(() => {
    const t = setInterval(load, 15000)
    return () => clearInterval(t)
  }, [load])

  async function runNow(s) {
    setRunningId(s.id)
    try {
      const r = await runScheduleNow(s.id)
      if (r.error) {
        setToast({ message: r.error, tone: 'error' })
      } else if (isJiraResult(r)) {
        // Jira sync: name what changed / is new, not pass/fail.
        const changed = r.changed_requirements || []
        const flagged = r.flagged_cases || []
        const created = r.new_requirements || []
        let msg
        if (!changed.length && !flagged.length && !created.length) {
          msg = `${r.project_key}: no changes since last check`
        } else {
          const parts = []
          if (changed.length) parts.push(`changed: ${changed.join(', ')}`)
          if (flagged.length) parts.push(`${flagged.length} test case${flagged.length > 1 ? 's' : ''} flagged`)
          if (created.length) parts.push(`new: ${created.join(', ')}`)
          msg = `${r.project_key} — ${parts.join(' · ')}`
        }
        setToast({ message: msg + webhookNote(r.webhook_status) })
      } else {
        // Suite run: the original pass/fail summary.
        setToast({
          message: `${r.suite}: ${r.passed} passed, ${r.failed} failed` +
                   (r.skipped ? `, ${r.skipped} skipped` : '') +
                   webhookNote(r.webhook_status),
          tone: r.failed ? 'error' : undefined,
        })
      }
      refresh()
    } catch (e) {
      setToast({ message: e.message, tone: 'error' })
    } finally { setRunningId(null) }
  }

  async function toggleEnabled(s) {
    await updateSchedule(s.id, { enabled: !s.enabled })
    load()
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <div className={styles.pageHead}>
        <div>
          <h2 className={styles.pageTitle}>Schedules</h2>
          <p className={styles.pageSub}>
            Suites that run on their own, and Jira checks that flag changed
            requirements. Nobody has to remember to press anything.
          </p>
        </div>
        <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={() => setCreating(true)}>
          <Plus size={15} strokeWidth={2} style={{ verticalAlign: -3, marginRight: 6 }} />
          New schedule
        </button>
      </div>

      {schedules === null && <div className="skeleton" style={{ height: 120 }} />}

      {schedules && schedules.length > 0 && filters.length > 1 && (
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, marginBottom: 16, flexWrap: 'wrap' }}>
          {filters.map(f => (
            <button key={f.key} className={styles.actBtn}
                    onClick={() => setFilter(f.key)}
                    style={filter === f.key
                      ? { borderColor: 'var(--accent)', color: 'var(--accent)' }
                      : undefined}>
              {f.label}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}

      {schedules && schedules.length === 0 && (
        <div className="card" style={{ padding: 40, textAlign: 'center' }}>
          <Calendar size={30} strokeWidth={1.5} className={styles.emptyIcon} />
          <p className={styles.emptyTitle}>No schedules yet</p>
          <p className={styles.emptySub}>
            Create one to run a suite automatically, or a Jira sync to watch a
            project for requirement changes.
          </p>
        </div>
      )}

      {schedules && visible.map(s => (
        <ScheduleCard
          key={s.id}
          schedule={s}
          tick={tick}
          pending={pendingByApp[s.application_id]}
          running={runningId === s.id}
          onRun={() => runNow(s)}
          onToggle={() => toggleEnabled(s)}
          onReviewed={refresh}
          onDelete={async () => { await deleteSchedule(s.id); load() }}
        />
      ))}

      {creating && (
        <ScheduleForm
          onClose={() => setCreating(false)}
          onSaved={() => { setCreating(false); refresh() }}
        />
      )}

      {toast && (
        <div className={`${styles.toast} ${toast.tone === 'error' ? styles.toastError : ''}`}>
          {toast.message}
          <button className={styles.toastClose} onClick={() => setToast(null)}>✕</button>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

/** One schedule, with its countdown, recent results and controls. */
function ScheduleCard({ schedule: s, tick, pending, running, onRun, onToggle, onReviewed, onDelete }) {
  const countdown = useCountdown(s.next_run_at, tick)
  const last = s.last_summary || {}
  const isJira = s.job_type === 'jira_sync'
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(null)
  const [opening, setOpening] = useState(false)
  const router = useRouter()

  // Regenerate / Generate reuse the existing New Test Suite wizard (survey →
  // ScenarioReview → accept → generate → report), deep-linked and scoped to one
  // Jira requirement. No modal, no duplicated review screen — just the wizard
  // you already have. The requirement's flag is cleared server-side on accept.
  async function openWizard(issueKey) {
    setOpening(true)
    try {
      const app = await getApplication(s.application_id)
      const base_url = app?.application?.base_url || app?.base_url || ''
      const params = new URLSearchParams({
        source: 'jira',
        project: s.jira_project_key || '',
        issue: issueKey,
        app: s.application_name || '',
        url: base_url,
      })
      router.push(`/new-test-suite?${params.toString()}`)
    } catch {
      setOpening(false)
    }
  }

  // The requirement changed but this test is still valid: clear the flag,
  // regenerate nothing. This is the explicit "reviewed, no change" decision.
  async function noChange(id) {
    setBusy(id)
    try { await markTestCaseReviewed(id); onReviewed && onReviewed() }
    catch { /* parent refresh reconciles */ }
    finally { setBusy(null) }
  }

  // This test no longer applies: archive it (row + history kept for audit).
  async function reject(id) {
    setBusy(id)
    try { await archiveScenario(id); onReviewed && onReviewed() }
    catch { /* parent refresh reconciles */ }
    finally { setBusy(null) }
  }

  // Which test cases this schedule will actually run. Suite-only: a Jira
  // schedule has no suite to expand.
  const [members, setMembers] = useState(null)
  const [showMembers, setShowMembers] = useState(false)

  async function toggleMembers() {
    const next = !showMembers
    setShowMembers(next)
    if (next && members === null && s.suite_id) {
      try {
        const d = await getSuite(s.suite_id)
        setMembers(d.suite?.members || [])
      } catch { setMembers([]) }
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className={`card ${styles.schedCard}`}>
      <div className={styles.schedTop}>
        <span className={`${styles.dot} ${s.enabled ? styles.dotOn : ''}`} />
        <div className={styles.schedMain}>
          <div className={styles.schedName}>{s.name}</div>
          <div className={styles.schedMeta}>
            {/* Type comes first so the list is unambiguous at a glance. */}
            {isJira ? 'Jira sync' : 'Suite'} · {s.application_name}
            {isJira && s.jira_project_key && <> · project {s.jira_project_key}</>}
            {!isJira && s.suite_name && (
              <> · <button className={styles.suiteChip} data-kind={s.suite_kind}
                           onClick={toggleMembers}
                           title="Show the test cases this suite runs">
                {s.suite_name}
                <ChevronRight size={10} strokeWidth={2.5}
                  style={{ verticalAlign: -1, marginLeft: 3,
                           transform: showMembers ? 'rotate(90deg)' : 'none',
                           transition: 'transform .15s' }} />
              </button></>
            )}
            {!isJira && s.environment && <> · {s.environment}</>}
            {!isJira && typeof s.member_count === 'number' && <> · {s.member_count} test cases</>}
          </div>
        </div>

        <div className={styles.schedWhen}>
          <div className={styles.freq}>
            <Clock size={12} strokeWidth={2} style={{ verticalAlign: -1, marginRight: 5 }} />
            {FREQUENCIES.find(f => f.value === s.frequency)?.label || s.frequency}
            {s.next_run_at && ` · ${formatTime(s.next_run_at)}`}
          </div>
          {s.enabled && countdown && (
            <div className={`${styles.countdown} ${countdown.soon ? styles.countdownSoon : ''}`}>
              {countdown.text}
            </div>
          )}
          {!s.enabled && <div className={styles.paused}>paused</div>}
        </div>

        <div className={styles.schedActions}>
          <button className={styles.actBtn} onClick={onRun} disabled={running}
                  title={isJira
                    ? 'Check Jira for changes now — the same path the scheduler uses'
                    : 'Run this schedule now — the same path the scheduler uses'}>
            {running
              ? <RefreshCw size={14} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.spin} />
              : <Play size={14} strokeWidth={2} />}
            {running ? (isJira ? 'Checking…' : 'Running…') : (isJira ? 'Check now' : 'Run now')}
          </button>
          <button className={styles.actBtn} onClick={onToggle}
                  title={s.enabled ? 'Pause' : 'Resume'}>
            {s.enabled ? <Pause size={14} strokeWidth={2} /> : <Play size={14} strokeWidth={2} />}
          </button>
          <button className={`${styles.actBtn} ${styles.actDanger}`} onClick={onDelete} title="Delete">
            <Trash2 size={14} strokeWidth={2} />
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>

      {showMembers && (
        <div className={styles.memberBox}>
          {members === null && <div className="skeleton" style={{ height: 40 }} />}
          {members && members.length === 0 && (
            <div className={styles.memberEmpty}>This suite has no test cases.</div>
          )}
          {members && members.map(m => (
            <div key={m.id} className={styles.memberRow}>
              {m.priority && <span className={styles.memberPrio}>{m.priority}</span>}
              <span className={styles.memberName}>{m.title}</span>
              {m.automated
                ? <span className={styles.memberAuto}>automated</span>
                : <span className={styles.memberManual}>no script · will be skipped</span>}
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}

      {s.last_run_at && (
        <div className={styles.schedLast}>
          <span className={styles.lastLabel}>{isJira ? 'review queue' : 'last run'}</span>
          <span className={styles.lastTime}>{formatWhen(s.last_run_at)}</span>

          {isJira ? (
            <span className={styles.counts}>
              {pending
                ? (pending.changed_count > 0 || pending.new_count > 0
                    ? `${pending.changed_count} awaiting review · ${pending.new_count} new`
                    : 'nothing pending')
                : <JiraLastSummary last={last} />}
            </span>
          ) : (
            <span className={styles.counts}>
              <CheckCircle2 size={13} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.pass} />
              {last.passed ?? 0}
              <XCircle size={13} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.fail} />
              {last.failed ?? 0}
              {(last.skipped ?? 0) > 0 && (
                <>
                  <MinusCircle size={13} strokeWidth={2} className={styles.skip} />
                  {last.skipped}
                </>
              )}
            </span>
          )}

          {s.last_summary?.webhook_status && (
            <span className={styles.webhook}>
              <Mail size={12} strokeWidth={2} style={{ verticalAlign: -2, marginRight: 4 }} />
              {s.last_summary.webhook_status}
            </span>
          )}

          {!isJira && (
            <Link href="/executions" className={styles.detailLink}>
              see details →
            </Link>
          )}

          {!isJira && s.recent_runs?.length > 0 && (
            <span className={styles.spark}>
              {s.recent_runs.slice().reverse().map((r, i) => (
                <span key={i}
                      className={`${styles.sparkBar} ${r.failed ? styles.sparkFail : styles.sparkPass}`}
                      title={`${r.passed} passed, ${r.failed} failed`} />
              ))}
            </span>
          )}
        </div>
      )}

      {/* Jira: the standing review queue for this app — the CURRENT backlog,
          not one check's delta. Each item persists until a human clears it, so
          a changed requirement no longer vanishes on the next check. */}
      {isJira && pending && (pending.changed?.length > 0 || pending.new?.length > 0) && (
        <div className={styles.memberBox}>
          {pending.changed?.length > 0 && (
            <div className={styles.memberRow}
                 style={{ background: 'var(--bg-card-alt)', fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 11,
                          textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.05em', color: 'var(--amber)' }}>
              Changed — needs review
            </div>
          )}
          {pending.changed.map(g => (
            <div key={`chg-${g.requirement_id}`}>
              <div className={styles.memberRow}>
                <span className={styles.memberPrio} style={{ color: 'var(--amber)' }}>changed</span>
                <span className={styles.memberName} style={{ fontWeight: 500, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>
                  {g.requirement_id}{g.summary ? ` — ${g.summary}` : ''}
                </span>
                <button className={styles.actBtn} disabled={opening}
                        onClick={() => openWizard(g.requirement_id)}
                        title="Re-derive this requirement's test(s) in the Test Suite wizard, review the steps, then generate. Clears the flag on accept.">
                  {opening ? 'Opening…' : 'Regenerate'}
                </button>
              </div>
              {g.cases.map(c => (
                <div key={`case-${c.id}`} className={styles.memberRow} style={{ paddingLeft: 40 }}>
                  <span className={styles.memberPrio}>↳ test</span>
                  <span className={styles.memberName}>{c.title}</span>
                  <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', gap: 6, flexShrink: 0 }}>
                    <button className={styles.actBtn} disabled={busy === c.id}
                            onClick={() => noChange(c.id)}
                            title="The requirement changed but this test is still valid — clear the flag. Nothing is regenerated.">
                      {busy === c.id ? '…' : 'No change needed'}
                    </button>
                    <button className={`${styles.actBtn} ${styles.actDanger}`} disabled={busy === c.id}
                            onClick={() => reject(c.id)}
                            title="This test no longer applies — archive it. The row and its run history are kept for audit.">
                      Reject
                    </button>
                  </span>
                </div>
              ))}
            </div>
          ))}

          {pending.new?.length > 0 && (
            <div className={styles.memberRow}
                 style={{ background: 'var(--bg-card-alt)', fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 11,
                          textTransform: 'uppercase', letterSpacing: '0.05em', color: 'var(--accent)',
                          borderTop: pending.changed?.length ? '1px solid var(--border)' : 'none' }}>
              New — no test coverage
            </div>
          )}
          {pending.new.map(n => (
            <div key={`new-${n.requirement_id}`} className={styles.memberRow}>
              <span className={styles.memberPrio} style={{ color: 'var(--accent)' }}>new</span>
              <span className={styles.memberName} style={{ fontWeight: 500, color: 'var(--text-primary)' }}>
                {n.requirement_id}{n.summary ? ` — ${n.summary}` : ''}
              </span>
              <button className={styles.actBtn} disabled={opening}
                      onClick={() => openWizard(n.requirement_id)}
                      title="Survey this requirement in the Test Suite wizard, review the proposed test, then generate it.">
                {opening ? 'Opening…' : 'Generate tests'}
              </button>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

/** Change-detection counts for a Jira schedule's last run (changed / flagged /
 *  new), reusing the same understated row styling as suite counts. */
function JiraLastSummary({ last }) {
  const changed = (last.changed_requirements || []).length
  const flagged = (last.flagged_cases || []).length
  const created = (last.new_requirements || []).length
  if (!changed && !flagged && !created) {
    return <span className={styles.counts}>no changes</span>
  }
  return (
    <span className={styles.counts}>
      {changed} changed · {flagged} flagged · {created} new
    </span>
  )
}

/** Create a schedule — a suite run or a Jira sync. Defaults to five minutes
 *  from now, the common case being "set it just ahead and watch it fire". */
function ScheduleForm({ onClose, onSaved }) {
  const [apps, setApps] = useState([])
  const [suites, setSuites] = useState([])
  const [form, setForm] = useState({
    job_type: 'suite_run',
    application_id: '', suite_id: '', jira_project_key: '', name: '',
    frequency: 'once', run_at: defaultRunAt(),
    environment: '', webhook_url: '', recipients: '',
  })
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)
  const [error, setError] = useState(null)

  const isJira = form.job_type === 'jira_sync'

  useEffect(() => { getApplications().then(setApps).catch(() => setApps([])) }, [])

  // Suites are only relevant to a suite-run schedule.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isJira || !form.application_id) { setSuites([]); return }
    getSuites(form.application_id)
      .then(d => setSuites(d.suites || []))
      .catch(() => setSuites([]))
  }, [form.application_id, isJira])

  function set(k, v) { setForm(f => ({ ...f, [k]: v })) }

  function onPickApp(v) {
    set('application_id', v)
    // Helpful default name for a Jira schedule so the list reads clearly.
    if (isJira && !form.name) {
      const a = apps.find(x => String(x.id) === v)
      if (a) set('name', `Jira Sync – ${a.name}`)
    }
  }

  async function save() {
    // Type-specific required fields.
    if (isJira) {
      if (!form.application_id || !form.jira_project_key.trim() || !form.name.trim()) {
        setError('Application, Jira project and a name are required.'); return
      }
    } else {
      if (!form.application_id || !form.suite_id || !form.name.trim()) {
        setError('Application, suite and a name are required.'); return
      }
    }

    setSaving(true); setError(null)
    try {
      const payload = {
        job_type: form.job_type,
        application_id: Number(form.application_id),
        name: form.name.trim(),
        frequency: form.frequency,
        run_at: new Date(form.run_at).toISOString(),
        webhook_url: form.webhook_url,
        recipients: form.recipients,
      }
      if (isJira) {
        payload.jira_project_key = form.jira_project_key.trim()
        payload.suite_id = null
        payload.enabled = false          // Jira schedules start paused
      } else {
        payload.suite_id = Number(form.suite_id)
        payload.environment = form.environment
        payload.enabled = true           // unchanged suite behaviour
      }

      const res = await createSchedule(payload)
      if (res.error) setError(res.error)
      else onSaved()
    } catch (e) { setError(e.message) } finally { setSaving(false) }
  }

  return (
    <div className={styles.backdrop} onClick={onClose}>
      <div className={styles.modal} onClick={e => e.stopPropagation()}>
        <div className={styles.modalHead}>
          <span className={styles.modalTitle}>New schedule</span>
          <button className={styles.ghost} onClick={onClose}>Close</button>
        </div>

        <div className={styles.modalBody}>
          <Field label="Schedule type">
            <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8 }}>
              <button type="button"
                      className={form.job_type === 'suite_run' ? 'btn btn-primary' : styles.ghost}
                      onClick={() => set('job_type', 'suite_run')}>
                Suite run
              </button>
              <button type="button"
                      className={form.job_type === 'jira_sync' ? 'btn btn-primary' : styles.ghost}
                      onClick={() => set('job_type', 'jira_sync')}>
                Jira sync
              </button>
            </div>
          </Field>

          <Field label="Application">
            <select className={styles.input} value={form.application_id}
                    onChange={e => onPickApp(e.target.value)}>
              <option value="">Select…</option>
              {apps.map(a => <option key={a.id} value={a.id}>{a.name}</option>)}
            </select>
          </Field>

          {!isJira && (
            <Field label="Suite">
              <select className={styles.input} value={form.suite_id}
                      onChange={e => {
                        set('suite_id', e.target.value)
                        const s = suites.find(x => String(x.id) === e.target.value)
                        if (s && !form.name) set('name', `${s.name} run`)
                      }}
                      disabled={!form.application_id}>
                <option value="">{form.application_id ? 'Select…' : 'Choose an application first'}</option>
                {suites.map(s => (
                  <option key={s.id} value={s.id}>
                    {s.name} ({s.member_count} test cases)
                  </option>
                ))}
              </select>
              {form.application_id && suites.length === 0 && (
                <span className={styles.hint}>
                  This application has no suites yet — create one on its page first.
                </span>
              )}
            </Field>
          )}

          {isJira && (
            <Field label="Jira project"
                   hint="The project key whose stories this schedule checks, e.g. KAN.">
              <input className={styles.input} value={form.jira_project_key}
                     onChange={e => set('jira_project_key', e.target.value)}
                     placeholder="e.g. KAN" />
            </Field>
          )}

          <Field label="Name">
            <input className={styles.input} value={form.name}
                   onChange={e => set('name', e.target.value)}
                   placeholder={isJira ? 'e.g. Jira Sync – Payroll' : 'e.g. Netra morning smoke'} />
          </Field>

          <div className={styles.row}>
            <Field label="Frequency">
              <select className={styles.input} value={form.frequency}
                      onChange={e => set('frequency', e.target.value)}>
                {FREQUENCIES.map(f => <option key={f.value} value={f.value}>{f.label}</option>)}
              </select>
            </Field>
            <Field label="First run">
              <input className={styles.input} type="datetime-local" value={form.run_at}
                     onChange={e => set('run_at', e.target.value)} />
            </Field>
          </div>

          {isJira && (
            <div className={styles.hint} style={{ marginTop: -6, marginBottom: 14 }}>
              Jira schedules start paused. Use “Check now” to detect changes on
              demand; enable it to run on the cadence above.
            </div>
          )}

          {!isJira && (
            <Field label="Environment"
                   hint="Leave blank to use the application's default environment.">
              <input className={styles.input} value={form.environment}
                     onChange={e => set('environment', e.target.value)}
                     placeholder="dev / test / stage" />
            </Field>
          )}

          <Field label="Webhook URL"
               hint="Posted to when the run finishes. Point this at your n8n webhook and n8n sends the email — NextGen2 never holds mail credentials.">
            <input className={styles.input} value={form.webhook_url}
                   onChange={e => set('webhook_url', e.target.value)}
                 placeholder="https://n8n.example.com/webhook/nextgen2" />
          </Field>

          <Field label="Recipients" hint="Recorded for reference; n8n decides delivery.">
            <input className={styles.input} value={form.recipients}
                   onChange={e => set('recipients', e.target.value)}
                   placeholder="qa-team@baxter.com" />
          </Field>

          {error && <div className={styles.error}>{error}</div>}
        </div>

        <div className={styles.modalFoot}>
          <button className={styles.ghost} onClick={onClose}>Cancel</button>
          <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={save} disabled={saving}>
            {saving ? 'Creating…' : 'Create schedule'}
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

function Field({ label, hint, children }) {
  return (
    <div className={styles.field}>
      <label className={styles.label}>{label}</label>
      {children}
      {hint && <span className={styles.hint}>{hint}</span>}
    </div>
  )
}

/**
 * Time remaining until the next run.
 *
 * Recomputed every second from the `tick` prop so the page has a single
 * timer rather than one per row.
 */
function useCountdown(nextRunAt, tick) {  // eslint-disable-line
  if (!nextRunAt) return null
  const ms = new Date(nextRunAt).getTime() - Date.now()
  if (ms <= 0) return { text: 'due now', soon: true }
  const s = Math.floor(ms / 1000)
  const d = Math.floor(s / 86400)
  const h = Math.floor((s % 86400) / 3600)
  const m = Math.floor((s % 3600) / 60)
  const sec = s % 60
  const text =
    d > 0 ? `in ${d}d ${h}h`
    : h > 0 ? `in ${h}h ${m}m`
    : m > 0 ? `in ${m}m ${String(sec).padStart(2, '0')}s`
    : `in ${sec}s`
  return { text, soon: ms < 10 * 60 * 1000 }
}

function cap(s) {
  return s ? s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1) : s
}

// Only mention the webhook when one actually fired — avoids the confusing
// "webhook no webhook configured" line when none is set.
function webhookNote(status) {
  if (!status || status === 'no webhook configured') return ''
  return ` · notified (${status})`
}

function defaultRunAt() {
  const d = new Date(Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000)   // five minutes ahead
  d.setSeconds(0, 0)
  const pad = n => String(n).padStart(2, '0')
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}T${pad(d.getHours())}:${pad(d.getMinutes())}`
}

function formatTime(iso) {
  const d = new Date(iso)
  return d.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' })
}

function formatWhen(iso) {
  const d = new Date(iso)
  const today = new Date().toDateString() === d.toDateString()
  return today
    ? `today ${d.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' })}`
    : d.toLocaleString([], { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' })
}

'use client'

/**
 * app/settings/page.js
 *
 * Local settings.
 *
 * Only one thing lives here today, and it matters more than it looks: the
 * name Kavach attributes actions to.
 *
 * Kavach has no authentication yet. Every request carries an X-Triggered-By
 * header, and the backend writes that value into the training record, the
 * approval fields on a test case, the healing decision log and the support
 * ticket. If it is always "anonymous", those records exist but say nothing —
 * a training record that cannot name who was trained is not evidence.
 *
 * So this is deliberately honest about what it is. It is a label, not a
 * login. Anyone can change it and nothing verifies it. What it buys is an
 * audit trail with real names in it before SSO lands, and exactly one place
 * to change when SSO does land: lib/api.js::getCurrentUser.
 */

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { Check, UserCircle, AlertTriangle } from 'lucide-react'
import { getCurrentUser, setCurrentUser, API_BASE } from '../../lib/api'

export default function SettingsPage() {
  const [name, setName] = useState('')
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(false)

  useEffect(() => {
    const current = getCurrentUser()
    setName(current === 'anonymous' ? '' : current)
  }, [])

  function save() {
    setCurrentUser(name.trim())
    setSaved(true)
    setTimeout(() => setSaved(false), 2500)
    // The sidebar chip reads the same value, so tell it to re-read rather
    // than letting the two disagree until the next full page load.
    window.dispatchEvent(new Event('kavach-user-changed'))
  }

  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <h1 style={{ fontSize: 26, fontWeight: 600, margin: '0 0 4px' }}>Settings</h1>
      <p style={{ fontSize: 14, color: 'var(--text-muted)', margin: '0 0 22px' }}>
        Preferences stored in this browser.
      </p>

      <section className="card" style={{ padding: '20px' }}>
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 10, marginBottom: 6 }}>
          <UserCircle size={17} strokeWidth={1.9} style={{ color: 'var(--accent)' }} />
          <h2 style={{ fontSize: 16, fontWeight: 600, margin: 0 }}>Your name</h2>
        </div>
        <p style={{ fontSize: 14, color: 'var(--text-muted)', margin: '0 0 16px', lineHeight: 1.6 }}>
          Used to attribute what you do in NextGen2 &mdash; training records, approvals,
          healing decisions and support tickets. Without it, those entries read
          &ldquo;anonymous&rdquo; and cannot show who did what.
        </p>

        <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 10, alignItems: 'flex-start' }}>
          <input
            className="form-input"
            value={name}
            onChange={e => { setName(e.target.value); setSaved(false) }}
            onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') save() }}
            placeholder="e.g. User Name"
            style={{ flex: 1 }}
          />
          <button className="btn btn-primary" onClick={save}>
            {saved ? <Check size={15} /> : null}
            {saved ? 'Saved' : 'Save'}
          </button>
        </div>

        {/* Said plainly rather than implied. Someone reading a training record
            needs to know what level of assurance it carries. */}
        <div style={{
          display: 'flex', gap: 9, marginTop: 16, padding: '11px 13px',
          background: 'var(--amber-bg)', color: 'var(--amber)',
          borderRadius: 'var(--radius-sm)', fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 1.55,
        }}>
          <AlertTriangle size={15} strokeWidth={2} style={{ flexShrink: 0, marginTop: 1 }} />
          <span>
            This is a label, not a login. Nothing verifies it, and anyone using
            this browser can change it. It gives the audit trail real names
            ahead of single sign-on, which will replace it.
          </span>
        </div>
      </section>

      <section className="card" style={{ padding: '20px', marginTop: 14 }}>
        <h2 style={{ fontSize: 16, fontWeight: 600, margin: '0 0 12px' }}>Connection</h2>
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between', fontSize: 14 }}>
          <span style={{ color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}>Backend</span>
          <code style={{ fontFamily: 'var(--font-mono)', fontSize: 12 }}>{API_BASE}</code>
        </div>
        <p style={{ fontSize: 12, color: 'var(--text-muted)', margin: '10px 0 0', lineHeight: 1.55 }}>
          Set by NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL at build time.
        </p>
      </section>
    </div>
  )
}

'use client'

/**
 * components/AppShell/AppShell.jsx
 * Persistent shell: Kavach shield sidebar, topbar with search +
 * light/dark toggle, primary actions. Uses Tabler icon classes.
 *
 * ChatPanel ("Ask Kavach") is mounted here so it is available on every
 * screen — it answers questions about coverage and failures using the real
 * database, and those questions come up wherever you happen to be.
 */

import Link from 'next/link'

const NAV_ITEMS = [
  { href: '/dashboard',    label: 'Dashboard',    icon: 'ti-layout-dashboard' },
  { href: '/applications', label: 'Applications', icon: 'ti-apps' },
  { href: '/scenarios',    label: 'Scenarios',    icon: 'ti-clipboard-list' },

]

  // standards that feed generation, this holds how to use Kavach. Different

  { href: '/help', label: 'Help & support', icon: 'ti-lifebuoy' },
]


/**
 * Reduce a name to at most two initials for the avatar.
 *
 * @param {string} name - The user's name, possibly empty.
 * @returns {string} Initials, or a dash when no name is set.
 */
function initials(name) {
  const parts = (name || '').trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)
  if (!parts.length) return '—'
  return (parts[0][0] + (parts.length > 1 ? parts[parts.length - 1][0] : '')).toUpperCase()
}


export default function AppShell({ children }) {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const { user, isAuthenticated } = useAuth()
  const [theme, setThemeState] = useState('dark')

  const signedInUserName = user?.name || user?.username || ''
  const signedInUserEmail = user?.username || ''

  // The name shown here is the same one sent as X-Triggered-By, so what the
  // sidebar says and what the audit trail records cannot disagree. Read on
  // mount rather than at module load, because localStorage does not exist
  // during server rendering.
  // The sidebar collapses to an icon rail. On a 1280px laptop the shell,
  // the content and an open assistant panel compete for the same width, and
  // the navigation is the part a user needs least while reading an answer.
  const [navCollapsed, setNavCollapsed] = useState(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    try { setNavCollapsed(localStorage.getItem('kavach-nav-collapsed') === '1') } catch {}
  }, [])
  function toggleNav() {
    setNavCollapsed(v => {
      const next = !v
      try { localStorage.setItem('kavach-nav-collapsed', next ? '1' : '0') } catch {}
      return next
    })
  }

  const [userName, setUserName] = useState('')
  useEffect(() => {
    const read = () => {
      const who = getCurrentUser()
      setUserName(who === 'anonymous' ? '' : who)
    }
    read()
    // Settings dispatches this after a save, so the chip updates without a
    // page reload.
    window.addEventListener('kavach-user-changed', read)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('kavach-user-changed', read)
  }, [])

  useEffect(() => {
    const saved = (typeof window !== 'undefined' && localStorage.getItem('kavach-theme')) || 'dark'
    setThemeState(saved)
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', saved)
  }, [])

  function setTheme(t) {
    setThemeState(t)
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', t)
    try { localStorage.setItem('kavach-theme', t) } catch {}
  }

  const isActive = (href) => pathname === href || pathname.startsWith(href + '/')

  const titleMap = {
    '/dashboard':'Home','/applications':'Applications','/scenarios':'Scenarios',
    '/executions':'Executions','/schedules':'Schedules','/reports':'Reports','/knowledge-base':'Knowledge base',
    '/help':'Help & support',
    '/settings':'Settings','/new-test-suite':'New Test Suite',
  }
  const pageTitle = titleMap[Object.keys(titleMap).find(k => isActive(k)) || ''] || 'NextGen2'

  return (
    <div className={styles.shell}>
      <aside
        className={`${styles.sidebar} ${navCollapsed ? styles.sidebarNarrow : ''}`}
        aria-label="Main navigation">
        <button
          className={styles.navToggle}
          onClick={toggleNav}
          title={navCollapsed ? 'Expand navigation' : 'Collapse navigation'}
          aria-label={navCollapsed ? 'Expand navigation' : 'Collapse navigation'}>
          {navCollapsed ? '›' : '‹'}
        </button>
        <div className={styles.logoArea}>
          <div className={styles.logoRow}>
            <div className={styles.logoMark} aria-hidden="true">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" width="34" height="34">
                <path d="M16 2L28 7v9c0 7.5-5.1 12.5-12 14C9.1 28.5 4 23.5 4 16V7l12-5z" fill="url(#kg)" stroke="url(#kg2)" strokeWidth="1"/>
                <path d="M11 16.5l3.2 3.2L21 12" stroke="#fff" strokeWidth="2.2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round"/>
                <defs>
                  <linearGradient id="kg" x1="4" y1="2" x2="28" y2="30"><stop stopColor="#6366f1"/><stop offset="1" stopColor="#4f7cff"/></linearGradient>
                  <linearGradient id="kg2" x1="4" y1="2" x2="28" y2="30"><stop stopColor="#818cf8"/><stop offset="1" stopColor="#4f7cff"/></linearGradient>
                </defs>
              </svg>
            </div>
            <div className={styles.brandText}>
              <div className={styles.brandName}>NextGen2</div>
              <div className={styles.brandSub}>Test Insights & Actions</div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

        <nav className={styles.nav}>
          {NAV_ITEMS.map(item => (
            <Link key={item.href} href={item.href}
              title={navCollapsed ? item.label : undefined}
              className={`${styles.navItem} ${isActive(item.href) ? styles.navItemActive : ''}`}>
              <i className={`ti ${item.icon} ${styles.navIcon}`} aria-hidden="true" />
              {/* Wrapped so the collapsed rail can hide it. A bare text node
                  cannot be targeted by CSS, which is why collapsing used to
                  shrink the sidebar and leave the words overflowing it. */}
              <span className={styles.navText}>{item.label}</span>
            </Link>
          ))}
          <div className={styles.navLabel}>Resources</div>
          {RESOURCE_ITEMS.map(item => (
            <Link key={item.href} href={item.href}
              title={navCollapsed ? item.label : undefined}
              className={`${styles.navItem} ${isActive(item.href) ? styles.navItemActive : ''}`}>
              <i className={`ti ${item.icon} ${styles.navIcon}`} aria-hidden="true" />
              {/* Wrapped so the collapsed rail can hide it. A bare text node
                  cannot be targeted by CSS, which is why collapsing used to
                  shrink the sidebar and leave the words overflowing it. */}
              <span className={styles.navText}>{item.label}</span>
            </Link>
          ))}
        </nav>

        <div className={styles.sidebarFoot}>
          <Link href="/settings"
            title={navCollapsed ? 'Settings' : undefined}
            className={`${styles.navItem} ${isActive('/settings') ? styles.navItemActive : ''}`}>
            <i className={`ti ti-settings ${styles.navIcon}`} aria-hidden="true" />
            <span className={styles.navText}>Settings</span>
          </Link>
          <div className={styles.userChip}>
            <div className={styles.avatar}>
              {initials(isAuthenticated ? signedInUserName : userName)}
            </div>
            <div className={styles.userMeta}>
              <div className={styles.userName}>
                {isAuthenticated ? signedInUserName : userName || 'Not signed in'}
              </div>
              <div
                className={styles.userRole}
                title={isAuthenticated ? signedInUserEmail : undefined}
              >
                {isAuthenticated ? (
                  signedInUserEmail
                ) : userName ? (
                  'Quality Lead'
                ) : (
                  <Link href="/settings">Set your name</Link>
                )}
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </aside>

      <div className={styles.main}>
        <div className={styles.topbar}>
          <div className={styles.pageTitle}>{pageTitle}</div>
          <div className={styles.spacer} />
          <div className={styles.search}>
            <i className="ti ti-search" aria-hidden="true" />
            <input placeholder="Search applications, scenarios…" />
          </div>
          <div className={styles.themeToggle}>
            <button className={theme === 'light' ? styles.themeOn : ''} onClick={() => setTheme('light')} aria-label="Light mode"><i className="ti ti-sun" /></button>
            <button className={theme === 'dark' ? styles.themeOn : ''} onClick={() => setTheme('dark')} aria-label="Dark mode"><i className="ti ti-moon" /></button>
          </div>
          <Link href="/new-test-suite"><button className="btn btn-primary"><i className="ti ti-plus" /> New Test Suite</button></Link>
        </div>
        <div className={styles.content}>{children}</div>
      </div>

      {/* Ask NextGen2 — available on every screen, answering from the database */}
      <ChatPanel />
    </div>
  )
}

'use client'

/**
 * components/AuthGuard/AuthGuard.jsx
 *
 * Shared protected layout covering every page in Kavach.
 *
 * Uses MsalAuthenticationTemplate from @azure/msal-react, which:
 *   - Renders children only when the user is authenticated.
 *   - Automatically triggers a login redirect when not authenticated.
 *   - Waits for MSAL's initialisation to complete before acting (avoids
 *     spurious redirects during the startup window).
 *
 * URL preservation is handled by MSAL's built-in mechanism
 * (navigateToLoginRequestUrl: true in msalConfig).  No manual
 * sessionStorage handling is required.
 *
 * The loadingComponent renders nothing while MSAL is starting up or while
 * the redirect is in flight; the browser navigates away almost immediately
 * so this blank state is imperceptible in practice.
 */

import { useEffect } from 'react'
import { InteractionType, InteractionRequiredAuthError } from '@azure/msal-browser'
import { MsalAuthenticationTemplate, useMsal } from '@azure/msal-react'
import { loginRequest } from '../../lib/msalConfig'

/** Blank while MSAL initialises or the redirect is in progress. */
function LoadingState() {
  return null
}

// Error codes that mean "the session/token expired or the silent refresh
// timed out" — i.e. the fix is simply to sign in again, not to show an
// error. monitor_window_timeout is the slow-iframe silent-refresh timeout;
// the interaction_required family means Entra wants the user to
// re-authenticate (expired session, Conditional Access, MFA, etc.).
const RECOVERABLE_ERROR_CODES = new Set([
  'monitor_window_timeout',
  'interaction_required',
  'login_required',
  'consent_required',
])

// Loop guard: if we auto-redirected within this window and we're still
// landing on the error screen, stop auto-redirecting and show the manual
// screen instead, so the user can never get trapped in a redirect cycle.
const AUTO_REDIRECT_FLAG = 'kavach.authAutoRedirectAt'
const AUTO_REDIRECT_COOLDOWN_MS = 30000

function isRecoverable(error) {
  if (!error) return false
  if (error instanceof InteractionRequiredAuthError) return true
  return RECOVERABLE_ERROR_CODES.has(error.errorCode)
}

function redirectedRecently() {
  try {
    const last = Number(sessionStorage.getItem(AUTO_REDIRECT_FLAG) || 0)
    return last > 0 && Date.now() - last < AUTO_REDIRECT_COOLDOWN_MS
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}

/**
 * Shown when authentication fails.
 *
 * For recoverable errors (expired session / silent-refresh timeout), the
 * user is sent straight to the Microsoft sign-in page instead of seeing an
 * error — if their Microsoft session is still valid the round-trip is
 * invisible, otherwise they simply sign in again and return to their page.
 * A full-page loginRedirect also avoids the hidden-iframe path that causes
 * monitor_window_timeout on slow corporate networks.
 *
 * A 30-second loop guard ensures that if the redirect does not resolve the
 * problem, we fall back to the manual "Try again" screen rather than
 * bouncing the user to login repeatedly.
 */
function AuthError({ error }) {
  const { instance } = useMsal()
  const recoverable = isRecoverable(error) && !redirectedRecently()

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!recoverable) return
    try {
      sessionStorage.setItem(AUTO_REDIRECT_FLAG, String(Date.now()))
    } catch {
      /* sessionStorage unavailable — still attempt the redirect */
    }
    instance.loginRedirect(loginRequest).catch(() => {
      /* If the redirect itself fails, the render below shows the manual
         screen on the next error cycle. */
    })
  }, [recoverable, instance])

  // While the recoverable redirect is in flight, render nothing — the
  // browser is navigating to Microsoft sign-in.
  if (recoverable) {
    return null
  }

  return (
    <div
      style={{
        display: 'flex',
        flexDirection: 'column',
        alignItems: 'center',
        justifyContent: 'center',
        height: '100vh',
        gap: '12px',
        fontFamily: 'var(--font-body)',
        padding: '24px',
        textAlign: 'center',
      }}
    >
      <p style={{ fontSize: 16, margin: 0 }}>
        Sign-in failed:{' '}
        {error?.message ?? 'An unexpected authentication error occurred.'}
      </p>
      <button
        onClick={() => window.location.reload()}
        style={{ padding: '8px 16px', cursor: 'pointer' }}
      >
        Try again
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

export default function AuthGuard({ children }) {
  return (
    <MsalAuthenticationTemplate
      interactionType={InteractionType.Redirect}
      authenticationRequest={loginRequest}
      loadingComponent={LoadingState}
      errorComponent={AuthError}
    >
      {children}
    </MsalAuthenticationTemplate>
  )
}

'use client'

/**
 * components/ChatPanel/ChatPanel.jsx
 *
 * "Next Gen AI" — the right-side copilot panel (the industry-standard
 * pattern: available from any page, keeps your context, doesn't take
 * over the screen).
 *
 * Answers come from the LOCAL model, grounded in real database facts —
 * the backend gathers the numbers via SQL first, so nothing is invented.
 */

import { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import { Sparkles, Send, X, Clock, List, Play, Check, AlertTriangle, Trash2,
         BookOpen, FileText, LifeBuoy, ExternalLink, Loader2 } from 'lucide-react'
import Markdown from '../Markdown/Markdown'
import { askKavach, getChatSuggestions, interpretInstruction, executeAction, resummarise,
         raiseSupportTicket, collectSupportContext } from '../../lib/api'
import styles from './ChatPanel.module.css'


/** ISO -> the value a datetime-local input expects, in local time. */
function toLocalInput(iso) {
  if (!iso) return ''
  const d = new Date(iso)
  const pad = n => String(n).padStart(2, '0')
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}` +
         `T${pad(d.getHours())}:${pad(d.getMinutes())}`
}


/** One editable field on a proposal, chosen by name. */
function EditableField({ field, proposal, onChange }) {
  if (field === 'frequency') {
    return (
      <label className={styles.editField}>
        <span>Repeat</span>
        <select value={proposal.frequency || 'once'}
                onChange={e => onChange(e.target.value)}>
          <option value="once">Once</option>
          <option value="hourly">Every hour</option>
          <option value="daily">Every day</option>
          <option value="weekdays">Every weekday</option>
          <option value="weekly">Every week</option>
        </select>
      </label>
    )
  }
  if (field === 'run_at') {
    return (
      <label className={styles.editField}>
        <span>First run</span>
        <input type="datetime-local" value={toLocalInput(proposal.run_at)}
               onChange={e => onChange(new Date(e.target.value).toISOString())} />
      </label>
    )
  }
  return null
}


/**
 * Where the conversation is kept between visits.
 *
 * This is deliberately temporary. The right home is the database: once the
 * assistant can create a schedule or run a suite, "who instructed it and
 * who approved" belongs in the audit trail alongside
 * test_case_proposals.accepted_by and healing_proposals.decided_by. Browser
 * storage cannot answer that — it is one laptop, invisible to anyone else.
 *
 * What it does give: survives refresh, browser restart and server restart,
 * and is shared across tabs.
 */
const STORE_KEY = 'kavach-chat-history'
const MAX_STORED = 60          // enough to scroll back through, small enough to write

function loadHistory() {
  try {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem(STORE_KEY)
    if (!raw) return []
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw)
    return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : []
  } catch {
    return []                  // corrupt or unavailable — start clean rather than crash
  }
}

function saveHistory(messages) {
  try {
    // A proposal that was never decided is not carried over: the action it
    // describes may no longer be valid, and offering a stale "Yes, do it"
    // after a reload would be worse than losing it.
    const keep = messages
      .filter(m => !(m.proposal && !m.done && !m.failed && !m.cancelled))
      .slice(-MAX_STORED)
    localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, JSON.stringify(keep))
  } catch {
    // Quota exceeded or storage disabled. The conversation still works in
    // this tab; it just will not survive a reload.
  }
}

// Panel width. The default is comfortable for a question; a long procedural
// answer with numbered steps needs more, and the person reading it knows how
// much better than a default does.
const MIN_W = 340
const DEFAULT_W = 380

// The sidebar's width, and the least the page content may be squeezed to.
// Below roughly 560px the tables on Executions and Reports start wrapping
// into unreadability, which is worse than a narrower assistant.
const SIDEBAR_W = 244
const MIN_CONTENT_W = 560

/**
 * The widest the panel may be, given the window.
 *
 * Derived from what the PAGE needs rather than from a share of the viewport.
 * A percentage cap looks reasonable and still starves a laptop: 45% of
 * 1280px is 576px, which leaves 460px of content beside a 244px sidebar —
 * exactly the cramped layout this is meant to prevent.
 *
 * @returns {number} Maximum panel width in pixels.
 */
function maxWidth() {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return 560
  const available = window.innerWidth - SIDEBAR_W - MIN_CONTENT_W
  return Math.max(MIN_W, Math.min(900, available))
}


export default function ChatPanelV2() {
  // Visible by default; closing it leaves a small button to bring it back.
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(true)

  // Remembered per browser: someone who widens the panel to read a procedure
  // wants it wide next time too.
  const [width, setWidth] = useState(DEFAULT_W)
  const draggingRef = useRef(false)

  useEffect(() => {
    try {
      const saved = parseInt(localStorage.getItem('kavach-chat-width') || '', 10)
      // Clamped on read as well as on write: a width saved on a wide monitor
      // must not cripple the layout when the same person opens a laptop.
      if (saved >= MIN_W) setWidth(Math.min(saved, maxWidth()))
    } catch { /* storage disabled — the default is fine */ }
  }, [])

  // Dragging is bound to the document, not the handle, so the pointer can
  // leave the 6px strip mid-drag without the panel sticking.
  useEffect(() => {
    function move(e) {
      if (!draggingRef.current) return
      const next = Math.min(maxWidth(), Math.max(MIN_W, window.innerWidth - e.clientX))
      setWidth(next)
    }
    function up() {
      if (!draggingRef.current) return
      draggingRef.current = false
      document.body.style.cursor = ''
      document.body.style.userSelect = ''
      try { localStorage.setItem('kavach-chat-width', String(widthRef.current)) } catch {}
    }
    window.addEventListener('mousemove', move)
    window.addEventListener('mouseup', up)
    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener('mousemove', move)
      window.removeEventListener('mouseup', up)
    }
  }, [])

  const widthRef = useRef(DEFAULT_W)
  useEffect(() => { widthRef.current = width }, [width])

  useEffect(() => {
    const clamp = () => setWidth(w => Math.min(w, maxWidth()))
    window.addEventListener('resize', clamp)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', clamp)
  }, [])

  function startDrag() {
    draggingRef.current = true
    // Set on the body so the cursor holds while dragging over other elements.
    document.body.style.cursor = 'col-resize'
    document.body.style.userSelect = 'none'
  }
  const [messages, setMessages] = useState([])
  const [restored, setRestored] = useState(false)
  const [input, setInput] = useState('')
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)
  const [suggestions, setSuggestions] = useState([])

  // Restore once, on mount. Guarded so the empty initial state is never
  // written back over a real history.
  useEffect(() => {
    setMessages(loadHistory())
    setRestored(true)
  }, [])

  useEffect(() => {
    if (restored) saveHistory(messages)
  }, [messages, restored])

  // Another tab wrote to storage. Without this the tabs share the data but
  // not the view, and they drift apart until one is reloaded.
  useEffect(() => {
    function onStorage(e) {
      if (e.key !== STORE_KEY) return
      setMessages(loadHistory())
    }
    window.addEventListener('storage', onStorage)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('storage', onStorage)
  }, [])
  const endRef = useRef(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    getChatSuggestions().then(d => setSuggestions(d.suggestions || [])).catch(() => {})
  }, [])

  /**
   * Push the page content aside instead of covering it. On narrow screens
   * there isn't room to push, so the panel overlays instead.
   *
   * The padding must track the panel's ACTUAL width. It used to be a
   * constant 380px, which was correct while the panel could not be resized
   * and silently wrong the moment it could: widening the panel then covered
   * the page rather than making room, and the content underneath was simply
   * hidden. Any fixed-position panel that pushes content has to keep these
   * two numbers in step.
   *
   * No transition while dragging — animating padding against a mousemove
   * makes the content lag behind the edge being dragged.
   */
  useEffect(() => {
    const apply = () => {
      const roomToPush = window.innerWidth >= 1200
      document.body.style.transition = draggingRef.current
        ? 'none' : 'padding-right .22s ease'
      document.body.style.paddingRight = open && roomToPush ? `${width}px` : ''
    }
    apply()
    window.addEventListener('resize', apply)
    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener('resize', apply)
      document.body.style.paddingRight = ''
    }
  }, [open, width])

  useEffect(() => {
    endRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' })
  }, [messages, busy])

  /**
   * Send a message.
   *
   * An instruction ("run the smoke suite") is INTERPRETED first, which
   * executes nothing — it returns a proposal for the user to confirm. A
   * question goes to the existing read-only endpoint, unchanged.
   */
  async function send(text) {
    const q = (text ?? input).trim()
    if (!q || busy) return
    setInput('')
    setMessages(m => [...m, { role: 'user', text: q }])
    setBusy(true)
    try {
      const intent = await interpretInstruction(q)

      if (intent && !intent.not_an_action) {
        if (intent.proposal) {
          // Show what will happen and wait. Nothing has run.
          setMessages(m => [...m, {
            role: 'ai', proposal: intent.proposal, summary: intent.summary,
            confirmFields: intent.confirm_fields || [],
          }])
          return
        }
        if (intent.needs_clarification) {
          setMessages(m => [...m, {
            role: 'ai', text: intent.question, options: intent.options,
          }])
          return
        }
        if (intent.error) {
          setMessages(m => [...m, {
            role: 'ai', text: intent.error + (intent.detail ? ` ${intent.detail}` : ''),
            error: true,
          }])
          return
        }
      }

      const res = await askKavach(q)
      setMessages(m => [...m, {
        role: 'ai', text: res.answer, facts: res.facts_used, stats: res.stats,
        // Carried so the answer can show what it was built from, and so the
        // panel can offer a ticket at the moment the help content fell short
        // rather than telling the user to go and find the Help screen.
        sources: res.sources || [], helpGap: !!res.help_gap, question: q,
      }])
    } catch (e) {
      setMessages(m => [...m, { role: 'ai', text: `Couldn't reach the assistant: ${e.message}`, error: true }])
    } finally {
      setBusy(false)
    }
  }

  /** Carry out a proposal the user has confirmed. */
  async function confirmAction(idx, proposal) {
    setMessages(m => m.map((msg, i) => i === idx ? { ...msg, running: true } : msg))
    try {
      const res = await executeAction(proposal)
      setMessages(m => m.map((msg, i) => i === idx
        ? { ...msg, running: false, done: !res.error, result: res.message || res.error,
            failed: !!res.error }
        : msg))
    } catch (e) {
      setMessages(m => m.map((msg, i) => i === idx
        ? { ...msg, running: false, failed: true, result: e.message } : msg))
    }
  }

  /**
   * Change a value on a proposal before it is confirmed.
   *
   * The schedule's NAME is derived from its frequency, so it has to be
   * recomputed here too — otherwise changing "weekdays" to "once" left a
   * schedule called "Smoke Suite 1 — weekdays" that runs once.
   */
  async function editProposal(idx, field, value) {
    let next
    setMessages(m => m.map((msg, i) => {
      if (i !== idx) return msg
      next = { ...msg.proposal, [field]: value }
      return { ...msg, proposal: next }
    }))
    // The sentence is rebuilt by the backend so the wording — and any value
    // derived from these fields, like the schedule's name — comes from one
    // place rather than being duplicated here.
    try {
      const r = await resummarise(next)
      if (r?.summary) {
        setMessages(m => m.map((msg, i) => i === idx ? { ...msg, summary: r.summary } : msg))
      }
    } catch { /* the card still shows the previous sentence */ }
  }

  function cancelAction(idx) {
    setMessages(m => m.map((msg, i) => i === idx
      ? { ...msg, cancelled: true } : msg))
  }

  function onKeyDown(e) {
    if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) { e.preventDefault(); send() }
  }

  if (!open) {
    return (
      <button className={styles.reopen} onClick={() => setOpen(true)} title="Ask NextGen2 AI">
        <Sparkles size={16} strokeWidth={2} />
        Ask NextGen2
      </button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <aside className={styles.panel} style={{ width }} aria-label="NextGen2 AI">
      {/* Drag to resize. Keyboard users get the same range through the arrow
          keys, since a mouse-only control is not a control for everyone. */}
      <div
        className={styles.resizer}
        onMouseDown={startDrag}
        role="separator"
        aria-orientation="vertical"
        aria-label="Resize the assistant panel"
        tabIndex={0}
        onKeyDown={e => {
          if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft') setWidth(w => Math.min(maxWidth(), w + 24))
          if (e.key === 'ArrowRight') setWidth(w => Math.max(MIN_W, w - 24))
        }}
      />
      <div className={styles.head}>
        <div className={styles.orb}>
          <Sparkles size={16} strokeWidth={2} />
        </div>
        <div className={styles.headText}>
          <div className={styles.title}>NextGen2 AI</div>
          <div className={styles.subtitle}>Powered by Netra (Coming Soon)</div>
        </div>
        <button
            className={styles.close}
            onClick={() => { setMessages([]); try { localStorage.removeItem(STORE_KEY) } catch {} }}
            title="Clear this conversation"
            aria-label="Clear conversation"
          >
            <Trash2 size={14} />
          </button>
          <button className={styles.close} onClick={() => setOpen(false)} aria-label="Close"><X size={15} /></button>
      </div>

      <div className={styles.body}>
        {messages.length === 0 ? (
          <div className={styles.hero}>
            <div className={styles.heroOrb}>
              <Sparkles size={27} strokeWidth={1.8} />
            </div>
            <h2>Ask about your tests</h2>
            <p>Coverage, failures, flaky tests — answered from your real data.</p>
            <div className={styles.suggestions}>
              {suggestions.map((s, i) => (
                <button key={i} className={styles.suggestion} onClick={() => send(s.title)}>
                  <strong>{s.title}</strong>
                  <span>{s.sub}</span>
                </button>
              ))}
            </div>
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div className={styles.thread}>
            {messages.map((m, i) => (
              <div key={i} className={m.role === 'user' ? styles.userMsg : styles.aiMsg}>
                {m.role === 'ai' && <div className={styles.aiTag}>NextGen2 AI</div>}
                {m.text && (
                  m.role === 'ai' && !m.error
                    // Model replies arrive as markdown — numbered steps, bold
                    // field names, bare URLs. Rendered as raw text they read
                    // as a wall of asterisks with no line breaks, which is
                    // indistinguishable from a wrong answer.
                    ? <Markdown text={m.text} className={styles.prose} />
                    : <div className={m.error ? styles.errText : undefined}>{m.text}</div>
                )}

                {/* A proposal is shown, never performed. Nothing has run at
                    this point — the user decides. */}
                {m.proposal && (
                  <div className={styles.actionCard}>
                    <div className={styles.actionHead}>
                      <Play size={13} strokeWidth={2} />
                      About to do this
                    </div>
                    <div className={styles.actionSummary}>{m.summary}</div>

                    {/* A schedule is a commitment, so the time and frequency
                        are editable here rather than take-it-or-leave-it.
                        The model's reading is a starting point. */}
                    {m.confirmFields?.length > 0 &&
                     !m.done && !m.failed && !m.cancelled && (
                      <div className={styles.actionEdit}>
                        {m.confirmFields.map(f => (
                          <EditableField key={f} field={f} proposal={m.proposal}
                                         onChange={v => editProposal(i, f, v)} />
                        ))}
                      </div>
                    )}

                    {m.done && (
                      <div className={styles.actionDone}>
                        <Check size={13} strokeWidth={2} />
                        <Markdown text={m.result} className={styles.resultProse} />
                      </div>
                    )}
                    {m.failed && (
                      <div className={styles.actionFailed}>
                        <AlertTriangle size={13} strokeWidth={2} />
                        <Markdown text={m.result} className={styles.resultProse} />
                      </div>
                    )}
                    {m.cancelled && (
                      <div className={styles.actionCancelled}>Cancelled — nothing was changed.</div>
                    )}

                    {!m.done && !m.failed && !m.cancelled && (
                      <div className={styles.actionBtns}>
                        <button className={styles.actionGo} disabled={m.running}
                                onClick={() => confirmAction(i, m.proposal)}>
                          {m.running ? 'Working…' : 'Yes, do it'}
                        </button>
                        <button className={styles.actionNo} disabled={m.running}
                                onClick={() => cancelAction(i)}>
                          Cancel
                        </button>
                      </div>
                    )}
                  </div>
                )}

                {/* Ambiguous instruction — ask rather than guess. */}
                {m.options && (
                  <div className={styles.optionList}>
                    {m.options.map((o, k) => (
                      <button key={k} className={styles.optionChip} onClick={() => send(o)}>
                        {o}
                      </button>
                    ))}
                  </div>
                )}

                {m.sources?.length > 0 && <Sources sources={m.sources} />}

                {m.role === 'ai' && m.question && !m.proposal && (
                  <TicketFromChat
                    question={m.question}
                    answer={m.text}
                    prominent={m.helpGap || (m.sources || []).length === 0}
                  />
                )}

                {(m.facts || m.stats) && <MessageMeta facts={m.facts} stats={m.stats} />}
              </div>
            ))}
            {busy && (
              <div className={styles.aiMsg}>
                <div className={styles.aiTag}>NextGen2 AI</div>
                <div className={styles.thinking}><span /><span /><span /></div>
              </div>
            )}
            <div ref={endRef} />
          </div>
        )}
      </div>

      <div className={styles.inputWrap}>
        <div className={styles.inputBox}>
          <textarea
            value={input}
            onChange={e => setInput(e.target.value)}
            onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
            placeholder="Ask about coverage, failures, health…"
            rows={1}
          />
          <button className={styles.send} onClick={() => send()} disabled={busy || !input.trim()} aria-label="Send">
            <Send size={15} strokeWidth={2} />
          </button>
        </div>
        <div className={styles.disclaimer}>Answers come from your database. Verify before acting.</div>
      </div>
    </aside>
  )
}

/**
 * Compact footer under each answer:
 *  - a stats chip (latency + tokens + model) — click to expand
 *  - a link to the exact figures the answer was based on, so any number
 *    can be traced back to the database (useful for audit)
 */
function MessageMeta({ facts, stats }) {
  const [showFacts, setShowFacts] = useState(false)
  const [showStats, setShowStats] = useState(false)

  const secs = stats?.latency_ms ? (stats.latency_ms / 1000).toFixed(1) : null

  return (
    <div className={styles.meta}>
      <div className={styles.metaRow}>
        {stats && (
          <button className={styles.metaChip} onClick={() => setShowStats(!showStats)} title="Model, latency and tokens">
            <Clock size={11} strokeWidth={2} />
            {secs ? `${secs}s` : 'stats'}
          </button>
        )}
        {facts && Object.keys(facts).length > 0 && (
          <button className={styles.metaChip} onClick={() => setShowFacts(!showFacts)} title="The data this answer used">
            <List size={11} strokeWidth={2} />
            Source data
          </button>
        )}
      </div>

      {showStats && stats && (
        <div className={styles.statsBox}>
          <div><span>Model</span><code>{stats.model || '—'}</code></div>
          <div><span>Latency</span><code>{secs ? `${secs}s` : '—'}</code></div>
          <div><span>Input tokens</span><code>{stats.input_tokens ?? '—'}</code></div>
          <div><span>Output tokens</span><code>{stats.output_tokens ?? '—'}</code></div>
          <div className={styles.statsNote}>Runs locally — no tokens billed, no data sent externally.</div>
        </div>
      )}

      {showFacts && facts && Object.keys(facts).length > 0 && (
        <pre className={styles.factsPre}>{JSON.stringify(facts, null, 2)}</pre>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

/**
 * The help passages an answer was built from.
 *
 * Shown because a cited answer and an uncited one look identical otherwise,
 * and the difference matters: an answer with sources can be checked against
 * an approved article at a known version, which is what makes it usable in a
 * regulated setting. Each chip carries the version for the same reason — "we
 * told you that in v2" is a different claim from "we told you that".
 *
 * Clicking opens the article on the Help screen rather than expanding text
 * here: the article is the authority, so it should be read where it lives.
 */
function Sources({ sources }) {
  // The same article often supplies several passages. Collapse them, so the
  // row reads as two sources rather than five chips repeating one title.
  const unique = []
  const seen = new Set()
  for (const s of sources) {
    const key = `${s.source_type}:${s.label}:${s.version ?? ''}`
    if (seen.has(key)) continue
    seen.add(key)
    unique.push(s)
  }

  return (
    <div className={styles.sources}>
      <div className={styles.sourcesLabel}>Based on</div>
      <div className={styles.sourceChips}>
        {unique.map((s, i) => (
          s.source_type === 'article' ? (
            <a key={i} className={styles.sourceChip}
               href={`/help?article=${encodeURIComponent(s.label)}`}>
              <BookOpen size={11} strokeWidth={2} />
              {s.title}{s.version ? ` · v${s.version}` : ''}
            </a>
          ) : (
            <span key={i} className={styles.sourceChip}>
              <FileText size={11} strokeWidth={2} />
              {s.title}
            </span>
          )
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}


/**
 * Raise a support ticket without leaving the conversation.
 *
 * The point of a copilot is that you do not have to go somewhere else. Being
 * told "raise a ticket from the Help screen" by the thing you are already
 * talking to is the moment the pattern breaks, so the form is here.
 *
 * The question and the answer are carried into the ticket automatically. What
 * the user asked, and what Kavach told them, is most of what whoever picks
 * the ticket up needs — and re-typing it is exactly the friction that stops
 * people reporting gaps at all.
 *
 * `prominent` distinguishes the two situations: when the help content fell
 * short this is the obvious next step and is shown as a button; otherwise it
 * is a quiet line, so a good answer is not followed by a nag.
 */
function TicketFromChat({ question, answer, prominent }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [detail, setDetail] = useState('')
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)
  const [result, setResult] = useState(null)

  async function raise() {
    if (busy) return
    setBusy(true)
    try {
      const res = await raiseSupportTicket({
        // Asked in the assistant and unanswered: a how-to, not a defect.
        category: 'how-to',
        summary: question.slice(0, 180),
        description:
          `Asked NextGen2 AI:\n${question}\n\n` +
          `NextGen2 AI replied:\n${answer || '(no answer)'}\n\n` +
          (detail.trim() ? `The person added:\n${detail.trim()}\n` : ''),
        context: collectSupportContext({ source: 'kavach-ai', question }),
      })
      setResult(res)
    } catch (e) {
      setResult({ error: e.message })
    } finally {
      setBusy(false)
    }
  }

  if (result) {
    return (
      <div className={result.error ? styles.ticketFailed : styles.ticketDone}>
        {result.error ? (
          <><AlertTriangle size={12} strokeWidth={2} /> {result.error}</>
        ) : (
          <>
            <Check size={12} strokeWidth={2.4} />
            Ticket {result.external_ref || `#${result.id}`} raised.
            {result.external_url && (
              <a href={result.external_url} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
                Open <ExternalLink size={10} />
              </a>
            )}
          </>
        )}
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (!open) {
    return (
      <button
        className={prominent ? styles.ticketCta : styles.ticketLink}
        onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        <LifeBuoy size={prominent ? 13 : 11} strokeWidth={2} />
        {prominent ? 'Raise a ticket about this' : 'Not what you needed?'}
      </button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className={styles.ticketBox}>
      <div className={styles.ticketHead}>
        <LifeBuoy size={12} strokeWidth={2} /> Raise a ticket
      </div>
      <p className={styles.ticketNote}>
        Your question and this answer are attached automatically.
      </p>
      <textarea
        className={styles.ticketInput}
        value={detail}
        onChange={e => setDetail(e.target.value)}
        placeholder="Anything to add? (optional)"
        rows={2}
      />
      <div className={styles.ticketBtns}>
        <button className={styles.ticketGo} onClick={raise} disabled={busy}>
          {busy ? <Loader2 size={12} className={styles.spin} /> : null}
          {busy ? 'Raising…' : 'Raise ticket'}
        </button>
        <button className={styles.ticketNo} onClick={() => setOpen(false)} disabled={busy}>
          Cancel
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
