/** Wait for the existing generation SSE contract to finish, not just its headers. */
export async function readGenerationResult(response) {
  if (!response.ok) {
    let message = `Generation request failed (${response.status})`
    try {
      const body = await response.json()
      message = body?.detail?.message || body?.error?.message || body?.detail || message
    } catch { /* preserve the HTTP error */ }
    throw new Error(String(message))
  }
  if (!response.body) throw new Error('Generation response has no event stream')
  const reader = response.body.getReader()
  const decoder = new TextDecoder()
  let buffer = ''
  let failure = null
  let completed = null
  function consume(block) {
    const lines = block.split('\n')
    const event = lines.find(line => line.startsWith('event:'))?.slice(6).trim()
    const data = lines.filter(line => line.startsWith('data:')).map(line => line.slice(5).trimStart()).join('\n')
    if (!data) return
    const parsed = JSON.parse(data)
    // Kavach api.sse.event_stream uses data: {type, data}; also accept
    // standard named SSE events for backwards-compatible stream consumers.
    const type = event || parsed.type
    const value = event ? parsed : parsed.data
    if (type === 'error') failure = value?.message || 'Generation failed'
    if (type === 'complete') {
      if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') throw new Error('Invalid generation completion event')
      completed = value
    }
  }
  try {
    while (true) {
      const { value, done } = await reader.read()
      buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: !done })
      // Normalize only complete CRLF pairs; a chunk may end at the CR.
      buffer = buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')
      let boundary
      while ((boundary = buffer.indexOf('\n\n')) >= 0) {
        consume(buffer.slice(0, boundary))
        buffer = buffer.slice(boundary + 2)
      }
      if (done) {
        if (buffer.trim()) consume(buffer)
        break
      }
    }
  } finally {
    reader.releaseLock()
  }
  if (!completed) throw new Error(failure || 'Generation stream ended before completion')
  const rejected = (completed.results || []).filter(result => result.result !== 'generated')
  if (failure || completed.incomplete || completed.blocked || rejected.length) {
    const message = failure || rejected[0]?.notes || rejected[0]?.message || 'Generation is incomplete; review the test case details.'
    const error = new Error(message)
    error.results = completed.results || []
    throw error
  }
  return completed
}

import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { readGenerationResult } from './generationStream.mjs'

function response(text, chunkSize = 1) {
  const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(text)
  return new Response(new ReadableStream({
    start(controller) {
      for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += chunkSize) controller.enqueue(bytes.slice(i, i + chunkSize))
      controller.close()
    },
  }))
}

test('waits for completion across split CRLF and UTF-8 chunks', async () => {
  const result = await readGenerationResult(response(
    'event: step\r\ndata: {"message":"Génération"}\r\n\r\n' +
    'event: complete\r\ndata: {"generated":1,"incomplete":0,"results":[{"result":"generated"}]}\r\n\r\n'))
  assert.equal(result.generated, 1)
})

test('reports an incomplete procedure rather than treating HTTP 200 as success', async () => {
  await assert.rejects(readGenerationResult(response(
    'event: complete\ndata: {"generated":0,"incomplete":1,"results":[{"result":"incomplete","notes":"Missing captured field"}]}\n\n')),
  /Missing captured field/)
})

test('preserves blocked SSO error', async () => {
  await assert.rejects(readGenerationResult(response(
    'event: error\ndata: {"message":"SSO precheck failed"}\n\nevent: complete\ndata: {"blocked":1}\n\n')), /SSO precheck failed/)
})

test('interrupted stream is not a success', async () => {
  await assert.rejects(readGenerationResult(response('event: step\ndata: {"message":"Started"}\n\n')), /before completion/)
})

test('HTTP error body is exposed', async () => {
  await assert.rejects(readGenerationResult(new Response(JSON.stringify({ detail: { message: 'Invalid proposal' } }), { status: 400 })), /Invalid proposal/)
})

test('supports a final event without a trailing blank line', async () => {
  assert.equal((await readGenerationResult(response('event: complete\ndata: {"generated":1,"results":[{"result":"generated"}]}'))).generated, 1)
})

test('reads the actual api.sse data-only envelope', async () => {
  const result = await readGenerationResult(response(
    'data: {"type":"step","data":{"message":"Generating"}}\n\n' +
    'data: {"type":"complete","data":{"generated":1,"incomplete":0,"results":[{"result":"generated"}]}}\n\n'))
  assert.equal(result.generated, 1)
})

test('backend terminal error closes without a complete event', async () => {
  await assert.rejects(readGenerationResult(response(
    'data: {"type":"error","data":{"message":"Login unavailable"}}\n\n')), /Login unavailable/)
})

test('backend incomplete envelope is rejected', async () => {
  await assert.rejects(readGenerationResult(response(
    'data: {"type":"complete","data":{"incomplete":1,"results":[{"result":"incomplete","notes":"Review saved approval"}]}}\n\n')),
  /Review saved approval/)
})

/**
 * lib/msalConfig.js
 *
 * Centralised Microsoft Entra ID (MSAL) configuration for Kavach.
 * Every value comes from environment variables — nothing is hardcoded here.
 *
 * Required variables (defined in .env.local):
 *   NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_CLIENT_ID
 *       Entra app registration client ID (GUID).
 *   NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_AUTHORITY
 *       https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>
 *   NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_REDIRECT_URI
 *       URI Entra redirects to after a successful login (must match the
 *       app registration's redirect URI list).
 *   NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI
 *       URI Entra redirects to after logout.
 *   NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_API_SCOPE
 *       Backend API scope, e.g. api://<client-id>/access_as_user
 *       Including this scope ensures the acquired access token is issued
 *       for Kavach's own backend, not a generic Microsoft Graph token.
 */

export const msalConfig = {
  auth: {
    clientId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_CLIENT_ID,
    authority: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_AUTHORITY,
    redirectUri: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_REDIRECT_URI,
    postLogoutRedirectUri: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MS_AUTH_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI,
    // After a successful login redirect, MSAL navigates the user back to
    // the page they originally requested.  This is the built-in mechanism
    // for URL preservation — no manual sessionStorage handling is needed.
    navigateToLoginRequestUrl: true,
  },
  cache: {
    // sessionStorage is cleared when the browser tab closes, which is
    // appropriate for enterprise environments where shared computers are
    // common and persistent sessions are a security risk.
    cacheLocation: 'sessionStorage',
    storeAuthStateInCookie: false,
  },
}

/**
 * lib/msalInstance.js
 *
 * The one PublicClientApplication for Kavach.
 *
 * Import `msalInstance` wherever you need the MSAL instance.
 * Never call `new PublicClientApplication()` anywhere else in the codebase.
 *
 * The event callback keeps the active account in sync with every successful
 * auth event (initial login, silent renewal, SSO).  This ensures that
 * `instance.getActiveAccount()` always returns the current user for the
 * lifetime of the session, including after a page refresh where MSAL
 * restores state from sessionStorage.
 */

import { PublicClientApplication, EventType } from '@azure/msal-browser'
import { msalConfig } from './msalConfig'

export const msalInstance = new PublicClientApplication(msalConfig)

// Restore / update the active account after every successful authentication
// event.  MSAL fires these events both when the user first signs in and
// when a silent token renewal succeeds, so this handler covers all cases.
msalInstance.addEventCallback((event) => {
  if (
    (event.eventType === EventType.LOGIN_SUCCESS ||
      event.eventType === EventType.ACQUIRE_TOKEN_SUCCESS ||
      event.eventType === EventType.SSO_SILENT_SUCCESS) &&
    event.payload?.account
  ) {
    msalInstance.setActiveAccount(event.payload.account)
  }
})

FILE: frontend/lib/testDataImport.js
================================================
/**
 * lib/testDataImport.js
 *
 * Turns whatever a user drops into the "Import JSON" control for a
 * scenario's test data into a flat { key: string } object that
 * saveScenarioTestData() can write — even when the file is not perfectly
 * formed JSON.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS: a reviewer importing test data is very likely pasting
 * something exported from elsewhere (a JDE screen scrape, a spreadsheet
 * export, a hand-edited config) rather than something written specifically
 * for this tool. Rejecting anything that is not already a flat, strict
 * JSON object of scalars means the "Import JSON" button only works for
 * files that were already typed by hand in the exact right shape — which
 * defeats the point of an import feature. This module repairs and
 * reshapes common near-misses instead of failing on them, and reports
 * exactly what it changed so nothing is silently altered without the
 * reviewer seeing it before Save.
 *
 * Handles, in order:
 *   1. Strict JSON.parse (the common, already-correct case).
 *   2. Common syntax repairs, then parse again:
 *        - byte-order-mark removal
 *        - // line comments and /* block comments *\/
 *        - trailing commas before } or ]
 *        - unquoted object keys        { ItemNumber: "1" } -> { "ItemNumber": "1" }
 *        - single-quoted strings       'ItemNumber': '1'   -> "ItemNumber": "1"
 *   3. key=value / key: value line format (one pair per line), for files
 *      that are not JSON at all.
 *   4. Shape normalisation on whatever parsed successfully:
 *        - array of [key, value] pairs           -> object
 *        - array of {key, value} / {name, value} objects -> object
 *        - array of plain record objects         -> merged object
 *          (later records win on a shared key)
 *        - nested objects as values              -> flattened up one or
 *          more levels, dropping the grouping key (test data is stored
 *          flat; a key actually referenced by a script, e.g. "ItemNumber",
 *          must exist at the top level to be found by get_data() at
 *          runtime — see service/grounded_runtime.py)
 *        - array values                          -> JSON-stringified,
 *          since scenario test data values are scalars
 *
 * Every adjustment made in step 4 is recorded in the returned `notes`
 * array so the UI can show the reviewer exactly what was changed before
 * they click Save — this function never silently reinterprets data
 * without that being visible.
 *
 * @param {string} rawText - The raw contents of the uploaded file.
 * @returns {{ content: Record<string, string>, notes: string[] }}
 * @throws {Error} if the text cannot be salvaged into any usable shape.
 */
export function normalizeImportedTestData(rawText) {
  const notes = []
  const text = String(rawText || '').replace(/^\uFEFF/, '') // strip BOM

  let parsed = tryStrictJson(text)
  if (parsed === undefined) {
    const repaired = repairJsonText(text)
    parsed = tryStrictJson(repaired)
    if (parsed !== undefined && repaired !== text) {
      notes.push('The file was not strictly valid JSON (comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys, or single quotes) — it was repaired automatically before import.')
    }
  }
  if (parsed === undefined) {
    parsed = tryKeyValueLines(text)
    if (parsed !== undefined) {
      notes.push('The file did not look like JSON at all — it was read as one key/value pair per line instead.')
    }
  }
  if (parsed === undefined) {
    throw new Error(
      'Could not read this file as test data. Expected JSON (an object of key/value pairs), ' +
      'or one "key=value" pair per line.'
    )
  }

  const { content, flattenNotes } = normalizeShape(parsed)
  notes.push(...flattenNotes)

  return { content, notes }
}

function tryStrictJson(text) {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

/** Best-effort repair of common near-JSON authoring mistakes. */
function repairJsonText(text) {
  let t = text

  // Strip // line comments (naive — does not special-case // inside
  // strings, which is an accepted limitation for this recovery path).
  t = t.replace(/(^|[^:])\/\/.*$/gm, '$1')
  // Strip /* block */ comments.
  t = t.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '')
  // Remove trailing commas before } or ].
  t = t.replace(/,(\s*[}\]])/g, '$1')
  // Quote unquoted object keys: { ItemNumber: 1 } -> { "ItemNumber": 1 }
  t = t.replace(/([{,]\s*)([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\s*:/g, '$1"$2":')
  // Convert simple single-quoted strings to double-quoted. Skips values
  // that themselves contain a double quote, to avoid mangling those.
  t = t.replace(/'([^'"\\]*)'/g, '"$1"')

  return t
}

/** Fallback for files that are not JSON at all: one pair per line. */
function tryKeyValueLines(text) {
  const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.trim()).filter(l => l && !l.startsWith('#'))
  if (lines.length === 0) return undefined
  const out = {}
  let matched = 0
  for (const line of lines) {
    const m = line.match(/^([^=:]+)[:=](.*)$/)
    if (!m) continue
    const key = m[1].trim()
    let value = m[2].trim()
    // Strip a single layer of surrounding quotes, if present.
    if ((value.startsWith('"') && value.endsWith('"')) || (value.startsWith("'") && value.endsWith("'"))) {
      value = value.slice(1, -1)
    }
    if (key) { out[key] = value; matched += 1 }
  }
  return matched > 0 ? out : undefined
}

/**
 * Reshape whatever successfully parsed into a flat object of scalar
 * values, recording every structural change made along the way.
 */
function normalizeShape(parsed) {
  const flattenNotes = []

  if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
    if (parsed.length === 0) return { content: {}, flattenNotes }

    if (parsed.every(row => Array.isArray(row) && row.length === 2)) {
      flattenNotes.push('The file was a list of [key, value] pairs — converted to an object.')
      const out = {}
      for (const [k, v] of parsed) out[String(k)] = v
      return { content: flattenScalars(out), flattenNotes }
    }

    const kvShape = parsed.every(row =>
      row && typeof row === 'object' &&
      ('key' in row || 'name' in row || 'field' in row) &&
      'value' in row
    )
    if (kvShape) {
      flattenNotes.push('The file was a list of {key, value} entries — converted to an object.')
      const out = {}
      for (const row of parsed) {
        const key = row.key ?? row.name ?? row.field
        out[String(key)] = row.value
      }
      return { content: flattenScalars(out), flattenNotes }
    }

    if (parsed.every(row => row && typeof row === 'object' && !Array.isArray(row))) {
      flattenNotes.push(
        `The file was a list of ${parsed.length} record(s) — merged into one set of key/value pairs ` +
        '(later records override earlier ones for a shared key).'
      )
      const merged = Object.assign({}, ...parsed)
      return { content: flattenScalars(merged), flattenNotes }
    }

    throw new Error('This looks like a JSON array, but not one this importer recognises (expected key/value pairs or records).')
  }

  if (parsed && typeof parsed === 'object') {
    return { content: flattenScalars(parsed), flattenNotes }
  }

  throw new Error('This file is valid JSON but is not an object or a list of entries.')

  /**
   * Recursively lift nested-object values to the top level, since
   * scenario test data is stored flat and get_data() looks a key up by
   * its bare name (service/grounded_runtime.py) — a key buried inside a
   * grouping object would never be found at runtime.
   */
  function flattenScalars(obj) {
    const out = {}
    const collisions = new Set()
    const walk = (o) => {
      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(o || {})) {
        if (k.startsWith('_')) continue
        if (v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v)) {
          walk(v) // drop the grouping key, lift its children to top level
        } else {
          if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(out, k)) collisions.add(k)
          out[k] = Array.isArray(v) ? JSON.stringify(v) : (v == null ? '' : String(v))
        }
      }
    }
    walk(obj)
    if (collisions.size > 0) {
      flattenNotes.push(
        `Nested grouping was flattened; ${collisions.size} key(s) appeared more than once ` +
        `(${Array.from(collisions).join(', ')}) — the last value seen for each was kept.`
      )
    }
    return out
  }
}
